items.b: Describes the cost and usage incurred through using or purchasing a service provider's resources or services. The primary FOCUS dataset, describing the cost and usage incurred through using or purchasing a service provider's resources or services. Its columns are dimensions, qualitative values such as dates and resource or service provider information used to categorize and filter, and metrics, numeric values used for aggregation. Some columns must always be present, among them BilledCost, EffectiveCost, ListCost, ContractedCost, BillingAccountId, BillingCurrency, ChargeCategory, ChargePeriodStart, ChargePeriodEnd, ServiceName and ServiceProviderName; others must or should be included when the operating model includes a relevant feature, such as commitment discounts, split cost allocation, regions or tags. It joins to the Contract Commitment dataset through Contract Commitment ID, which is a column there and a property inside the JSON object array in ContractApplied here. The dataset must include charges for unused portions of a commitment, and separate discounted and non-discounted charges when a discount covers only part of a charge; discounts should be reflected in the charges they pertain to, not as separate offsetting charges. Under split cost allocation, the method must be documented and accessible to practitioners, and allocation should be offered on an opt-in basis. The page notes the data may carry personal data, most commonly in RequesterDetails and Tags. The Cost and Usage dataset can be joined to the Contract Commitment dataset through the use of the Contract Commitment ID. * In the Cost and Usage dataset, Contract Commitment ID is a property within a JSON object array provided in Contract Applied column. * In the Contract Commitment dataset, Contract Commitment ID is a column.

Describes the catalog rates, internal multipliers, and negotiated unit prices for resources or services offered by a service provider. The primary dataset for standardizing a service provider's catalog rates, multipliers and negotiated prices, letting practitioners perform precise rate lookups, analyze commitment discounts and understand how payable and consumable prices work. It describes the full price list a provider offers as of the date it is captured, not only the stock keeping units (SKUs) that appear in Cost and Usage, and is not derived from Cost and Usage data; a provider may partition delivery, for example by region. It must use the Overwrite delivery mechanism and should contain at least one record for every SkuPriceId referenced in Cost and Usage. It must not contain two records with identical values, including nulls, across ServiceProviderName, SkuPriceId, ContractId, SkuPriceEffectiveStart, PricingCurrency and UnitPriceType, nor overlapping effective periods for records sharing the other five. It joins to Cost and Usage through SkuPriceId in a one-to-many relationship, so resolving a charge's price also means matching ServiceProviderName, effective period, contract, pricing currency and a single UnitPriceType; it can optionally join to Contract Commitment on ContractId. SkuPrice is a preview in version 1.5: its columns, requirements and relationships may change, its requirements are not evaluated for conformance, and neither is the Data Model requirement to include it. The SKU Price dataset relates to the Cost and Usage dataset through the SKU Price ID, enabling the attribution of catalog rates to incurred usage. This is a one-to-many relationship: a single SKU Price ID corresponds to multiple SKU Price records, because a SKU's price varies by effective period, contract, pricing currency, and unit price type. Resolving the price that applies to a Cost and Usage charge therefore requires more than the SKU Price ID alone. The charge must also be aligned to the SKU Price record using the following criteria: * Service Provider: The Cost and Usage Service Provider Name matches the SKU Price record's Service Provider Name. * Effective Period: The Cost and Usage Charge Period Start is on or after the SKU Price record's SKU Price Effective Start and before its SKU Price Effective End; for this criterion, a null SKU Price Effective Start represents the earliest available time, and a null SKU Price Effective End represents the latest available time. Contract: The Contract ID matches a ContractId property extracted from the charge's Contract Applied array (ContractApplied.Elements[].ContractId), or is null for a public list price. Note that ContractApplied only resolves prices associated with contract commitments. * Pricing Currency: The SKU price's Pricing Currency matches the charge's PricingCurrency, or the charge's BillingCurrency when the operating model does not include pricing and billing currency differences. * Unit Price Type: The SKU Price record's Unit Price Type is filtered to a single value (e.g., "List"). Because one contract can carry more than one price type for the same SKU Price ID (e.g., a "Base" rate and a "Contracted" rate), the other criteria alone can match more than one record. Comparing a billed contracted rate against its published catalog rate, for example, requires looking up the corresponding SKU Price record where Unit Price Type is "List". The resolved record carries the unit price for that combination. Notes: * Because the unit prices in the Cost and Usage dataset (i.e., List Unit Price and Contracted Unit Price) are denominated in the Billing Currency, comparing a Cost and Usage rate against a resolved SKU Price record requires currency conversion whenever the charge's Billing Currency differs from its Pricing Currency. However, the Pricing Currency unit prices (i.e., Pricing Currency List Unit Price and Pricing Currency Contracted Unit Price) are denominated in the Pricing Currency and compare directly against Unit Price without conversion. * Because the SKU Price dataset is delivered as a point-in-time snapshot, historical charges in the Cost and Usage dataset may reference a superseded price record that is no longer included in the current catalog. Practitioners must retain historical SKU Price snapshots to reliably resolve older charges. Additionally, the SKU Price dataset can optionally join to the Contract Commitment dataset to relate a specific contracted price to an overarching contractual agreement.

The financial record of charges as they appear on invoices provided by an invoice issuer. A transactional dataset recording charges as they appear on invoices from an invoice issuer, so FinOps practitioners can perform financial reconciliation, tax reporting and payment processing. Where the CostAndUsage dataset gives granular visibility into consumption, InvoiceDetail keeps alignment with the physical or electronic billing documents. It must represent every invoice line item with a non-zero BilledCost on any invoice associated with a BillingAccountId, and its documentation must say how records correspond to invoice line items and whether line items with a BilledCost of 0 are excluded. Required columns include BilledCost, BillingAccountId, BillingCurrency, ChargeCategory, BillingPeriodStart and BillingPeriodEnd, InvoiceId, InvoiceDetailId, InvoiceIssueDate, InvoiceIssueStatus, InvoiceIssuerName, PaymentDueDate, PaymentTerms and ReferenceInvoiceId. PaymentCurrency, PaymentCurrencyBilledCost, PaymentCurrencyInvoiceDetailId and PurchaseOrderNumber are required only under specific operating model conditions, and custom columns must capture any invoice monetary metric with no FOCUS column equivalent. The dataset joins to CostAndUsage on InvoiceIssuerName and InvoiceId, optionally with InvoiceDetailId, though one or both need aggregating before comparison. Some data generators populate these keys in CostAndUsage while the billing period is open, others only after it closes and invoices are issued. It was introduced in version 1.4. The Invoice Detail dataset can be joined to the Cost and Usage dataset through Invoice Issuer Name, Invoice ID, and (optionally) Invoice Detail ID. Note: One or both datasets will need to be aggregated in order to facilitate any comparison. The timing of Invoice ID and Invoice Detail ID availability in Cost and Usage varies across data generators. Some data generators populate these values while the billing period is still open, while others do not populate them until after the billing period is closed and invoices have been issued. For more information, see the Invoice Reconciliation supported feature.

Describes the terms of contracts agreed between a service provider and a customer. Contract terms agreed between a service provider and a customer are the subject of this supporting dataset, introduced in version 1.3. Its 30 columns include the contract and commitment identifiers, ContractId and ContractCommitmentId; contract and commitment periods; commitment cost, quantity, unit and discount percentage; commitment category, benefit category, offer category and duration type; payment model, interval and upfront percentage; lifecycle status; applicability rules; billing currency; and the invoice issuer and service provider names. The dataset must include 27 of these columns in every case. The other three are conditional: ContractCommitmentPaymentUpfrontPercentage must be included when the operating model includes partial upfront payments, and PricingCurrency and PricingCurrencyContractCommitmentCost must be included when the operating model includes pricing and billing currency differences. It joins to the Cost and Usage dataset through ContractCommitmentId, which is a column here but, in Cost and Usage, a property inside the JSON object array held in the ContractApplied column. The dataset must also conform to the shared requirements for correction handling, dataset completeness, dataset configuration and delivery handling, and its specification-defined and custom columns must conform to the column handling and null handling requirements. The Contract Commitment dataset can be joined to the Cost and Usage dataset through the use of Contract Commitment ID. * In the Contract Commitment dataset, Contract Commitment ID is a column. * In the Cost and Usage dataset, Contract Commitment ID is a property within a JSON object array provided in Contract Applied column.

Describes the time intervals and statuses associated with an invoice issuer's billing cycles. A supporting dataset that defines the time intervals and statuses of an invoice issuer's billing cycles, which group and present charges on invoices. It helps FinOps practitioners understand how and when they can use CostAndUsage and InvoiceDetail data for formal financial reporting and for showback and chargeback processes. The dataset must include six mandatory columns, none of which allow nulls: BillingPeriodCreated, BillingPeriodEnd, BillingPeriodLastUpdated and BillingPeriodStart, all Date/Time, plus BillingPeriodStatus and InvoiceIssuerName, both String. Its main role is to give context to the CostAndUsage and InvoiceDetail datasets, which it joins to on the BillingPeriodStart and InvoiceIssuerName columns that those datasets also carry. The dataset must also conform to the specification's requirements for correction handling, dataset completeness, dataset configuration and delivery handling. Its FOCUS columns must follow the FOCUS column handling and null handling requirements, and any custom columns must follow the custom column handling requirements. BillingPeriod was introduced in version 1.4. The Billing Period dataset is primarily used to provide context for the Cost and Usage and Invoice Detail datasets. It is joined using the Billing Period Start and Invoice Issuer Name columns available in those datasets.

A set of properties describing how resources are allocated in data generator-defined split cost allocation. A JSON object, serialized as a String where necessary, describing how resources are allocated when usage records are split in a data generator-calculated split cost allocation. It is Recommended, under the Includes Split Cost Allocation operating model condition, and must be null when a charge is not related to such a split but should not be null when it is. Its Elements array holds entries with a required AllocatedRatio, the allocated charge's share of the origin charge, plus an optional UsageQuantity and a UsageUnit, required with UsageQuantity. Ratios across one origin charge's allocated charges must sum to 1.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Recommended · Dimension / Metric · JSON

items.t: AllocatedMethodDetails MUST adhere to the following requirements:
AllocatedMethodDetails MUST be of type JSON Object (serialized as a String where necessary).
AllocatedMethodDetails MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
AllocatedMethodDetails MUST conform to JsonObjectFormat requirements.
AllocatedMethodDetails MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
AllocatedMethodDetails MUST be null when a charge is not related to a data generator-calculated split cost allocation.
AllocatedMethodDetails SHOULD NOT be null when a charge is related to a data generator-calculated split cost allocation.
AllocatedMethodDetails MUST conform to AllocatedMethodDetailsObject requirements when AllocatedMethodDetails is not null.

items.b: A unique identifier defining the method of data generator-calculated split cost allocation. The identifier of the allocated method, defined by the service provider, that was used for a data generator-calculated split cost allocation; it lets users find in the provider's documentation how an allocated charge was calculated. It is a Conditional string, tied to operating models that include split cost allocation, and must conform to the String Handling requirements. It must be null when a charge is not related to a data generator-calculated split cost allocation and must not be null when it is. The documentation for each such allocation method must reference a single AllocatedMethodId value.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Dimension · String

items.t: AllocatedMethodId MUST adhere to the following requirements:
AllocatedMethodId MUST be of type String.
AllocatedMethodId MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
AllocatedMethodId MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
AllocatedMethodId MUST be null when a charge is not related to a data generator-calculated split cost allocation.
AllocatedMethodId MUST NOT be null when a charge is related to a data generator-calculated split cost allocation.
Data generator-calculated split cost allocation method documentation MUST reference a single AllocatedMethodId value.

items.b: The identifier of the object to which cost is allocated in data generator-calculated split cost allocation. An identifier, assigned by the data generator, for the object to which cost is allocated in a data generator-calculated split cost allocation, used when that target is something other than the charge's ResourceId, as with allocated charges. It is a String. It must be null when a charge is unrelated to such an allocation or represents the unallocated portion of the origin charge, and must not be null on the allocated portion. When present it should be locally unique within the associated ResourceId and ChargePeriod, but may not be unique across them. The feature level is Conditional.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Dimension · String

items.t: AllocatedResourceId MUST adhere to the following requirements:
AllocatedResourceId MUST be of type String.
AllocatedResourceId MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
AllocatedResourceId MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
AllocatedResourceId MUST be null when a charge is not related to a data generator-calculated split cost allocation.
AllocatedResourceId MUST be null when a charge represents the unallocated portion of the origin charge after split cost allocation.
AllocatedResourceId MUST NOT be null when a charge represents the allocated portion of the origin charge.
When AllocatedResourceId is not null, AllocatedResourceId MUST adhere to the following requirements:
AllocatedResourceId SHOULD be a locally unique identifier within the associated ResourceId and ChargePeriod.
AllocatedResourceId MAY NOT be unique across ResourceId or ChargePeriod values.

items.b: The display name of the object to which cost is allocated in data generator-calculated split cost allocation. The display name of the object to which cost is allocated in data generator-calculated split cost allocation. It shows what cost is being allocated to in charges where the service provider allocates costs to something other than the charge's ResourceId, as with allocated charges. It is a Conditional String dimension, applying when the operating model includes split cost allocation, and must conform to the String Handling requirements. It must be null when AllocatedResourceId is null and must not be null when AllocatedResourceId is not null. It may duplicate AllocatedResourceId when a separate display name is not applicable.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Dimension · String

items.t: AllocatedResourceName MUST adhere to the following requirements:
AllocatedResourceName MUST be of type String.
AllocatedResourceName MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
AllocatedResourceName MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
AllocatedResourceName MUST be null when AllocatedResourceId is null.
AllocatedResourceName MUST NOT be null when AllocatedResourceId is not null.
AllocatedResourceName MAY duplicate AllocatedResourceId when a separate display name is not applicable.

items.b: The display name of the service to which cost is allocated in data generator-calculated split cost allocation. The display name of the service to which cost is allocated in a data generator-calculated split cost allocation, identifying the consuming service on allocated charges. On those rows ServiceName keeps the origin charge's service, so this column gives the consuming service its own queryable field without overwriting ServiceName. A Conditional String dimension under the Includes Split Cost Allocation operating model condition, it must follow string handling requirements. It must be null when AllocatedMethodId is null and must not be null otherwise, and it should match the ServiceName the data generator uses for the equivalent service.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Dimension · String

items.t: AllocatedServiceName MUST adhere to the following requirements:
AllocatedServiceName MUST be of type String.
AllocatedServiceName MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
AllocatedServiceName MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
AllocatedServiceName MUST be null when AllocatedMethodId is null.
AllocatedServiceName MUST NOT be null when AllocatedMethodId is not null.
AllocatedServiceName SHOULD match the ServiceName used by the data generator for the equivalent service.

items.b: A set of tags assigned to tag sources that are applicable to allocated charges in data generator-calculated split cost allocation. The tags that apply specifically to allocated charges from a data generator-calculated split cost allocation. It is a JSON object, serialized as a String where necessary, in the key-value format. It must be null when a charge is unrelated to such an allocation and may be null otherwise. When present it must not repeat resource tags already in Tags, must include all applicable user-defined and data generator-defined tags for the AllocatedResourceId, and must give valueless tag keys the boolean value true. Data generator-defined keys must carry a prefix unique to each tag scheme. The feature level is Conditional.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Dimension · JSON

items.t: AllocatedTags MUST adhere to the following requirements:
AllocatedTags MUST be of type JSON Object (serialized as a String where necessary).
AllocatedTags MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
AllocatedTags MUST conform to KeyValueFormat requirements.
AllocatedTags MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
AllocatedTags MUST be null when a charge is not related to a data generator-calculated split cost allocation.
AllocatedTags MAY be null in all other cases.
When AllocatedTags is not null, AllocatedTags MUST adhere to the following requirements:
AllocatedTags MUST NOT include resource tags already present in Tags.
AllocatedTags MUST include all applicable user-defined and data generator-defined tags for the AllocatedResourceId.
Tag keys that do not support corresponding values MUST have a corresponding true (boolean) value set.
Tag values MUST match the provided values unless true (boolean) is applied to valueless tags.
Data generator-defined tags MUST adhere to the following requirements:
Data generator-defined tag keys MUST be prefixed with a predetermined, data generator-specified tag key prefix that is unique to each corresponding provider-specified tag scheme.
Data generator-specified tag key prefixes SHOULD be publicly documented.
User-defined tags MUST adhere to the following requirements:
User-defined tag keys MUST match the tag keys assigned to the tag source when no tag scheme-specific prefix is prepended.
User-defined tag keys MUST match the tag scheme-specific prefix followed by the tag key assigned to the tag source when a tag scheme-specific prefix is prepended.

User-defined tag keys in all user-defined tag schemes MUST include a predetermined, data generator-specified tag key prefix that is unique to each corresponding user-defined tag scheme when the data generator has more than one user-defined tag scheme.

items.b: A host-provider-assigned identifier for a physically separated and isolated area within a Region that provides high availability and fault tolerance. A host-provider-assigned identifier for a physically separated and isolated area within a Region that provides high availability and fault tolerance. It is commonly used to analyze cross-zone data transfer usage and its cost based on where resources are deployed. It is a String that must conform to string handling requirements, and it must be null when a charge is not specific to an availability zone. The feature level is Recommended, under the operating model condition Includes Availability Zones. It is a dimension in the Cost and Usage dataset, introduced in version 0.5.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Recommended · Dimension · String

items.t: AvailabilityZone MUST adhere to the following requirements:
AvailabilityZone MUST be of type String.
AvailabilityZone MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
AvailabilityZone MUST be null when a charge is not specific to an availability zone.

items.b: Cost of a charge as invoiced by the invoice issuer in a given billing period. The cost of a charge as invoiced by the invoice issuer in a billing period, used for invoice reconciliation, cash-based forecasting, budgeting and cost allocation. A Mandatory Decimal in BillingCurrency, it must not be null, must reflect all applicable discounts, and must show invoiced, not estimated, amounts. It must exclude covered-charge portions offset by covering charges and be 0 for fully covered charges, so it can differ from EffectiveCost. It must be 0 for charges from entities not responsible for invoicing. For issued invoices, its sum per InvoiceId and InvoiceIssuerName must match the payable amount within the Rounding Variance Tolerance.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Mandatory · Metric · Decimal

items.t: BilledCost MUST adhere to the following requirements:
BilledCost MUST be of type Decimal.
BilledCost MUST conform to NumericFormat requirements.
BilledCost MUST NOT be null.
BilledCost MUST be denominated in the BillingCurrency.
BilledCost MUST reflect all applicable pricing adjustments, including but not limited to negotiated discounts, commitment discounts, and other applicable discount programs.
BilledCost MUST NOT include any portion of a covered charge that is offset by a covering charge.
BilledCost MUST be 0 for charges that are fully covered by one or more covering charges.
BilledCost MUST reflect amounts as invoiced by the InvoiceIssuerName, not estimated or inferred values.
BilledCost MUST be 0 for charges generated by entities that are not responsible or authorized for invoicing, to avoid double-counting when merging multiple dataset instances.

The sum of BilledCost for a given InvoiceId and InvoiceIssuerName MUST NOT differ from the payable amount provided on the corresponding invoice by more than the Rounding Variance Tolerance when the corresponding invoice has been issued.
The sum of BilledCost MAY differ from preliminary or estimated invoiced amounts when the corresponding invoice has not yet been issued.

items.b: The identifier assigned to a billing account by the invoice issuer. The identifier an invoice issuer assigns to a billing account, commonly used for grouping by organizational constructs, invoice reconciliation and cost allocation. It is a Mandatory String dimension in the Cost and Usage dataset that must conform to the String Handling requirements and must not be null. It must be a unique identifier within an invoice issuer and should be a fully-qualified identifier. It was introduced in version 0.5.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Mandatory · Dimension · String

items.t: BillingAccountId MUST adhere to the following requirements:
BillingAccountId MUST be of type String.
BillingAccountId MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
BillingAccountId MUST NOT be null.
BillingAccountId MUST be a unique identifier within an invoice issuer.
BillingAccountId SHOULD be a fully-qualified identifier.
See Appendix: Grouping constructs for resources or services for details and examples of the different grouping constructs supported by FOCUS.

items.b: The display name assigned to a billing account. The display name assigned to a billing account; billing accounts are commonly used to group by organizational constructs, reconcile invoices and allocate costs. It is a Mandatory String dimension in the CostAndUsage dataset that must conform to the String Handling requirements. The column allows nulls, but it must not be null when the invoice issuer supports assigning a display name to the billing account. The specification's appendix on grouping constructs for resources or services gives details and examples.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Mandatory · Dimension · String

items.t: BillingAccountName MUST adhere to the following requirements:
BillingAccountName MUST be of type String.
BillingAccountName MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
BillingAccountName MUST NOT be null when the invoice issuer supports assigning a display name for the billing account.
See Appendix: Grouping constructs for resources or services for details and examples of the different grouping constructs supported by FOCUS.

items.b: An invoice-issuer-assigned name to identify the type of billing account. A readable display name, not a code, that the invoice issuer assigns to identify the type of billing account. It is commonly used to map FOCUS and provider constructs, summarize costs across providers, or support invoicing and chargeback. It is a String that must be a consistent, readable display value. It must be null when BillingAccountId is null and must not be null when BillingAccountId is not null. The feature level is Conditional, under the operating model condition Includes Multiple Billing Account Types. It is a dimension in the Cost and Usage dataset, introduced in version 1.2.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Dimension · String

items.t: BillingAccountType MUST adhere to the following requirements:
BillingAccountType MUST be of type String.
BillingAccountType MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
BillingAccountType MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
BillingAccountType MUST be null when BillingAccountId is null.
BillingAccountType MUST NOT be null when BillingAccountId is not null.
BillingAccountType MUST be a consistent, readable display value.

items.b: Represents the currency that a charge was billed in. The currency a charge was billed in, commonly used when costs need to be grouped or aggregated. It is a Mandatory string that must not be null and must conform to the String Handling and Currency Format requirements. It must match the currency used in the invoice generated by the invoice issuer, and it must be expressed in a national currency, such as US dollars (USD) or euros (EUR). It has been part of the specification since version 0.5.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Mandatory · Dimension · String

items.t: BillingCurrency MUST adhere to the following requirements:
BillingCurrency MUST be of type String.
BillingCurrency MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
BillingCurrency MUST conform to CurrencyFormat requirements.
BillingCurrency MUST NOT be null.
BillingCurrency MUST match the currency used in the invoice generated by the invoice issuer.
BillingCurrency MUST be expressed in national currency (e.g., USD, EUR).

items.b: The exclusive end bound of a billing period. In the Cost and Usage dataset, this is the exclusive end bound of a billing period. With a BillingPeriodStart of 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z and a BillingPeriodEnd of 2024-02-01T00:00:00Z, the period includes charges for January but not charges for February, because the start is the inclusive start bound and the end is the exclusive end bound. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements and must not be null. It dates from version 0.5.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Mandatory · Dimension · Date/Time

items.t: BillingPeriodEnd MUST adhere to the following requirements:
BillingPeriodEnd MUST be of type Date/Time.
BillingPeriodEnd MUST conform to DateTimeFormat requirements.
BillingPeriodEnd MUST NOT be null.
BillingPeriodEnd MUST be the exclusive end bound of the billing period.

items.b: The inclusive start bound of a billing period. The inclusive start bound of a billing period. A period whose BillingPeriodStart is 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z and whose BillingPeriodEnd is 2024-02-01T00:00:00Z includes charges for January but not February, because BillingPeriodEnd is the exclusive end bound. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension in the CostAndUsage dataset that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements, must not be null, and must be the inclusive start bound of the billing period.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Mandatory · Dimension · Date/Time

items.t: BillingPeriodStart MUST adhere to the following requirements:
BillingPeriodStart MUST be of type Date/Time.
BillingPeriodStart MUST conform to DateTimeFormat requirements.
BillingPeriodStart MUST NOT be null.
BillingPeriodStart MUST be the inclusive start bound of the billing period.

items.b: The identifier assigned to a capacity reservation by the service provider. The identifier a service provider assigns to a capacity reservation, commonly used to allocate charges for capacity reservation usage. It is a Conditional String dimension in CostAndUsage, applying under the Includes Capacity Reservations operating model condition, and must conform to the String Handling requirements. It must be null when a charge is not related to a capacity reservation, must not be null when a charge represents the unused portion of one, and should not be null whenever a charge is related to one. When present, it must be unique within the service provider and should be fully qualified.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Dimension · String

items.t: CapacityReservationId MUST adhere to the following requirements:
CapacityReservationId MUST be of type String.
CapacityReservationId MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
CapacityReservationId MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
CapacityReservationId MUST be null when a charge is not related to a capacity reservation.
CapacityReservationId MUST NOT be null when a charge represents the unused portion of a capacity reservation.
CapacityReservationId SHOULD NOT be null when a charge is related to a capacity reservation.
When CapacityReservationId is not null, CapacityReservationId MUST adhere to the following requirements:
CapacityReservationId MUST be a unique identifier within the service provider.
CapacityReservationId SHOULD be a fully-qualified identifier.

items.b: Indicates whether the charge represents either the consumption of a capacity reservation or when a capacity reservation is unused. Whether a charge represents consumption of the capacity reservation identified in CapacityReservationId or the unused portion of that reservation. It is a Conditional String dimension, applying when the operating model includes capacity reservations, with two allowed values, "Used" and "Unused". It must be null when CapacityReservationId is null, and must not be null when CapacityReservationId is not null and ChargeCategory is "Usage". When present it must be "Unused" for a charge representing the unused portion of a capacity reservation and "Used" for a charge representing the used portion.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Dimension · String
items.x: Includes Capacity Reservations Value Description Used Charges that utilized a specific amount of a capacity reservation. Unused Charges that represent the unused portion of a capacity reservation.

items.t: CapacityReservationStatus MUST adhere to the following requirements:
CapacityReservationStatus MUST be of type String.
CapacityReservationStatus MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
CapacityReservationStatus MUST be null when CapacityReservationId is null.
CapacityReservationStatus MUST NOT be null when CapacityReservationId is not null and ChargeCategory is "Usage".
When CapacityReservationStatus is not null, CapacityReservationStatus MUST adhere to the following requirements:
CapacityReservationStatus MUST be one of the allowed values.
CapacityReservationStatus MUST be "Unused" when the charge represents the unused portion of a capacity reservation.
CapacityReservationStatus MUST be "Used" when the charge represents the used portion of a capacity reservation.

items.b: Represents the highest-level classification of a charge based on the nature of how it is billed. The highest-level classification of a charge based on how it is billed. A Mandatory String dimension, it must not be null and must be one of five allowed values, each covering positive or negative amounts including refunds: "Usage" for consumption, "Purchase" for acquiring a service, resource or commitment, "Tax" for levied taxes, "Credit" for incentives or allowances unrelated to other charges, and "Adjustment" for billing modifications fitting no other category. For "Usage" and "Purchase" charges with a non-null SkuPriceId, it must match SkuPrice.ChargeCategory for the same SkuPriceId and ServiceProviderName, a rule excluded from conformance while SkuPrice is a preview.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Mandatory · Dimension · String
items.x: Not applicable Value Description Usage Positive or negative charges based on the quantity of a service or resource that was consumed over a given period of time including refunds. Purchase Positive or negative charges for the acquisition of a service or resource bought upfront or on a recurring basis including refunds. Tax Positive or negative applicable taxes that are levied by the relevant authorities including refunds. Tax charges may vary depending on factors such as the location, jurisdiction, and local or federal regulations. Credit Positive or negative charges granted by the service provider for various scenarios e.g., promotional credits or corrections to promotional credits. Adjustment Positive or negative charges the service provider applies that do not fall into other category values.

items.t: ChargeCategory MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ChargeCategory MUST be of type String.
ChargeCategory MUST NOT be null.
ChargeCategory MUST be one of the allowed values.
ChargeCategory MUST be "Usage" when the charge represents consumption of a service or resource.
ChargeCategory MUST be "Purchase" when the charge represents acquisition of a service, resource, or commitment.
ChargeCategory MUST be "Tax" when the charge represents taxes levied by the relevant authorities.
ChargeCategory MUST be "Credit" when the charge represents a financial incentive or allowance unrelated to other charges.
ChargeCategory MUST be "Adjustment" when the charge represents a billing modification that does not fall into other ChargeCategories.

ChargeCategory for a given SkuPriceId and ServiceProviderName MUST match SkuPrice.ChargeCategory for the same SkuPrice.SkuPriceId and SkuPrice.ServiceProviderName when SkuPriceId is not null and ChargeCategory is "Usage" or "Purchase".

items.b: Indicates whether a charge represents a correction to a previously closed billing period. A marker showing whether a charge is a correction to a previously closed billing period, separating those corrections from all other charges, including regular charges and corrections to open billing periods. It is a String whose only allowed value is "Correction", covering cases such as refunds and credit modifications. It must be null when the charge is not a correction to a previously closed billing period and must not be null when it is. The feature level is Mandatory, and the column allows nulls. It is a dimension introduced in version 1.0.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Mandatory · Dimension · String
items.x: Not applicable Value Description Correction Correction to a previously closed billing period (e.g., refunds and credit modifications).

items.t: ChargeClass MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ChargeClass MUST be of type String.
ChargeClass MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
ChargeClass MUST be null when the charge does not represent a correction to a previously closed billing period.
ChargeClass MUST NOT be null when the charge represents a correction to a previously closed billing period.
ChargeClass MUST be "Correction" when ChargeClass is not null.

items.b: Self-contained summary of the charge's purpose and price. A self-contained summary of a charge's purpose and price that gives high-level context for a row without further discovery, typically covering a select group of details from across a billing dataset or information not otherwise available. It is a Mandatory String dimension in the Cost and Usage dataset that must conform to the String Handling requirements. Although Mandatory, it allows nulls: the rule is only that it should not be null. Its maximum length should be provided in the corresponding FOCUS Metadata Schema.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Mandatory · Dimension · String

items.t: ChargeDescription MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ChargeDescription MUST be of type String.
ChargeDescription MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
ChargeDescription SHOULD NOT be null.
ChargeDescription maximum length SHOULD be provided in the corresponding FOCUS Metadata Schema.

items.b: Indicates how often a charge will occur. How often a charge occurs, used with the charge period columns to understand recurrence, forecast upcoming charges and tell one-time from recurring purchase fees. It is a Recommended String dimension that must not be null and must be one of three allowed values: "One-Time" for charges that happen once and will not repeat, "Recurring" for charges that repeat on a periodic cadence whether or not the service was used, and "Usage-Based" for charges that repeat every time the service is used and are not recorded when it is not. It must not be "Usage-Based" when ChargeCategory is "Purchase".
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Recommended · Dimension · String
items.x: Not applicable Value Description One-Time Charges that only happen once and will not repeat. One-time charges are typically recorded on the hour or day when the cost was incurred. Recurring Charges that repeat on a periodic cadence (e.g., weekly, monthly) regardless of whether the product or service was used. Recurring charges typically happen on the same day or point within every period. The charge date does not change based on how or when the service is used. Usage-Based Charges that repeat every time the service is used. Usage-based charges are typically recorded hourly or daily, based on the granularity of the cost data for the period when the service was used (referred to as charge period). Usage-based charges are not recorded when the service is not used.

items.t: ChargeFrequency MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ChargeFrequency MUST be of type String.
ChargeFrequency MUST NOT be null.
ChargeFrequency MUST be one of the allowed values.
ChargeFrequency MUST NOT be "Usage-Based" when ChargeCategory is "Purchase".

items.b: The exclusive end bound of a charge period. The exclusive end bound of a charge's effective period. With ChargePeriodStart at 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z and ChargePeriodEnd at 2024-01-02T00:00:00Z, the period includes charges for January 1 but not January 2, because the start is the inclusive bound and the end is the exclusive one. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension in the CostAndUsage dataset that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements and must not be null.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Mandatory · Dimension · Date/Time

items.t: ChargePeriodEnd MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ChargePeriodEnd MUST be of type Date/Time.
ChargePeriodEnd MUST conform to DateTimeFormat requirements.
ChargePeriodEnd MUST NOT be null.
ChargePeriodEnd MUST be the exclusive end bound of the effective period of the charge.

items.b: The inclusive start bound of a charge period. The inclusive start bound of a charge period, paired with ChargePeriodEnd as the exclusive end bound. A period starting 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z and ending 2024-01-02T00:00:00Z therefore includes charges for January 1 but not for January 2. It is a mandatory Date/Time dimension in the CostAndUsage dataset that must conform to date/time format requirements, must not be null, and must be the inclusive start bound of the charge's effective period.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Mandatory · Dimension · Date/Time

items.t: ChargePeriodStart MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ChargePeriodStart MUST be of type Date/Time.
ChargePeriodStart MUST conform to DateTimeFormat requirements.
ChargePeriodStart MUST NOT be null.
ChargePeriodStart MUST be the inclusive start bound of the effective period of the charge.

items.b: Indicates whether the commitment discount identified in the Commitment Discount ID column is based on usage quantity or cost (aka "spend"). Whether the commitment discount identified in CommitmentDiscountId is based on usage quantity or on cost, also called spend. It applies only to commitment discounts, not to negotiated discounts. This Conditional string, tied to operating models that include commitment discounts, must be one of two allowed values: Spend, for commitment discounts that require a predetermined amount of spend, or Usage, for those that require a predetermined amount of usage. It must be null when CommitmentDiscountId is null and must not be null when CommitmentDiscountId is not null.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Dimension · String
items.x: Includes Commitment Discounts Value Description Spend Commitment discounts that require a predetermined amount of spend. Usage Commitment discounts that require a predetermined amount of usage.

items.t: CommitmentDiscountCategory MUST adhere to the following requirements:
CommitmentDiscountCategory MUST be of type String.
CommitmentDiscountCategory MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
CommitmentDiscountCategory MUST be null when CommitmentDiscountId is null.
CommitmentDiscountCategory MUST NOT be null when CommitmentDiscountId is not null.
CommitmentDiscountCategory MUST be one of the allowed values.

items.b: The identifier assigned to a commitment discount by the service provider. The identifier a service provider assigns to a commitment discount, used for chargeback and savings per commitment discount; it does not apply to negotiated discounts. This Conditional string, tied to operating models that include commitment discounts, must be null when a charge is not related to a commitment discount and must not be null when it is. When present, it must be unique within the service provider and should be fully qualified. It must equal ResourceId when ChargeCategory is "Purchase" and the charge purchases that commitment discount, and when ChargeCategory is "Usage" and the charge is its unused portion.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Dimension · String

items.t: CommitmentDiscountId MUST adhere to the following requirements:
CommitmentDiscountId MUST be of type String.
CommitmentDiscountId MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
CommitmentDiscountId MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
CommitmentDiscountId MUST be null when a charge is not related to a commitment discount.
CommitmentDiscountId MUST NOT be null when a charge is related to a commitment discount.
When CommitmentDiscountId is not null, CommitmentDiscountId MUST adhere to the following requirements:
CommitmentDiscountId MUST be a unique identifier within the service provider.
CommitmentDiscountId MUST be equal to ResourceId when ChargeCategory is "Purchase" and the charge represents a purchase of that commitment discount.
CommitmentDiscountId MUST be equal to ResourceId when ChargeCategory is "Usage" and the charge represents an unused portion of that commitment discount.
CommitmentDiscountId SHOULD be a fully-qualified identifier.

items.b: The display name assigned to a commitment discount. The display name assigned to a commitment discount, applicable only to commitment discounts and not to negotiated discounts. It is a Conditional String dimension in the CostAndUsage dataset under the Includes Commitment Discounts operating model condition, and must follow string handling requirements. It must be null when CommitmentDiscountId is null. When CommitmentDiscountId is not null, it must not be null if a display name can be assigned to the commitment discount, and may be null if one cannot. No specific value format is defined.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Dimension · String

items.t: CommitmentDiscountName MUST adhere to the following requirements:
CommitmentDiscountName MUST be of type String.
CommitmentDiscountName MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
CommitmentDiscountName MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
CommitmentDiscountName MUST be null when CommitmentDiscountId is null.
When CommitmentDiscountId is not null, CommitmentDiscountName MUST adhere to the following requirements:
CommitmentDiscountName MUST NOT be null when a display name can be assigned to a commitment discount.
CommitmentDiscountName MAY be null when a display name cannot be assigned to a commitment discount.

items.b: The amount of a commitment discount purchased or accounted for in commitment discount related rows that is denominated in Commitment Discount Units. The amount of a commitment discount purchased or accounted for, denominated in CommitmentDiscountUnit. It is a Decimal. It must be null when SkuPriceId is null; on "Usage" or "Purchase" rows with a CommitmentDiscountId it must not be null unless ChargeClass is "Correction", when it may be null; otherwise it must be null. On purchases it is the eligible quantity over the term or per charge period, depending on ChargeFrequency; on usage it is the quantity consumed or left unused, depending on CommitmentDiscountStatus. The page advises excluding purchases from utilization totals to avoid double counting. The feature level is Conditional.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Metric · Decimal

items.t: CommitmentDiscountQuantity MUST adhere to the following requirements:
CommitmentDiscountQuantity MUST be of type Decimal.
CommitmentDiscountQuantity MUST conform to NumericFormat requirements.
CommitmentDiscountQuantity MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
CommitmentDiscountQuantity MUST be null when SkuPriceId is null.
When ChargeCategory is "Usage" or "Purchase" and CommitmentDiscountId is not null, CommitmentDiscountQuantity MUST adhere to the following requirements:
CommitmentDiscountQuantity MUST NOT be null when ChargeClass is not "Correction".
CommitmentDiscountQuantity MAY be null when ChargeClass is "Correction".
CommitmentDiscountQuantity MUST be null in all other cases.
When CommitmentDiscountQuantity is not null and ChargeCategory is "Purchase", CommitmentDiscountQuantity MUST adhere to the following requirements:

CommitmentDiscountQuantity MUST be the quantity of CommitmentDiscountUnit, paid fully or partially upfront, that is eligible for consumption over the commitment discount's term when ChargeFrequency is "One-Time".

CommitmentDiscountQuantity MUST be the quantity of CommitmentDiscountUnit that is eligible for consumption for each charge period that corresponds with the purchase when ChargeFrequency is "Recurring".
When CommitmentDiscountQuantity is not null and ChargeCategory is "Usage", CommitmentDiscountQuantity MUST adhere to the following requirements:
CommitmentDiscountQuantity MUST be the metered quantity of CommitmentDiscountUnit that is consumed in a given charge period when CommitmentDiscountStatus is "Used".
CommitmentDiscountQuantity MUST be the remaining, unused quantity of CommitmentDiscountUnit in a given charge period when CommitmentDiscountStatus is "Unused".

items.b: Indicates whether the charge corresponds with the consumption of a commitment discount or the unused portion of the committed amount. Whether a charge consumes part of the commitment discount identified in CommitmentDiscountId or represents the unused portion of the committed amount; it does not apply to negotiated discounts. This Conditional string, tied to operating models that include commitment discounts, must be one of two allowed values: Used, when the charge utilizes a specific amount of the commitment discount, or Unused, when the charge represents its unused portion. It must be null when CommitmentDiscountId is null, and it must not be null when CommitmentDiscountId is not null and ChargeCategory is "Usage".
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Dimension · String
items.x: Includes Commitment Discounts Value Description Used Charges that utilized a specific amount of a commitment discount. Unused Charges that represent the unused portion of the commitment discount.

items.t: CommitmentDiscountStatus MUST adhere to the following requirements:
CommitmentDiscountStatus MUST be of type String.
CommitmentDiscountStatus MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
CommitmentDiscountStatus MUST be null when CommitmentDiscountId is null.
CommitmentDiscountStatus MUST NOT be null when CommitmentDiscountId is not null and ChargeCategory is "Usage".
CommitmentDiscountStatus MUST be one of the allowed values.
CommitmentDiscountStatus MUST be "Used" when the charge utilizes a specific amount of a given CommitmentDiscountId.
CommitmentDiscountStatus MUST be "Unused" when the charge represents the unused portion of the given CommitmentDiscountId.

items.b: A service-provider-assigned identifier for the type of commitment discount applied to the row. A service-provider-assigned name for the type of commitment discount applied to a row, relevant only to commitment discounts and not to negotiated discounts. It is a Conditional String dimension under the Includes Commitment Discounts operating model condition and must follow string handling requirements. Its nullability mirrors CommitmentDiscountId: it must be null when CommitmentDiscountId is null and must not be null when CommitmentDiscountId is not null. The specification defines no allowed values or value format, so the provider supplies the names.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Dimension · String

items.t: CommitmentDiscountType MUST adhere to the following requirements:
CommitmentDiscountType MUST be of type String.
CommitmentDiscountType MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
CommitmentDiscountType MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
CommitmentDiscountType MUST be null when CommitmentDiscountId is null.
CommitmentDiscountType MUST NOT be null when CommitmentDiscountId is not null.

items.b: The service-provider-specified measurement unit indicating how a service provider measures the Commitment Discount Quantity of a commitment discount. The service-provider-specified unit in which a service provider measures the CommitmentDiscountQuantity of a commitment discount; it applies only to commitment discounts, not negotiated discounts. A Conditional String dimension, applying when the operating model includes commitment discounts, it must conform to the String Handling requirements and should conform to the Unit Format requirements. It must be null when CommitmentDiscountQuantity is null and must not be null otherwise. When present it must stay consistent over time for a given CommitmentDiscountId and must represent the unit used to measure the commitment discount, and should reflect commitment discount flexibility when that is accounted for.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Dimension · String

items.t: CommitmentDiscountUnit MUST adhere to the following requirements:
CommitmentDiscountUnit MUST be of type String.
CommitmentDiscountUnit MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
CommitmentDiscountUnit SHOULD conform to UnitFormat requirements.
CommitmentDiscountUnit MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
CommitmentDiscountUnit MUST be null when CommitmentDiscountQuantity is null.
CommitmentDiscountUnit MUST NOT be null when CommitmentDiscountQuantity is not null.
When CommitmentDiscountUnit is not null, CommitmentDiscountUnit MUST adhere to the following requirements:
CommitmentDiscountUnit MUST remain consistent over time for a given CommitmentDiscountId.
CommitmentDiscountUnit MUST represent the unit used to measure the commitment discount.
When accounting for commitment discount flexibility, the CommitmentDiscountUnit value SHOULD reflect this consideration.
See Examples: Commitment Discount Flexibility for more details around commitment discount flexibility.

items.b: The types of commitment programs available for a specific usage row. The commitment programs that could cover a charge, including commitment discounts and capacity reservations a service provider treats as commitments; it supplies the denominator for commitment coverage metrics. A Conditional JSON object under the Includes Commitment Programs condition, it must not be null for eligible charges, even if no commitment was applied. It must list every eligible public program, may add eligible negotiated programs not broadly applicable across the catalog, and must not reflect temporary restrictions such as quotas or include commitment periods or payment options. Its CommitmentPrograms array of ProgramType entries must include one matching any non-null CommitmentDiscountType.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Dimension · JSON

items.t: CommitmentProgramEligibilityDetails MUST adhere to the following requirements:
CommitmentProgramEligibilityDetails MUST be of type JSON Object (serialized as a String where necessary).
CommitmentProgramEligibilityDetails MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
CommitmentProgramEligibilityDetails MUST conform to JsonObjectFormat requirements.
CommitmentProgramEligibilityDetails MUST NOT be null when a charge is eligible for a commitment program, regardless of whether a commitment was actually applied to the charge.
CommitmentProgramEligibilityDetails MUST NOT reflect restrictions (e.g., transient account configurations, quotas) that might temporarily prevent purchase or participation in a commitment program.
CommitmentProgramEligibilityDetails MUST include all publicly available commitment programs for which the usage is eligible.
CommitmentProgramEligibilityDetails MAY include negotiated commitment programs when the usage is eligible and the program is not broadly applicable across the service provider's service catalog.
CommitmentProgramEligibilityDetails MUST NOT include data related to commitment periods or payment options.
CommitmentProgramEligibilityDetails MUST conform to CommitmentProgramEligibilityDetailsObject requirements when CommitmentProgramEligibilityDetails is not null.

items.b: The volume of a metered SKU associated with a resource or service used, based on the Consumed Unit. The volume of a metered SKU used by a resource or service, measured in the Consumed Unit; it focuses on consumption, not pricing, and is often finer-grained than Pricing Quantity. It is a Decimal. It must be null when SkuPriceId is null, when ChargeCategory is not "Usage", or when CommitmentDiscountStatus is "Unused"; on other usage rows it must not be null unless ChargeClass is "Correction", when it may be null. A row whose SkuPriceDetails lacks TokenCacheAction "Read" or "Write" must not include tokens counted on a row that has one. The feature level is Conditional.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Metric · Decimal

items.t: ConsumedQuantity MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ConsumedQuantity MUST be of type Decimal.
ConsumedQuantity MUST conform to NumericFormat requirements.
ConsumedQuantity MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
ConsumedQuantity MUST be null when SkuPriceId is null.
ConsumedQuantity MUST be null when ChargeCategory is not "Usage", or when ChargeCategory is "Usage" and CommitmentDiscountStatus is "Unused".
When ChargeCategory is "Usage" and CommitmentDiscountStatus is not "Unused", ConsumedQuantity MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ConsumedQuantity MUST NOT be null when ChargeClass is not "Correction".
ConsumedQuantity MAY be null when ChargeClass is "Correction".

ConsumedQuantity MUST NOT include tokens counted on a different row with TokenCacheAction "Read" or "Write" in SkuPriceDetails when SkuPriceDetails on the same row includes neither value (e.g., a cached token that a usage report also counts inside a prompt token total is counted on the "Read" row only).

items.b: Service-provider-specified measurement unit indicating how a service provider measures usage of a metered SKU associated with a resource or service. The service-provider-specified unit in which a service provider measures usage of a metered stock keeping unit (SKU) associated with a resource or service, complementing ConsumedQuantity. It focuses on consumption rather than pricing and cost, and is often at a finer granularity or over a different time interval than PricingUnit. It is a Conditional String dimension, applying when the operating model includes usage measurement, that must conform to the String Handling requirements and should conform to the Unit Format requirements. It must be null when ConsumedQuantity is null and must not be null when ConsumedQuantity is not null.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Dimension · String

items.t: ConsumedUnit MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ConsumedUnit MUST be of type String.
ConsumedUnit MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
ConsumedUnit SHOULD conform to UnitFormat requirements.
ConsumedUnit MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
ConsumedUnit MUST be null when ConsumedQuantity is null.
ConsumedUnit MUST NOT be null when ConsumedQuantity is not null.

items.b: A set of properties that associate a charge with one or more contract commitments. A JSON object, serialized as a string where necessary, that links a charge to one or more contract commitments to track progress against agreed commitments. This Conditional column, tied to operating models that include contract commitments, must not be null when one or more contract commitments are applied to the charge. Its required Elements array holds objects with ContractId, ContractCommitmentId and at least one of ContractCommitmentAppliedCost, denominated in BillingCurrency, or ContractCommitmentAppliedQuantity, which then needs ContractCommitmentAppliedUnit. ContractCommitmentId must match ResourceId for a purchase of that commitment or its unused portion. Custom keys must start with "x_".
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Dimension / Metric · JSON

items.t: ContractApplied MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ContractApplied MUST be of type JSON Object (serialized as a String where necessary).
ContractApplied MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
ContractApplied MUST conform to JsonObjectFormat requirements.
ContractApplied MUST NOT be null when one or more contract commitments are applied to the charge.
ContractApplied MUST conform to ContractAppliedObject requirements when ContractApplied is not null.

items.b: Cost of a charge based on negotiated pricing terms before any discount-bearing commitment programs (e.g., commitment discounts) are applied to the charge. Cost of a charge under negotiated pricing terms, before any discount-bearing commitment programs apply. This Mandatory Decimal must not be null and must be denominated in the BillingCurrency. It must equal ContractedUnitPrice multiplied by PricingQuantity when both are not null, and for usage and purchase charges that are not corrections it must equal ListCost when no negotiated pricing terms apply. It must equal BilledCost when ChargeCategory is "Credit" and be calculated from the related charges' ContractedCost when ChargeCategory is "Tax". For savings aggregation, exclude covered charges on a billed basis or covering charges on an accrual basis.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Mandatory · Metric · Decimal

items.t: ContractedCost MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ContractedCost MUST be of type Decimal.
ContractedCost MUST conform to NumericFormat requirements.
ContractedCost MUST NOT be null.
ContractedCost MUST be denominated in the BillingCurrency.
When ChargeCategory is "Usage" or "Purchase" and ChargeClass is not "Correction", ContractedCost MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ContractedCost MUST reflect negotiated pricing terms that are independent of any discount-bearing commitment programs being applied to the charge.
ContractedCost MUST NOT reflect any cost impact dependent on a discount-bearing commitment program being applied to the charge.
ContractedCost MUST equal ListCost when no negotiated pricing terms apply to the charge.
ContractedCost MUST equal BilledCost when ChargeCategory is "Credit".
ContractedCost MUST be calculated based on the ContractedCost of the related charges when ChargeCategory is "Tax".
ContractedCost MUST equal the product of ContractedUnitPrice and PricingQuantity when ContractedUnitPrice is not null and PricingQuantity is not null.

items.b: The negotiated unit price per Pricing Unit for the SKU Price identified by the given SKU Price ID. The negotiated unit price per PricingUnit for the SKU price that SkuPriceId identifies, before any discount-bearing commitment program applies, in BillingCurrency. A Conditional Decimal metric under the Includes Unit Pricing operating model condition, it must be non-negative and must equal ListUnitPrice when no negotiated pricing terms apply. It must be null when SkuPriceId is null or ChargeCategory is "Tax", must not be null when SkuPriceId is not null or for "Usage" and "Purchase" charges whose ChargeClass is not "Correction", and may be null otherwise. Negotiated discounts appear in it, commitment discounts only in EffectiveCost. Values should not be aggregated.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Metric · Decimal

items.t: ContractedUnitPrice MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ContractedUnitPrice MUST be of type Decimal.
ContractedUnitPrice MUST conform to NumericFormat requirements.
ContractedUnitPrice MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
ContractedUnitPrice MUST be null when SkuPriceId is null.
ContractedUnitPrice MUST be null when ChargeCategory is "Tax".
ContractedUnitPrice MUST NOT be null when SkuPriceId is not null.
ContractedUnitPrice MUST NOT be null when ChargeCategory is "Usage" or "Purchase" and ChargeClass is not "Correction".
ContractedUnitPrice MAY be null in all other cases.
When ContractedUnitPrice is not null, ContractedUnitPrice MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ContractedUnitPrice MUST be a non-negative decimal value.
ContractedUnitPrice MUST be denominated in the BillingCurrency.

ContractedUnitPrice MUST reflect negotiated pricing terms for the SKU Price identified by the given SkuPriceId that are independent of any discount-bearing commitment programs being applied to the charge.
ContractedUnitPrice MUST NOT reflect any unit price impact dependent on a discount-bearing commitment program being applied to the charge.
ContractedUnitPrice MUST equal ListUnitPrice when no negotiated pricing terms apply to the charge.

items.b: Identifier representing the credential presented on the request that produced a charge. An identifier for the credential presented on the request that produced a charge, used to tell apart charges that share a principal but were authenticated with different credentials; descriptive attributes belong in Requester Details. It is a String. It must be null when a charge has no associated credential or the credential has no published identifier, and must not be null when it has one. When present it must be unique within the service provider, and must not contain a credential value that authenticates a request, such as an access token or password. The feature level is Conditional.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Dimension · String

items.t: CredentialId MUST adhere to the following requirements:
CredentialId MUST be of type String.
CredentialId MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
CredentialId MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
CredentialId MUST be null when a charge is not associated with a credential.
CredentialId MUST be null when the credential associated with a charge has no published identifier.
CredentialId MUST NOT be null when the credential associated with a charge has a published identifier.
When CredentialId is not null, CredentialId MUST adhere to the following requirements:
CredentialId MUST be an identifier that references a credential.
CredentialId MUST be a unique identifier within the service provider.
CredentialId MUST NOT contain a credential value that authenticates a request (e.g., an API key string, an access token, a password).

items.b: Cost of a charge based on the resources used, services used, or contract commitments recognized in a given charge period. The cost of a charge based on the resources used, services used or contract commitments recognized in its charge period, reflecting all applicable pricing adjustments, including discounts. It is a Mandatory, non-null Decimal in BillingCurrency. It must equal BilledCost for uncovered usage, for purchases that neither cover nor are covered by other charges, and for taxes and credits; it may differ for adjustments. Covered charges must include their applied share of a covering purchase's BilledCost, and the purchase's own value must be 0. Charges from entities that do not originate the data must be 0, to avoid double counting.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Mandatory · Metric · Decimal

items.t: EffectiveCost MUST adhere to the following requirements:
EffectiveCost MUST be of type Decimal.
EffectiveCost MUST conform to NumericFormat requirements.
EffectiveCost MUST NOT be null.
EffectiveCost MUST be denominated in the BillingCurrency.
EffectiveCost MUST reflect all applicable pricing adjustments, including but not limited to negotiated discounts, commitment discounts, and other applicable discount programs.
EffectiveCost MUST equal BilledCost when ChargeCategory is "Usage" and the charge is not covered by other eligible charges.
EffectiveCost MUST equal BilledCost when ChargeCategory is "Purchase" and the charge is neither intended to cover other eligible charges nor covered by other eligible charges.
EffectiveCost MUST equal BilledCost when ChargeCategory is "Tax" or "Credit".
EffectiveCost MAY differ from BilledCost when ChargeCategory is "Adjustment".
EffectiveCost MUST include any portion of the BilledCost of covering purchase charges (i.e., ChargeCategory is "Purchase") that is applied to this charge.

EffectiveCost MUST be 0 when ChargeCategory is "Purchase" and the purchase is intended to cover related eligible charges. This requirement applies even when the covered charges originate from different CostAndUsage dataset instances, possibly from a different ServiceProviderName.
EffectiveCost MUST be 0 for charges generated by entities that do not originate the cost and usage data, to avoid double-counting when merging multiple dataset instances.

The sum of EffectiveCost across all related covering and covered charges MUST equal the sum of BilledCost across the same set of charges, within the charge period of the covering charges, when both the covering and covered charges are present in the dataset instance.

The sum of EffectiveCost for a given billing period MAY differ from the sum of BilledCost when covered and covering charges span multiple billing periods or billing accounts, or when only one side of a covering relationship is present in the dataset instance.

items.b: The name of the entity whose resources are used by the Service Provider to make their resources or services available. The name of the entity providing the underlying infrastructure on which the service provider's resources or services are deployed, sometimes the service provider itself. A Mandatory String dimension, it must conform to the String Handling requirements. It may be null when the ServiceName involves no underlying infrastructure, such as professional services or software licenses, or when the host cannot be uniquely determined, as for "Tax" or "Adjustment" charges; otherwise it must not be null. It must name the host provider when the customer explicitly selects it or the service provider exposes it, and must match ServiceProviderName in all other cases.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Mandatory · Dimension · String

items.t: HostProviderName MUST adhere to the following requirements:
HostProviderName MUST be of type String.
HostProviderName MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
HostProviderName MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
HostProviderName MAY be NULL when the associated ServiceName does not involve deployment on any underlying infrastructure (e.g., professional services, software licenses).
HostProviderName MAY be NULL when the information about the entity providing the underlying infrastructure cannot be uniquely determined (e.g., when the ChargeCategory is "Tax" or "Adjustment").
HostProviderName MUST NOT be null in all other cases.
When HostProviderName is not null, HostProviderName values MUST adhere to the following requirements:
HostProviderName MUST reflect the name of the host provider when explicitly selected by the customer.
HostProviderName MUST reflect the name of the host provider when the service provider exposes the underlying hosting provider.
HostProviderName MUST match ServiceProviderName in all other cases.
See Appendix: Participating Entity Identification Examples section for examples of Host Provider values across various use case scenarios.

items.b: The invoice-issuer-assigned identifier for an Invoice Detail record encapsulating charges in the corresponding billing period for a given billing account. The invoice-issuer-assigned identifier of the Invoice Detail record that encapsulates charges in a billing period for a billing account, letting practitioners map invoice line items to granular charge data for reconciliation and audit. This Conditional string, tied to operating models that include payable invoices, must be null when a charge is associated with neither an invoice nor a pre-generated provisional invoice, and must not be null when it is associated with an issued invoice or a pre-generated provisional invoice. It may be generated before an invoice is issued, and it must uniquely identify a record within a given InvoiceId.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Dimension · String

items.t: InvoiceDetailId MUST adhere to the following requirements:
InvoiceDetailId MUST be of type String.
InvoiceDetailId MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
InvoiceDetailId MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
InvoiceDetailId MUST be null when the charge is not associated either with an invoice or with a pre-generated provisional invoice.
InvoiceDetailId MUST NOT be null when the charge is associated with either an issued invoice or a pre-generated provisional invoice.
InvoiceDetailId MAY be generated prior to an invoice being issued.
InvoiceDetailId MUST uniquely identify a specific record within a given InvoiceId.

items.b: The invoice-issuer-assigned identifier for an invoice encapsulating charges in the corresponding billing period for a given billing account. The invoice issuer's identifier for the invoice encapsulating charges in a billing period for a given billing account, used for tracking billing transactions and invoice reconciliation. A Conditional String dimension, applying when the operating model includes payable invoices, it must conform to the String Handling requirements. It must be null when the charge is associated with neither an invoice nor a pre-generated provisional invoice, and must not be null otherwise. It may be generated before the invoice is issued, and must be associated with the related charge and BillingAccountId when a pre-generated or provisional invoice exists.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Dimension · String

items.t: InvoiceId MUST adhere to the following requirements:
InvoiceId MUST be of type String.
InvoiceId MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
InvoiceId MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
InvoiceId MUST be null when the charge is not associated either with an invoice or with a pre-generated provisional invoice.
InvoiceId MUST NOT be null when the charge is associated with either an issued invoice or a pre-generated provisional invoice.
InvoiceId MAY be generated prior to an invoice being issued.
InvoiceId MUST be associated with the related charge and BillingAccountId when a pre-generated invoice or provisional invoice exists.
See Appendix: Grouping constructs for resources or services for details and examples of the different grouping constructs supported by FOCUS.

items.b: The name of the entity responsible for invoicing for the resources or services consumed. Name of the entity responsible for issuing payable invoices for the resources or services consumed, commonly used in cost analysis and reporting. In the CostAndUsage dataset it is a mandatory String dimension that must not be null, must follow string handling requirements and must represent the entity that issues invoices. No specific value format is defined; the specification's appendix on participating entity identification gives example values across different use case scenarios.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Mandatory · Dimension · String

items.t: InvoiceIssuerName MUST adhere to the following requirements:
InvoiceIssuerName MUST be of type String.
InvoiceIssuerName MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
InvoiceIssuerName MUST NOT be null.
InvoiceIssuerName MUST represent the entity that issues invoices.
See Appendix: Participating Entity Identification Examples section for examples of Invoice Issuer Name values across various use case scenarios.

items.b: Cost of a charge based on the service-provider-suggested pricing. Cost of a charge at the service-provider-suggested pricing, before any negotiated pricing terms or discount-bearing commitment programs apply. This Mandatory Decimal must not be null and must be denominated in the BillingCurrency. For non-correction usage and purchase charges, it must reflect neither negotiated pricing terms nor commitment program effects. It must equal ListUnitPrice multiplied by PricingQuantity when both are not null, must equal BilledCost when ChargeCategory is "Credit", and must be calculated from the related charges' ListCost when ChargeCategory is "Tax". For savings aggregation, exclude covered charges on a billed basis or covering charges on an accrual basis.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Mandatory · Metric · Decimal

items.t: ListCost MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ListCost MUST be of type Decimal.
ListCost MUST conform to NumericFormat requirements.
ListCost MUST NOT be null.
ListCost MUST be denominated in the BillingCurrency.
When ChargeCategory is "Usage" or "Purchase" and ChargeClass is not "Correction", ListCost MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ListCost MUST represent the cost of the charge based on the service-provider-suggested pricing.
ListCost MUST NOT reflect negotiated pricing terms.
ListCost MUST NOT reflect any cost impact dependent on a discount-bearing commitment program being applied to the charge.
ListCost MUST equal BilledCost when ChargeCategory is "Credit".
ListCost MUST be calculated based on the ListCost of the related charges when ChargeCategory is "Tax".
ListCost MUST equal the product of ListUnitPrice and PricingQuantity when ListUnitPrice is not null and PricingQuantity is not null.

items.b: The service-provider-suggested unit price per Pricing Unit for the SKU Price identified by the given SKU Price ID. The service-provider-suggested unit price per PricingUnit for the price identified by SkuPriceId, before negotiated pricing terms or discount-bearing commitment programs, and commonly the starting point for negotiation. A Conditional Decimal metric, applying when the operating model includes unit pricing, it must be non-negative and denominated in BillingCurrency. It must be null when SkuPriceId is null or ChargeCategory is "Tax", and must not be null when SkuPriceId is not null or when a "Usage" or "Purchase" charge has a ChargeClass other than "Correction". It does not reflect negotiated tiers or negotiated exchange rates, and should be read per row, not summed.
items.s: Column in Cost and Usage · Conditional · Metric · Decimal

items.t: ListUnitPrice MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ListUnitPrice MUST be of type Decimal.
ListUnitPrice MUST conform to NumericFormat requirements.
ListUnitPrice MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
ListUnitPrice MUST be null when SkuPriceId is null.
ListUnitPrice MUST be null when ChargeCategory is "Tax".
ListUnitPrice MUST NOT be null when SkuPriceId is not null.
ListUnitPrice MUST NOT be null when ChargeCategory is "Usage" or "Purchase" and ChargeClass is not "Correction".
ListUnitPrice MAY be null in all other cases.
When ListUnitPrice is not null, ListUnitPrice MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ListUnitPrice MUST be a non-negative decimal value.
ListUnitPrice MUST be denominated in the BillingCurrency.
ListUnitPrice MUST represent the service-provider-suggested unit price per PricingUnit for the SKU Price identified by the given SkuPriceId.
ListUnitPrice MUST NOT reflect negotiated pricing terms for the associated SKU Price.
