BilledCost MUST reflect all applicable pricing adjustments, including but not limited to negotiated discounts, commitment discounts, and other applicable discount programs.
BilledCost MUST NOT include any portion of a covered charge that is offset by a covering charge.
BilledCost MUST be 0 for charges that are fully covered by one or more covering charges.

The sum of BilledCost for a given InvoiceDetailId, InvoiceId, and InvoiceIssuerName MUST be equal to the payable amount provided in the corresponding entries on the issued invoice when InvoiceIssueStatus is "Issued".

When comparing BilledCost aggregated by InvoiceId and InvoiceIssuerName with CostAndUsage.BilledCost aggregated by CostAndUsage.InvoiceId and CostAndUsage.InvoiceIssuerName, BilledCost MUST adhere to the following requirements:

When ChargeCategory is not "Tax" and InvoiceIssueStatus is not "Open", the sum of BilledCost MUST NOT differ from the sum of CostAndUsage.BilledCost by more than MAX(100 × Subunit, (SQRT(Rows) × 0.5) × Subunit) as defined in Rounding Variance Tolerance.
When ChargeCategory is "Tax" or InvoiceIssueStatus is "Open", the sum of BilledCost MAY differ from the sum of CostAndUsage.BilledCost.

When comparing BilledCost aggregated by InvoiceDetailId, InvoiceId, and InvoiceIssuerName with CostAndUsage.BilledCost aggregated by CostAndUsage.InvoiceDetailId, CostAndUsage.InvoiceId, and CostAndUsage.InvoiceIssuerName, BilledCost MUST adhere to the following requirements:

When InvoiceIssueStatus is not "Open", the sum of BilledCost MUST NOT differ from the sum of CostAndUsage.BilledCost by more than MAX(100 × Subunit, (SQRT(Rows) × 0.5) × Subunit) as defined in Rounding Variance Tolerance.
When InvoiceIssueStatus is "Open", the sum of BilledCost MAY differ from the sum of CostAndUsage.BilledCost.

items.b: The identifier assigned to a billing account by the invoice issuer. An invoice-issuer-assigned identifier for a billing account; billing accounts are commonly used for grouping by organizational constructs, invoice reconciliation and cost allocation strategies. In the InvoiceDetail dataset it is a mandatory String dimension that must not be null, must follow string handling requirements and must be unique within an invoice issuer. It should be a fully qualified identifier. No specific value format is defined, and an appendix describes the grouping constructs FOCUS supports.
items.s: Column in Invoice Detail · Mandatory · Dimension · String

items.t: BillingAccountId MUST adhere to the following requirements:
BillingAccountId MUST be of type String.
BillingAccountId MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
BillingAccountId MUST NOT be null.
BillingAccountId MUST be a unique identifier within an invoice issuer.
BillingAccountId SHOULD be a fully-qualified identifier.
See Appendix: Grouping constructs for resources or services for details and examples of the different grouping constructs supported by FOCUS.

items.b: Represents the currency that a charge was billed in. The currency in which a charge was billed, commonly used when costs need to be grouped or aggregated. In the Invoice Detail dataset it is a Mandatory String dimension that must conform to the String Handling and Currency Format requirements and must not be null. It must match the currency used in the invoice generated by the invoice issuer and must be expressed in a national currency. It was introduced in version 1.4.
items.s: Column in Invoice Detail · Mandatory · Dimension · String

items.t: BillingCurrency MUST adhere to the following requirements:
BillingCurrency MUST be of type String.
BillingCurrency MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
BillingCurrency MUST conform to CurrencyFormat requirements.
BillingCurrency MUST NOT be null.
BillingCurrency MUST match the currency used in the invoice generated by the invoice issuer.
BillingCurrency MUST be expressed in national currency (e.g., USD, EUR).

items.b: Represents the highest-level classification of a charge based on the nature of how it is billed. The highest-level classification of a charge by how it is billed, used to distinguish charge types that may need different handling. In the InvoiceDetail dataset it is a mandatory String dimension that must not be null and must be one of five allowed values, each covering positive or negative charges: Usage, Purchase, Tax, Credit and Adjustment. A charge that does not aggregate several classifications must take the value matching its nature, such as "Tax" for taxes levied by authorities. Unlike the strict per-row categorization in CostAndUsage, an invoice line aggregating several allowed values other than "Tax" may be "Usage".
items.s: Column in Invoice Detail · Mandatory · Dimension · String
items.x: Not applicable Value Description Usage Positive or negative charges based on the quantity of a service or resource that was consumed over a given period of time including refunds. Purchase Positive or negative charges for the acquisition of a service or resource bought upfront or on a recurring basis including refunds. Tax Positive or negative applicable taxes that are levied by the relevant authorities including refunds. Tax charges may vary depending on factors such as the location, jurisdiction, and local or federal regulations. Credit Positive or negative charges granted by the service provider for various scenarios (e.g., promotional credits, corrections to promotional credits). Adjustment Positive or negative charges the service provider applies that do not fall into other category values.

items.t: ChargeCategory MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ChargeCategory MUST be of type String.
ChargeCategory MUST NOT be null.
ChargeCategory MUST be one of the allowed values.
When the charge does not aggregate multiple classifications, ChargeCategory MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ChargeCategory MUST be "Usage" when the charge represents consumption of a service or resource.
ChargeCategory MUST be "Purchase" when the charge represents acquisition of a service, resource, or commitment.
ChargeCategory MUST be "Tax" when the charge represents taxes levied by the relevant authorities.
ChargeCategory MUST be "Credit" when the charge represents a financial incentive or allowance unrelated to other charges.
ChargeCategory MUST be "Adjustment" when the charge represents a billing modification that does not fall into other ChargeCategories.
When the charge aggregates multiple classifications, ChargeCategory MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ChargeCategory MAY be "Usage" when the record aggregates charges across multiple allowed values other than "Tax" (e.g., aggregation of "Usage" and "Credit" is allowed, but not "Usage" and "Tax").

items.b: The exclusive end bound of a billing period. Within the Invoice Detail dataset, the exclusive end bound of a billing period: a period from 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z to 2024-02-01T00:00:00Z includes January's charges but not February's, because BillingPeriodStart is the inclusive start bound. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements and must not be null. For a given InvoiceId and InvoiceIssuerName, it must match CostAndUsage.BillingPeriodEnd for the same CostAndUsage.InvoiceId and CostAndUsage.InvoiceIssuerName.
items.s: Column in Invoice Detail · Mandatory · Dimension · Date/Time

items.t: BillingPeriodEnd MUST adhere to the following requirements:
BillingPeriodEnd MUST be of type Date/Time.
BillingPeriodEnd MUST conform to DateTimeFormat requirements.
BillingPeriodEnd MUST NOT be null.
BillingPeriodEnd MUST be the exclusive end bound of the billing period.
BillingPeriodEnd for a given InvoiceId and InvoiceIssuerName MUST match CostAndUsage.BillingPeriodEnd for the same CostAndUsage.InvoiceId and CostAndUsage.InvoiceIssuerName.

items.b: The inclusive start bound of a billing period. Start of the billing period in the Invoice Detail dataset, given as an inclusive start bound. With BillingPeriodEnd as the exclusive end bound, a start of 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z and an end of 2024-02-01T00:00:00Z includes charges for January but not February. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements and must not be null. For a given InvoiceId and InvoiceIssuerName it must match CostAndUsage.BillingPeriodStart for the same CostAndUsage.InvoiceId and CostAndUsage.InvoiceIssuerName.
items.s: Column in Invoice Detail · Mandatory · Dimension · Date/Time

items.t: BillingPeriodStart MUST adhere to the following requirements:
BillingPeriodStart MUST be of type Date/Time.
BillingPeriodStart MUST conform to DateTimeFormat requirements.
BillingPeriodStart MUST NOT be null.
BillingPeriodStart MUST be the inclusive start bound of the billing period.
BillingPeriodStart for a given InvoiceId and InvoiceIssuerName MUST match CostAndUsage.BillingPeriodStart for the same CostAndUsage.InvoiceId and CostAndUsage.InvoiceIssuerName.

items.b: The timestamp when the Invoice Detail record was first created. The moment an InvoiceDetail record was first instantiated, which supports auditing of the charge and invoice lifecycle by separating when a service was consumed from when its financial record was generated. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements and must not be null. When the matching BillingPeriod record's BillingPeriodStatus is "Closed", InvoiceDetailCreated for a given BillingPeriodStart and InvoiceIssuerName must be earlier than or equal to that record's BillingPeriodLastUpdated.
items.s: Column in Invoice Detail · Mandatory · Dimension · Date/Time

items.t: InvoiceDetailCreated MUST adhere to the following requirements:
InvoiceDetailCreated MUST be of type Date/Time.
InvoiceDetailCreated MUST conform to DateTimeFormat requirements.
InvoiceDetailCreated MUST NOT be null.
InvoiceDetailCreated MUST represent the moment in time the InvoiceDetail record was instantiated.

InvoiceDetailCreated for a given BillingPeriodStart and InvoiceIssuerName MUST be earlier than or equal to BillingPeriod.BillingPeriodLastUpdated for the same BillingPeriod.BillingPeriodStart and BillingPeriod.InvoiceIssuerName when BillingPeriod.BillingPeriodStatus is "Closed".

items.b: The invoice-issuer-provided description of an invoice line item. The invoice issuer's description of an invoice line item, giving context for the charge as it appears on the invoice and often summarizing the service, resource or period the line covers, to help with human-readable reconciliation. It is a String that must describe the charges represented by the InvoiceDetailId. The feature level is Mandatory; the column allows nulls, but the value should not be null. Its maximum length should be provided in the corresponding FOCUS Metadata Schema. It is a dimension in the Invoice Detail dataset, introduced in version 1.4.
items.s: Column in Invoice Detail · Mandatory · Dimension · String

items.t: InvoiceDetailDescription MUST adhere to the following requirements:
InvoiceDetailDescription MUST be of type String.
InvoiceDetailDescription MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
InvoiceDetailDescription SHOULD NOT be null.
InvoiceDetailDescription maximum length SHOULD be provided in the corresponding FOCUS Metadata Schema.
InvoiceDetailDescription MUST describe the charges represented by the InvoiceDetailId.

items.b: The set of key-value pairs that defines the granularity of the invoice line item. Key-value pairs defining the granularity of an invoice line item, used instead of separate columns because the grain varies within one invoice and across invoice issuers, and supporting reconciliation and cost allocation. It is a JSON object, serialized as a String where necessary. It must not be null when one or more properties uniquely define the line's granularity, and must contain all such properties. It should use FOCUS-defined properties where applicable, such as Service Name, Resource ID and SKU ID, whose keys must match the specified spelling and casing; other keys must begin with "x_". The feature level is Mandatory.
items.s: Column in Invoice Detail · Mandatory · Dimension · JSON

items.t: InvoiceDetailGrain MUST adhere to the following requirements:
InvoiceDetailGrain MUST be of type JSON Object (serialized as a String where necessary).
InvoiceDetailGrain MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
InvoiceDetailGrain MUST conform to KeyValueFormat requirements.
InvoiceDetailGrain MUST NOT be null when one or more properties uniquely define the granularity of the invoice line item.
InvoiceDetailGrain MUST contain the set of all properties that uniquely define the granularity of the invoice line item.
InvoiceDetailGrain SHOULD use the applicable FOCUS-defined InvoiceDetailGrain properties listed below to represent the granularity of the invoice line item.
InvoiceDetailGrain MUST include all custom InvoiceDetailGrain properties that are applicable to the granularity of the invoice line item when there is no equivalent FOCUS-defined property.
InvoiceDetailGrain property keys SHOULD conform to PascalCase format.
InvoiceDetailGrain property keys MUST begin with the string "x_" unless it is a FOCUS-defined property.
FOCUS-defined InvoiceDetailGrain properties MUST adhere to the following requirements:
Property key MUST match the spelling and casing specified for the FOCUS-defined property.
Property value MUST be of the type specified for that property.

items.b: The invoice-issuer-assigned identifier for an Invoice Detail record encapsulating charges in the corresponding billing period for a given billing account. The invoice-issuer-assigned identifier for an InvoiceDetail record, which encapsulates charges in the corresponding billing period for a given billing account. It lets FinOps practitioners map specific invoice line items to granular charge data, supporting detailed reconciliation and auditability. It is a mandatory String dimension that must not be null and must follow string handling requirements. It must uniquely identify a record within a given InvoiceId.
items.s: Column in Invoice Detail · Mandatory · Dimension · String

items.t: InvoiceDetailId MUST adhere to the following requirements:
InvoiceDetailId MUST be of type String.
InvoiceDetailId MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
InvoiceDetailId MUST NOT be null.
InvoiceDetailId MUST uniquely identify a record within a given InvoiceId.

items.b: The timestamp when the Invoice Detail record was last updated. The timestamp when an Invoice Detail record was last updated: the most recent moment when any column value of the record identified by InvoiceDetailId was created or modified. It helps practitioners confirm they are working with the current version after corrections or status changes. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements and must not be null, and it must be greater than or equal to InvoiceDetailCreated.
items.s: Column in Invoice Detail · Mandatory · Dimension · Date/Time

items.t: InvoiceDetailLastUpdated MUST adhere to the following requirements:
InvoiceDetailLastUpdated MUST be of type Date/Time.
InvoiceDetailLastUpdated MUST conform to DateTimeFormat requirements.
InvoiceDetailLastUpdated MUST NOT be null.
InvoiceDetailLastUpdated MUST represent the most recent moment in time when any column value of the record identified by InvoiceDetailId was created or modified.
InvoiceDetailLastUpdated MUST be greater than or equal to InvoiceDetailCreated.

items.b: The invoice-issuer-assigned identifier for an invoice encapsulating charges in the corresponding billing period for a given billing account. The identifier an invoice issuer assigns to an invoice that gathers the charges in a billing period for a given billing account. Invoices are commonly used to track billing transactions, support payment processes and reconcile charges against billing periods. In the InvoiceDetail dataset it is a Mandatory String dimension that must conform to the String Handling requirements and must not be null. It must uniquely identify the invoice as provided by the invoice issuer, and it may be generated before the invoice is issued.
items.s: Column in Invoice Detail · Mandatory · Dimension · String

items.t: InvoiceId MUST adhere to the following requirements:
InvoiceId MUST be of type String.
InvoiceId MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
InvoiceId MUST NOT be null.
InvoiceId MAY be generated prior to an invoice being issued.
InvoiceId MUST uniquely identify the invoice as provided by the invoice issuer.

items.b: The date the invoice was issued by the invoice issuer. The date the invoice issuer issued an invoice, serving as the official point of record for the billing document, the start of payment terms, and a reference point for financial audits and period closing. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension in the InvoiceDetail dataset that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements. The column may be null, and it must represent the official date of issuance for the corresponding InvoiceId.
items.s: Column in Invoice Detail · Mandatory · Dimension · Date/Time

items.t: InvoiceIssueDate MUST adhere to the following requirements:
InvoiceIssueDate MUST be of type Date/Time.
InvoiceIssueDate MUST conform to DateTimeFormat requirements.
InvoiceIssueDate MAY be null.
InvoiceIssueDate MUST represent the official date of issuance for the corresponding InvoiceId.

items.b: The publication state of the invoice and the reliability of its associated delivered data, indicating if it is provisional ("Open"), issued ("Issued"), or voided ("Voided"). The publication state of an invoice, which also signals how reliable its delivered CostAndUsage and InvoiceDetail data is. It is a mandatory String dimension that must not be null, must reflect the invoice's current state and must be one of three allowed values: "Open", provisional and subject to change; "Issued", formally issued as a valid financial obligation with finalized data; or "Voided", previously issued but retracted, and not a valid obligation. The status must not return to "Open" after "Issued" unless the customer explicitly requests or approves it, for example to reopen an invoice for corrections.
items.s: Column in Invoice Detail · Mandatory · Dimension · String
items.x: Not applicable Value Description Open The invoice is provisional and subject to change. It is not a valid financial obligation and the associated delivered data is preliminary. Issued The invoice has been formally issued by the provider. It represents a valid financial obligation with finalized associated data. Voided The invoice was previously issued but has been retracted or nullified. It is not a valid financial obligation.

items.t: InvoiceIssueStatus MUST adhere to the following requirements:
InvoiceIssueStatus MUST be of type String.
InvoiceIssueStatus MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
InvoiceIssueStatus MUST NOT be null.
InvoiceIssueStatus MUST be one of the allowed values.
InvoiceIssueStatus MUST represent the current publication state of the invoice.
InvoiceIssueStatus MUST NOT be "Open" following a previous status of "Issued", except when explicitly requested or approved by the customer.

items.b: The name of the entity responsible for invoicing for the resources or services consumed. The name of the entity responsible for issuing payable invoices for the resources or services consumed, commonly used in cost analysis and reporting. It is a String that must conform to string handling requirements, must not be null, and must represent the entity that issues invoices. The feature level is Mandatory. It is a dimension in the Invoice Detail dataset, introduced in version 1.4, and the specification's appendix gives example values across different use case scenarios.
items.s: Column in Invoice Detail · Mandatory · Dimension · String

items.t: InvoiceIssuerName MUST adhere to the following requirements:
InvoiceIssuerName MUST be of type String.
InvoiceIssuerName MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
InvoiceIssuerName MUST NOT be null.
InvoiceIssuerName MUST represent the entity that issues invoices.
See Appendix: Participating Entity Identification Examples section for examples of Invoice Issuer Name values across various use case scenarios.

items.b: The currency in which the invoice is paid. The currency in which the invoice issuer requires settlement, which is the currency of the financial obligation the invoice creates. It may differ from the Billing Currency and from the currency of the payer's funds or bank account, and it lets practitioners track settlement obligations and foreign exchange impacts. This Conditional string, tied to operating models that include billing and payment currency differences, must not be null, must represent the currency in which the invoice payment was made or is expected to be made, and must be a national currency such as US dollars (USD) or euros (EUR).
items.s: Column in Invoice Detail · Conditional · Dimension · String
items.x: Includes Billing and Payment Currency Differences

items.t: PaymentCurrency MUST adhere to the following requirements:
PaymentCurrency MUST be of type String.
PaymentCurrency MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
PaymentCurrency MUST NOT be null.
PaymentCurrency MUST represent the currency in which the invoice payment was made or expected to be made.
PaymentCurrency MUST be expressed in national currency (e.g., USD, EUR).

items.b: The Billed Cost as expressed in Payment Currency. BilledCost expressed in the PaymentCurrency, used to reconcile financial records in the currency of actual settlement when it differs from the billing currency. This Conditional Decimal, tied to operating models that include billing and payment currency differences, must not be null and must be denominated in the PaymentCurrency. Its grain may differ from BilledCost: it may be non-zero while BilledCost is 0 when it aggregates amounts stated in other records, and it may be 0 while BilledCost is non-zero when that amount is represented in a separate aggregate record. The page's examples link such records through PaymentCurrencyInvoiceDetailId.
items.s: Column in Invoice Detail · Conditional · Metric · Decimal
items.x: Includes Billing and Payment Currency Differences

items.t: PaymentCurrencyBilledCost MUST adhere to the following requirements:
PaymentCurrencyBilledCost MUST be of type Decimal.
PaymentCurrencyBilledCost MUST conform to NumericFormat requirements.
PaymentCurrencyBilledCost MUST NOT be null.
PaymentCurrencyBilledCost MUST be denominated in the PaymentCurrency.
PaymentCurrencyBilledCost MUST be the PaymentCurrency-denominated equivalent of BilledCost.

PaymentCurrencyBilledCost MAY be non-zero while BilledCost is 0 when PaymentCurrencyBilledCost represents the aggregation of BilledCost amounts (denominated in PaymentCurrency) stated in other records.
PaymentCurrencyBilledCost MAY be 0 while BilledCost is non-zero when BilledCost (denominated in PaymentCurrency) is represented in a separate aggregate record.

items.b: The identifier linking a granular record to the specific Invoice Detail record where its Payment Currency Billed Cost is represented or aggregated. A reference to the InvoiceDetailId of the record where the current row's PaymentCurrencyBilledCost is aggregated, linking granular records to aggregate records stated in the currency chosen for settlement so that reconciliation works across different grains. It is a Conditional String dimension under the Includes Aggregation Level Currency Differences operating model condition; it must not be null and must follow string handling requirements. It must match the InvoiceDetailId of the record holding that aggregation, and when PaymentCurrencyBilledCost is non-zero it must match the current record's own InvoiceDetailId.
items.s: Column in Invoice Detail · Conditional · Dimension · String

items.t: PaymentCurrencyInvoiceDetailId MUST adhere to the following requirements:
PaymentCurrencyInvoiceDetailId MUST be of type String.
PaymentCurrencyInvoiceDetailId MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
PaymentCurrencyInvoiceDetailId MUST NOT be null.
PaymentCurrencyInvoiceDetailId MUST match the InvoiceDetailId of the record representing the PaymentCurrencyBilledCost aggregation for the current row.
PaymentCurrencyInvoiceDetailId MUST match InvoiceDetailId of the current record when PaymentCurrencyBilledCost is non-zero.

items.b: The date by which the payment for an invoice is expected to be received by the invoice issuer. The deadline by which the invoice issuer expects to receive payment for an invoice, used by FinOps practitioners and finance teams to manage cash flow, prioritize payments and avoid late fees or service interruptions. It is a Date/Time that must conform to date/time format requirements and must be the date the invoice issuer specifies as the payment deadline for the corresponding InvoiceId. It may be null. The feature level is Mandatory, and the column allows nulls. It is a dimension in the Invoice Detail dataset, introduced in version 1.4.
items.s: Column in Invoice Detail · Mandatory · Dimension · Date/Time

items.t: PaymentDueDate MUST adhere to the following requirements:
PaymentDueDate MUST be of type Date/Time.
PaymentDueDate MUST conform to DateTimeFormat requirements.
PaymentDueDate MAY be null.
PaymentDueDate MUST be the date specified by the invoice issuer as the deadline for payment for the corresponding InvoiceId.

items.b: The terms (typically focused on timeframe) by which the invoice issuer expects to receive payment for an invoice. The terms, typically focused on timeframe, under which the invoice issuer expects to receive payment for an invoice, such as "Net 30". They define the agreed period for settling the invoice, helping the provider and the customer manage financial expectations and payment schedules. It is a String that must conform to string handling requirements, must not be null, and must represent the payment terms as defined on the corresponding invoice. The feature level is Mandatory. It is a dimension in the Invoice Detail dataset, introduced in version 1.4.
items.s: Column in Invoice Detail · Mandatory · Dimension · String

items.t: PaymentTerms MUST adhere to the following requirements:
PaymentTerms MUST be of type String.
PaymentTerms MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
PaymentTerms MUST NOT be null.
PaymentTerms MUST represent the payment terms (e.g., "Net 30") as defined on the corresponding invoice.

items.b: The unique customer-issued identifier for tracking the lifecycle of a purchase. The unique customer-issued identifier for tracking the lifecycle of a purchase, typically given to the invoice issuer so that charges map to the customer's internal procurement records or purchase orders. This Conditional string, tied to operating models that include purchase order numbers, must conform to the String Handling requirements and may be null. It must represent the identifier the customer uses to uniquely identify the purchase order responsible for the charge.
items.s: Column in Invoice Detail · Conditional · Dimension · String

items.t: PurchaseOrderNumber MUST adhere to the following requirements:
PurchaseOrderNumber MUST be of type String.
PurchaseOrderNumber MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
PurchaseOrderNumber MAY be null.
PurchaseOrderNumber MUST represent the identifier used by the customer to uniquely identify the purchase order responsible for the charge.

items.b: The invoice-issuer-assigned identifier for an invoice that affects charges as stated on a previous invoice. An invoice-issuer-assigned identifier that links an invoice affecting charges stated on a previous invoice back to that original invoice, typically for credits, refunds or corrections, giving direct lineage between adjustments and the original billing records. It is a Mandatory String dimension in the Invoice Detail dataset that must conform to the String Handling requirements and must not be null. It must match the InvoiceId of the original invoice when the invoice adjusts another, and must match the current invoice's own InvoiceId when it does not, rather than being null.
items.s: Column in Invoice Detail · Mandatory · Dimension · String

items.t: ReferenceInvoiceId MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ReferenceInvoiceId MUST be of type String.
ReferenceInvoiceId MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
ReferenceInvoiceId MUST NOT be null.
ReferenceInvoiceId MUST match the InvoiceId of the original invoice when it adjusts another invoice.
ReferenceInvoiceId MUST match the InvoiceId of the current invoice when it does not adjust another invoice.

items.b: Represents the currency of a contract commitment. The currency of a contract commitment, recorded in the ContractCommitment dataset as a String identifier. It must conform to the String Handling and Currency Format requirements, must match the currency used on the invoice generated by the invoice issuer, and must be expressed in a national currency such as USD or EUR. Its feature level is Mandatory and the column allows nulls, but it must not be null when ContractCommitmentCategory is "Spend".
items.s: Column in Contract Commitment · Mandatory · Dimension · String

items.t: BillingCurrency MUST adhere to the following requirements:
BillingCurrency MUST be of type String.
BillingCurrency MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
BillingCurrency MUST conform to CurrencyFormat requirements.
BillingCurrency MUST NOT be null when ContractCommitmentCategory is "Spend".
BillingCurrency MUST match the currency used in the invoice generated by the invoice issuer.
BillingCurrency MUST be expressed in national currency (e.g., USD, EUR).

items.b: A structured definition of the specific entities to which a contract commitment applies, including inclusion/exclusion logic and applicability percentages. A JSON object defining which entities a contract commitment covers and what fraction, from 0.0 to 1.0, of an eligible charge's cost and usage applies. This Mandatory column must not be null and must conform to its JSON schema. IsGlobalScope must be true when the commitment applies to all entities, and IsComplexScope must be true when its logic exceeds the schema. Otherwise Inclusions are required. Inclusions and optional Exclusions hold rules comparing a Dimension, which should be a CostAndUsage column, with Values using operators such as In or StartsWith. A wildcard "*" must be the only value when present.
items.s: Column in Contract Commitment · Mandatory · Dimension / Metric · JSON

items.t: ContractCommitmentApplicability MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ContractCommitmentApplicability MUST be of type JSON Object (serialized as a String where necessary).
ContractCommitmentApplicability MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
ContractCommitmentApplicability MUST conform to JsonObjectFormat requirements.
ContractCommitmentApplicability MUST conform to ContractCommitmentApplicabilityObject requirements.
ContractCommitmentApplicability MUST NOT be null.

items.b: Defines the primary value or advantage received for a contract commitment. The primary value or advantage received for a contract commitment. This Mandatory string must not be null and must be one of four allowed values: Discount, a reduction in unit price or list rate; Entitlement, the right to use products, features or software tiers that would otherwise be unavailable; Availability, an assurance of resource access and capacity; and Other. The value reflects the benefit received, not the funding mechanism such as a prepaid pool. When a commitment brings several benefits, it should reflect the primary commercial driver. Availability must not be confused with technical fields such as CapacityReservationId.
items.s: Column in Contract Commitment · Mandatory · Dimension · String
items.x: Not applicable Value Sort Order Description Typical Use Case Discount 10 A financial reduction in the unit price or list rate, whether applied immediately or conditionally upon meeting usage or spend thresholds. Flat rate negotiated reductions, Savings Plans, growth rebates, or volume-tier discounts. Entitlement 20 The contractual right to access and consume specific products, features, or software tiers that would otherwise be unavailable. Marketplace SaaS purchases, Enterprise Agreements (e.g., Snowflake), or paid Proof of Concepts. Availability 30 A contractual assurance of resource access and physical capacity. Capacity reservations or dedicated host guarantees. Other 40 Benefits not captured by standard categories. Support access, training, or professional services.

items.t: ContractCommitmentBenefitCategory MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ContractCommitmentBenefitCategory MUST be of type String.
ContractCommitmentBenefitCategory MUST NOT be null.
ContractCommitmentBenefitCategory MUST be one of the allowed values.

items.b: Represents the highest-level classification of a contract commitment based on the nature of how it is applied to a charge. The highest-level classification of a contract commitment, based on how the commitment is applied to a charge, commonly used to tell apart categories of contract commitments that may need different handling. It is a mandatory String dimension in the ContractCommitment dataset that must not be null and must be one of two allowed values: "Spend", for commitments that require a predetermined amount of spend, and "Usage", for commitments that require a predetermined amount of usage.
items.s: Column in Contract Commitment · Mandatory · Dimension · String
items.x: Not applicable Value Description Spend Contract commitments that require a predetermined amount of spend. Usage Contract commitments that require a predetermined amount of usage.

items.t: ContractCommitmentCategory MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ContractCommitmentCategory MUST be of type String.
ContractCommitmentCategory MUST NOT be null.
ContractCommitmentCategory MUST be one of the allowed values.

items.b: The monetary value of the contract commitment. The monetary value of a contract commitment, commonly used to monitor progress towards fulfilling contractual commitments that may facilitate discounts for resources or services. It is a Mandatory metric of type Decimal that must conform to the Numeric Format requirements, accepts any valid decimal value and must be denominated in the BillingCurrency. It must not be null when ContractCommitmentCategory is "Spend" and may be null when ContractCommitmentCategory is "Usage". It was introduced in version 1.3.
items.s: Column in Contract Commitment · Mandatory · Metric · Decimal

items.t: ContractCommitmentCost MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ContractCommitmentCost MUST be of type Decimal.
ContractCommitmentCost MUST conform to NumericFormat requirements.
ContractCommitmentCost MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
ContractCommitmentCost MUST NOT be null when ContractCommitmentCategory is "Spend".
ContractCommitmentCost MAY be null when ContractCommitmentCategory is "Usage".
ContractCommitmentCost MUST be denominated in the BillingCurrency.

items.b: The timestamp when the contract commitment record was first created. The timestamp at which a ContractCommitment record was first created, which supports auditability of the contract commitment lifecycle. It is a mandatory Date/Time dimension in the ContractCommitment dataset that must conform to the specification's date/time format requirements and must not be null. The value must represent the moment the ContractCommitment record was instantiated.
items.s: Column in Contract Commitment · Mandatory · Dimension · Date/Time

items.t: ContractCommitmentCreated MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ContractCommitmentCreated MUST be of type Date/Time.
ContractCommitmentCreated MUST conform to DateTimeFormat requirements.
ContractCommitmentCreated MUST NOT be null.
ContractCommitmentCreated MUST represent the moment in time the ContractCommitment record was instantiated.

items.b: The self-contained summary of the contract commitment's terms. A self-contained summary of a contract commitment's terms that gives high-level context without requiring additional discovery, covering what the other columns of the Contract Commitment dataset may not sufficiently describe. It is a String that must conform to the specification's string handling requirements, and its maximum length should be provided in the corresponding FOCUS Metadata Schema. The feature level is Mandatory. The column allows nulls, but the value should not be null. It is a dimension column, introduced in version 1.3.
items.s: Column in Contract Commitment · Mandatory · Dimension · String

items.t: ContractCommitmentDescription MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ContractCommitmentDescription MUST be of type String.
ContractCommitmentDescription MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
ContractCommitmentDescription SHOULD NOT be null.
ContractCommitmentDescription maximum length SHOULD be provided in the corresponding FOCUS Metadata Schema.

items.b: The effective percentage reduction applied to the list price of resources or services covered by a contract commitment. The effective percentage reduction from list price for resources or services covered by a contract commitment, held as a Decimal from 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive. It is a mandatory metric that allows nulls: it must not be null when ContractCommitmentBenefitCategory is "Discount" and must be null when it is "Availability". In a tiered contract, each ContractCommitment row must reflect the discount of the single pricing tier it represents. With several contractual layers it should be the net effective discount, one minus contracted over list unit price, so a 20% commitment discount plus a 10% negotiated discount gives 28%, not 30%.
items.s: Column in Contract Commitment · Mandatory · Metric · Decimal

items.t: ContractCommitmentDiscountPercentage MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ContractCommitmentDiscountPercentage MUST be of type Decimal.
ContractCommitmentDiscountPercentage MUST conform to NumericFormat requirements.
ContractCommitmentDiscountPercentage MUST adhere to the following nullability requirements:
ContractCommitmentDiscountPercentage MUST NOT be null when ContractCommitmentBenefitCategory is "Discount".
ContractCommitmentDiscountPercentage MUST be null when ContractCommitmentBenefitCategory is "Availability".
ContractCommitmentDiscountPercentage MUST be a value between 0.0 and 1.0, inclusive.
For contracts with multiple tiers (e.g., 5% discount up to 1M, 10% above 1M), ContractCommitmentDiscountPercentage MUST adhere to the following additional requirements:
ContractCommitmentDiscountPercentage MUST reflect the discount percentage defined for the specific pricing tier represented by the ContractCommitment row.
ContractCommitmentDiscountPercentage MUST correspond to only one pricing tier per ContractCommitment row.
ContractCommitmentDiscountPercentage SHOULD represent the net effective discount when multiple contractual layers are applicable (e.g., a negotiated discount on top of a standard commitment).

items.b: Represents the categorical length of the contract commitment offering. The categorical length of a contract commitment, such as "3 Years", based on the commercial agreement or pricing model. A mandatory String dimension, it must not be null and must follow string handling requirements. It should use a "[Numeric Value] [Unit]" format with a time unit from Minute through Year, and should reflect the offering's standard duration, not a precise count of days or hours. A time-based value must use the largest whole-number unit, so "1 Year", not "12 Months". It may differ from the span between ContractCommitmentPeriodStart and ContractCommitmentPeriodEnd: an exchanged 3-year commitment keeps "3 Years".
items.s: Column in Contract Commitment · Mandatory · Dimension · String

items.t: ContractCommitmentDurationType MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ContractCommitmentDurationType MUST be of type String.
ContractCommitmentDurationType MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
ContractCommitmentDurationType MUST NOT be null.
ContractCommitmentDurationType SHOULD use the "[Numeric Value] [Unit]" format (e.g., "1 Day", "1 Year", "3 Months", "3 Years").
ContractCommitmentDurationType SHOULD present the unit of time as one of the allowed time-based unit names defined by UnitFormat, from Minute through Year.
ContractCommitmentDurationType SHOULD correspond to the standard duration of the purchased offering (e.g., "1 Year", "3 Years") rather than a precise calculation of days or hours.

When ContractCommitmentDurationType expresses a time-based unit, ContractCommitmentDurationType MUST use the largest time-based unit defined by UnitFormat that expresses the duration as a whole number (e.g., "1 Year" rather than "12 Months", "1 Week" rather than "7 Days").

ContractCommitmentDurationType MAY differ from the actual duration calculated between ContractCommitmentPeriodStart and ContractCommitmentPeriodEnd (e.g., if a 3-year commitment is exchanged in its final month, the resulting record may have a short lifespan but retains a value of "3 Years").

items.b: Represents the specific period used to measure and reset the fulfillment of a contract commitment. The period over which fulfillment of a contract commitment is measured and reset: the window in which usage is aggregated to decide whether commitment obligations have been met. At the end of each interval the ContractCommitmentModel logic applies, either expiring unused capacity (Continuous) or calculating a balance or true-up (Discontinuous). It is a Mandatory String that must not be null and must be one of ten allowed values, from Hourly, Daily and Weekly up to Annual, plus Full Period, Transactional and Custom. Continuous models are typically Hourly, and the value must not be "Full Period" when ContractCommitmentModel is "Continuous".
items.s: Column in Contract Commitment · Mandatory · Dimension · String
items.x: Not applicable Value Sort Order Description Typical Use Case Hourly 10 Measured over a 60-minute period. Continuous Model: Cloud-native RIs and Savings Plans. Daily 20 Measured over a calendar day. Daily active user (DAU) caps or daily license minimums. Weekly 30 Measured over a rolling or fixed 7-day period. Burstable bandwidth or weekly sprint-based SaaS usage. Monthly 40 Measured over a calendar month. Discontinuous Model: SaaS MRR minimums or tiered discounts. Quarterly 50 Measured over a 3-month fiscal period. Enterprise true-ups or volume-based rebate targets. Semi-Annual 60 Measured over a 6-month period. Mid-year budget alignments or review cycles. Annual 70 Measured over a 12-month period. Discontinuous Model: Cloud EAs (Enterprise Agreements). Full Period 80 The full duration of the contract commitment, with no internal resets. "Pool-of-funds commitments" spanning the full commitment duration. Transactional 90 No time-based reset; based purely on event volume or credit consumption. API call bundles or "Credit Packs" with no expiration date. Custom 100 A bespoke interval that does not fit standard calendar units. Bridge contracts, unique POCs, or non-standard durations (e.g., 100 days).

items.t: ContractCommitmentFulfillmentInterval MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ContractCommitmentFulfillmentInterval MUST be of type String.
ContractCommitmentFulfillmentInterval MUST NOT be null.
ContractCommitmentFulfillmentInterval MUST be one of the allowed values.
ContractCommitmentFulfillmentInterval MUST NOT be "Full Period" when ContractCommitmentModel is "Continuous".

items.b: A service-provider-assigned identifier describing a single contract term agreed between a service provider and a customer. A service-provider-assigned identifier for a single contract term agreed between a service provider and a customer; contracts can include commitments to a certain amount of spend or usage over an agreed period. This Mandatory string must not be null, must conform to the String Handling requirements and must be unique within the service provider, and it should be a fully-qualified identifier. Each ContractCommitmentId must have one and only one parent ContractId, and it may match that ContractId.
items.s: Column in Contract Commitment · Mandatory · Dimension · String

items.t: ContractCommitmentId MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ContractCommitmentId MUST be of type String.
ContractCommitmentId MUST conform to StringHandling requirements.
ContractCommitmentId MUST NOT be null.
ContractCommitmentId MUST be a unique identifier within the service provider.
ContractCommitmentId SHOULD be a fully-qualified identifier.
ContractCommitmentId MUST have one and only one parent ContractId.
ContractCommitmentId MAY match ContractId.

items.b: The timestamp when the contract commitment record was last updated. The timestamp when a Contract Commitment record was last updated, which helps FinOps practitioners confirm they are working with the most current version of the record, particularly after corrections or status changes applied since it was created. It must represent the most recent moment at which any column value of the record was created or modified, and it must be greater than or equal to ContractCommitmentCreated. It is a Mandatory Date/Time dimension that must conform to the Date/Time Format requirements and must not be null.
items.s: Column in Contract Commitment · Mandatory · Dimension · Date/Time

items.t: ContractCommitmentLastUpdated MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ContractCommitmentLastUpdated MUST be of type Date/Time.
ContractCommitmentLastUpdated MUST conform to DateTimeFormat requirements.
ContractCommitmentLastUpdated MUST NOT be null.
ContractCommitmentLastUpdated MUST represent the most recent moment in time when any column value of the ContractCommitment record was created or modified.
ContractCommitmentLastUpdated MUST be greater than or equal to ContractCommitmentCreated.

items.b: The current lifecycle state of a contract commitment. The current lifecycle state of a contract commitment, which determines whether the commitment applies to a given period of CostAndUsage data. It is a Mandatory String that must not be null and must be one of seven allowed values: Proposed (being negotiated or modeled, with no legal or financial impact), Pending (finalized or signed, with a future start date), Active (in effect with remaining value), Exhausted (in effect but fully consumed), Expired, Canceled and Superseded. When a record is modified in a way that requires a new ContractCommitmentId, the previous record's status must be "Superseded".
items.s: Column in Contract Commitment · Mandatory · Dimension · String
items.x: Not applicable Value Sort Order Description Proposed 10 The commitment is being negotiated or modeled; it has no legal or financial impact on current data. Pending 20 The commitment is finalized or signed, but the effective start date is in the future. Active 30 The commitment is currently in effect, and it has remaining value. Exhausted 40 The commitment is currently in effect, but its value has been fully consumed. Expired 50 The commitment is no longer active because it reached its scheduled end date. Canceled 60 The commitment is no longer active because it was terminated by either party prior to its scheduled end date. Superseded 70 The commitment is no longer active because it was replaced by a newer version prior to its scheduled end date.

items.t: ContractCommitmentLifecycleStatus MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ContractCommitmentLifecycleStatus MUST be of type String.
ContractCommitmentLifecycleStatus MUST NOT be null.
ContractCommitmentLifecycleStatus MUST be one of the allowed values.
When a contract commitment record is modified in a way that requires a new ContractCommitmentId, ContractCommitmentLifecycleStatus for the previous record MUST be "Superseded".

items.b: Represents the operational behavior and consumption flexibility of a contract commitment. The operational behavior and consumption flexibility of a contract commitment. It is a Mandatory String that must not be null and must be one of two allowed values. "Continuous" is a flat, constant floor of commitment, such as reserved instances or savings plans, applied at a fixed rate per fulfillment interval (usually hourly) with no carry-over, so any dip in usage is unrecoverable waste. "Discontinuous" is a flexible, aggregate commitment, such as an enterprise agreement or software-as-a-service minimum spend, measured over a broad window or against a total monetary value. It must be "Discontinuous" when ContractCommitmentFulfillmentInterval is "Full Period".
items.s: Column in Contract Commitment · Mandatory · Dimension · String
items.x: Not applicable Value Description Continuous A flat, constant "floor" of commitment (e.g., RIs, Savings Plans). Coverage is applied at a fixed rate per Contract Commitment Fulfillment Interval (usually hourly), and benefits are not carried over to subsequent intervals. Discontinuous A flexible, aggregate commitment (e.g., Enterprise Agreements, SaaS Minimum Spend). Coverage is measured over a broad window or against a total monetary value.

items.t: ContractCommitmentModel MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ContractCommitmentModel MUST be of type String.
ContractCommitmentModel MUST NOT be null.
ContractCommitmentModel MUST be one of the allowed values.
ContractCommitmentModel MUST be "Discontinuous" when ContractCommitmentFulfillmentInterval is "Full Period".

items.b: Indicates whether the pricing and terms of a contract commitment are based on a standard, publicly accessible offering or have been specifically brokered through private negotiation. Whether a contract commitment's pricing and terms come from a standard, publicly accessible offering or were brokered through private negotiation. A Mandatory String, it must not be null and must be one of two allowed values: "Public", for terms generally available to all customers through a service provider's standard rate card or portal, or "Negotiated", for terms and pricing modified by agreement between customer and service provider. The page suggests Public as a market-comparison baseline and Negotiated for tracking procurement discounts, noting Negotiated records often fall under non-disclosure agreements, so the field can support data masking or access control.
items.s: Column in Contract Commitment · Mandatory · Dimension · String
items.x: Not applicable Value Description Typical Use Case Public Terms that are generally available to all customers via a service provider's standard rate card or portal. Standard Savings Plans or Reserved Instances purchased via the cloud console without a custom discount. Negotiated Terms and pricing that have been specifically modified through an agreement between the customer and the service provider. Enterprise Agreements (EA), private marketplace offers, or custom SaaS contracts with volume-based discounting.

items.t: ContractCommitmentOfferCategory MUST adhere to the following requirements:
ContractCommitmentOfferCategory MUST be of type String.
ContractCommitmentOfferCategory MUST NOT be null.
ContractCommitmentOfferCategory MUST be one of the allowed values.

items.b: Represents the frequency by which a contract commitment is invoiced. How often a contract commitment is invoiced: the ongoing billing cycle for payment models with deferred financial obligations, or the single settlement event for upfront models. It is a Mandatory String dimension that must not be null and must be one of the allowed values One-Time, Monthly, Quarterly, Semi-Annual, Annual or Custom, for hourly, daily or other irregular cycles. It must be "One-Time" when ContractCommitmentPaymentModel is "All Upfront" and should represent a time granularity equal to or less than ContractCommitmentDurationType's. It differs from ContractCommitmentFulfillmentInterval: a spend-based commitment discount may have an Hourly fulfillment interval but a Monthly payment interval.
items.s: Column in Contract Commitment · Mandatory · Dimension · String
items.x: Not applicable Value Sort Order Description Typical Use Case One-Time 10 A single invoice is generated for the entire obligation. All Upfront models (e.g., 3yr All-Upfront RI) or single-invoice arrears paid at the end of a term. Monthly 20 Invoices for the deferred balance are generated once per month. No Upfront Savings Plans or Monthly SaaS. Quarterly 30 Invoices for the deferred balance are generated every three months. Partial Upfront deals with 90-day true-ups. Semi-Annual 40 Invoices for the deferred balance are generated every six months. Split-payment agreements. Annual 50 Invoices for the deferred balance are generated once per year. Partial Upfront EAs billed yearly. Custom 60 Hourly/Daily or other irregular cycles. Irregular bridge contracts or non-standard terms.

items.b: Defines how corrections to previously delivered FOCUS dataset artifacts are represented in subsequent deliveries. Corrections to previously delivered FOCUS dataset artifacts, whether they update, omit or supplement earlier records, are what CorrectionHandling governs. It exists to keep delivered data consistent over time, protect invoice reconciliation for issued invoices and closed billing periods, and keep changes auditable. It applies to datasets and recognises three correction styles. Under Replacement, which uses the Overwrite delivery mechanism, the dataset must provide a complete snapshot of the affected delivery scope, such as a billing period or a contract, superseding earlier artifacts. Under Delta, which uses Append, the dataset must include additive records within the same delivery scope. Under Ledger, also Append, it must include explicit reversal and re-entry records; a reversal repeats the original record with additive metrics such as cost and quantity carrying the opposite sign. The dataset must document which styles it uses and when each applies, accessible to practitioners. Easy to miss: under Delta or Ledger, an accurate view needs every artifact delivered for the scope.

Formatting for currency columns appearing in a FOCUS dataset. Columns that hold currency information follow CurrencyFormat, which keeps currency values consistent to reduce friction for practitioners analysing and reporting on cost data. A currency can be a national currency, such as USD or EUR, or a consumption currency, such as platform credits or normalized billing units. When a value represents a national currency, the column must conform to ISO 4217:2015 and must use its three-letter alphabetic code. When a value does not represent a national currency, the column must not use an ISO 4217:2015 code. Whether a value is a national currency follows from the column's own definition or documentation, not from the format of the value, and a single column can carry both types, for example a national currency on purchase rows and a consumption currency on usage rows. Which currency types a column allows is set by that column's own requirements, not by this attribute.

Column ID naming, formatting, and value requirements for custom columns appearing in a FOCUS dataset. When the standard FOCUS columns cannot capture everything about a service, data generators may add custom columns, and CustomColumnHandling sets their naming, formatting and value rules. The one mandatory naming rule is that every custom column ID must start with the x_ prefix, marking it as external and avoiding conflicts with FOCUS columns in future releases. After the prefix, the ID should use Pascal case and only alphanumeric characters, should avoid abbreviations other than Id and acronyms other than Sku, should not exceed 50 characters, and should end in Id for identifiers or Name for names. Two value rules are also mandatory: a custom column containing JSON objects must have its object schema documented and accessible to practitioners, and a numeric custom column must contain a single numeric value. Otherwise, custom columns should conform to NullHandling, DateTimeFormat, NumericFormat, StringHandling, CurrencyFormat and UnitFormat where relevant, and to DataGeneratorCalculatedSplitCostAllocationHandling when the data generator supports that allocation. Documentation for a currency column should say how to tell whether a value is a national currency.

items.n: Data Generator-Calculated Split Cost Allocation Handling
items.b: An attribute that allows data generators to offer more detailed cost and usage information based on a method defined and documented by the data generator, including support for allocating costs in cases where the usage of a resource might not match the units the resource is measured in. Some data generators offer split cost allocation for their own services: one charge record in a FOCUS dataset, the origin charge, is split into several allocated charges that show more granular detail, or detail the origin charge does not show, such as unused capacity. DataGeneratorCalculatedSplitCostAllocationHandling sets the column rules that keep such a split consistent, so the origin charge can be derived from its allocated charges. Practitioners use the feature for chargeback and to understand resource usage, and the allocation method is defined and documented by the data generator. A column representing a dimension must match the origin charge's value when present in an allocated charge, and so must a column representing a non-summable metric, such as a unit price. For a summable metric, such as cost or quantity, the values across the allocated charges must add up to the origin charge's value. The distinction matters: summable metrics are divided among allocated charges, while dimensions and non-summable metrics are carried over unchanged.

items.b: Defines requirements for a FOCUS dataset to include custom columns for native dataset columns not represented in FOCUS columns. If useful data exists only in a native dataset, practitioners cannot rely on a FOCUS dataset as their primary source, so DatasetCompleteness requires datasets to carry custom columns for native dataset columns. Every native column must appear as a custom column unless it is listed as an exclusion with justification in publicly available documentation, and only columns unrelated to invoice reconciliation may be excluded. Custom columns needed for invoice reconciliation must be included when the invoice issuer supports payable invoices and FOCUS columns are not sufficient. Every included custom column must be publicly documented with its description, purpose and relationship to native columns. Values must keep native fidelity, with no lossy transformations such as rounding or truncation, and adding custom columns must not alter aggregated summable metrics such as costs and quantities. Datasets should include columns that correlate records with native records, such as native charge identifiers, even when excludable, and should drop custom columns that duplicate FOCUS columns except during a documented transitional period. Columns should be sorted with FOCUS columns alphabetically first, then custom columns alphabetically.

Defines configuration options for controlling the structure and content of a FOCUS dataset. Because datasets from data generators are often massive, DatasetConfiguration lets practitioners tailor a FOCUS dataset's structure and content, removing large, static or irrelevant columns to cut storage costs and processing time. The page cites managing scale, reducing noise for specific workflows, lowering barriers for spreadsheet users, and removing custom x_ columns for cross-provider comparison. It applies to datasets: a FOCUS dataset must be configurable to include only a user-defined selection of columns. It may offer a default column set, and if it does, that default must include all applicable FOCUS columns. Whatever the selection, the dataset must still meet every column-level requirement in the FOCUS schema. The subtle point is that leaving columns out does not relax the rules for the columns kept: if CommitmentDiscountId and ResourceId are excluded, BilledCost and EffectiveCost still reflect commitment discounts correctly, because each included column follows all its requirements, including those that reference columns not in the dataset.

Rules and formatting requirements for date/time-related columns appearing in a FOCUS dataset. Date and time values follow DateTimeFormat so that they are clear, accurate and easy for both humans and systems to interpret. Every conforming column must be expressed in Coordinated Universal Time, to avoid ambiguity across time zones, and must conform to the ISO 8601 standard, as governed by ISO 8601-1:2019. Stricter rules apply when a column represents a specific moment in time: it must use the extended ISO 8601 format with a Coordinated Universal Time offset, written YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. Both the date and the time components must be present, separated by the letter T; hours, minutes and seconds must each use two digits; and the value must end with the ISO 8601 Coordinated Universal Time designator Z. Easy to get wrong: a value for a moment in time that omits the time component, is given in a local time zone, or lacks the trailing Z does not meet these requirements.

Defines how a data generator delivers a FOCUS dataset to a customer. How a data generator delivers a FOCUS dataset to a customer is the subject of DeliveryHandling, which applies to datasets and recognises two delivery mechanisms that are often combined. With Overwrite, the dataset must provide a complete snapshot for a delivery scope, such as a billing period or a contract, and must supersede all earlier dataset artifacts for that scope; it is simple but lacks inherent auditability. With Append, new records are added and all earlier artifacts must be preserved, with updates and omissions arriving as new entries for net effects or reversals, which supports auditability at higher data volume. Under either mechanism, the dataset must not require practitioners to deduplicate records within or across artifacts. Delivered artifacts should come with corresponding FOCUS Metadata. Documentation must be accessible to practitioners and must state the mechanism used, the conditions for each when more than one is used, and, when metadata is delivered, how artifacts correlate with the FOCUS Metadata Schema object. A common hybrid uses Overwrite for open billing periods and Append for closed ones.

Naming conventions for FOCUS columns appearing in a FOCUS dataset. Naming conventions for the standard FOCUS columns come from FocusColumnHandling, so that column IDs in dataset artifacts are consistent for practitioners and display names suit reports and documentation. A FOCUS column's display name must match its column ID with spaces between words: BillingAccountName becomes Billing Account Name, and BillingAccountId becomes Billing Account ID, with Id written as ID. Column IDs must use Pascal case and only alphanumeric characters, must not include special characters, and must not use abbreviations other than Id. They should not use acronyms other than Sku and should not exceed 50 characters, to suit the column length limits of various data repositories. An identifier column must end in Id, a name column must end in Name, and a column representing the product offering that incurred a charge must include Sku. Any column whose ID ends in Category must, when not null, contain one of the FOCUS-defined allowed values.

Rules and formatting requirements for columns appearing in a FOCUS dataset that convey data as complex, hierarchical objects or arrays. JsonObjectFormat extends KeyValueFormat to support complex data such as arrays and nested key-value pairs, for cases the simpler format cannot represent, such as several sets of key-value pairs applying to the same charge record. A conforming column must contain a serialized JSON string that is an object or an array as defined by ECMA 404, and must also meet its own column definition, which may restrict the shape or contents. Keys within an object must be unique, and each value must be a number, string, boolean (true or false), array, object or null. Objects should not exceed three levels of nesting. Objects inside an array must be of a consistent type, must be unique, and must not be null or empty, and they too should not exceed three levels of nesting. Note the difference in strength: the nesting limit is only a recommendation, whereas null, empty or duplicate objects in an array break the format.

Rules and formatting requirements for columns appearing in a FOCUS dataset that convey data as key-value pairs. Key-value pairs, also called name-value, attribute-value or field-value pairs, are often used in place of separate columns when the data would be sparse or has no predetermined keys, which consolidates related information and keeps the schema more consistent. KeyValueFormat sets the rules for columns holding them. A conforming column must be a serialized JSON string consistent with the ECMA 404 definition of an object, so a bare array does not qualify. Keys must be unique within the object. Each value must be a number, a string, a boolean (true or false) or null. Values must not be objects or arrays, which rules out any nesting: a value that contains another object or a list breaks this format even though it is valid JSON.

Indicates how to handle columns that don't have a value. Records that have no value to present for a column need consistent handling, and NullHandling provides it to reduce friction for practitioners using the data for analysis and reporting. It applies to the columns that conform to it. When a column is defined as nullable, it must use null for absent values. A column containing string values must not fill an absent value with an empty string or a placeholder string such as Not Applicable. A column containing numeric values must not fill an absent value with a placeholder number such as 0. Easy to get wrong: substituting a blank, a label or a zero where no value exists; an absent value in a nullable column must be null, not something that looks like real data.

Rules and formatting requirements for numeric columns appearing in a FOCUS dataset. Numeric columns follow NumericFormat so their values are clear, accurate and easy for humans and systems to interpret. FOCUS does not require a specific precision; the provider determines it, and it should be part of the provider's published data definition. A conforming column must contain a single numeric value written as an integer, decimal or scientific notation, and non-null values must fit an allowed data type and precision: Integer as Short (16-bit), Long (32-bit) or Extended (64-bit or higher), or Decimal as Single, Double or Extended (128-bit or higher). Values must not include mathematical symbols, functions or operators, units of measure, currency symbols, commas or other punctuation, apart from one decimal point where needed. Negative values must use a minus sign, and positive values must not carry a plus sign. Scientific notation must use E notation, mEn, with a minus sign for a negative exponent and no plus sign for a positive one, so 35.2E-7 is valid but 35.2E+7 is not. Thousands separators, as in 3,432,342, are also invalid.

Requirements for string-capturing columns appearing in a FOCUS dataset. String values follow StringHandling to support data integrity, interoperability, consistency and reliable analysis and reporting. A conforming column must preserve the original casing and spacing of string values, plus any other consistency factors the data generator or end user specifies. Immutable strings, such as a resource identifier or region identifier, must stay consistent across all billing periods. For mutable strings, such as a resource name or region name, records for periods after a change must show the new value, and records for periods before the change must keep the earlier value, unless the record is a correction to a previously closed billing period, in which case it may show the new value. Columns whose string values are not nullable should not contain empty strings or strings made only of whitespace. Easy to get wrong: altering the case or spacing of values, or carrying a renamed value back into earlier-period records that are not corrections to a closed billing period.

Indicates standards for expressing measurement units in columns appearing in a FOCUS dataset. Units of measure in FOCUS dataset columns, covering data size, time, counts and other dimensions, are standardised by UnitFormat. A unit must include at least one base unit. Data size units must use the allowed abbreviations, such as b, B, KB, GiB or EB, in the same form for singular and plural, so TBs and terabyte are invalid; values above 10^18 must use the exabit, exabyte, exbibit or exbibyte abbreviation, and values below one byte must use bit or byte. Time units must use the allowed names from Year down to Microsecond. Count units should use recommended names such as Request, Token or Core, though unlisted count units may be used, and any unlisted base unit should be a capitalized noun. Compound units must join base units with a hyphen and should read singular-then-plural, as in GB-Hours; ratio units must use a slash, as in GB/Hour. Positive-integer unit and denominator quantities may be added, as in 1000 Tokens or Units/2 Weeks. Time units should be the largest whole unit: 1 Year, not 12 Months.

The Includes Aggregation Level Currency Differences operating model condition represents a verifiable state indicating whether the operating model includes the representation of billing currency and payment currency at different aggregation levels on payable invoices. IncludesAggregationLevelCurrencyDifferences is an operating model condition, introduced in version 1.5, that records whether the operating model represents billing currency and payment currency at different aggregation levels on payable invoices. It is a verifiable state with two outcomes. It must evaluate to true when the operating model includes this representation, and it must evaluate to false when the operating model does not. The page gives its display name as Includes Aggregation Level Currency Differences.

items.b: Operating model conditions represent verifiable states of an operating model that determine the requirement for specific data elements to be present in a FOCUS-compliant dataset. Operating model conditions are verifiable states of an operating model that determine the requirement for specific data elements to be present in a FOCUS-compliant dataset. This page lists 26 conditions, sorted alphabetically by name and grouped into the categories billing, resource, commitment, pricing, account, and allocation. Each entry describes one operating model state, such as including payable invoices, regions, commitment discounts, or tags. Two conditions, Includes Purchases and Includes Quantity Tier Pricing, are marked as preview.

The following examples illustrate how a Cost and Usage FOCUS dataset represents usage-based billing for AI model APIs, where consumption is measured in tokens rather than in the compute, storage, or networking units common to infrastructure services. Provider and model names below are illustrative. This appendix illustrates how a Cost and Usage FOCUS dataset represents token-based billing for AI model APIs using existing columns, with no AI-specific column needed. Six scenarios, with illustrative providers such as Solora AI, Aura Web and LatticeScale, cover a model developer billing directly, several models on one invoice, purchases through a cloud marketplace, a cloud provider serving a third-party model as its own service, a prepaid commitment drawn down by usage, and cache read and cache write metering. Each token type is its own SKU and row: SkuMeter names it, ConsumedQuantity and ConsumedUnit hold raw tokens, and PricingQuantity and PricingUnit hold the priced block, such as 1000000 Tokens. ServiceCategory is "AI and Machine Learning" and ServiceSubcategory "Generative AI". SkuPriceDetails carries model identity and the TokenDirection and TokenCacheAction properties. Marketplace examples show ServiceProviderName differing from HostProviderName and InvoiceIssuerName, and the drawdown example uses CommitmentDiscountId with PricingCategory "Committed". Examples: AI Model Billing Cached Tokens via CSP Marketplace CSP-Served Third-Party Model Drawdown via Prepayment Multi-Model Invoice via CSP Marketplace Multi-Model Usage Per-Token AI Model API

The following examples illustrate how a Cost and Usage FOCUS dataset represents the identity of an AI model using FOCUS-defined SKU Price Details properties. They also demonstrate how the TokenDirection property labels the structural split between input (i.e., prompt) and output (i.e., generated) tokens. Provider and model names below are illustrative. This appendix shows how a Cost and Usage FOCUS dataset records the identity of an AI model through the FOCUS-defined SkuPriceDetails properties ModelDeveloper, ModelFamily, ModelId and ModelVersion, and how the TokenDirection property labels input (prompt) and output (generated) tokens. In the baseline, Acme Corp uses a per-token model API priced separately for input and output per 1,000,000 tokens. In Scenario A it buys directly from the developer Solora AI: input and output are separate SKUs with distinct SkuId, SkuPriceId and SkuMeter values, TokenDirection normalizes the split, ConsumedQuantity holds raw tokens while PricingUnit is "1000000 Tokens", and the cost columns are equal at list price. In Scenario B, LatticeScale serves the same model as service provider, host provider and invoice issuer. ModelDeveloper still names Solora AI, which no participating-entity column represents, and because ModelId is namespaced by the provider, the other identity properties link charges to the underlying model. Provider and model names are illustrative.

The following examples illustrate how a Cost and Usage FOCUS dataset uses the FOCUS-defined SKU Price Details properties TokenCacheAction and TokenDirection to distinguish cached from uncached token charges. They also show how charges for retaining cached content over time remain a separate metered operation. Provider and model names below are illustrative. This appendix shows how a Cost and Usage FOCUS dataset uses the SkuPriceDetails properties TokenCacheAction and TokenDirection to separate cached from uncached token charges, because service providers meter prompt caching inconsistently and SkuMeter names vary. One Acme Corp workload is priced two ways. In Scenario A, Solora AI charges a premium for cache writes and no separate retention charge, so the input rows carry TokenCacheAction "Uncached", "Write" and "Read" with TokenDirection "Input", and the output row carries only TokenDirection "Output". In Scenario B, LatticeScale charges cache writes at the ordinary input rate and bills retention in token-hours, so no row carries "Write", the combined input row carries no TokenCacheAction, and the Context Cache Storage row carries neither property. Return-on-investment calculations follow each scenario, and the text warns that comparing cache meters alone misleads: the comparable figure is total input-side cost, $11.40 against $15.90. Provider and model names are illustrative.

This appendix section defines the concept of a commitment discount. It then lays out a series of FOCUS dataset examples. This appendix defines a commitment discount, a billing model that offers reduced rates on preselected SKUs in exchange for an obligated usage amount (usage-based) or spend amount (spend-based) over a period, then walks through sample FOCUS datasets. It explains the All Upfront, No Upfront and Partial Upfront payment options, the use-it-or-lose-it amortization of a purchase over each charge period, and why each price point (product, payment option and charge role) carries its own SkuPriceId. Scenarios for Aura Web, CrestNode and LatticeScale cover Resource Reservations (CommitmentDiscountCategory Usage, quantities in Hours) and spend plans (Spend, quantities in USD) at 0, 50, 75 and 100 percent utilization and with overage. They show purchase rows with BilledCost but an EffectiveCost of 0, partial upfront split into One-Time and Recurring purchase rows, Used rows with BilledCost 0 and amortized EffectiveCost, Unused rows exposing wasted commitment, overage at PricingCategory Standard, and savings appearing in EffectiveCost rather than ContractedUnitPrice.
