items.t: Measure What Negotiation Reduces the Rate By
items.b: The result is the reduction from negotiation, not the total reduction an organization gets on that [*SKU*](#glossary:sku). Any further reduction from applying a *commitment discount* shows in Effective Cost. The reduction is measured from the public rate in force at the point in time. When the *contract* also has a "Base" record for the same SKU Price ID, measuring from that record instead gives the reduction from the list price the *contract* fixed.
items.x: WITH Review AS ( SELECT ? AS ServiceProviderName, ? AS PricingServiceName, ? AS ContractId, ? AS PointInTime ), PublicPrices AS ( SELECT SP.ServiceProviderName, SP.SkuPriceId, SP.PricingCurrency, SP.UnitPrice FROM SkuPrice SP INNER JOIN Review R ON SP.ServiceProviderName = R.ServiceProviderName AND SP.PricingServiceName = R.PricingServiceName AND (SP.SkuPriceEffectiveStart IS NULL OR SP.SkuPriceEffectiveStart <= R.PointInTime) AND (SP.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd IS NULL OR SP.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd > R.PointInTime) WHERE SP.UnitPriceType = 'List' ), ContractedPrices AS ( SELECT SP.ServiceProviderName, SP.ContractId, SP.SkuPriceId, SP.PricingUnit, SP.PricingCurrency, SP.QuantityTierMinimum, SP.QuantityTierMaximum, SP.UnitPrice FROM SkuPrice SP INNER JOIN Review R ON SP.ServiceProviderName = R.ServiceProviderName AND SP.PricingServiceName = R.PricingServiceName AND SP.ContractId = R.ContractId AND (SP.SkuPriceEffectiveStart IS NULL OR SP.SkuPriceEffectiveStart <= R.PointInTime) AND (SP.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd IS NULL OR SP.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd > R.PointInTime) WHERE SP.ChargeCategory = 'Usage' AND SP.UnitPriceType = 'Contracted' ) SELECT CP.ServiceProviderName, CP.ContractId, CP.SkuPriceId, CP.PricingUnit, CP.PricingCurrency, CP.QuantityTierMinimum, CP.QuantityTierMaximum, PP.UnitPrice AS PublicUnitPrice, CP.UnitPrice AS ContractedUnitPrice, PP.UnitPrice - CP.UnitPrice AS UnitPriceReduction, (PP.UnitPrice - CP.UnitPrice) / NULLIF(PP.UnitPrice, 0) AS DiscountRate FROM ContractedPrices CP LEFT JOIN PublicPrices PP ON PP.ServiceProviderName = CP.ServiceProviderName AND PP.SkuPriceId = CP.SkuPriceId AND PP.PricingCurrency = CP.PricingCurrency ORDER BY DiscountRate DESC

items.t: Compare Public and Negotiated Prices at a Given Quantity
items.b: The public side reads only records with a tier boundary, as described above. So an offering without quantity tiers returns no rows. For such an offering, the query above compares the negotiated rate with the public rate. A *contract* with more than one rate that contains the quantity, such as a tier and a flat rate for the same offering, returns one row for each. Several sets of inputs can be compared in one run, and a set entered more than once returns its rows only once.
items.x: WITH Comparison (ServiceProviderName, SkuId, PricingRegionId, PricingUnit, PricingCurrency, Quantity, PointInTime, ContractId) AS ( VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?) ), PublicTier AS ( SELECT C.ServiceProviderName, C.SkuId, C.PricingRegionId, C.PricingUnit, C.PricingCurrency, C.Quantity, C.PointInTime, C.ContractId, SP.SkuPriceId, SP.QuantityTierMinimum, SP.QuantityTierMaximum, SP.UnitPrice FROM SkuPrice SP INNER JOIN Comparison C ON SP.ServiceProviderName = C.ServiceProviderName AND SP.SkuId = C.SkuId AND (SP.PricingRegionId = C.PricingRegionId OR (SP.PricingRegionId IS NULL AND C.PricingRegionId IS NULL)) AND SP.PricingUnit = C.PricingUnit AND SP.PricingCurrency = C.PricingCurrency AND C.Quantity > SP.QuantityTierMinimum AND (SP.QuantityTierMaximum IS NULL OR C.Quantity <= SP.QuantityTierMaximum) AND (SP.SkuPriceEffectiveStart IS NULL OR SP.SkuPriceEffectiveStart <= C.PointInTime) AND (SP.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd IS NULL OR SP.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd > C.PointInTime) WHERE SP.ChargeCategory = 'Usage' AND SP.UnitPriceType = 'List' AND (SP.QuantityTierMinimum > 0 OR SP.QuantityTierMaximum IS NOT NULL) ), ContractedTier AS ( SELECT C.ServiceProviderName, C.SkuId, C.PricingRegionId, C.PricingUnit, C.PricingCurrency, C.Quantity, C.PointInTime, C.ContractId, SP.SkuPriceId, SP.QuantityTierMinimum, SP.QuantityTierMaximum, SP.UnitPrice FROM SkuPrice SP INNER JOIN Comparison C ON SP.ServiceProviderName = C.ServiceProviderName AND SP.SkuId = C.SkuId AND (SP.PricingRegionId = C.PricingRegionId OR (SP.PricingRegionId IS NULL AND C.PricingRegionId IS NULL)) AND SP.PricingUnit = C.PricingUnit AND SP.PricingCurrency = C.PricingCurrency AND SP.ContractId = C.ContractId AND C.Quantity > SP.QuantityTierMinimum AND (SP.QuantityTierMaximum IS NULL OR C.Quantity <= SP.QuantityTierMaximum) AND (SP.SkuPriceEffectiveStart IS NULL OR SP.SkuPriceEffectiveStart <= C.PointInTime) AND (SP.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd IS NULL OR SP.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd > C.PointInTime) WHERE SP.ChargeCategory = 'Usage' AND SP.UnitPriceType = 'Contracted' ) SELECT DISTINCT PT.ServiceProviderName, PT.SkuId, PT.PricingRegionId, PT.PricingUnit, PT.PricingCurrency, PT.Quantity, PT.PointInTime, PT.ContractId, PT.SkuPriceId AS PublicSkuPriceId, PT.QuantityTierMinimum AS PublicTierMinimum, PT.QuantityTierMaximum AS PublicTierMaximum, PT.UnitPrice AS PublicUnitPrice, CT.SkuPriceId AS ContractedSkuPriceId, CT.QuantityTierMinimum AS ContractedTierMinimum, CT.QuantityTierMaximum AS ContractedTierMaximum, CT.UnitPrice AS ContractedUnitPrice, PT.UnitPrice - CT.UnitPrice AS UnitPriceReduction FROM PublicTier PT LEFT JOIN ContractedTier CT ON CT.ServiceProviderName = PT.ServiceProviderName AND CT.SkuId = PT.SkuId AND (CT.PricingRegionId = PT.PricingRegionId OR (CT.PricingRegionId IS NULL AND PT.PricingRegionId IS NULL)) AND CT.PricingUnit = PT.PricingUnit AND CT.PricingCurrency = PT.PricingCurrency AND CT.Quantity = PT.Quantity AND CT.PointInTime = PT.PointInTime AND CT.ContractId = PT.ContractId

items.t: Resolve the Quantity Tier That Applies to Observed Consumption
items.b: > **Note:** The published pricing terms for the offering, not the tier boundaries, decide whether the rate of the tier returned here applies only to the units inside that tier or to every unit consumed. So this query returns the tier the total quantity reached and that tier's rate. It does not recalculate the charge.
items.x: WITH ChargeTierSet AS ( SELECT CU.ServiceProviderName, SP.SkuId, SP.PricingRegionId, SP.PricingUnit, CU.BillingCurrency, CU.ChargePeriodStart, CU.PricingQuantity, CU.EffectiveCost FROM CostAndUsage CU INNER JOIN SkuPrice SP ON SP.ServiceProviderName = CU.ServiceProviderName AND SP.SkuPriceId = CU.SkuPriceId AND SP.PricingCurrency = CU.BillingCurrency AND SP.UnitPriceType = 'List' AND SP.ChargeCategory = 'Usage' AND (SP.QuantityTierMinimum > 0 OR SP.QuantityTierMaximum IS NOT NULL) AND (SP.SkuPriceEffectiveStart IS NULL OR CU.ChargePeriodStart >= SP.SkuPriceEffectiveStart) AND (SP.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd IS NULL OR CU.ChargePeriodStart < SP.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd) WHERE CU.ChargePeriodStart >= ? AND CU.ChargePeriodEnd <= ? AND CU.ChargeCategory = 'Usage' ), PeriodQuantity AS ( SELECT ServiceProviderName, SkuId, PricingRegionId, PricingUnit, BillingCurrency, MIN(ChargePeriodStart) AS EarliestChargePeriodStart, SUM(PricingQuantity) AS TotalPricingQuantity, SUM(EffectiveCost) AS TotalEffectiveCost FROM ChargeTierSet GROUP BY ServiceProviderName, SkuId, PricingRegionId, PricingUnit, BillingCurrency ) SELECT PQ.ServiceProviderName, PQ.SkuId, PQ.PricingRegionId, PQ.PricingUnit, PQ.BillingCurrency, PQ.TotalPricingQuantity, PQ.TotalEffectiveCost, SP.SkuPriceId, SP.ContractId, SP.QuantityTierMinimum, SP.QuantityTierMaximum, SP.UnitPrice FROM PeriodQuantity PQ INNER JOIN SkuPrice SP ON SP.ServiceProviderName = PQ.ServiceProviderName AND SP.SkuId = PQ.SkuId AND (SP.PricingRegionId = PQ.PricingRegionId OR (SP.PricingRegionId IS NULL AND PQ.PricingRegionId IS NULL)) AND SP.PricingUnit = PQ.PricingUnit AND SP.PricingCurrency = PQ.BillingCurrency AND SP.ChargeCategory = 'Usage' AND ( SP.UnitPriceType = 'Contracted' OR (SP.UnitPriceType = 'List' AND (SP.QuantityTierMinimum > 0 OR SP.QuantityTierMaximum IS NOT NULL)) ) AND PQ.TotalPricingQuantity > SP.QuantityTierMinimum AND (SP.QuantityTierMaximum IS NULL OR PQ.TotalPricingQuantity <= SP.QuantityTierMaximum) AND (SP.SkuPriceEffectiveStart IS NULL OR PQ.EarliestChargePeriodStart >= SP.SkuPriceEffectiveStart) AND (SP.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd IS NULL OR PQ.EarliestChargePeriodStart < SP.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd) ORDER BY PQ.TotalEffectiveCost DESC

items.t: Identify the Next Quantity Tier
items.b: > **Note:** The published pricing terms for the offering decide how the next tier's rate applies, not the tier boundaries. The rate may apply only to the units inside that tier, or to every unit consumed. So the difference between the two rates is the change in rate at the boundary. It is not the change in cost from reaching the next tier.
items.x: WITH RequestedSkus (ServiceProviderName, SkuId) AS ( VALUES -- (ServiceProviderName, SkuId) (?, ?), (?, ?), (?, ?) ), ActiveTiers AS ( SELECT SP.ServiceProviderName, SP.SkuId, SP.PricingRegionId, SP.ContractId, SP.UnitPriceType, SP.PricingUnit, SP.PricingCurrency, SP.ChargeCategory, SP.SkuPriceId, SP.QuantityTierMinimum, SP.QuantityTierMaximum, SP.UnitPrice FROM SkuPrice SP WHERE EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM RequestedSkus RS WHERE RS.ServiceProviderName = SP.ServiceProviderName AND RS.SkuId = SP.SkuId ) AND (SP.QuantityTierMinimum > 0 OR SP.QuantityTierMaximum IS NOT NULL) AND (SP.SkuPriceEffectiveStart IS NULL OR SP.SkuPriceEffectiveStart <= ?) -- point in time AND (SP.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd IS NULL OR SP.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd > ?) -- point in time ) SELECT CURRENT_TIER.ServiceProviderName, CURRENT_TIER.SkuId, CURRENT_TIER.PricingRegionId, CURRENT_TIER.ContractId, CURRENT_TIER.UnitPriceType, CURRENT_TIER.PricingUnit, CURRENT_TIER.PricingCurrency, CURRENT_TIER.SkuPriceId AS CurrentSkuPriceId, CURRENT_TIER.QuantityTierMinimum AS CurrentTierMinimum, CURRENT_TIER.QuantityTierMaximum AS CurrentTierMaximum, CURRENT_TIER.UnitPrice AS CurrentUnitPrice, NEXT_TIER.SkuPriceId AS NextSkuPriceId, NEXT_TIER.QuantityTierMaximum AS NextTierMaximum, NEXT_TIER.UnitPrice AS NextUnitPrice, CURRENT_TIER.UnitPrice - NEXT_TIER.UnitPrice AS UnitPriceReduction, CURRENT_TIER.QuantityTierMaximum - CURRENT_TIER.QuantityTierMinimum AS TierWidth FROM ActiveTiers CURRENT_TIER INNER JOIN ActiveTiers NEXT_TIER ON NEXT_TIER.ServiceProviderName = CURRENT_TIER.ServiceProviderName AND NEXT_TIER.SkuId = CURRENT_TIER.SkuId AND ( NEXT_TIER.PricingRegionId = CURRENT_TIER.PricingRegionId OR ( NEXT_TIER.PricingRegionId IS NULL AND CURRENT_TIER.PricingRegionId IS NULL ) ) AND NEXT_TIER.PricingUnit = CURRENT_TIER.PricingUnit AND NEXT_TIER.PricingCurrency = CURRENT_TIER.PricingCurrency AND NEXT_TIER.ChargeCategory = CURRENT_TIER.ChargeCategory AND ( NEXT_TIER.ContractId = CURRENT_TIER.ContractId OR ( NEXT_TIER.ContractId IS NULL AND CURRENT_TIER.ContractId IS NULL ) ) AND NEXT_TIER.UnitPriceType = CURRENT_TIER.UnitPriceType AND NEXT_TIER.QuantityTierMinimum = CURRENT_TIER.QuantityTierMaximum WHERE CURRENT_TIER.QuantityTierMaximum IS NOT NULL ORDER BY CURRENT_TIER.SkuId, CURRENT_TIER.ContractId, CURRENT_TIER.UnitPriceType, CURRENT_TIER.QuantityTierMinimum

items.t: Evaluate the Purchase Terms Offered for a SKU
items.b: Ranking these options means finding the effective unit price of each one: what one unit of covered usage costs under that option. The SKU Price dataset does not carry what that takes. For a commitment to an amount of usage, the fees are spread over the term. That takes two facts: which usage the purchase covers, and how much usage one unit of it covers. A commitment to an amount of spend needs the rate it gives on each covered *SKU*. FOCUS has no standard way to carry that rate. So the comparison depends on commitment terms from outside the dataset.
items.x: SELECT SkuId, SkuPriceId, ContractId, UnitPriceType, SkuPriceDescription, CommitmentDiscountCategory, PurchaseDurationType, PurchasePaymentModel, PricingUnit, PricingCurrency, UnitPrice FROM SkuPrice WHERE ServiceProviderName = ? AND SkuId = ? AND ChargeCategory = 'Purchase' AND (SkuPriceEffectiveStart IS NULL OR SkuPriceEffectiveStart <= ?) AND (SkuPriceEffectiveEnd IS NULL OR SkuPriceEffectiveEnd > ?) ORDER BY PurchaseDurationType, PurchasePaymentModel, SkuPriceId, ContractId, UnitPriceType

items.t: Project the Effect of Moving Consumption to a Contracted Rate
items.b: Effective Cost is in the Billing Currency, while Unit Price is in the Pricing Currency. So the join matches the two currencies before taking the difference. Consumption billed in a currency the negotiated rate is not quoted in does not return, because the SKU Price dataset has no conversion rate.
items.x: WITH ObservedUsage AS ( SELECT ServiceProviderName, SkuPriceId, BillingCurrency, MIN(ChargePeriodStart) AS EarliestChargePeriodStart, SUM(PricingQuantity) AS TotalPricingQuantity, SUM(EffectiveCost) AS TotalEffectiveCost FROM CostAndUsage WHERE ChargePeriodStart >= ? AND ChargePeriodEnd <= ? AND ChargeCategory = 'Usage' AND SkuPriceId IS NOT NULL AND CommitmentDiscountId IS NULL GROUP BY ServiceProviderName, SkuPriceId, BillingCurrency ) SELECT SP.ContractId, OU.ServiceProviderName, OU.SkuPriceId, SP.PricingUnit, OU.TotalPricingQuantity, OU.TotalEffectiveCost, SP.QuantityTierMinimum, SP.QuantityTierMaximum, SP.UnitPrice, SP.PricingCurrency, OU.TotalPricingQuantity * SP.UnitPrice AS ProjectedContractedAmount, OU.TotalEffectiveCost - (OU.TotalPricingQuantity * SP.UnitPrice) AS ProjectedReduction FROM ObservedUsage OU INNER JOIN SkuPrice SP ON SP.ServiceProviderName = OU.ServiceProviderName AND SP.SkuPriceId = OU.SkuPriceId AND SP.PricingCurrency = OU.BillingCurrency AND (SP.SkuPriceEffectiveStart IS NULL OR OU.EarliestChargePeriodStart >= SP.SkuPriceEffectiveStart) AND (SP.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd IS NULL OR OU.EarliestChargePeriodStart < SP.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd) WHERE SP.ServiceProviderName = ? AND SP.ContractId = ? AND SP.UnitPriceType = 'Contracted' AND SP.ChargeCategory = 'Usage' ORDER BY ProjectedReduction DESC

items.t: Compare Recorded Unit Prices with Published Rates
items.b: Nothing in the query proves that the given *contract* applies to a charge. A charge billed under a different agreement shows a difference that is not a billing error. A charge that SKU Price Eligibility excludes from the negotiated rate does too. For this reason, the comparison assumes `Charges` is first limited to the consumption the agreement covers (e.g., with a Billing Account ID filter for the *billing accounts* it covers). For a charge applied to a [*contract commitment*](#glossary:contract-commitment), the Contract ID can instead be read from [Contract Applied](#datamodel.costandusage.contractapplied), at `ContractApplied.Elements[*].ContractId`, as the relationship between the SKU Price and Cost and Usage datasets describes.
items.x: WITH Comparison AS ( SELECT ? AS ServiceProviderName, ? AS ContractId, ? AS RangeStart, ? AS RangeEnd ), Charges AS ( SELECT CU.ServiceProviderName, CU.BillingAccountId, CU.ChargePeriodStart, CU.SkuPriceId, CU.PricingUnit, CU.PricingQuantity, CU.BillingCurrency, CU.ListUnitPrice, CU.ContractedUnitPrice FROM CostAndUsage CU INNER JOIN Comparison V ON CU.ServiceProviderName = V.ServiceProviderName WHERE CU.ChargePeriodStart >= V.RangeStart AND CU.ChargePeriodEnd <= V.RangeEnd AND CU.ChargeCategory = 'Usage' AND CU.SkuPriceId IS NOT NULL ), Prices AS ( SELECT SP.ServiceProviderName, SP.UnitPriceType, SP.SkuPriceId, SP.PricingCurrency, SP.SkuPriceEffectiveStart, SP.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd, SP.UnitPrice FROM SkuPrice SP INNER JOIN Comparison V ON SP.ServiceProviderName = V.ServiceProviderName AND (SP.UnitPriceType = 'List' OR (SP.ContractId = V.ContractId AND SP.UnitPriceType = 'Contracted')) WHERE SP.ChargeCategory = 'Usage' AND SP.SkuPriceId IN (SELECT SkuPriceId FROM Charges) ) SELECT C.ServiceProviderName, C.BillingAccountId, C.ChargePeriodStart, C.SkuPriceId, C.PricingUnit, C.PricingQuantity, C.BillingCurrency, C.ListUnitPrice, PP.UnitPrice AS PublishedListUnitPrice, C.ListUnitPrice - PP.UnitPrice AS ListUnitPriceDifference, C.ContractedUnitPrice, CP.UnitPrice AS PublishedContractedUnitPrice, C.ContractedUnitPrice - CP.UnitPrice AS ContractedUnitPriceDifference, C.PricingQuantity * (C.ContractedUnitPrice - CP.UnitPrice) AS ContractedCostDifference FROM Charges C LEFT JOIN Prices PP ON PP.ServiceProviderName = C.ServiceProviderName AND PP.SkuPriceId = C.SkuPriceId AND PP.PricingCurrency = C.BillingCurrency AND PP.UnitPriceType = 'List' AND (PP.SkuPriceEffectiveStart IS NULL OR C.ChargePeriodStart >= PP.SkuPriceEffectiveStart) AND (PP.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd IS NULL OR C.ChargePeriodStart < PP.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd) LEFT JOIN Prices CP ON CP.ServiceProviderName = C.ServiceProviderName AND CP.SkuPriceId = C.SkuPriceId AND CP.PricingCurrency = C.BillingCurrency AND CP.UnitPriceType = 'Contracted' AND (CP.SkuPriceEffectiveStart IS NULL OR C.ChargePeriodStart >= CP.SkuPriceEffectiveStart) AND (CP.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd IS NULL OR C.ChargePeriodStart < CP.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd) ORDER BY ContractedCostDifference DESC NULLS LAST

items.t: Cache Hit Rate for Token-Metered SKUs
items.b: Computes the share of input tokens served from a cache, per model, using the TokenDirection, TokenCacheAction, and ModelId properties. The denominator is every input token row, including rows that carry no TokenCacheAction, so it holds whether or not a service provider meters cache writes as their own charge. Where a service provider emits cache read rows but no row for its other input tokens, the denominator loses that bucket and the ratio overstates the hit rate. Where a service provider bills request and response tokens on a single meter, TokenDirection is not populated and those rows are excluded entirely.
items.x: SELECT ServiceProviderName, JSON_VALUE(SkuPriceDetails, '$.ModelId') AS ModelId, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN JSON_VALUE(SkuPriceDetails, '$.TokenCacheAction') = 'Read' THEN ConsumedQuantity END), 0) / NULLIF(SUM(ConsumedQuantity), 0) AS CacheHitRate FROM CostAndUsage WHERE ChargeCategory = 'Usage' AND ChargeClass IS NULL AND ConsumedUnit = 'Tokens' AND JSON_VALUE(SkuPriceDetails, '$.TokenDirection') = 'Input' AND ChargePeriodStart >= ? AND ChargePeriodEnd <= ? GROUP BY ServiceProviderName, ModelId

items.t: Input-to-Output Token Ratio by Model
items.b: Compares the tokens consumed from requests with the tokens generated in responses for each model, using the TokenDirection and ModelId properties. Where a service provider bills request and response tokens on a single meter, TokenDirection is not populated and those rows fall out of both sums.
items.x: SELECT ServiceProviderName, JSON_VALUE(SkuPriceDetails, '$.ModelId') AS ModelId, SUM(CASE WHEN JSON_VALUE(SkuPriceDetails, '$.TokenDirection') = 'Input' THEN ConsumedQuantity END) AS InputTokens, SUM(CASE WHEN JSON_VALUE(SkuPriceDetails, '$.TokenDirection') = 'Output' THEN ConsumedQuantity END) AS OutputTokens, SUM(CASE WHEN JSON_VALUE(SkuPriceDetails, '$.TokenDirection') = 'Input' THEN ConsumedQuantity END) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN JSON_VALUE(SkuPriceDetails, '$.TokenDirection') = 'Output' THEN ConsumedQuantity END), 0) AS InputToOutputRatio FROM CostAndUsage WHERE ChargeCategory = 'Usage' AND ChargeClass IS NULL AND ConsumedUnit = 'Tokens' AND ChargePeriodStart >= ? AND ChargePeriodEnd <= ? GROUP BY ServiceProviderName, ModelId

items.t: FOCUS #169: Pricing Unit Dimension
items.b: • Notes: • represents a specific measurement increment designated by the provider to determine the cost of utilizing a particular resource or service • forms the basis upon which cost calculations are built JGrubb opened this PR to define a Pricing Unit dimension (issue #169). Reviewers went through many rewrites of the definition: flanakin objected to the word "basis" as jargon, and udam-f2 asked whether a recommended unit list was needed, as for Usage Unit. In November 2023 the group renamed the column PricingMeasure and left it non-normalized. shawnalpay went on record against the name, saying "Measure" means something else in reporting models, and rileyjenk warned the rename would confuse. Days later the group reversed course and chose a semi-normalized Pricing Unit that follows the Unit Format attribute, like Usage Unit. flanakin asked for a separate PricingBlockSize, which udam-f2 proposed as a fast follow in v1.x. The PR merged on 13 November 2023.

items.t: FOCUS #181: Usage Unit Dimension
items.b: Spec change for Usage Unit: A unit of measurement for consumption or usage of resources or services amitw-g proposed a UsageUnit column for #181, defining the unit in which consumption is measured. tobrien reworked the text and, after a working-group call, made clear that UsageUnit must not be confused with its pricing equivalents; ijurica had found the comparison with PricingUnit unclear. udam-f2 wanted the definition limited to usage, while flanakin wanted purchases covered for consistency. Reviewers shaped the formats: flanakin proposed three unit patterns and raised billing in blocks of time, cnharris10 noted that AWS and GCP use a dash in units such as GB-Hours, which a later call adopted, and udam-f2 asked about dimensions beyond time, data and count. tobrien renamed Allowed Values to Recommended Values and moved some rules to SHOULD. joshk0 did a style pass and approved. It was merged in November 2023.

items.t: FOCUS #182: Usage Quantity
items.b: FOCUS-182-Usage-Quantity: Adding Usage Quantity Specification & Supporting Content MichaelArkoosh-vega proposed a usage quantity column for #182. The name shifted from amitw-g's QuantityInUsageUnit to UsageQuantity after flanakin argued it should sit beside PricingQuantity. Reviewers fixed contradictory nullability wording, tobrien clarified that it measured usage rather than pricing, and ghost requested changes to use a non-normalized PricingMeasure. udam-f2 approved, and it merged in November 2023.

items.t: FOCUS #190: Numeric Format Attribute
items.b: This Pull Request contains proposed language for the numeric format attribute. Note that this also proposes the ability to define more granular numeric types. tobrien proposed a Numeric Format attribute for #190, with optional Integer and Decimal subtypes and a way to state data precision. After review, tobrien removed quotes from examples, which udam-f2 and ljadvey felt implied strings, dropped mention of scientific notation after ljadvey called it not compute friendly (marc-perreaut noted E notation appears in Azure data), left precision for providers to document, and replaced float with decimal based on IEEE 754. flanakin asked to make the decimal point explicitly a period, and joshk0 suggested matching scope wording in the other format attributes. joshk0 also suggested prescribing wire formats, citing precision loss with FLOAT64; tobrien proposed covering that in separate implementation guidance, and joshk0 approved. It was merged in November 2023.

items.t: FOCUS #161: Pricing Category column
items.b: First draft from 0.5 rodneyjoyce opened this PR from a 0.5 draft of a column first written as PricingModel and merged as Pricing Category (issue #161), with flanakin drafting much of the text. The values were contested. marc-perreaut and flanakin questioned how Fixed differed from On-Demand. shawnalpay proposed Standard instead of On-Demand, but rodneyjoyce said the VS2 squad preferred On-Demand as better understood. sarahcloudpm saw overlap between Dynamic and On-Demand and asked why Other was needed; mike-finopsorg defended Other as better than null or a wrong value. A Shared value for dedicated hosts, raised by flanakin, was deferred to a point release. udam-f2 argued for a broader Discounted value, which flanakin said grouped too much, and aqu-erp placed finer levels after v1.0. It merged in November 2023.

items.t: Remove broken ChargeType link
items.b: Removing a link that was accidentally left in 0.5 when we moved the allowed values into the column spec. flanakin opened #217 in October 2023 to remove a broken ChargeType link left from 0.5. shawnalpay approved it. SanjnaSrivatsaVMware asked whether out-of-cycle bills, refunds and credits count as Adjustments. flanakin said refunds and credits on them would be adjustments, while other line items appear as usual. flanakin suggested taking any 1.0 gap to Slack. ljadvey and udam-f2 approved, and the pull request was merged on 18 October 2023.

items.t: FOCUS #185: Key-Value Format
items.b: Second iteration of the Key-Value Format after much discussion and lots of help from the people mentioned below kk09v opened a second iteration of the Key-Value Format for #185, co-authored with flanakin, rileyjenk, cnharris10 and udam-f2. udam-f2 suggested consistency edits, including requiring a serialized JSON string per ECMA-404 and possibly naming it KeyValue Format, which ljadvey liked. joshk0 raised key case sensitivity and empty object versus null, then judged both better left to Tags. It was merged in November 2023.

items.t: Add Charge Description dimension
items.b: cnharris10 opened this pull request to add a Charge Description column, closing #220. ljadvey requested changes so the provider mappings named specific columns, as the AWS row did. anatri1 asked whether "Charge" was the right term, since providers used it as a synonym for cost; cnharris10 said that naming debate could happen separately. joshk0 approved and proposed examples of good and bad descriptions, warning against pricing text, marketing copy and opaque SKU codes. flanakin commented without approving, saying the column's purpose and how to fill it were unclear, and asked for such guidance to become MUST or SHOULD requirements. Inline threads also debated nullability, a length limit (cnharris10 said SaaS descriptions can be much longer) and the Azure and GCP mappings. udam-f2 approved, and it was merged in November 2023.

items.t: service-category-dimension update
items.b: All other Dimensions use this standard (checked all 0.5 and 1.0) At udam-f2's suggestion, rodneyjoyce changed the ServiceCategory dimension to the format used by all other 0.5 and 1.0 dimensions, though rodneyjoyce preferred the more user-friendly form. flanakin approved for consistency but argued the spec should eventually go the other way. udam-f2 added the broader question to a list of spec-wide consistency changes. It merged in October 2023.

items.t: FOCUS #165: Pricing Quantity
items.b: FOCUS #165 - initial import ahullah opened this PR to define a column for the quantity of a resource or service measured in its pricing unit, first named QuantityInPricingUnit. flanakin proposed renaming it PricingQuantity, alongside UsageQuantity, so related columns would sit together, and the PR adopted the new name. joshk0 approved but asked why the column was needed; udam-f2 explained that block pricing makes it differ from usage quantity. Reviewers debated provider mappings: rupagcp and shruthinambi pointed to different Google Cloud fields, and marc-perreaut questioned the Azure mapping, which ijurica left to the converters group. ijurica also questioned requiring credits to be negative, and kk09v noted that unit prices cannot be summed. The PR was merged in November 2023.

items.t: Add Tags dimension
items.b: cnharris10 opened this pull request to add a Tags column, closing #226, and most discussion happened in inline review threads. ljadvey, mike-finopsorg and others asked what a "finalized" tag meant, and cnharris10 offered alternative wordings; joshk0 favored dropping the terms static, dynamic and finalized altogether. udam-f2 and ljadvey wanted the data type stated as JSON. Reviewers also covered prefixes for provider-defined tags, null values for keys without values (marc-perreaut doubted such tags existed, and cnharris10 pointed to GCP network tags) and whether a survey of provider practice belonged in the spec. marc-perreaut noted that tag inheritance differs by provider. mattray, udam-f2 and shawnalpay approved, joshk0 said they would follow up with tweaks, and it was merged in November 2023.

items.t: Minor edits
FOCUS #232: BilledCost metric review
items.b: • BilledCost spec update: included discounts list, description and content constraints review/update • /specification/metrics/metrics.mdpp update: arranging metrics in alphabetical order ijurica revised the BilledCost metric's description and content constraints, adding a list of discounts, and put the metrics in alphabetical order (#232). udam-f2 suggested naming the discounts explicitly rather than grouping them under "all". mattray said it looked good, udam-f2 approved it as mostly wording changes, and it was merged in November 2023.

items.t: FOCUS #231: ListUnitPrice metric review
items.b: • Normative paragraph adjustment • Supporting content - Providers mappings adjustments Pull request #234, by ijurica, revised the ListUnitPrice metric's normative text and provider mapping guidance for #231. nfonrose proposed tying the price to a SkuId, and the definition went through several drafts; after noting that providers also publish commitment-inclusive prices, ijurica removed the SkuPriceId association and stated explicitly which discounts are excluded. yprikhodko questioned whether the column was redundant, since it could be derived from List Cost and usage, and raised spot discounts. flanakin pressed for an explicit warning that prices in billing currency will not match pricing APIs, deferring it to a separate PR. shawnalpay asked that a TODO in supporting content be resolved or struck; ijurica merged anyway, acknowledging the gap. udam-f2 and shawnalpay approved, and it merged in November 2023.

items.t: FOCUS #174: List Cost metric
items.b: List Cost metric specification and supporting content ijurica proposed the List Cost metric for #174. jpickardgreen requested changes, offering a definition that included free-tier and volume-based rates but excluded other discounts and amortization. yprikhodko asked that spot discounts also be excluded so savings from spot could be measured, and ijurica folded that in. flanakin wanted the definition simplified towards a public retail price. shawnalpay asked for the formula to be stated explicitly, and jpickardgreen noted that would need applying to every price-times-quantity metric; shawnalpay also proposed that normative statements start with the keyword. udam-f2 suggested defining it as List Unit Price multiplied by Pricing Quantity, added rules for null prices and approved. It merged in November 2023.

items.t: FOCUS #241: Commitment Discount Type Dimension
items.b: First version for consideration rodneyjoyce proposed a Commitment Discount Type dimension for #241: a provider-assigned name for the type of commitment discount applied. flanakin asked for cloud-specific examples to move to supporting content, and debated with udam-f2 whether the definition should say identify or label. cnharris10 suggested more provider mappings, such as AWS Capacity Blocks and BigQuery Reservations. jasonkellyAP and udam-f2 approved, and it was merged in November 2023.

items.t: FOCUS #243: SKU Price ID Dimension
items.b: SKU Price ID dimension definition and supporting content shawnalpay opened this pull request defining the SKU Price ID column and its supporting content (#243). ijurica asked for a rule that one SkuPriceId cannot relate to more than one SkuId, which shawnalpay added. ijurica later asked how practitioners would find the list unit price when the SKU price already includes commitment discounts, and suggested a future column holding the matching list price ID, while approving. In inline threads the description was reworded on a VS3 working group call; marc-perreaut objected to wording implying a SKU has only one price; udam-f2 asked whether column names should use Sku or SKU; mike-finopsorg proposed tying each SkuPriceId to a single list unit price; and aqu-erp and flanakin refined the OCI, Azure and GCP mappings. It was merged in November 2023.

items.t: Corrections on some typographic conventions
items.b: As titled.

items.t: Clean up random uses of "record"
items.b: @flowerinthenight noticed we use both "row" and "record" as generic references to a charge. "Row" is used more, so at least normalizing on that. There are a few places where "charge" makes less sense or is needed to differentiate from the monetary value of a "charge". This mostly editorial pull request by flanakin replaced scattered uses of "record" and "line item" with "row", after flowerinthenight noticed the mixed terms. udam-f2 objected to unrelated auto-formatting changes in the diff. shawnalpay asked whether this meant line item and charge were not synonyms; flanakin said the terms were roughly synonymous and suggested a fuller terminology pass after 1.0. It was merged in November 2023.

items.t: FOCUS #249: EffectiveCost review
items.b: Effective Cost spec review ijurica's pull request reviewed the EffectiveCost definition (#249), with related BilledCost wording. rileyjenk objected that Effective Cost is a value, not a charge, so ijurica switched to "cost". Reviewers also refined amortization wording and example tables, and flanakin questioned a sentence saying totals may not match invoices. udam-f2 approved, and it merged in November 2023.

items.t: FOCUS #252: Identifying custom columns
items.b: FOCUS needs a way to differentiate between FOCUS and custom columns that won't conflict as FOCUS evolves and adds more columns over time. flanakin proposed marking custom columns with a leading underscore so they could not clash with future FOCUS columns and would sort apart from them. rupagcp asked about vendor prefixes instead; flanakin explained the trade-offs, including prefix registration, sorting and duplicated columns. arrarama and lbernalposada worried about providers reusing the same names, and a working-group call then chose a vendor prefix, though flanakin noted absolute uniqueness was not needed. yprikhodko warned that leading underscores need special handling in engines such as Athena, and flanakin finally settled on a required x_ prefix, for external, which others may extend with their own identifier. flanakin kept the term custom over udam-f2's provider-defined, since tools also add columns, and defended column ordering on usability grounds. It was merged in November 2023.

items.t: FOCUS #242: Creating SKU ID based on work done by @arrarama
items.b: Creating SKU ID (continuation from https://github.com/FinOps-Open-Cost-and-Usage-Spec/FOCUS_Spec/pull/239) Author: arrarama udam-f2 continued arrarama's work from #239 to define the SKU ID column (#242). shruthinambi said GCP's SKU data came from the BigQuery pricing export; udam-f2 replied that the mapping referred to the billing data and added a note about the pricing export. Inline threads set nullability rules tying SkuId to SkuPriceId, and joshk0 asked about refunds. shawnalpay approved, and it was merged in November 2023.

items.t: Standardize on "row"
items.b: Found extra occurrences of "line item" Pull request #263, opened by flanakin in November 2023, aimed to standardize on the term "row" after finding extra occurrences of "line item." Reviewers ljadvey, cnharris10 and rileyjenk approved it on 10 November 2023, and udam-f2 approved it on 11 November with a brief LGTM. It was merged on 11 November 2023. This was a small editorial change.

items.t: Fix PDF generation build errors
items.b: Fix da build

items.t: Scrub v1
items.b: Rename 'dimensions' folders in spec and supporting content to 'columns' and merge in metrics into the same columns folder. Must preserve git history and committers (renames not delete and add new). Pull request #272, opened by udam-f2 on 14 November 2023, proposed renaming the 'dimensions' folders in the specification and supporting content to 'columns' and merging the metrics content into that same folder. The author required that git history and committers be preserved, so files were renamed rather than deleted and re-added. cnharris10, ijurica and mike-finopsorg approved it the same day, and it was merged on 14 November 2023.

items.t: Final batch of scrubs (outside of glossary)
items.b: Move DataType down to be co-located with value format. Fix value-format in constraints. Other formatting fixes ChargeCategory rename Fixing Quotes, column types, links etc. Remove and/or, update for cost and usage -> billing, null or empty -> null udam-f2 opened this largely editorial PR as a final scrub outside the glossary, moving DataType beside value format, fixing quotes, column types and links, and changing wording such as "cost and usage" to "billing" and "null or empty" to "null". flanakin suggested casing fixes and asked whether price columns are dimensions or metrics; shawnalpay said either view was defensible. It was merged in November 2023.

items.t: Update skupriceid.md
items.b: casing

items.t: Minor grammar/formatting cleanup around Tags and Charge Description
items.b: Minor grammar/format cleanup around Tags and Charge Description • Minor sentence restructure • Past tense -> Present tense • Formatting a prefix as `code` cnharris10 made minor grammar and formatting fixes to the Tags and Charge Description columns, such as moving from past to present tense and formatting a prefix as code. shawnalpay suggested further wording tweaks, including questioning an "(italicized)" note. The change was purely editorial and merged in November 2023.

items.t: Glossary hyperlinks - final merge
FOCUS #317: BillingAccountType and SubAccountType
items.b: Suggesting adding BillingAccountType and SubAccountType to include the provider-specific labels for the BillingAccountId/Name and SubAccountId/Name. This is similar to ResourceType and CommitmentDiscountType for their respective ID and Name columns. flanakin proposed BillingAccountType and SubAccountType columns carrying provider labels for account IDs (for example "Subscription" or "Project"), mirroring ResourceType. TDubovchenko suggested metadata instead; flanakin replied that types vary across billing accounts and providers, so metadata could not describe multi-provider datasets. rupagcp opposed adding them to v1.0 without alignment, and udam-f2 reported in March 2024 that maintainers leaned toward metadata first. ijurica favored mandatory columns, while mlohmeijer, AWS-ZachErdman and rupagcp questioned their practical value and the added schema size. At an April 2024 members meeting some members did not see them as critical for v1.0. Later suggestions from flanakin made them conditional columns introduced in 1.2. Members agreed to the pull request on February 6, 2025, and it merged that month.

items.t: Fix 'Column required' value to 'True' based on column description #295
items.b: Based on this description, this column should be marked as required ... In December 2023, cnharris10 opened #295 to change a column's "Column required" value to True, because the column description calls for it. The change relates to #290. shawnalpay and aqu-erp approved on 6 December 2023, flanakin on 7 December, and rupagcp commented LGTM on 8 December. udam-f2 approved on 24 January 2024, and the pull request was merged on 29 January 2024. No disagreements are recorded.

items.t: Numeric columns should not use 0 when no value
items.b: Adding additional clarity to ensure numeric columns do not use `0` in place of a null when there is no value. flanakin proposed clarifying the null-handling rules so that numeric columns do not use 0 in place of a null. Inline, rileyjenk noted that values like "Not set" can be legitimate, and udam-f2 questioned applying the rule regardless of whether a column allows nulls, since non-nullable columns need some value. udam-f2 approved, suggesting separate nullable and non-nullable rules could come later. It was merged in March 2024.

items.t: FOCUS #294: PricingQuantity, PricingUnit, UsageQuantity and UsageUnit review
items.b: Multiple Pricing and Usage related columns review: Usage Quantity; definition adjustment; normative paragraph adjustment; Usage Unit ijurica revised the definitions and normative text of PricingQuantity, PricingUnit, UsageQuantity and UsageUnit for #294. rileyjenk worried that separate pricing and usage units would often hold identical values and might imply they should differ; ijurica deferred that to a separate PR with sample data (#327) and noted that unused commitments and credits should be excluded when reconciling usage. tobrien, jvdwiel and udam-f2 approved, and it was merged in February 2024.

items.t: FOCUS feature level introduction - mandatory / conditional / optional
items.b: Should FOCUS encapsulate all possible billing data, inclusive of a 1 line item, $1 invoice up through a 1 cloud's billion line item cost and usage dataset? udam-f2 proposed grading columns by how required they were, first as a "FOCUS Essential" set and, once #372 was merged in, as mandatory, conditional or optional feature levels. flanakin disliked an Essential label and pushed for conditional presence, such as requiring SkuId when a provider has several SKUs; udam-f2 saw Essential as an easy marketing term for a basic requirement set. ijurica proposed adding SkuId to the essentials and mapped references to non-essential columns; marc-perreaut thought PricingUnit and PricingQuantity sufficed and saw no problem when a referenced column was absent. rupagcp doubted Charge Frequency was essential, rileyjenk asked whether ListCost needed a published list price, and flanakin's objection to making AvailabilityZone a MUST moved to #367. cnharris10 and marc-perreaut approved, and members approved it in April 2024.

items.t: Related to Issue #342 - Tag key differentation when a supporting value can or cannot exist.
items.b: Related to Issue: https://github.com/FinOps-Open-Cost-and-Usage-Spec/FOCUS_Spec/issues/342 cnharris10 clarified Tags handling (#342): keys that cannot hold values get a true value, and tags not set on a resource are left out. rileyjenk argued null and missing values differ and providers should choose. AWS-ZachErdman and rupagcp asked for fuller examples, and flanakin sought practitioner agreement on Booleans, getting a small acknowledgment on a call. Members approved it in March 2024 and it merged.

items.t: #343: EffectiveCost clarification
items.b: Updating EffectiveCost to be explicit it does not use blended rates. AWS-ZachErdman proposed, for #343, stating explicitly that EffectiveCost does not use blended rates, plus a small grammar fix. flanakin warned that many readers misunderstand "blending", so AWS-ZachErdman offered simpler wording saying Effective Cost does not mix costs across charges of the same service. rileyjenk approved it as reflecting the original intent, and it was merged in March 2024.

items.t: Adding Region ID
items.b: Region dimension is getting split into 2 dimensions: Region ID and Region Name. This is the change to set up Region ID dimension. ilia-semenov opened this PR to create a Region ID column as part of splitting Region into Region ID and Region Name. cnharris10 questioned a firm MUST because Region was not a FOCUS Essential column, while SanjnaSrivatsaVMware argued a resource's region must be reported; ljadvey proposed requiring the column only when providers offer regional deployment. After the files were renamed, it was approved and merged in March 2024.

items.t: Creating a new dimension Region Name
items.b: @ljadvey to add more details in the supporting documents. I am pushing a skeleton of that currently. SanjnaSrivatsaVMware opened a PR adding a Region Name column, with ljadvey to fill in the supporting content. udam-f2 asked that it reference RegionId rather than duplicate it, cnharris10 proposed conditional presence wording matching #352 and marking it non-essential, and aqu-erp asked about services spanning several regions. mike-finopsorg approved, noting that providers sometimes use region names rather than IDs in APIs. It was merged in March 2024.

items.t: 330 charge category credit refund
items.b: Updated to breakout refunds and credits from charge category. to be handled in a new adjustment category column. This will allow all main charge categories (Usage, Purchase, Tax) to easily classify regular usage, from usage specific refunds or general purpose incentives / credits ahullah opened this PR for #330 to move refunds and credits out of ChargeCategory into a separate column, so Usage, Purchase and Tax charges could each be marked as regular or a correction. flanakin asked to keep Adjustment in ChargeCategory for rounding errors and unexpected charges, which ahullah restored, and to merge stray supporting content. The new column's name was contested: udam-f2, shawnalpay and flanakin offered alternatives, Transaction Category was floated, and Charge Class was approved on a joint working group call. cnharris10 found "Regular" and "Correction" too abstract. thecloudman doubted the column's value, wanted an adjustment type instead and moved that to a new issue. Later suggestions were left for future issues. udam-f2 approved, and it merged in April 2024.

items.t: FOCUS #336: Negotiated/Contracted List Unit Price and Cost
items.b: • Negotiated List Unit Price specification and supporting content • Negotiated List Cost specification and supporting content • glossary update - _Negotiated List Unit Price included_ ijurica's PR, implementing #336, added unit price and cost columns reflecting negotiated discounts, with naming debated among Negotiated, OnDemand and NegotiatedList. After a vote moved away from "Negotiated", the columns became ContractedUnitPrice and ContractedCost; shawnalpay objected that "negotiated discount" is established FinOps parlance and the new term would confuse adopters, while accepting being in the minority. The group approved it on April 4, 2024, and it was merged.

items.t: FOCUS #330: CommitmentDiscountStatus column
items.b: Related to #330 flanakin's PR, for #330, added a column showing whether a commitment discount portion was used or unused. AWS-ZachErdman asked why not use ChargeCategory values instead; flanakin said practitioners wanted unused amounts included when filtering on "Usage". Members agreed the content on April 11, 2024, pending a naming poll among options such as CommitmentDiscountUsage and Commitment Status. The group chose CommitmentDiscountStatus and approved it on April 18, and it was merged.

items.t: FOCUS #330: Pricing Category value updates
items.b: Updates PricingCategory values: • "On-Demand" to "Standard" • "Commitment-Based" to "Committed" flanakin's PR carried out decisions from #330, renaming the PricingCategory values On-Demand to Standard and Commitment-Based to Committed, with minor bullet formatting changes. marc-perreaut approved, the member group approved the content in April 2024, and it merged that month.

items.t: Fix introduced version references to be accurate
items.b: While we still need to decide whether to reference pre-release versions in the spec, the current spec already does and many of them are wrong. This PR fixes those that are wrong to at least be accurate. I figure we can have a separate conversation about excluding pre-release versions and update everything based on that. Pull request #384, opened by flanakin on 4 April 2024, corrected introduced-version references in the spec that were wrong, while leaving the question of pre-release versions for later discussion. udam-f2 reported that the member group approved it for check-in but raised concern about citing unreleased or release-candidate versions. ahullah and mike-finopsorg approved it on 11 April 2024, and it was merged on 12 April 2024.

items.t: Metadata structure simple
items.b: Metadata structure simplified for Version 1.0 specification Moved examples to supporting content for now Added normative text to schema items Use structure more similar to columns / attributes mike-finopsorg proposed a simplified metadata structure for version 1.0, written like the column and attribute definitions, with normative text added and examples moved to supporting content. udam-f2 questioned keeping separate column and tag prefixes; mike-finopsorg replied that they need not match, and udam-f2 and marc-perreaut suggested allowing several tag prefixes. marc-perreaut proposed clearer names, including Data Generator in place of Billing Generator, which flanakin backed as more forward-looking, and argued metadata MUST be supplied. flanakin also asked for a DataGeneratorVersion. The main dispute was removing SchemaId: rileyjenk argued DataGeneratorVersion could not identify a schema and that dropping it broke the schema metadata. The group approved it on April 18, agreeing to open an issue to bring back SchemaId, and it merged in April 2024.

items.t: FOCUS #104: ConsistencyHandling or StringFormat attribute
items.b: • Adding StringFormat attribute specification and supporting content • Removing current references to value-format consistency requirements from the following columns: • RegionId • RegionName • ResourceType • CommitmentDiscountType • Making a small adjustment in the NumericFormat specification ijurica added a string attribute, first called StringFormat and later String Handling, and removed value-format consistency rules from four columns (#104). Inline threads covered rules for mutable and immutable strings; cnharris10 doubted providers could always follow them, and udam-f2 preferred keeping MUST with stated exceptions. ijurica worried that null-handling rules clashed with leaving empty strings unaddressed. The group approved it on April 18, 2024, and it was merged that month.

items.t: Further specify inclusive/exclusive datetime values for BillingPeriod{Start,End} and ChargePeriod{Start,End}
items.b: Issue: https://github.com/FinOps-Open-Cost-and-Usage-Spec/FOCUS_Spec/issues/380 cnharris10 proposed, for #380, stating that BillingPeriodStart and ChargePeriodStart are inclusive and the matching End columns exclusive. At the weekly meeting, members including mike-finopsorg asked what inclusive and exclusive meant, prompting glossary entries and examples. projectlocale requested changes over ambiguous sentences and suggested interval notation, and udam-f2 raised formatting points. The group approved it on April 25, 2024, and it was merged that month.

items.t: FOCUS #319: Track (sometimes differing) commitment burndown units separately from consumed quantity/unit columns
items.b: Lead Maintainers: Chris Harris, @cnharris10, Irena Jurica, @ijurica ### Documents: • PR: #400 Commitment Utilization and Normalization • PR: #524 rename Commitment-Based Discount to Commitment-Discount by christopher.harris@datadoghq.com • Usage vs Pricing Quantity and unit examples • 24.07.21-CommitmentUtilization-sample-datasets • #400-commitment-utilization folder • Document: 24.09.08 - Commitment utilization disc… For #319, cnharris10 and ijurica proposed columns tracking commitment discount consumption in the commitment's own units, which often differ from resource units, such as normalized hours or currency. The PR also made ConsumedQuantity and ConsumedUnit null on unused commitment rows. After a hold in mid-2024, thecloudman feared redundant columns bloating datasets and AWS-ZachErdman wanted stronger justification; cnharris10 pointed to the differing units. ijurica and cnharris10 agreed list and contracted costs should be zero for unused commitments. When approval failed in late August, with timwright2000 objecting, separate consumed and purchased quantity columns were merged into one, CommitmentDiscountQuantity, which ijurica endorsed. rileyjenk argued normalization should wait for v1.2 because it only fitted compute; ijurica suggested moving size-flexibility detail into supporting content. Members approved it in September 2024 and it was merged.

items.t: FOCUS #330: Replace ChargeSubcategory references after ChargeClass inclusion
items.b: Pull request #402, by flanakin, replaced references to ChargeSubcategory across the specification after ChargeClass was introduced (#330). Review was largely mechanical: udam-f2 found leftover ChargeSubcategory mentions, flanakin updated constraint tables to use Feature level, and ijurica asked for the ChargeCategory description and the grouping constructs appendix to be updated too. A PricingQuantity suggestion from aqu-erp was moved to a separate PR after a TF-1 discussion on #366. thecloudman approved and proposed renaming ChargeClass's 'Regular' value to 'Standard' in a separate PR, #410, which ahullah replied had been approved. The group approved #402 on 18 April 2024, though udam-f2 asked that open conversations be resolved first, and it merged in April 2024.

items.t: FOCUS #330: Update chargeclass value from "Regular" to "Standard"
items.b: Pricing category had the value "on-demand" changed to "Standard", so recommend keeping consistency in naming and have charge class value as "Standard" instead of "Regular" thecloudman proposed renaming the ChargeClass value "Regular" to "Standard", matching an earlier change to pricing category values. ahullah and flanakin saw it as an improvement, but udam-f2 relayed marc-perreaut's task force suggestion of "Original", and marc-perreaut also floated renaming the column ChargeOccurrence. ahullah merged it in April 2024, then said that was too soon and opened #422 to change the value to "Original".

items.t: FOCUS #366: SkuId, SkuPriceId, and Pricing-related columns review due to ChargeCategory and ChargeClass cleanup
items.b: ChargeCategory and ChargeClass cleanup impacted multiple columns. Based on current ChargeCategory references, the following columns must be revisited: SkuId; SkuPriceId; ContractedUnitPrice; ListUnitPrice ijurica reworked SkuId, SkuPriceId and the price, cost and quantity columns for #366 after the ChargeCategory and ChargeClass cleanup, using a table of when values must be per SKU or may be null. flanakin suggested wording for several columns. Members approved it on April 25, 2024, with a final MAY lowered to "may" and a changelog entry added. It merged in April 2024.

items.t: Updated versioning/id approach to metadata
items.b: Removed DataGeneratorVersion Added SchemaId under schema section Moved ProviderTagPrefixes to live under the column definition of the Schema mike-finopsorg revised the metadata versioning and identifier approach: removing DataGeneratorVersion, adding SchemaId to the schema section and moving ProviderTagPrefixes under the schema's column definition. rileyjenk updated the supporting content to match, and kotzenjh approved it as a uniform way to show provider tags. Members approved it on 25 April and it merged in April 2024.

items.t: #409 Path 1 - Usage Unit/Quantity restricted to usage charges and renamed to Consumed Unit/Quantity
items.b: PR 1 of 2 aqu-erp proposed, as one of two paths for #409, limiting UsageQuantity and UsageUnit to usage charges and renaming them ConsumedQuantity and ConsumedUnit, leaving purchase quantities for later. AWS-ZachErdman, udam-f2 and thecloudman preferred this path; marc-perreaut wanted a broader column with a better name, such as StandardizedPricingQuantity. udam-f2 replied that purchase quantities would be handled after v1.0. The group approved it in May 2024.

items.t: Clarify NULL handling for placeholders
items.b: As discussed regarding #417. Added a little more clarifying language to say don't use placeholders to represent NULLs #421, opened by mike-finopsorg on 25 April 2024, followed discussion in #417 by stating that columns must not use placeholder values, such as 0, or empty strings to represent nulls. flanakin questioned the casing and parentheses and suggested rewording. ijurica, flanakin and kotzenjh approved on 25 April 2024, the day members agreed to it at their meeting. udam-f2 approved on 29 April 2024, and it was merged that day.

items.t: 424: Description updates on when to exclude to avoid double counting List/Contracted
items.b: Issue #424 udam-f2 updated the List Cost and Contracted Cost descriptions to say which purchase charges to exclude to avoid double counting in savings calculations (#424). AWS-ZachErdman suggested clearer wording. flanakin argued that required filtering needed a prescriptive method and asked to avoid "billed basis" jargon; UdamDewaraja defended these as industry terms. The group approved it, planning a follow-up item for remaining concerns, and it was merged in May 2024.

items.t: FOCUS #430: EffectiveCost spec change - addressing purchases paid to cover future eligible charges
items.b: EffectiveCost spec change - addressing purchases paid to cover future eligible charges Pull request #431, by ijurica, changed the EffectiveCost definition to cover purchases paid in advance of future eligible charges (#430). thecloudman asked whether it meant amortizing such purchases while excluding the up-front charge, and AWS-ZachErdman and kk09v both saw the wording as a clarification rather than an exception. flanakin approved but found it hard to follow. Members agreed it on 2 May 2024 and it merged that month.

items.t: FOCUS #425: ChargeClass (Path 1) - spec updates and associated columns adjustments
items.b: • ChargeClass spec change: • Clarification indicating that Corrections apply specifically to charges invoiced in previous billing periods. • Allowed values reduced to 'Correction'; otherwise, null is expected. ijurica revised ChargeClass so that "Correction" covered charges invoiced in earlier billing periods, with null otherwise, and adjusted nine related columns (#425). flanakin pointed out that corrections within the same billing period also needed handling, which ijurica accepted, then proposed further values in #435. thecloudman requested a wording change. The group approved it on May 9, 2024, and it was merged that month.

items.t: 426-consistency-review-chargecategory-definition-and-description-review
items.b: Parts of the initial definition are no longer applicable since changes to the allowed values list (credit is no longer part of the adjustment category but a separate category) and the introduction of additional columns. It has beeb raised for example, how this column would be used for separate charges that may require special handling from regular usage. kotzenjh's PR, from consistency review item #426, updated the ChargeCategory definition because parts no longer applied after Credit became its own category and new columns were added. flanakin asked to keep a "commonly used" sentence for consistency, and udam-f2 suggested simpler wording. The group agreed it on May 2, 2024, thecloudman approved, and it was merged that month.

items.t: #441 ChargePeriod Start and End spec change
items.b: Based on #441 aqu-erp proposed, based on #441, clarifying ChargePeriodStart and ChargePeriodEnd so they match the boundaries of a charge's effective period, covering usage, time-bound purchases and purchases with no end date. udam-f2 asked whether the glossary and a generic End statement needed updating, and AWS-ZachErdman suggested "incurred" wording and dropping the purchase-specific clause. The group approved it on May 9, 2024, and it was merged that day.

items.t: #436 Add helpful text for identifying records that need to be burned-down
items.b: • Add helpful text to help readers identify purchases eligible for burndown (billed cost >0 & effective cost = 0) • Add that Commitment-Based Discounts are an example of the described scenarios • Minor formatting fixes Pull request #443 resolved #436 by adding text to help readers find purchases needing burn-down, where billed cost is above zero and effective cost is zero. It also named Commitment-Based Discounts as an example and fixed minor formatting. udam-f2 opened it on 8 May 2024. ijurica, cnharris10 and mike-finopsorg approved it, and jpradocueva reported the group's approval on the 9 May call. It was merged on 9 May 2024.

items.t: #441 Clarifications for various Commitment discount scenarios
items.b: Clarification on some Commitment purchase, Unused commitment, and Burndown questions needed PR #444, opened by udam-f2, resolved concerns in #441 about recording commitment purchases and usage. ijurica asked whether the MUST for the purchased ID could become SHOULD when only an order ID was available. udam-f2 wanted the ID to map to the discount, not vague wording. flanakin noted no instance ID exists at purchase, only the order ID. Members agreed on the 9 May 2024 call; it merged that day.

items.t: [EDITORIAL] v1.0 Correct typo in consumedunit.md
items.b: Correct typo in column ID This editorial pull request, opened by TDubovchenko on 14 May 2024, fixed a typo in a column ID in the consumedunit.md file. cnharris10 approved it on 15 May. On 17 May, jpradocueva noted that members had agreed at the 16 May Members meeting to merge it and asked for approval. udam-f2 approved it that day, and the change was merged on 17 May 2024.

items.t: [EDITORIAL] Correct a typographical error in the ChargeCategory.
items.b: Fix a typo. Pull request #461 fixed a typographical error in the ChargeCategory section. jpradocueva opened it on 15 May 2024. cnharris10 approved it that day, and thecloudman approved it on 16 May. jpradocueva then asked udam-f2 and mike-finopsorg for approval, noting that the Members meeting on 16 May had agreed to merge it. udam-f2 approved it on 17 May, and it was merged the same day, 17 May 2024.

items.t: FOCUS dataset consistency review
items.b: Resolving #472 aqu-erp proposed, resolving #472, adopting "FOCUS Dataset" as the single term for a dataset meeting FOCUS compliance criteria, defining it in the glossary and using it instead of billing data or cost data in normative statements. ijurica asked whether custom columns must also be listed in the schema metadata and how to write glossary anchors. Maintainers approved it on August 1, 2024, and it was merged that month.

items.t: [EDITORIAL] Update billingperiodend.md
items.b: I think we have the wrong word at the very beginning. This is supposed to be billing period end. The group agreed it on its 13 June 2024 call and it merged that month.

items.t: [ADMIN] Ratification of v1.0 by FOCUS Steering Committee
items.b: v1.0-cr Pull request #486 sought Steering Committee ratification of the v1.0 candidate releases after a 30-day IPR review was completed on 11 June 2024 with no exclusion notices. Editorial fixes #459, #460, #461 and #470 had already merged into v1.1, while #480 and #483 were pending. #484 applied all of them on a branch from the 1.0-cr tag. udam-f2 and mike-finopsorg approved, and the pull request merged on 14 June 2024.

items.t: FOCUS #497: SkuPriceDetails column
items.b: Introduction of _KeyValueFormat_ columns _SkuDetails_ and _SkuPriceDetails_ to capture properties of a SKU ID and SKU Price ID, respectively. kk09v opened this PR to add two key-value columns, SkuDetails and SkuPriceDetails, describing properties of a SKU and of a SKU price (issue #497). ijurica asked for sample records across pricing models, and robmartin33 worried that excluding properties already held in other columns would hurt compatibility, so a MAY clause was added. TF-2 voted for PascalCase keys, though flanakin noted JSON usually uses camel case, and in August 2024 directed merging the two into one SkuPriceDetails column; flanakin and thecloudman preferred the name SKU Details. flanakin asked for SHOULD rather than MUST on consistent properties, fearing it would block support, but maintainers kept MUST because "no data is better than bad data". #530 covered charges without a SkuPriceId. Members approved it on 5 September 2024 and it merged.

items.t: FOCUS #491: ChargeClass - 'Corrections' as a result of late arriving charge records
items.b: Specification and supporting content update. ijurica opened a pull request on 11 July 2024 to update ChargeClass for late-arriving costs, responding to #491. It lets corrections cover the whole invoiced billing period. cnharris10 approved on 12 July 2024. A 25 July 2024 members' call set action items to clarify the normative text. The Maintainers' meeting agreed to the change on 1 August 2024, and udam-f2 approved on 2 August 2024. Merged 3 August 2024.

items.t: [EDITORIAL] Reclassify ConsumedUnit as Dimension instead of Metric
items.b: Correct ConsumedUnit column type to Dimension from Metric (similar to PricingUnit) because it is an attribute of how the consumption is measured and is not able to have mathematical operations applied to it. Pull request #506, opened by kk09v on 11 July 2024, proposed moving the ConsumedUnit column from Metric to Dimension, like PricingUnit. The reason was that ConsumedUnit describes how consumption is measured and cannot take mathematical operations. cnharris10, rileyjenk and udam-f2 approved between 12 and 15 July 2024 with no written comments. jpradocueva recorded Members' group approval on 18 July 2024, and the change was merged that day.

items.t: Improvements To Metadata
items.b: Improvements to schema metadata including examples. rileyjenk's pull request improved the schema metadata section and added examples of schema changes, with TF-3 asking for more scenarios such as column removal, fixing a wrong schema and provider version changes, and for example folder structures to be marked as conceptual. Reviewers left many editorial suggestions. cnharris10 asked for consistent ACME naming and a standard examples path; udam-f2 asked whether fixing an erroneous schema should bump the version, and rileyjenk said only the metadata object was wrong, not the schema. ahullah asked about the ProviderVersion format, which rileyjenk said is unspecified, though SemVer is suggested. shawnalpay asked to align UUID and GUID and to review it as a PDF in context, and ijurica suggested stronger SchemaId uniqueness. Members approved it on 12 September and it merged in September 2024.

items.t: Dedicated SKU column (for issue #495)
items.b: Lead Maintainer: Zach ### Documents: • Folder #495 : SKU Properties & Providers Alignment by Zach moved to folder #495 • Document: SKU Details from Providers (FOCUS) • Spreadsheet: 24.08.08 - Alternative-Column-Names-for-UsageType • PR #516 Initial Draft of UsageType • Approval date: Sep 05 AWS-ZachErdman's pull request, tied to #495, added a dedicated column describing what a SKU meters, first drafted as UsageType. Through TF-2, maintainers and members calls from August 2024, the group used naming spreadsheets and polls, settling on SKU Meter, with a revote that included alternatives from flanakin, who did not want the name to look chosen by Microsoft. ijurica wanted the column focused on the SKU and its nullability aligned with SkuId; AWS-ZachErdman said not every AWS SKU has a meter name, so values should not be forced. cnharris10 and ahullah noted that mixing coded and readable strings was a problem for a longer-term solution, not a blocker. udam-f2 asked for supporting content, which was added. Members approved it on September 19, 2024, and it merged that month.

items.t: FOCUS #404: Service Subcategory
items.b: Introduction of column _ServiceSubcategory_ underneath the existing column _ServiceCategory_ to capture finer grouping detail for Services. For #404, shawnalpay proposed a ServiceSubcategory column giving finer groupings beneath each ServiceCategory. udam-f2 asked for short, non-marketing descriptions and questioned names such as Language AI, later renamed NLP; shawnalpay rewrote Networking as a model and applied that style elsewhere. Whether the column should be mandatory or optional was debated without a clear result in the thread. Answering a quoted suggestion to keep the categories in a separate repository, flanakin argued they must stay in the spec so versioned data stays consistent, and warned against frequent changes. After sessions with flanakin, shawnalpay added subcategories such as AI Platform and Endpoint Management and renamed several networking and storage ones, while the placement of search services was still being debated. Members approved it in September 2024 and it was merged.

items.t: Capacity Reservation Proposal for ID & Status
items.b: Proposal based on Action Items, TF-3, Aug 16: TF3-[#397] George will draft a PR for the new “ID” and “Status” columns related to ODCRs.; TF3-[#397] to consult AWS for further guidance on the feasibility of providing a CR ID in the billing data. Pull request #523, by gparker-at-sf, came out of #397 and proposed Capacity Reservation ID and Capacity Reservation Status columns. The main dispute was how firmly to require the ID: cnharris10 suggested SHOULD because AWS would not initially provide values, flanakin preferred MUST, and AWS-ZachErdman opposed MUST as unproven and wanted conformance possible without labelling used reservation charges. ijurica proposed requiring a status only when an ID is present, which AWS-ZachErdman endorsed. cnharris10's global uniqueness suggestion met the objection that other ID columns don't enforce it. A generic glossary entry for capacity reservation was added, and udam-f2 asked for supporting content explaining the SHOULD. Members approved it on 5 September 2024 and it merged.

items.t: Rename all mentions on "commitment-based discount" (or similar) to "commitment discount" (or similar) to match updated iteration of term in FinOps Terminology page.
items.b: Rename all mentions on "commitment-based discount" (or similar) to "commitment discount" (or similar) to match updated iteration of term in FinOps Terminology page: https://www.finops.org/assets/terminology/#commitment-discounts cnharris10 renamed "commitment-based discount" and similar phrases to "commitment discount" throughout the spec to match the FinOps terminology page. The change was editorial. shawnalpay approved and suggested also scrubbing terms such as usage-based, spend-based and tier-based. Members approved it on 22 August 2024 and it merged.

items.t: Commitment Discount Appendix
items.b: An appendix detailing how various commitment discount purchases and usage records are modeled through various examples. cnharris10 proposed an appendix showing, through examples, how commitment discount purchases and usage appear in FOCUS data. shawnalpay asked for a generic partial payment option rather than a half-upfront one, Recurring in place of Monthly, and explanations of terms such as spend-based for new readers; cnharris10 accepted Recurring but kept the definition consistent with the columns and argued that the same logic would require defining many other terms. shawnalpay also wanted a size flexibility example, which cnharris10 agreed to work toward later. ijurica preferred All-Upfront, No-Upfront and Partial-Upfront naming, and udam-f2 approved while noting missing glossary links. Task force 2 asked for partial instead of hybrid, Members approved it on September 19, remaining fixes were left to the consistency review, and it merged in September 2024.

items.t: #503a - Update SkuPriceId per SkuPriceDetails
items.b: This change is dependent on #503 being merged as it links to SkuPriceDetails. This change to SkuPriceId solves for a case where a provider does not have a SkuPriceId but wants to include SkuPriceDetails. This case was introduced when there was a change in scope of #503 to not include SkuDetails. kk09v's PR, dependent on #503, let providers without a SkuPriceId repeat SkuId as SkuPriceId when they include SkuPriceDetails, and reformatted the requirements as bullets. Task Force 2 asked for refinements and an offline discussion of edge cases. flanakin approved but asked that reformatting and content edits not be mixed in one PR. Members approved it on September 5, 2024, and it was merged.

items.t: FOCUS #532: PricingCategory update - Classify commitment discount purchase records as Standard instead of Committed
items.b: Lead Maintainer: Irena For #532, ijurica proposed classing commitment discount purchase rows as Standard rather than Committed in PricingCategory, by adding an exception for purchases of the commitment itself. flanakin suggested dropping the link to CommitmentDiscountId so other purchase commitments fit, and cnharris10 suggested limiting Committed to usage charges; ijurica questioned whether commitments could never apply to purchases. Members approved it in September 2024, with ijurica to update the phrasing to match.

items.t: WI #634: Commitment Discount Flexibility Appendix
items.b: An appendix detailing how various commitment discount purchases and usage records with and without commitment discount flexibility are modeled through various examples. cnharris10 opened this PR to add an appendix of examples showing how commitment discount purchases and usage are modelled with and without flexibility. flanakin warned that calling it "size flexibility" would constrain later naming, so cnharris10 renamed it. At an October 2024 call, members agreed to keep it for v1.2 under a backfilled work item. rileyjenk and UdamDewaraja requested changes, asking that it move to the examples section and that the JSON samples become externally stored CSV files; cnharris10 split it into separate example files but preferred to leave format conversion to a later consistency review. ijurica asked for appendix links to sit outside normative requirements and for consistent column names and unit price terms. Members approved it on 27 March 2025, and it was merged that month.

items.t: Fix CDStatus column reference
items.b: flanakin opened #538 on 3 September 2024 to fix a wrong column name reference in the CommitmentDiscountStatus specification, with no functional change. The suggested edit revised the column definition. cnharris10 approved on 4 September 2024, and udam-f2 and rileyjenk approved on 12 September. jpradocueva reported that the Members approved it on the 12 September call, and the pull request was merged that day.

items.t: Fix capacityreservation*, sku* build issues

Adds linter correction across all capacityreservation*, sku* columns: • `-` --> `*` bullets • spaces around lists cnharris10's PR was purely mechanical: it made the working_draft branch build by adding the capacity reservation columns to columns.mdpp and fixing linter issues, such as bullet style and spacing, in the capacity reservation and SKU column files. There was no content change or discussion, and it was merged in September 2024.

items.b: "Commitment Flexibility" -> "Commitment Discount Flexibility" This editorial pull request, #545, opened by cnharris10 on 24 September 2024, aimed to standardize the term "commitment discount flexibility" by replacing "Commitment Flexibility" throughout the specification. A TF-1 call action item from 24 September asked cnharris10 to make sure the team reviewed it. udam-f2 approved it on 25 September, and jpradocueva recorded approval on the 26 September call. It was merged on 27 September 2024. No disagreement was recorded.

items.t: FOCUS #547: Consistency Review - Standardize column specs for correction charges
items.b: Standardize the column specifications, i.e. allow nulls in the case of corrections for all columns except cost metrics, and explicitly define value ranges for all metrics, for the following columns: PricingUnit; ConsumedUnit; CommitmentDiscountUnit; PricingQuantity Pull request #549, by ijurica, set out to standardize how columns handle correction charges, allowing nulls for corrections except in cost metrics and defining value ranges. Because of deadlines, scope was cut to ConsumedUnit and ConsumedQuantity, with other columns left as they were for 1.1. cnharris10 proposed simpler requirements and putting 'usage' in the descriptions, and ijurica reworked them. Members approved it on 3 October 2024 and it merged.

items.t: Commitment Discount {Quantity,Unit} - Consistency review edits
items.b: Adds correction-based logic and reduces duplication of clauses Pull request #550, by cnharris10, edited CommitmentDiscountQuantity and CommitmentDiscountUnit during the 1.1 consistency review to add correction handling and cut duplicated clauses. ijurica set out what the columns should require for regular and correction charges and favoured a restructured Option B, while cnharris10 preferred Option A's minimal edits, arguing that months of approved work should not be reworked. ijurica then offered an Option C keeping the original flow as bullets. At TF-1 on 1 October 2024 the group agreed to defer readability improvements to a later 1.x release. ijurica also spotted that CommitmentDiscountUnit lacked the correction allowance given to the quantity column; the group backed ijurica's changes, cnharris10 integrated them, and Members approved the PR on 3 October 2024.

items.t: Service Subcategory language inconsistency fixes
items.b: Minor inconsistency where we're using Optional for ChargeSubCategory when it should be using the "Recommended" term as that is consistent with ChargeFrequency and the pattern we outlined in 1.0. This inconsistency shows up in the normative paragraph and in the content constraints. udam-f2 proposed ServiceSubcategory wording fixes agreed at a September 2024 consistency review meeting. ijurica suggested stating that each subcategory has exactly one parent ServiceCategory, asked whether FOCUS should define that parent, and suggested referencing the ServiceName column; arrarama asked how services that depend on other services would fit. shawnalpay approved, and members approved it on October 3, 2024, when it was merged.

items.t: Adding Usability Constraints for Aggregation
items.b: Adding Usability Constraints for Aggregation, to support commitment utilization calculation ahullah added notes on aggregation to cost, price and quantity columns to support commitment utilization calculations. ijurica said ConsumedQuantity had no double-counting issue, so that section was removed, and cnharris10 reworded the unit price notes to say values should not be summed. Members made the constraints advisory rather than mandatory and approved it on October 3, 2024. It merged in October 2024.

items.t: Editorial changes to columns names and ids
