items.t: WI #314: `SKU ID`, `SKU Price ID` and `SKU Price Details` clarification
items.b: This PR provides clarification on the specifications, purpose, and guidance for the following columns: SKU ID,; SKU Price ID,; and SKU Price Details, ijurica's PR for #314 clarified the SkuId, SkuPriceId and SkuPriceDetails columns. ijurica asked whether the presence conditions could be merged and when SkuId may equal SkuPriceId, and recorded TF-2 assumptions that SkuPriceId should exclude variable pricing properties and have one parent SkuId. cnharris10 requested changes, asking whether the edits let providers do as they pleased (flanakin said the intent was unchanged) and objecting to the single-parent rule with an RDS size-flexibility example. UdamDewaraja and ljadvey opposed requiring one SkuId across single and multi-AZ offerings; mike-finopsorg and rileyjenk agreed those lines went too far, and flanakin deferred several to a future release. UdamDewaraja questioned typing SkuPriceDetails as a String, and kk09v moved its requirements into #683. Members approved it on April 3, 2025, and it merged in April 2025.

items.t: WI #619: `SKU Price Details` preferred keys
items.b: Although the SKU Price Details column provides relevant SKU and SKU Price properties, and the SKU Meter helps practitioners understand the functionalities being metered by different SKUs, the existing FOCUS specification still lacks a user-friendly approach to presenting other prominent SKU properties (such as SKU terms, tiered pricing details, SKU regions/locations, size, etc.), which are essential for understanding… Pull request #683, by kk09v, defined preferred keys for the SKU Price Details column (#619), narrowed to that column at shawnalpay's request. kk09v added an F_ prefix for FOCUS-defined keys and tightened them to MUST, but flanakin strongly objected that it made FOCUS feel second-class and withheld approval; shawnalpay agreed and suggested a reserved list instead. After a working group vote, provider-defined keys took an x_ prefix instead. aws-letianfeng requested changes over what InputOutput covered and how burstable 'up to' values work, leading to separate network and disk properties and a baseline-value rule. Other threads debated naming such as CoreCount and Iops, null versus empty objects, and reverting the data type to JSON. Members approved it on 3 April 2025 and it merged.

items.t: WI #643: Specification Change Guidelines
items.b: FinOps practitioners who adopt FOCUS will need to upgrade to new versions over time as they are released in order to be able to receive the new features provided. However, upgrading to a new version from an old version becomes challenging if, between the new and previous version, there are changes requirement dictating how data must appear in a given column. rileyjenk proposed guidelines for how the specification handles additions, deprecations, renames and removals, with a structured changelog and metadata properties for deprecated and previous column names. shawnalpay briefly returned it to draft in March 2025 until a TODO section was written. flanakin suggested grouping changelog entries by area and listing distinct process steps, which rileyjenk took up, but held back approval wanting a broader Status property instead of the Deprecated flag; rileyjenk argued that would turn metadata into a transactional record. rileyjenk also rejected flanakin's view that change details were too much for the changelog. mohitamzn asked about version types and support for older versions, which rileyjenk left to providers, and aws-letianfeng noted one column could replace several. Members approved it on April 3 and it merged in April 2025.

items.t: WI #615: `Invoice ID` definition and supporting content
items.b: Discussion space for invoice ID to facilitate how we make available invoice ID in FOCUS data thecloudman opened this pull request for #615 to define an InvoiceId column and supporting content. After talking with rileyjenk, thecloudman added notes proposing a separate invoice ID table mapping invoices to rows, so providers would not need to update every row when an invoice is issued. cnharris10 asked whether the wording made the column conditional; mike-finopsorg read it as present, and null when no invoice applies. udam-f2 worried that providers such as GCP cannot restate exported data and found the uniqueness wording too strong. ijurica proposed many normative rewrites, and ljadvey and UdamDewaraja debated saying issued invoices. thecloudman dropped a rule tying each invoice to one billing account and added an editor's note on unresolved credit handling. Members approved it on February 27, 2025, and it was merged.

items.t: Fix 2 Bugs
items.b: Fix 2 Bugs: 1. Correct column names: `{Billing,Charge}Period{Start,End}Date` --> `{Billing,Charge}Period{Start,End}`; 2. On-demand charge should have both a positive BilledCost and EffectiveCost cnharris10 fixed two bugs: period column names wrongly ending in Date, and an on-demand charge example that should have positive BilledCost and EffectiveCost. ijurica pointed out a sentence that contradicted itself for lack of a "not", plus grammatical slips in the commitment discount text. shawnalpay approved, Members approved it on 30 January, and it merged in January 2025.

items.t: WI #540: Ensure all user-defined Tags are encapsulated within the Tags column
items.b: This change address Issue #540 and encapsulates the updates to multiple tag schemes in the documentation, decided by a previous survey among the FinOps community. beau-nelford-anglepoint's PR implemented #540, putting all user-defined tags in the Tags column and setting rules for providers with multiple tag schemes, following an earlier community survey. cnharris10 answered aws-letianfeng's question about tag keys containing "/" by saying providers must reserve any prefix they define, as AWS does with "aws:". ijurica suggested handling provider tag prefixes in metadata as part of #540. flanakin asked whether labels and categories clearly count as tags, wanted a MUST NOT with an exception split in two, and proposed requiring prefixes to be published in metadata; cnharris10 defended the valueless-tag exception and kept publication open-ended. kk09v confirmed exactly one user-defined scheme stays unprefixed. UdamDewaraja and shawnalpay fixed casing and punctuation. Members approved it on February 27, 2025, and it was merged.

items.t: WI #616: Proposed change to billed cost to prevent double counting billed cost betwen vendor and marketplace FOCUS records.
items.b: The FOCUS specification, so far, has chiefly been engineered to support cost and usage data as it is generated by cloud service providers (CSP) such as AWS, Azure, GCP, and OCI. rileyjenk proposed BilledCost changes (#616) to prevent double counting between vendor and marketplace FOCUS records, tying BilledCost sums to invoices from the invoice issuer. Reviewers debated the wording: cnharris10 suggested it SHOULD match and MUST NOT exceed payable invoices, while flanakin urged being ambitious and letting data generators document coverage gaps. thecloudman proposed saying "finalized" invoices rather than listing estimate invoices, and ijurica asked whether such charges should be zero and whether naming the invoice issuer added anything. UdamDewaraja found combining billing period, billing account and InvoiceId problematic. After TF-2 on March 27, ijurica suggested matching the sum for a given InvoiceId to that invoice's payable amount. shawnalpay asked rileyjenk to resolve open threads before the members vote. Members approved it on April 3, 2025, and it merged that month.

items.t: WI #557: Normative Requirements Refinement - Part 1
items.b: Updating normative requirements for a subset of FOCUS columns in line with the attached FOCUS Columns Normative Guidelines. The remaining columns are addressed in a separate PR (#798) For #557 and FOCUS 1.2, ijurica set out guidelines for writing column normative requirements and rewrote a first set of columns to match, with the rest in #798; reviewers were asked to flag unintended changes. flanakin questioned dropping "globally" from globally unique identifiers, doubted providers could guarantee unique billing account names, a point thecloudman echoed, and found "exclusive ending bound" unclear. shawnalpay resisted changing requirement strength within a consistency review, keeping ChargeDescription length a SHOULD. qquigley asked why both SHOULD and RECOMMENDED appeared; ijurica said RECOMMENDED marked presence rules tied to feature levels. smokemonster99 queried renamed column references, which ijurica said followed the editorial guidelines. Unresolved points went to a list of discussion topics. Members approved it in March 2025 and it was merged.

items.t: WI #557: Normative Requirements Refinement - Part 2
items.b: Updating normative requirements for a subset of FOCUS columns in line with the FOCUS Columns Normative Guidelines. This was the second part of ijurica's rewrite of column normative requirements under the #557 guidelines, with #787 covering the other columns. ijurica flagged deliberate changes already agreed in TF-1: fixing CommitmentDiscountQuantity's positive-only value range as a bug, rewording EffectiveCost rules for unused commitments, and aligning nullability for quantity and unit pairs. flanakin proposed EffectiveCost wording linking purchase and usage costs, and answered thecloudman's doubt about tax examples. SkuPriceDetails was declared a String with key-value format, and another SkuPriceDetails change was reverted after UdamDewaraja raised a concern, with follow-up logged as #855. cnharris10 and ijurica reworked how the Tags requirements were grouped, and smokemonster99 caught typos. Members approved it in April 2025 and it was merged.

items.t: WI #643: SemVer Usage clarification from Maintainers Aug 19 2024 meeting in the spec
items.b: FinOps practitioners who adopt FOCUS will need to upgrade to new versions over time as they are released in order to be able to receive the new features provided. However, upgrading to a new version from an old version becomes challenging if, between the new and previous version, there are changes requirement dictating how data must appear in a given column. rileyjenk added to the spec a clarification on how FOCUS uses Semantic Versioning, agreed at an August 2024 maintainers meeting but never written in (#643). shawnalpay suggested README wording. Members approved it on March 27, 2025, and it was merged that month.

items.t: WI #616: Addition of four columns related to `Pricing Currency`
items.b: This pull request replaces #799, which proposed adding two columns `PricingCurrency` and `PricingToBillingExchangeRate` to the FOCUS specification. The issues with that PR as expressed async in Slack and reiterated during the Mar 14 TF3 call were: Expression of existing Unit Price columns (e.g. shawnalpay proposed four columns for prices set in a virtual or different currency (PricingCurrency, PricingCurrencyEffectiveCost, PricingCurrencyListUnitPrice and PricingCurrencyContractedUnitPrice), replacing #799 because some members rejected redefining existing unit price columns; existing columns stayed unchanged. cnharris10 supported the aim but feared moving too fast without modelled data, so mike-finopsorg shared a sample sheet. thecloudman asked whether a priced cost column duplicated Billed Cost, and ijurica proposed simpler presence conditions. daviddinhgcp proposed separate token and local currency columns; mike-finopsorg replied that conversion works the same for national and virtual currencies and extra columns would widen the spec. On March 31, 2025 maintainers struck the exchange rate column and deferred exchange rates to a future release. Members approved the PR on April 3, 2025, and it was merged that day.

items.t: AI #909: SkuPriceDetails req. fix -  prefer FOCUS-defined over Provider-defined properties

In July ijurica adopted kk09v's rewording and reverted a SHOULD-to-MUST change after kk09v objected. Members approved it on September 4, 2025.

items.t: AI #874: Alignment with column normative reqs - BilledCost and PricingCurrencyEffectiveCost
items.b: The scope of this PR is limited to editorial changes to the BilledCost and PricingCurrencyContractedUnitPrice columns. It includes: Reordering of normative requirements; Adding a few links to glossary terms and columns in the spec

items.t: AI #913: Editorial Adjustments (Best Effort) – Links and Formatting
items.b: The scope of this PR is limited to editorial adjustments (best effort), primarily focusing on column specs - adding links to glossary terms, columns, etc., and aligning formatting with editorial guidelines. ijurica's pull request (#913) made best-effort editorial adjustments, mainly to column specs, adding links to glossary terms and columns and aligning formatting with the editorial guidelines. shawnalpay approved it with one small suggestion on Charge Category. Members approved it on April 17, 2025, and it merged.

items.t: FRs #1055/1073: Refactor Provider Identification, Host Provider, Invoice Issuer
items.b: We've received feedback from multiple sources indicating that our column names and definitions for Provider and Publisher are confusing. Additionally, we want to add support for vendors that host their systems on other providers, as reporting this information is important for cost analysis. rileyjenk opened this pull request in June 2025 for #1055 and #1073, after feedback that the Provider and Publisher columns were confusing. It deprecated PublisherName and ProviderName and added Service Provider and Host Provider columns, the latter for vendors running on other providers' infrastructure. Because this was FOCUS's first deprecation, shawnalpay asked for a summary and a link to the deprecation guidelines. flanakin objected that renaming Provider would force customers to change their queries and suggested calling the new column Host; rileyjenk replied that Host alone was ambiguous and naming was better fixed now. Reviewers also debated whether a FinOps vendor is a data generator, with editorial follow-ups moved to #1226 and #1336. Members approved it on October 16, 2025, and it was merged that month.

items.t: FR #1082: Clarify requirements to cover all invoiced charges in FOCUS datasets
items.b: Introducing an invoice handling attribute that incorporates feedback given on draft doc associated with [FR] Clarify requirements to cover all invoiced charges in FOCUS datasets. Also added invoice_handling.md to the attributes.mdpp file in alphanumeric order. Fixes #1082 Matt-Cowsert proposed an invoice handling attribute for FR #1082, requiring FOCUS datasets to cover every invoiced charge. shawnalpay asked for it to be applied to every affected column and for Invoice ID to cover all charges; flanakin objected that one billing period can have several invoices, so the original wording returned with a clarification. UdamDewaraja wanted prepaid usage statements included, warned invoices cannot be expected to use FOCUS terms, and argued the core rule was that totals per invoice ID match the invoice. flanakin asked where the line lay; ijurica floated limiting it to IT costs, and shawnalpay and ijurica proposed scoping it to invoices issued to a billing account. Task Force 3 struck duplicative requirements. Members approved it on September 25, 2025; it merged the next day.

items.t: FR #1090: Add multi dataset support to FOCUS spec layout
items.b: This pull request updates the repo layout to support multiple FOCUS datasets Pull request #1337, by mike-finopsorg, reorganized the repository layout to support multiple FOCUS datasets (#1090). shawnalpay requested that the existing dataset be called Cost and Usage rather than the FOCUS dataset, since any FOCUS dataset should count as one. flanakin objected that duplicating columns per dataset would not scale; shawnalpay replied that maintainers had reached consensus on it in August. Members approved it on 28 August 2025 and it merged.

items.t: FR #976: Add support for contract commitments
items.b: This PR adds: • A new column called `Contract Applied` to the `Cost and Usage` dataset. This allows practitioners to see how their cost and usage applies to the progress of their various contract commitments. • A net-new dataset called `Contract Commitment`. This allows practitioners to: • Analyze and aggregate their cost and usage by various contract commitment properties. For #976, shawnalpay proposed a ContractApplied JSON column linking each cost row to the contract commitments it counts toward, plus a new Contract Commitment dataset describing those commitments. kk09v argued for a true JSON object format with a defined schema, which led to #1383 and kk09v's #1462, and ijurica wanted custom properties declared in metadata. After flanakin asked how several contracts could apply to one charge, ContractId moved inside the array. cnharris10 questioned having both type and description columns, and marc-perreaut's idea for handling values redundant with other columns was weighed against added complexity. Maintainers let data generators omit inapplicable cost, quantity or unit values, and BillingCurrency replaced a separate currency column. shawnalpay offered to defer ContractCommitmentType to #1459. Members approved it in September 2025 and it was merged.

items.t: FR #966: Add recency to metadata
items.b: Practitioners want to understand how up-to-date FOCUS data is and how complete. rileyjenk proposed adding recency metadata under feature request #966, with properties for time sectors, completeness and last-updated dates, and examples for datasets that do and do not change over time. shawnalpay asked for a more specific name than Complete, which rileyjenk agreed to fix. Matt-Cowsert requested changes, mostly cleanup and tighter wording, preferred the terms time-series and non-time-series, and asked whether the JSON examples were meant to be prescriptive; rileyjenk replied that metadata structure had traditionally been non-prescriptive and that a should would have to become a must everywhere. Matt-Cowsert then approved, and ijurica approved while noting editorial items for the 1.3 consistency review. It moved to Member review in September 2025, was approved at the October 2 Members' meeting and merged in October 2025.

items.t: FR #1056: Create json_object_format.md
items.b: Reviving the Object format previously proposed by @flanakin because multiple FRs have had considerations to use a complex JSON object, which is not compatible with key-value format. kk09v revived an earlier object format idea from flanakin for #1056, because several feature requests needed complex JSON objects that the key-value format could not hold. kk09v renamed it from JSON Object Format to Object Format, since the data type already says JSON, and explored how to describe object shapes, finding RFC 8927 useful but not very human-readable. In maintainer meetings, ijurica asked that custom provider object columns carry public documentation or schema metadata, which kk09v added, and the group settled a nesting limit, worded as SHOULD NOT exceed 3 levels. A straw poll was planned on keeping JTD schemas inside column definitions, which ijurica favoured. qquigley raised wording points. shawnalpay approved, and it was approved at the September 18 members' meeting and merged in September 2025.

items.t: FR #956: Provider-calculated split cost allocation
items.b: Added columns: • AllocatedResourceId • AllocatedResourceName • AllocatedMethodId • AllocatedTags • AllocatedMethodDetails kk09v and qquigley proposed provider-calculated split cost allocation (#956), adding AllocatedResourceId, AllocatedResourceName, AllocatedMethodId, AllocatedTags and a details column, plus an attribute, a supported feature and glossary terms. TF-2 reshaped the details column into an array of objects with a JSON schema, later named AllocatedMethodDetails, and moved the method into its own column. jpradocueva asked that requirements target dataset entities rather than providers, and rileyjenk objected to requiring providers to support a feature, so kk09v softened the wording. flanakin questioned the term "allocated method" and whether ratios were fractions or percentages, and Cosmos DB cases went to #1479. shawnalpay pressed for a change summary, a fixed PDF build and resolved conflicts. Members approved it on 25 September 2025 and it merged.

items.t: FR #1090: Associate attributes with datasets
items.b: We need to finesse the spec to associate specific attributes with specific datasets. shawnalpay proposed this for #1090 because the spec said attributes applied to all FOCUS datasets, which would be inaccurate once more existed; it associated every current attribute with the Cost and Usage dataset. flanakin questioned a line on when datasets are required, and shawnalpay explained only Cost and Usage is always required. ijurica suggested more dataset glossary terms. Members approved it on September 11, 2025, and it was merged.

items.t: FR #962: Adding Correction Handling Examples
items.b: This PR introduces the Correction Handling Examples section (part of the FOCUS appendix), including scenarios covering: Corrections to open billing periods (current and previous open periods); Corrections to previously closed billing periods ijurica proposed a Correction Handling Examples appendix section (feature request #962) covering corrections to current and previous open billing periods and to closed periods, using Overwrite and Append delivery and Replacement, Delta and Ledger correction styles. Task force 1 asked for a scenario overview, then in October 2025 agreed to postpone the work, and shawnalpay closed the pull request. It resumed for 1.4, with ijurica updating the terminology in January 2026. caligo-erik flagged repeated links, and pydi-aws questioned assigning corrections to the next open billing period rather than the original, which shawnalpay agreed to revisit in task force 1. Once the examples became CSV files, shawnalpay found many errors, including swapped Delta and Ledger data, which ijurica fixed. Members approved it on April 2 and it merged in April 2026.

items.t: FR #1055: Standardize column display names by adding 'Name' suffix
items.b: • Updated display names for 3 columns to match their Column IDs by adding " Name" suffix • InvoiceIssuerName: "Invoice Issuer" → "Invoice Issuer Name" • ProviderName: "Provider" → "Provider Name" • PublisherName: "Publisher" → "Publisher Name" • Updated references throughout documentation to use standardized display names flanakin added "Name" to the display names of InvoiceIssuerName, ProviderName and PublisherName so they matched their column IDs (#1055). shawnalpay asked for a full scrub of other references and worried about overlap with #1139, which would deprecate Publisher; ijurica asked that descriptions begin with the column name. Members approved it on October 2, 2025, and it was merged that month.

items.t: FR #966: Improving dataset metadata
items.b: Practitioners want to understand how up-to-date FOCUS data is and how complete. rileyjenk opened this pull request for FR #966 to let data generators declare dataset instances, each with an ID and a name, after finding the recency work could not cleanly handle a generator supplying several outputs of the same FOCUS dataset. ijurica and rileyjenk went back and forth on what to call the dataset reference property, and rileyjenk kept free-form instance names in the examples and noted that FOCUS version already sits in schema metadata. udam-stitcher asked for crisper definitions separating a FOCUS dataset from a dataset instance, and shawnalpay's request to move prose out of the mdpp file was deferred to consistency review. Matt-Cowsert requested editorial changes, then approved. Members approved it on 2 October and it merged in October 2025, with a terminology consistency pass added to #1380.

items.t: FR #1070: Clarify use of "period" vs "duration" vs "term"
items.b: When authoring the spec, we have been inconsistent in our use of the following words: `period`; `duration`; `term` shawnalpay proposed using "period" consistently for lengths of time, replacing "term" and "duration", because #1350's contract commitments needed "term" to mean a contract provision. aws-jrmarks and robmartin33 asked to keep a Term glossary entry that points readers to Period, which shawnalpay added. ijurica suggested defining period as a time window, and SatyaVandrangi1 asked to avoid the word "condition". Members approved it and it merged in October 2025.

items.t: FR #962: Add Correction Handling and Delivery Handling attributes and refactor Invoice Handling
items.b: Both cases confirm these status columns were intended to also represent the state of the underlying delivered data across the three FOCUS datasets (BillingPeriod, InvoiceDetail, CostAndUsage), a role the original definitions did not explicitly articulate. shawnalpay opened this pull request for #962 to add Correction Handling and Delivery Handling attributes and rework Invoice Handling. In October 2025 maintainers closed it, deferring the work until an Invoice dataset existed (#1500), but work resumed in 2026. The final version defined Replacement, Delta and Ledger correction styles and Overwrite and Append delivery, and moved Invoice Handling to an appendix. Matt-Cowsert recorded a decision not to rename the ChargeClass value "Correction", since that would be a breaking change. rileyjenk and pydi-aws warned that limits on correcting closed billing periods could deter vendors, while ijurica held that data must be accurate before being marked final; rileyjenk and ijurica converged on separating invoice status from data delivery status. Members approved it on April 2, 2026, and it was merged that month.

items.t: Process #1380: Address trivial consistency issues
items.b: This PR is a grab-bag of very simple changes as part of 1.3 consistency review. Mostly editorial: shawnalpay bundled simple consistency fixes for the 1.3 consistency review under #1380. shawnalpay asked whether reordering requirements would change their conformance IDs, and the Maintainers confirmed in October 2025 that the IDs would stay durable. ijurica contributed edits to the dataset overview. Members approved it without objections in October 2025.

items.t: AI #1517: Reduce nesting from 3 to 2 levels in CommitmentDiscountQuantity
items.b: This PR simplifies the structure of several CommitmentDiscountQuantity requirements by reducing their nesting from three to two levels, without introducing any material changes. ijurica's editorial PR reduced the nesting of several CommitmentDiscountQuantity requirements from three levels to two, with no material change, on the assumption that this suited conformance work better. Matt-Cowsert approved after a TF-2 review, saying it simplified the null check, and jpradocueva approved pending a check against #1209. Members approved it on 16 October 2025 and it merged.

items.t: AI #1516: Address ambiguous normative requirement for EffectiveCost
items.b: This PR clarifies an ambiguous EffectiveCost requirement. The original wording: This phrasing is ambiguous due to the use of "may not", which can be interpreted either as a possibility ("might not match") or as a soft prohibition ("is not allowed to match"). ijurica proposed rewording the EffectiveCost requirement because the phrase may not match could mean either might not match or must not match. The replacement says the sums may differ, with no intended material change. shawnalpay first opposed the change, preferring a broader fix through #982, but reversed after discussion with mike-finopsorg. rileyjenk also approved. Members approved it on 16 October 2025, and it merged on 17 October 2025.

items.t: AI #1520: Address editorial refinements to Metadata specification
items.b: This PR implements a set of editorial, definitional, and structural refinements to the Metadata specification including: Application of editorial clean-ups and consistency improvements across object and property descriptions.; Minor refinements to several definitions and descriptive texts for improved precision.; Consistent usage of key terms such as “Dataset ID” and “Dataset Instance ID.”; Minimal reordering of top-… ijurica opened this editorial pull request on the Metadata specification: tidier wording, consistent use of Dataset ID and Dataset Instance ID, top-level elements reordered by dependency, and normative requirements turned from paragraphs into bullet lists, without changing intent. shawnalpay added revisions and noted inconsistent underscores in file names, proposing a separate future action item. ijurica committed bullet-list rewrites for several objects without waiting for feedback, to speed review, and asked why Recency was MAY rather than SHOULD; rileyjenk replied that Recency is not required in this version. Wrapping some examples in square brackets was left to rileyjenk or the next release, and ijurica said a metadata layout overview was planned for the next release. Members approved it without objection and it merged in October 2025.

items.t: AI #1512: Remove use of markdown directly within .mdpp files
items.b: This PR completes AI #1512 by removing all markdown directly included with .mdpp files and adds it to an overview .md file. shawnalpay moved all Markdown content out of the .mdpp build files into separate overview .md files, under action item #1512, leaving the metadata folder out of scope. The change was mechanical: ijurica spotted a broken appendix table of contents and wrong file extensions, which shawnalpay fixed. Matt-Cowsert approved, noting it separated build instructions from content. Members approved it on October 16 and it merged in October 2025.

items.t: AI #1522: Renaming recency last update date to recency last updated
items.b: The table below lists all Date/Time fields defined in the Metadata section. Given that the last five are newly introduced, their naming (suffix) should be aligned for consistency. rileyjenk renamed the recency metadata property RecencyLastUpdateDate to RecencyLastUpdated under action item #1522. ijurica shared naming conventions being drafted in #1533, including past-participle suffixes for state indicators and an At suffix for timestamps. shawnalpay requested fixes to a file name, the requirement wording and a broken example link, then approved. Members approved it on October 30 and it merged in October 2025.

items.t: AI #1508: Update Requirements headers for allocatedresourceid.md through chargeperiodend.md
items.b: Requirements subheader Mostly mechanical: davidearney updated the Requirements headers in column files from allocatedresourceid.md to chargeperiodend.md for #1508. shawnalpay requested changes because a trailing colon broke the PDF build and the introductory requirements sentence had to stay, following example PR #1509. davidearney fixed both, and Members approved it without objection on October 30, 2025, when it merged.

items.t: AI #1508: Update Requirements headers for chargeperiodstart.md through tags.md
items.b: Updated the Requirements header for consistency. This editorial PR by davidearney standardised the Requirements headers for the columns from ChargePeriodStart through Tags. shawnalpay requested changes so that each column also kept a lead-in sentence saying it adheres to the requirements that follow, as agreed in #1536. Members approved it without objections on 30 October 2025, and it was merged that day.

items.t: AI #1508: Update Requirements headers for contract_commitment columns
items.b: Changed to match the language in the other Requirements areas throughout the document. Editorial: for #1508, davidearney changed the Requirements headers of the contract commitment columns to match the rest of the spec. shawnalpay requested changes, asking that every column keep a lead-in sentence saying it adheres to the following requirements, following a pattern agreed in #1536. jpradocueva approved, and members approved it without objections in October 2025.

items.t: AI #1565: Apply dataset-level normative requirements guidelines to existing datasets
items.b: This PR applies the dataset-level normative requirements guidelines to the existing datasets CostAndUsage and ContractCommitment. ijurica applied the new dataset-level normative requirement guidelines to the Cost and Usage and Contract Commitment datasets. shawnalpay asked why DiscountHandling had moved and suggested alphabetical order, but accepted ijurica's explanation that the order put technical requirements before business ones, per the forthcoming #1529. Members approved it without objections on 30 October 2025, and it was merged.

items.t: AI #1336: Refactor entity name references and usage
items.b: This PR attempts to consistently apply usage of the following entity identification terms: `service provider`; `host provider`; `data generator`; `invoice issuer` rileyjenk opened this PR to apply four entity terms consistently, service provider, host provider, data generator and invoice issuer, in place of loose uses of provider and publisher. rileyjenk renamed the new split cost allocation feature as service-provider-calculated, but the group voted for data generator, and shawnalpay committed those renames per an October 2025 TF-2 agreement. shawnalpay requested changes while agreeing with about 80% of the edits, and resolved heavy merge conflicts. ijurica supplied line-specific fixes and flagged broken titles and anchors left by the renaming. Approval was postponed to no later than 6 November 2025, when members approved it without objections, and it merged.

items.t: AI #1458: Update FOCUS dataset references to include "Cost and Usage" delineation
items.b: • Modified multiple columns in the cost_and_usage dataset specifications to clarify that they must be present in a Cost and Usage FOCUS dataset when applicable. • Ensured consistency in terminology across various columns, including commitment discounts, consumed quantities, contracted costs, pricing categories, and more. Matt-Cowsert's PR, for #1458, added explicit "Cost and Usage" dataset references across column definitions and an appendix example. shawnalpay requested changes, agreeing with the appendix edits but objecting to naming the dataset in attributes, since the 1.3 team had agreed that link belongs in dataset requirements. Matt-Cowsert removed those references, shawnalpay approved, and Members approved it on October 30, 2025, when it was merged.

items.t: AI #1515: Fixing data generator version
items.b: PR #1464 introduced the concept of a `FOCUS dataset artifact`, which is meant to represent a delivered physical output of a `FOCUS dataset`.

items.t: Fix #1608 EffectiveCost-C-004-M has incorrectly defined requirements
items.b: Add unittest to ensure no other similar issues found and to keep this happening again Signed-off-by: Mike Fuller <mike@finops.org> Pull request #1610, opened by mike-finopsorg in November 2025, fixed the incorrectly defined requirements for EffectiveCost-C-004-M raised in #1608 and added a unit test to catch similar errors and prevent them recurring. shawnalpay and ijurica approved it in November 2025. jpradocueva reported that members approved it without objections on the 13 November call and planned merging after IPR review. It was merged on 8 December 2025.

items.t: AI #1613: Change ChargeType reference to ChargeCategory
items.b: We have an old reference to ChargeType that we need to address. PR #1614, opened by shawnalpay on 13 November 2025, changed a ChargeType reference to ChargeCategory to fix #1613. Reviewers ijurica and Matt-Cowsert approved on 13 November, and Matt-Cowsert thanked mike-finopsorg for catching the error. jpradocueva said members approved it without objection on the 13 November call and that the same change was applied to the candidate_recommendation branch via #1616. mike-finopsorg approved on 18 November. Merged 21 November 2025.

items.t: AI #1613: Change ChargeType reference to ChargeCategory
items.b: We have an old reference to ChargeType that we need to address. shawnalpay opened pull request #1616 on 13 November 2025, covering action item #1613, to change a reference to ChargeType so it reads ChargeCategory. The thread gives no further description of the reasoning. jpradocueva recorded that the Members approved it without objections or abstentions on the 13 November call, with merging planned for 4 December after the IPR review. ijurica and jpradocueva also approved. It was merged on 8 December 2025.

items.t: AI #1618: Repair value format references
items.b: A couple of consistency fixes for the value formats. shawnalpay opened a pull request on 13 November 2025 to make a couple of consistency fixes to value format references, tied to #1618. ijurica approved it on 20 November 2025. jpradocueva reported that the members approved it without objections or abstentions on the 20 November call, and that the change was also applied to the candidate_recommendation branch. The pull request was merged on 21 November 2025.

items.t: #1380: Address 1.3 candidate release typos
items.b: This PR represents my final pass of checking for typos across the 1.3 candidate release. Unfortunately there were quite a few... 😅 shawnalpay opened this pull request on 21 November 2025 as a final typo check across the 1.3 candidate release, resolving #1380. ijurica approved it on 1 December 2025. On 4 December 2025, members approved it without objections during their call, and jpradocueva noted the same fix was applied to #1641 on the candidate_recommendation branch. It was merged on 4 December 2025. The discussion was editorial.

items.t: #1380: Address 1.3 candidate release typos
items.b: This PR represents my final pass of checking for typos across the 1.3 candidate release. Unfortunately there were quite a few... 😅

items.t: #1380: Fix copy/paste issue and clarify example for split cost
items.b: This is a placeholder task to group the work associated with consistency review, which will occur Oct 16 to Oct 30. qquigley's PR, under #1380, fixed a copy-and-paste error and clarified the split cost example. shawnalpay relayed mike-finopsorg's suggestion to state that the ContractApplied and AllocatedMethodDetails examples describe a single Cost and Usage row, so readers do not assume AllocatedRatio sums to 1. Members approved it on December 4, 2025, and jpradocueva noted the change also went to the candidate_recommendation branch, citing #1649.

items.t: FR #1646: Standardize Normative Language: Convert All RECOMMENDED Statements to SHOULD
items.b: As suggested in FR #1646, replace normative statements RECOMMENDED with SHOULD jpradocueva opened this pull request for #1646 to replace every RECOMMENDED normative statement with SHOULD. shawnalpay and ijurica asked for the editorial and normative requirements guidelines to be updated too, and maintainers set it to draft on December 1, 2025 until the guidelines stopped distinguishing SHOULD from RECOMMENDED. ijurica listed further places to change in the introduction and requirements model guidelines, and kk09v suggested rewordings in several column files. On December 15 maintainers also agreed to strike OPTIONAL from the allowed keywords. Matt-Cowsert confirmed that timwright2000 for Google and vikramdesai01 for Microsoft were content with the change. Members approved it without objection on December 18, 2025, and it was merged that month.

items.t: #1380: Fix copy/paste issue and clarify example for split cost
items.b: shawnalpay opened this pull request on 24 November 2025 to fix a copy/paste problem and clarify a split cost example in #1649 and #1380. narlaadbe suggested removing an unused import and a guide wording change. shawnalpay deferred the guide change to a future pull request and left the import to be discussed with mike-finopsorg. ijurica and jpradocueva approved, and it was merged on 8 December 2025.

items.t: AI #1582: Handle for HTML/PDF anchor links for columns used in multiple datasets
items.b: Signed-off-by: Mike Fuller <mike@finops.org> Pull request #1656, by mike-finopsorg, was mechanical work fixing HTML and PDF anchor links for columns used in more than one dataset (#1582). ijurica asked for Metadata section links to be fixed too and listed broken ones, which mike-finopsorg corrected over several passes. Matt-Cowsert requested two link fixes in the provider name files, which shawnalpay committed. Members approved it on 8 January 2026 and it merged.

items.t: #1541: Fix minor typos
items.b: This is a placeholder issue for any action items associated with process, maintenance, etc to be performed outside of the task forces and the specification itself. An editorial PR in which narlaadbe fixed minor typos for #1541. shawnalpay and jpradocueva approved it, and Members approved it without objections on December 11, 2025, when it merged.

items.t: AI #1663: Billed Cost and Effective Cost definitions update
items.b: This PR updates the definitions of `Billed Cost` and `Effective Cost` (provided in the column specification preambles) and aligns their descriptions with the first sentence of each definition. ijurica opened this PR, the first milestone of #982, to rewrite the definitions of Billed Cost and Effective Cost and remove their outdated glossary entries. robmartin33 objected to framing them as cash-based and accrual-based accounting, Matt-Cowsert wanted a section on two practitioner challenges cut, and a TF-3 meeting on 9 January 2026 agreed the wording. ljadvey warned that dropping amortization from the definition would leave practitioners asking where net amortized costs are; shawnalpay suggested citing amortization as an example. udam-stitcher kept deliberately exhaustive wording and chose "recognized" over "consumed", which has a specific FOCUS meaning. shawnalpay approved on condition that Matt-Cowsert bring back the cut amortization sentence as a normative requirement in TF-3 work. Members approved it on 29 January 2026 and it merged.

items.t: FR #1094: Add Dataset Completeness attribute for custom columns
items.b: FinOps practitioners need complete dataset coverage to adopt FOCUS datasets. When FOCUS datasets lack columns needed for critical scenarios (organizational hierarchy attribution, commitment discount tracking, provider-specific optimizations), practitioners cannot fully adopt FOCUS and must continue using proprietary native datasets. flanakin's pull request (#1094) added a Dataset Completeness attribute, first called Scenario Completeness, requiring FOCUS datasets to include x_ custom columns for native columns that FOCUS does not cover. Matt-Cowsert pushed for entity-focused wording, shawnalpay objected to any aggregation or granularity requirements, and the requirements-model JSON was dropped at mike-finopsorg's request. pydi-aws asked for SHOULD instead of MUST, warning AWS exports would exceed 100 columns; mike-finopsorg called the omission clause an impossible bar, and shawnalpay proposed relying on column selection with a default column set. sarahcloudpm raised data-volume concerns. TF2 settled on including everything and documenting exclusions with justification. shawnalpay objected that flanakin's AI-assisted workflow recommitted suggestions separately, denying commenters co-authorship. Members approved it on March 26, 2026, and it merged that month.

items.t: FR #1091: Add Dataset Configuration attribute
items.b: Introduces the Dataset Configuration attribute for FOCUS 1.4, which defines how practitioners can configure the structure and content of FOCUS datasets. For #1091 and FOCUS 1.4, flanakin proposed a Dataset Configuration attribute requiring that a dataset can be limited to user-selected columns while still meeting column rules. Row aggregation, time granularity, version selection and row filtering went into supporting content as deferred ideas. Matt-Cowsert wanted that deferred material out of the PR; ijurica asked how conformance works when excluded columns are referenced by others, and flanakin softened the metadata rule to SHOULD after ijurica's feedback. mike-finopsorg had requirements-model files removed until 1.3 modelling finished, and jpradocueva said the rules described the dataset rather than an attribute. shawnalpay supplied rewrites and had it applied to Contract Commitment too. flanakin also reclassified unit price columns as dimensions and posted AI-generated update summaries. Members approved it in February 2026 and it was merged.

items.t: AI #1844: Relocate and rephrase the presence rules of FOCUS datasets to be attached to the dataset level
items.b: Signed-off-by: Mike Fuller <mike@finops.org> For #1844, mike-finopsorg moved column presence requirements out of individual column files and into each dataset's definition. shawnalpay noted readers would lose the presence rule beside each column's feature level and suggested a Content Constraints entry naming and linking the dataset, which mike-finopsorg added to every column. ijurica proposed matching changes to the requirements guidelines and a rule order. Members approved it without objections in February 2026.

items.t: FR #1488: Add Line-Item Examples for Non-Negotiated Commitment Scenarios
items.b: This PR replaces the existing Commitment Discount appendix content with comprehensive, provider-specific line-item examples covering non-negotiated commitment discount scenarios across AWS, Azure, and GCP. ljadvey's pull request for FR #1488 replaced the commitment discount appendix with 14 provider-specific scenarios for AWS, Azure and GCP, each with CSV data and column-by-column explanations. shawnalpay required a working PDF build and an overview page, and briefly insisted the PR fix SQL wrapping in the PDF before finding that problem already existed in 1.3 and opening #1965. Matt-Cowsert's large review centred on ContractedUnitPrice, which ijurica had said must equal ListUnitPrice in non-negotiated scenarios, and udam-stitcher called some cost explanations incorrect. mike-finopsorg asked for another proofreading pass, noting AI-generated content still needs the author's quality check. TF-2 then cut non-EC2 rows and savings calculations to keep the examples simple. With six approvals, Members approved it and it merged in March 2026.

items.t: AI #1793: Create Commitment Program Eligibility Details column
items.b: Introduces a new Commitment Program Eligibility Details column (`CommitmentProgramEligibilityDetails`) to the Cost and Usage dataset (AI #1793, in support of FR #958). Enables practitioners to calculate true commitment coverage rates and identify uncovered savings opportunities by identifying which commitment programs a usage line item is eligible for. Pull request #1882, by SanjnaSrivatsaVMware, added a Commitment Program Eligibility Details column listing the commitment programs a usage row is eligible for, to support coverage calculations (#1793, FR #958). The name kept changing: flanakin asked for a Details suffix like other JSON columns, rileyjenk said the scope was too narrow, TF-3 dropped 'Discount' to cover capacity reservations and SaaS commitments, and ijurica later suggested a full rename. Matt-Cowsert twice requested changes over type contradictions and redundant requirements; negotiated programs became optional and presence rules moved to dataset level. sarahcloudpm questioned the value of listing multiple programs. At shawnalpay's suggestion, separate lists became one CommitmentPrograms array, and shawnalpay warned it would be cut from 1.4 if unresolved by 9 April. Members approved it on 9 April 2026.

items.t: AI #1785: Add Invoice Detail and Billing Period datasets
items.b: This PR expands the FOCUS schema by introducing two new datasets: Invoice Detail (for granular invoice reconciliation) and Billing Period (for standardized billing cycle tracking). These additions are critical for supporting advanced use cases like correction handling and financial alignment. Pull request #1900, by shawnalpay, added two datasets, Invoice Detail for invoice reconciliation and Billing Period for billing cycle status, to support correction handling. rileyjenk asked about marketplace cases where both provider and invoice issuer produce invoice-like records. thecloudman argued an exchange rate column was vital; shawnalpay replied that TF-1 had not supported it, since a single invoice rate would create rounding errors against daily rates, and an effective rate can be derived. Matt-Cowsert suggested more invoice status values, but payment-related states had been ruled out of scope. ijurica wanted invoice-handling requirements from #1501 placed in these columns, and shawnalpay applied agreed changes such as making InvoiceId mandatory in Cost and Usage. Members approved it on 12 March 2026 and it merged.

items.t: AI #1803: Contract Commitment dataset extension
items.b: This PR adds the following new columns to the Contract Commitment dataset. shawnalpay opened this PR to extend the Contract Commitment dataset with 17 columns covering commitment model, fulfilment and payment intervals, payment terms, discount and upfront percentages, lifecycle status, categories, currency and provider names, plus a JSON applicability column with its own schema and appendix scenarios. Review renamed several columns: Scope became Eligibility, then Applicability, after robmartin33 flagged overlap with FinOps Scopes, Interval became Fulfillment Interval, and Duration became Duration Type after rileyjenk's concern. ljadvey proposed dropping "Commitment" from the dataset name, which shawnalpay ruled out of scope because 1.3 had approved it. mike-finopsorg and Matt-Cowsert refined wording and constraints, and ijurica's late feedback removed Monetary Pool as a benefit category. Members approved it without objections on 12 March 2026, and it was merged.

items.t: AI #1889: Remove deprecated ProviderName and PublisherName columns
items.b: Addresses issue #1888: Remove ProviderName and PublisherName from the specification as they were deprecated in v1.3. TechinMama's pull request removed the ProviderName and PublisherName columns deprecated in v1.3 (#1888), updating the dataset table, includes, changelog and migration guidance, and adding a column-removal process to the spec-change guidelines. TechinMama also fixed a CI failure caused by a deleted appendix file. Matt-Cowsert requested changes and pointed out two missed files. shawnalpay asked whether supporting-content files should be deleted, noting there was no precedent, and said the columns should be described as removed, not deprecated. davidearney questioned keeping references that would have to come out in v1.5. TF2 agreed to call spec components "entities" rather than "entries", aligning with #1960, and qquigley applied it. With six approvals, members approved it on February 26, 2026, and it merged.

items.t: FR #982: Update Billed and Effective Cost Normative Requirements
items.b: This PR updates BilledCost and EffectiveCost normative requirements for 1.4. The old marketplace and commitment-discount-specific rules are replaced with a provider-agnostic covered/covering framework. Matt-Cowsert opened this pull request for #982 to rewrite the BilledCost and EffectiveCost requirements for 1.4, replacing marketplace and commitment-discount rules with a general covered and covering charge framework, new glossary terms and a rounding tolerance for invoice matching. beau-nelford-anglepoint called it a breaking change needing migration guidance; Matt-Cowsert replied that it clarified gaps in 1.3 rather than broke it. udam-stitcher argued a tolerance that grows with dataset size could mask real billing errors, while ijurica defended it as fixing a precision mismatch; maintainers reached no decision in March 2026, and Matt-Cowsert later added a formula co-authored with shawnalpay. Members approved it without objection on April 2, 2026, and it was merged that month.

items.t: AI #1944: Refactor Attribute normative requirements to align with guidelines
items.b: The reference to `ColumnHandling` in the design principles section has been updated to `FocusColumnHandling`. ijurica opened this pull request for #1059 to rewrite every attribute's normative requirements under the new guidelines in #1967: one subject and one BCP 14 keyword per requirement, a fixed set of subjects, and requirements moved to the dataset or column where they belong. It split ColumnHandling into FOCUS and custom column versions. Reviewers debated details: qquigley flagged conflicts with existing Id and Sku naming, thecloudman questioned rules on custom column abbreviations, which davidearney defended, and the requirements model team preferred singular subjects. A MAY-to-SHOULD change for alphabetical column order was agreed. On binding format rules to custom columns, shawnalpay set out options and mike-finopsorg's hybrid path was applied. Matt-Cowsert requested changes, then approved. Members approved it without objection on April 9, 2026, and it was merged.

items.t: AI #1985: Restructure the JSON Object columns
items.b: This PR proposes using JSON Schema to define JSON Objects, replacing much of the lengthy normative text with a formalized, industry-standard schema definition. This approach aims to reduce wordiness and leverage standard validation formats to define the object requirements more concisely. mike-finopsorg proposed replacing the lengthy normative text for JSON Object columns with formal JSON Schemas and moving inline examples to an appendix. After February 2026 maintainers discussion, shawnalpay closed the alternative #1986 in its favor, calling this approach easier to understand, implement and validate. kk09v requested changes on process grounds, since bundling the errata from #2041 broke the errata process, so shawnalpay moved those fixes to #2052. jpradocueva flagged uppercase MUST statements in implementation guidance, which mike-finopsorg considered non-normative. The new ContractCommitmentApplicability column moved to #1924, and mike-finopsorg decided to stay with JSON Schema for now under #2019. thecloudman warned that transferring requirements would need care. Members approved it on March 19, 2026, and it merged.

items.t: AI #1880: Update composite normative requirements to include `MUST`
items.b: This PR promotes any composite (parent) statement to a normative requirement with MUST as discussed in AI #1880 - Comment jpradocueva made composite parent statements in normative requirements into explicit MUST statements, following #1880. shawnalpay raised consistency questions, such as varied sentence openings and whether conditional "when not null" composites should exist at all, and noted deprecated columns no longer needed changes. After approvals from thecloudman, shawnalpay and ijurica, Members approved it on March 5, 2026, and it was merged that month.

items.t: AI #2016: Fix ContractCommitmentID - ResourceID mapping for specific Purchase and Unused Usage charges
items.b: This PR updates validation logic so that ContractCommitmentID MUST be equal to ResourceID in these cases: Charges representing a Purchase of that specific contract commitment; Charges representing Usage of the unused portion ijurica's pull request required ContractCommitmentId to equal ResourceId on purchases of that specific commitment and on usage of its unused portion, rather than on all purchases, matching Discount Handling. shawnalpay noted it needed a parent feature request for 1.4. udam-stitcher asked about credits and adjustments and noted the description overstated the change, which ijurica corrected. Members approved it on March 19, 2026, and it merged.

items.t: AI #2014: Add billing scenario examples
items.b: Adds seven SaaS/PaaS billing scenario examples to the appendix, illustrating how BilledCost and EffectiveCost behave across common billing models. Each scenario uses a fictional service provider from the canonical list established in #2115, includes a validated 38-column CSV data file, and is accompanied by a markdown narrative with inline summary tables explaining the FOCUS column values. Matt-Cowsert proposed seven appendix examples of SaaS and PaaS billing models, including credit-based, seat-based and tiered pricing, showing how BilledCost and EffectiveCost behave, each with a CSV file, addressing #1897 and #982. shawnalpay requested changes and objected to naming real providers such as MongoDB and Atlassian; Matt-Cowsert switched to fictional names, later aligned with #2115 after kk09v and thecloudman flagged conflicts there. Task force 3 agreed, at shawnalpay's prompting, to give all seven CSVs the same 38 columns. shawnalpay also asked for an overview table, inline data tables and service provider in place of provider. gparker-at-sf asked for clearer reasoning and, like davidearney, flagged dollar signs that did not render, while ijurica suggested unique CommitmentDiscountId values. Members approved it on April 2 and it merged in April 2026.

items.t: AI #1929: Add supported features and appendix content for commitment program eligibility details
items.b: Adds supported features content for Commitment Program Eligibility Details (AI #1929, in support of FR #958). Congruent with PR #1882 (column definition); uses the `CommitmentPrograms`/`ProgramType` structure with fictitious entity names from PR #2115. Matt-Cowsert added a supported feature and appendix example for Commitment Program Eligibility Details (action item #1929, FR #958), with four SQL queries, depending on the column definition in #1882. shawnalpay warned it would be descoped without resolved threads and an approval by 2 April, so Matt-Cowsert rewrote it to match the CommitmentPrograms and ProgramType structure in #1882. shawnalpay also asked for a glossary entry for commitment program, explicit dataset references, examples moved to the appendix and "Total" dropped from metric names. ijurica argued that supported features should assume conformant data and proposed restructured queries; Matt-Cowsert added a conformance note and adopted them. SanjnaSrivatsaVMware queried the handling of Unused rows and some wording, then approved. With five approvals, Members approved it and it merged in April 2026.

items.t: AI #2046: Remove redundant requirements using `X MUST be a valid decimal value` pattern
items.b: This PR implements action item AI #2046 by removing redundant requirements containing the stament `X MUST be a valid decimal value`. jpradocueva's pull request (#2046) removed redundant "MUST be a valid decimal value" requirements, since the Decimal type and numeric format rules already covered them. shawnalpay and Matt-Cowsert requested changes after finding missed files, including pricingquantity.md, contractcommitmentcost.md and quantity columns using a "when not null" variant, which jpradocueva then fixed. Reviewers asked that supporting content be left alone and that the normative-requirements guidelines template be updated, where ijurica and Matt-Cowsert refined the placeholder syntax. shawnalpay asked whether "any valid decimal value" in content constraints was equally duplicative, and jpradocueva took that question to TF-RM. thecloudman and kk09v approved. Members approved it on March 26, 2026, and it merged the next day.

items.t: AI #2040: Address 1.3 errata in Spec and RM
items.b: --- shawnalpay's PR applied non-material errata to FOCUS 1.3 found while building validation tooling, including scoping contract presence rules to the ContractApplied Elements object, fixing JSON paths and a type, standardizing "Id" casing, correcting AllocatedTags, and bumping the requirements model to 1.3.0.1. kk09v, Matt-Cowsert and jpradocueva approved. Members approved it on March 19, 2026, and it was merged.

items.t: AI #1940: ToC Fixes
items.b: This PR repairs a couple of formatting issues that were introduced through the merging of multiple PRs today, but were not reconciled in #1942 before it was merged. Pull request #2057, opened and merged by shawnalpay on 13 March 2026, fixed formatting problems in the table of contents. The problems came from several pull requests merged that same day, which had not been reconciled in #1942 before it was merged. Reviewer jpradocueva approved it, noting that resolving the merge conflicts meant rearranging content. This is an editorial cleanup, and the thread records no broader decision.

items.t: Merge 1.4 `working_draft` into `candidate_recommendation`
items.b: THIS PR WILL REMAIN IN DRAFT UNTIL THE END OF APRIL. It is here merely to demonstrate the accumulating net changes between `working_draft` and `candidate_recommendation`. Please do not leave comments or review until the PR has been pulled out of draft. shawnalpay opened this PR to merge the 1.4 working draft into the candidate recommendation branch, keeping it in draft until late April 2026 to show the accumulating changes. mike-finopsorg set out how to resolve 15 merge conflicts left by 1.3 editorial work, and automated review findings were logged as non-blocking follow-ups such as #2145 and #2147. It was merged in May 2026, starting the 30-day IP review for 1.4.

items.t: AI #2065: Remove duplicative cost requirements from unit price columns
items.b: • Removes duplicative normative requirements from ListUnitPrice and ContractedUnitPrice that restate requirements already defined in their respective cost columns • "ListCost MUST equal the product of ListUnitPrice and PricingQuantity..." already exists in `listcost.md` • "ContractedCost MUST equal the product of ContractedUnitPrice and PricingQuantity..." already exists in `contractedcost.md` • Additional duplicate… Matt-Cowsert removed requirements from ListUnitPrice and ContractedUnitPrice that restated rules already in ListCost and ContractedCost, following feedback in #1797. ijurica proposed also dropping a similar PricingQuantity requirement, which shawnalpay questioned, and that case was deferred to #2081; at shawnalpay's request, Requirements Model changes moved to #2049. Members approved it without objections on 26 March 2026, and it was merged.

items.t: FR #1500: Apply consistency to feature level of Invoice related columns
items.b: PR #1500 was inconsistent in the application of the term "when the invoice issuer supports payable invoices". Pull request #2100, by shawnalpay, made the InvoiceId and InvoiceDetailId feature levels Conditional, applying when the invoice issuer supports payable invoices, to match their requirements, and changed 'if' to 'when' across invoice-related datasets. shawnalpay acknowledged one change was not purely editorial, but ijurica judged it consistency rather than a material change. kk09v found the phrasing odd but not blocking. Members approved it on 2 April 2026.

items.t: FR #1124: Add Tag Scheme to glossary
items.b: Adding a definition of Tag Scheme to the glossary and adding glossary references where it was used. kk09v added a Tag Scheme definition to the glossary, with links where the term was used, as a subset of the descoped #1904 (#1124). kk09v noted inconsistent use of provider-defined and data generator-defined and covered both in the definition, while shawnalpay and Matt-Cowsert suggested wording and grammar fixes. Members approved it without objection on April 2, 2026, and it was merged that month.

items.t: FR #1091: Apply Dataset Configuration to Invoice Detail and Billing Period
items.b: We created Dataset Configuration per PR #1816, but we did not apply it to Invoice Detail or Billing Period because those had not yet been approved via PR #1900. This PR applies that attribute to those datasets. Pull request #2113, by shawnalpay, applied the Dataset Configuration attribute from #1816 to the Invoice Detail and Billing Period datasets, which had not yet been approved via #1900 when that attribute was created. It was mechanical: ijurica, davidearney and Matt-Cowsert approved without issues, and Members approved it on 2 April 2026.

items.t: FR #1389: Complete move of column presence requirements to dataset level
items.b: PR #1865 attempted to move all column presence requirements to the dataset level. There are three columns that had a composite presence requirement that were not fully ported over in that PR. For #1389, shawnalpay finished moving column presence rules to the dataset level, covering three PricingCurrency columns whose composite presence requirements #1865 had not fully ported, and applied composite nullability to ContractCommitmentDiscountPercentage. jpradocueva confirmed the changes were valid under the requirements model extraction workflows. Members approved it without objections in April 2026.

items.t: AI #2064: Replace $ entities with literal $ and harden makescripts
items.b: • replace HTML $ with literal $ across commitment discount, SaaS, and rounding appendix markdown examples • update vendored MarkdownPP LaTeXRender heuristics to avoid false-positive $...$ rendering for currency/prose/table content • preserve intentional inline LaTeX rendering behavior while suppressing noisy "Rendering:" output during spec build • disable pandoc dollar-math parsing and harden LaTeXRender for c… mike-finopsorg replaced HTML dollar entities with literal dollar signs in appendix examples, under action item #2064, and changed the build so currency amounts were no longer mistaken for math formulas. An automated reviewer and Matt-Cowsert suggested regular-expression fixes, and ijurica confirmed dollar signs rendered correctly in HTML and PDF. Members approved it on April 9 and it merged in April 2026.

items.t: AI #2110: Perform many small editorial fixes
items.b: This PR introduces several editorial cleanups, formatting improvements, and structural fixes across the specification documents to better align with our normative language guidelines and improve overall readability. shawnalpay proposed small editorial fixes for AI #2110, such as mentioning PaaS beside SaaS, dropping unused normative keywords, alphabetising the appendix and removing a duplicate include. shawnalpay asked whether notes should follow the blockquote rule in AGENTS.md, and mike-finopsorg suggested keeping current practice and updating the guideline. Members approved it on April 16, 2026, and it was merged that day.

items.t: AI #1998: Reconcile "match" vs "equal" verbiage
items.b: Align usage of terms match and equal for consistency across the specification. kk09v proposed using "equal" for numeric metric values and "match" for identifiers and other values, and applied it across the spec for #1998. jpradocueva requested changes because the edits also altered the 1.2 and 1.3 requirements models, which kk09v reverted. Matt-Cowsert said the approach fitted the comparison guideline in #2236 and flagged one missed instance. Members approved it without objections in April 2026, when it merged.

items.t: AI #2086: Clarify InvoiceIssuerName requirement across datasets
items.b: • Billing Period: Updates wording from "issued the invoice" (past, singular) to "issues invoices" (present, plural) to match Invoice Detail. • Contract Commitment: Adds the missing semantic requirement bullet. • Cost and Usage: Adds the missing semantic requirement bullet. Matt-Cowsert's pull request (#2086) gave InvoiceIssuerName the same requirement in Billing Period, Invoice Detail, Contract Commitment and Cost and Usage, using present-tense "issues invoices" wording. shawnalpay pointed out that Contract Commitment also needed it, and it was added. TF3 floated tying the issuer to InvoiceId, assigning ijurica to draft wording; udam-stitcher liked the idea but did not require it. Members approved it on April 23, 2026, and it merged.

items.t: Process #1878: 1.4 consistency review fixes
items.b: Addresses all editorial consistency issues raised by @davidearney in #1878 during the 1.4 consistency review. Mostly editorial: davidearney applied 1.4 consistency fixes from #1878 across many files, covering heading capitalization, broken anchors, spacing and grammar, plus a workflow fix. Following shawnalpay and ijurica, double quotes were kept out of allowed-values tables; shawnalpay also said contractions could stay and dashes should be spaced hyphens. Matt-Cowsert noted the description no longer matched the diff. Members approved it without objections in April 2026.

items.t: AI #2129: Replace real-world names with fictitious entities in contract commitments
items.b: • Replace real-world vendor names (AWS, Azure, GCP, Snowflake, Datadog) and non-standard fictitious names (Acme Co, DataStreamer) with established fictitious entities (Aura Web, CrestNode, LatticeScale, OmniQuery, StackLens, PipelCRM) in the contract commitments appendix • Replace real-world commitment program names (Savings Plan, Reserved Instance, Flex CUD, ODCR, EDP/MACC) with fictitious commitment programs (Flexi… thecloudman replaced real vendor and commitment program names in the contract commitments appendix and its CSV files with fictitious ones, under #2129. shawnalpay, the content's author, thought adding fictitious data generators to some text hurt understanding more than removing them, and also flagged an unapproved name and a contradiction, all of which thecloudman changed. Members approved it on April 16 and it merged in April 2026.

items.t: AI #2129: Replace Acme Co with Aura Web in invoice detail appendix
items.b: • Replace "Acme Co" with the established fictitious data generator "Aura Web" across all three invoice detail scenarios • Rename "AcmeStore" service to "AuraStore" for consistency with the Aura Web provider name • Update corresponding CSV scenario files to match thecloudman replaced Acme Co with the fictitious provider Aura Web, and AcmeStore with AuraStore, in the invoice detail appendix and its CSVs under #2129. shawnalpay asked for leftover "RI" and "reserved instance" wording to become Resource Reservation and for a CSV that had drifted from the Markdown to be fixed, which thecloudman did. Matt-Cowsert approved, Members approved it, and it merged in April 2026.

items.t: AI #2129: Rename ACME to CrestNode in metadata examples
items.b: • Minor consistency rename: replace the ad-hoc placeholder "ACME"/"Acme" with the approved fictitious data generator "CrestNode" across all 18 metadata example files • Update provider tag prefixes from `awecorp`/`ac` to `crestnode`/`cn` • No structural or content changes — purely a naming alignment tweak thecloudman renamed the placeholder ACME to the approved fictitious data generator CrestNode across 18 metadata example files, under #2129. The change was mechanical; shawnalpay noticed that most JSON blocks still carried the old tag prefixes, and thecloudman fixed them. Members approved it on April 16 and it merged in April 2026.

items.t: AI #2129: Replace unapproved fictitious names in SaaS examples
items.b: Replaces ad-hoc placeholder entity names across 3 markdown files and 15 CSV files in the SaaS examples appendix with approved fictitious names from the reference tables. thecloudman replaced ad hoc company names in the SaaS examples with approved fictitious names, under #2129. shawnalpay found a misfired find-and-replace, a thematic mismatch and an AI working folder to remove, and flanakin and davidearney objected to large additions to AGENTS.md, which were pulled out. It missed one Members' meeting, then Members approved it on April 23 and it merged in April 2026.

items.t: AI #2129: Replace TinyCloud with LatticeScale in commitment discount flexibility examples
items.b: • Replaces non-approved fictitious name "TinyCloud" with approved Data Generator name "LatticeScale" in all 4 commitment discount flexibility example scenarios • CSV files were reviewed and require no changes (they use generic placeholders only) • Minor consistency update to align with the approved fictitious entity names from PR #2115 A mechanical pull request by thecloudman under #2129 that replaced the unapproved fictitious name TinyCloud with LatticeScale, an approved name from #2115, in the four commitment discount flexibility examples. Matt-Cowsert approved it as a clean replacement, Members approved it, and it merged in April 2026.

items.t: AI #2129: Replace ACME Corp with CrestNode in correction handling examples
items.b: • Replaces "ACME Corp" with approved Data Generator name "CrestNode" in correction handling example markdown files • ACME Corp was incorrectly used as a service provider/invoice issuer — per PR #2115, Acme Corp is an approved customer name, not a provider • Only 2 markdown files affected (closed_billing_period.md, open_billing_period.md) — all 41 CSV files were reviewed and contain no ACME references thecloudman replaced ACME Corp with CrestNode in the correction handling examples under #2129, because #2115 made Acme Corp an approved customer name, not a provider. shawnalpay asked whether the linked CSV files also needed updating, and thecloudman confirmed none contained ACME. Matt-Cowsert approved, Members approved it, and it merged in April 2026.

items.t: AI #2129: Comprehensive fictitious names in commitment discount examples
items.b: Comprehensive replacement of all real-world vendor names with approved fictitious equivalents across the entire commitment discounts appendix. Supersedes #2241 which only updated the index file. thecloudman replaced every real vendor and product name in the commitment discounts appendix with approved fictitious equivalents, renaming 14 scenario files and 14 CSVs and superseding #2241. shawnalpay asked thecloudman to close either this or the overlapping #2243, and thecloudman also removed SKU prefixes that still pointed to real vendors. shawnalpay, Matt-Cowsert and davidearney approved, Members approved it, and it merged in April 2026.

items.t: AI #2140: Pivot scaled-down tables from horizontal to vertical
items.b: Pivots the two tables in `paymentcurrencybilledcost.md` from horizontal to vertical, removing the `<div class="small-table">` wrappers added in #2038. The `.small-table` CSS class in `base.css` is retained per the #2140 directive. Matt-Cowsert pivoted two example tables in the PaymentCurrencyBilledCost column from horizontal to vertical, removing scaling wrappers added in #2038 that had shrunk the whole PDF. thecloudman approved but found the transposed layout hard to read and asked whether all examples would be made consistent; shawnalpay doubted that could be done in this round. Members approved it without objections on 16 April 2026, and it was merged.

items.t: AI #2256: Update invoice issuer references to use glossary entry
items.b: • Link generic "invoice issuer" references to the glossary entry (`*invoice issuer*`) across the specification • Follows the editorial guideline that glossary terms are hyperlinked on first occurrence per section only (editorial-guidelines.md:108, 143) • 38 references updated across 24 files, organized in 6 reviewable commits by spec area thecloudman linked generic mentions of "invoice issuer" to its new glossary entry, which depended on #2257 adding that entry. shawnalpay asked for hyphenated anchors and, per a recent Maintainers agreement, a link only on the first mention in each file, noting the normative PR could go straight to approval because it only changed links. Members approved it without objections on 23 April 2026, and it was merged.

items.t: AI #2106: Standardize Allowed Values subheaders across datasets
items.b: Converts bare \`Allowed values:\` text labels to proper \`## Allowed Values\` markdown headings and moves the section to appear immediately after \`## Requirements\` in all 21 columns that define allowed values. davidearney opened this pull request for #2106 to turn plain "Allowed values:" labels into proper Allowed Values headings placed directly after the Requirements section, in the 21 columns that define allowed values. This was an editorial change. shawnalpay asked davidearney to strip changes already made in #2200, such as header capitalization and anchor links, and to apply the move to every file; davidearney said the AI tool used had been told to skip #2200's changes, struck them by hand and rebased into one clean commit. shawnalpay asked whether moving the section would affect requirements extraction, and jpradocueva said it would not. An exception in one file was deferred to #2262. Members approved it without objection on April 23, 2026, and it was merged that month.

items.t: AI #2261: Clean up DeliveryHandling and CorrectionHandling attributes
items.b: This PR removes leftover empty ## Exceptions sections (containing None) from DeliveryHandling and CorrectionHandling attribute specifications and aligns their section ordering with the convention used across other attribute specifications. An editorial cleanup in which ijurica removed empty Exceptions sections from the DeliveryHandling and CorrectionHandling attributes and reordered their sections to match other attributes. shawnalpay noted it touched normative text but could be approved immediately because requirements only moved, which Matt-Cowsert confirmed. It was approved at the April 16 members' call and merged in April 2026.

items.t: AI #2178: Update ProgramType examples to Title Case in Commitment Program Eligibility Details
items.b: Flips informative `ProgramType` value examples from PascalCase to Title Case in the Commitment Program Eligibility Details supported feature, appendix, and CSV data files. Informative only: no normative requirements change. Matt-Cowsert changed the ProgramType example values in the Commitment Program Eligibility Details feature, appendix and CSVs from PascalCase to Title Case, following a TF-3 decision on #1882 that FOCUS uses display names; no requirements changed. At shawnalpay's request, Matt-Cowsert moved the column-file edits to #2283 to avoid merge conflicts, dropped an out-of-scope note and replaced HTML dollar entities with dollar signs. Members approved it and it merged in April 2026.

items.t: AI #2179: Replace `$` entities with literal $ in Commitment Program Eligibility Details appendix
items.b: • Addresses #2179 (appendix portion). • Follow-up to #2167 (working draft-wide `$` → `$` sweep and `make` hardening), which merged concurrently with #2025. PR #2025 introduced new `$` instances in Commitment Program Eligibility Details content that the sweep didn't catch. • Mechanical substitution only. No semantic changes. Matt-Cowsert replaced dollar entities with literal dollar signs in the Commitment Program Eligibility Details appendix, under #2179, because #2025 had added new ones after the earlier sweep in #2167. The change was mechanical; at shawnalpay's request the column-file edits were reverted, since #2283 covered them. Members approved it on April 23 and it merged in April 2026.

items.t: AI #1957: Augment normative requirement guidelines with dataset terminology in non-subject positions and apply it
items.b: This PR updates normative requirement guidelines to define dataset terminology usage in non-subject positions and applies the rule to relevant column-level requirements. ijurica added a guideline that requirements referring to datasets outside the subject position use precise glossary terms such as "dataset instance", and applied it across the spec. shawnalpay asked whether every case had been caught; ijurica described the regex scan used and later added one missed instance, and Matt-Cowsert noted circular guideline definitions were fixed. Members approved it without objections on 30 April 2026, and it was merged.

items.t: AI #2272: Add format detection for title case
