items.b: Improved format detection to identify title case formatting issues. rileyjenk opened this pull request to make the spec's linter flag headers that broke the newly adopted Title Case rule. shawnalpay found bugs, such as acronyms and camelCase names being lowercased and hyphenated words being skipped, suggested exceptions such as is, are and vs., and proposed renaming "Introduced (version)" to "Version Introduced", which rileyjenk accepted. thecloudman reported false positives on On-Demand and Up-Front, which rileyjenk fixed. Because merging the rule alone would break the PDF build, shawnalpay held it until a companion PR applied the fixes; rileyjenk's #2302 was closed and shawnalpay's #2308 took its place. Members approved it without objection on April 30, 2026, and it was merged that month.

items.t: AI #2114: Add JSON data type requirement to Key-Value columns
items.b: Adding JSON as the data type to the normative requirements which specify the key-value format kk09v's pull request (#2114) added a JSON data type requirement to key-value columns such as Tags, AllocatedTags and SkuPriceDetails. ijurica suggested wording that reads "JSON Object (serialized as a String where necessary)", and shawnalpay requested those changes. A review bot flagged the requirements model, which shawnalpay said would be handled separately. Members approved it on April 30, 2026, and it merged.

items.t: AI #2127: Fix attribute linking, enforce Attribute IDs, and correct anchor generation description in MarkdownPP Guidelines
items.b: The current markdown documentation contains inconsistencies and errors in how internal links, anchors, and attributes are referenced. These issues include missing parent section prefixes in anchor links (e.g., needing `#attributes.`), referencing display names instead of proper Attribute IDs in the text, and using improperly formatted anchors containing hyphens. ijurica's editorial PR, for #2127, fixed broken attribute links, used Attribute IDs in normative text, corrected the attributes overview table, and changed the MarkdownPP guidelines to say anchor generation keeps hyphens, matching the script. ijurica asked mike-finopsorg whether the regex was meant to strip hyphens; no reply is recorded. shawnalpay and jpradocueva approved, and Members approved it on April 23, 2026, and it was merged.

items.t: AI #2142: Remove redundant "more granular" wording in split cost allocation handling
items.b: Removes the parenthetical aside "(or in some cases provides more granular detail about)" from the opening paragraph of `specification/attributes/data_generator_calculated_split_cost_allocation_handling.md`. The original sentence used variants of "more granular" three times, making it harder to read than necessary. A mostly editorial change for #2142: thecloudman removed a redundant parenthetical about more granular detail from the opening of the data generator-calculated split cost allocation handling attribute. ijurica noted the wording covered only allocation, not cases such as a fully idle resource, and shawnalpay offered alternative wording; a suggested revision was adopted as agreed in TF2. It was merged in April 2026 after approval at the April 23 members' call.

items.t: AI #2278: Fix broken internal links in non-Attributes sections
items.b: This PR addresses broken internal links in sections outside Attributes (Datasets, Appendix, Glossary, Metadata, and others), including wrong path segments, missing glossary anchors, case mismatches, and incorrect separators. ijurica proposed fixing broken internal links outside the Attributes section, such as wrong paths, missing glossary anchors and case mismatches, for AI #2278. shawnalpay noted that FOCUS appeared in three different casings in anchors, and ijurica pointed to wider glossary anchor inconsistencies to handle separately. Members approved this editorial PR on April 30, 2026, and it was merged.

items.t: AI #2117: Refactor format of CommitmentProgramEligibilityDetails
items.b: This PR refactors the `CommitmentProgramEligibilityDetails` column definition to align with the formatting and validation standards established by other JSON object columns (e.g., `ContractApplied` and `AllocatedMethodDetails`). shawnalpay's editorial PR, for #2117, refactored the CommitmentProgramEligibilityDetails column to match other JSON object columns such as ContractApplied and AllocatedMethodDetails. It replaced the informal type definition with a formal JSON Schema, dropped structural requirements the schema now enforces, moved fictitious examples to an appendix, and used glossary terms in the intro. Matt-Cowsert requested changes twice, first for a duplicate bullet and a heading level, then for invalid JSON left after a Title Case suggestion from #2266 was applied, and approved once both were fixed. ijurica asked for "match" rather than "equal" in string comparisons and questioned whether the intro narrowed the scope; shawnalpay said no material change was intended and offered new wording. Members approved it on April 30, 2026, and it was merged.

items.t: AI #2284: Align AllocatedMethodDetails.AllocatedRatio aggregate requirement wording with guidelines
items.b: This PR aligns the wording of the AllocatedMethodDetails aggregation requirement with: Allowed Subject Exception for Aggregate Expressions (outlined in the Normative Requirements Guidelines); Comparison Terminology (outlined in the Editorial Guidelines); PR #2175 ijurica's editorial PR reworded the AllocatedRatio sum requirement in AllocatedMethodDetails to the guidelines' "The sum of" and "be equal to" phrasing, matching #2175. shawnalpay confirmed at TF-1 that it followed kk09v's pattern, and jpradocueva approved it for the requirements model. Members approved it on 30 April 2026 and it merged.

items.t: AI #2286: Add data volume considerations to Correction Style descriptions in Appendix section
items.b: Data volume considerations are already outlined in the Correction Handling attribute, but were not reflected in the Appendix overview of correction styles. Given that the current descriptions primarily emphasize aspects such as traceability, the absence of data volume context could lead to an unintended interpretation that Ledger is the preferred approach. ijurica added data volume considerations to the Appendix overview of correction styles, so that its focus on traceability would not imply Ledger was preferred. On shawnalpay's advice the attribute text now says net rather than total data volume, since total volume can be highest for Replacement, and ThavronNan's wording "is the lowest" replaced "remains the lowest". It was approved at the April 23 members' call and merged in April 2026.

items.t: AI #2288: Revisit `Total Term` allowed value in `Contract Commitment Fulfillment Interval` column
items.b: This PR addresses issues with the `Total Term` allowed value in `ContractCommitmentFulfillmentInterval`: The name uses `Term`, which per the FOCUS glossary means "An agreement specified on a contract or invoice" — not a time duration, making it inconsistent with the other time-based allowed values.; The description and use case reference the contract rather than the contract commitment, but the latter might be prefer… ijurica proposed renaming the Total Term value of ContractCommitmentFulfillmentInterval, because the glossary defines a term as an agreement rather than a duration, and scoping its description to the contract commitment. shawnalpay preferred Full Period to Full Commitment Period, asked for the rename to be applied everywhere and for merge conflicts to be resolved. Members approved it on April 30, 2026, and it was merged.

items.t: AI #2279: Apply consistent section ordering within column files
items.b: 1. Column Description 2. Requirements 3. [JSON Object + requirements, if applicable] 4. [Schema structure, if applicable] 5. [JSON object example, if applicable] 6. [non-standard naming section, if it exists] 7. Column ID 8. Display Name 9. Description 10. Content Constraints 11. Introduced Version Editorial: for #2279, Matt-Cowsert applied a standard section order to column files, moving sections without changing content. shawnalpay argued JSON examples should directly follow the schema, and Matt-Cowsert swapped the order. flanakin asked about standardizing the varied names of extra sections; shawnalpay and ijurica said that belonged to #2108, with this PR a prerequisite. Members approved it without objections in April 2026.

items.t: AI #2096: Add normative requirement guidance for same column names across datasets
items.b: This PR addresses the handling of identically named columns that have diverging definitions across different datasets (specifically, `ChargeCategory` in `CostAndUsage` vs. `InvoiceDetail`). It introduces a global editorial guideline for documenting these differences and applies a structural fix to `InvoiceDetail.ChargeCategory` to eliminate overlapping normative constraints. shawnalpay added a guideline allowing identically named columns to be defined differently across datasets, provided the spec explains why. The PR also restructured InvoiceDetail's ChargeCategory to fix overlapping MAY and MUST rules, explaining that invoice lines may aggregate charge types while Tax stays separate. ijurica offered non-blocking wording suggestions, and the section was renamed Implementation Guidance per #2310. Members approved it on 30 April 2026 and it merged.

items.t: AI #2128: Enforce first-occurrence linking rule in column files
items.b: Remove duplicate links to the same entity/glossary anchor within each column definition file under datasets/*/columns/. Each anchor now keeps its first standard-form link; later standard-form occurrences and identical-text functional duplicates are converted to plain text, preserving surrounding markdown (italics, casing, spacing). Functional links with distinct anchor text remain untouched. Editorial: deejacruz removed repeat links to the same anchor within column files for #2128, keeping only the first, across 46 files. shawnalpay asked whether once per file was too strict, and the April 23 Members' call exempted links in markdown tables, tracked as #2305. jpradocueva flagged one leftover charge period link. Members approved it without objections on April 30, 2026, when it merged.

items.t: AI #2297: Use semicolons in nested comma lists
items.b: Addresses #2297. When a comma-separated list contains items with internal commas, the reader loses track of where each top-level item ends. This PR adopts semicolons as the separator in those cases. Matt-Cowsert added an editorial rule to use semicolons in lists whose items contain commas, for #2297, and applied it to eight passages. shawnalpay found further instances, and kk09v argued one case was two separate clauses, which shawnalpay accepted; kk09v also noted an em dash suited one clause. Members approved it without objections on April 30, 2026, when it merged.

items.t: AI #2097: Add missing Dataset row to Content Constraints tables for Invoice Detail, Billing Period, and Cost and Usage
items.b: Adds the missing `Dataset` row as the first entry in the `## Content Constraints` table for all column files in the Billing Period and Invoice Detail datasets. This matches the pattern already established in Cost and Usage and Contract Commitment column files. davidearney added the missing Dataset row to the Content Constraints tables of 29 column files, closing #2097. davidearney asked whether that cell should be an anchor link or plain text, and ijurica pointed out a Cost and Usage file also missing the row, which was then added. Members approved this editorial PR on April 30, 2026, and it was merged; the thread doesn't record an answer on links.

items.t: AI #2309: Improve column heading structure and ordering; consolidate Implementation sections
items.b: This PR addresses action item #2309 by improving heading structure, order, and consolidating implementation section headings across all columns. ijurica proposed restructuring column headings for AI #2309, merging Implementation Context into Implementation Guidance and regrouping JSON object headings. shawnalpay opposed placing other headings between the column and object requirements, and mike-finopsorg said major structural changes came too late. Nesting all object sections under one object heading resolved the concern. Members approved it on April 30, 2026, and it was merged.

items.t: AI #2320: Address remaining Content Constraints inconsistencies
items.b: Based on the review of Content Constraints tables across all four datasets, the following changes were agreed upon in this thread: 1. Column type: Dimension → Metric for ContractCommitmentDiscountPercentage and ContractCommitmentPaymentUpfrontPercentage (Contract Commitment). These are the only two Decimal columns classified as Dimension — all other 17 Decimal columns are Metric. ijurica proposed fixing remaining Content Constraints inconsistencies across all four datasets for AI #2320, such as column types and value format casing. shawnalpay and davidearney asked for matching dataset.md updates and consistent Allowed values casing, and Matt-Cowsert filed #2326 for a link text convention. Members approved this editorial PR on April 30, 2026, and it was merged.

items.t: AI #2339: Fix broken internal links in JSON Object Format columns
items.b: The heading restructuring introduced as part of the 1.4 release renamed and relocated several headings in JSON Object Format columns (Schema Structure → Object Schema Structure, Object Example repositioned under {ColumnName} Object). ijurica's pull request fixed six internal links in JSON Object Format columns broken by the 1.4 heading restructuring, plus two schema anchors with an extra path segment. Matt-Cowsert checked all eight targets and confirmed no other files had the broken anchors. The change was editorial; members approved it on May 7, 2026, and it merged.

items.t: AI #2334: Align remaining normative requirement inconsistencies with updated guidelines
items.b: This PR intentionally does not address all issues listed in the original task and also includes several additional consistency updates that were not explicitly identified there. Additionally, most Metadata guideline-alignment updates were intentionally deferred. ijurica opened this PR to fix a subset of normative wording inconsistencies found in the 1.4 review (#2334), such as replacing actor-based subjects like "data generator" with state-based wording, swapping "if" for "when" and splitting multi-part requirements, with most metadata changes deferred. shawnalpay and ijurica reworked BillingPeriodStatus and InvoiceIssueStatus into parallel previous-status phrasing, and agreed to leave some process verbs in dataset completeness for now. kk09v warned that removing the data generator from a Tags requirement changed its meaning, and questioned verbs in SkuPriceId. Matt-Cowsert restored dropped links. jpradocueva noted the IP review period and said the Tags and delivery handling changes bordered on non-editorial, acceptable only with unanimous agreement. Members approved it without objections on May 7, 2026, and it merged in May 2026.

items.t: AI #2348: Graduate dataset presence requirements to data model level
items.b: This pull request centralizes the dataset presence requirements into the primary `data_model.md` file. shawnalpay's PR moved the rules for when each dataset must be present out of the individual dataset files into one section of data_model.md, with minor phrasing cleanups. jpradocueva first requested changes because the file lacked the entity type and sections the requirements model needs, then approved. After normative edits, approvals were reset under the 1.5 practice and Matt-Cowsert re-approved. Members approved it on May 14, 2026, and it was merged.

items.t: AI #2350: Add Conditions to the spec
items.b: _No response_ shawnalpay opened this PR to replace inline conditional wording such as "when the service provider supports X" with 25 formal, verifiable Condition files, linked from the dataset tables, plus an Operating Model glossary term in place of mixed references to providers and generators. After feedback shawnalpay shortened the terms to "Operating model" and "Condition". ijurica suggested consistent Includes or Supports names, a capability-centred Operating Model definition, and letting providers expose a value when only one exists, which shawnalpay partly deferred to #2375. A Baseline condition was struck to be proposed separately, and ContractedCost and ChargeFrequency changes moved to #2374 and #2375. Matt-Cowsert requested editorial fixes, and jpradocueva noted requirements-model assumptions needing validation. Members approved it without objections on May 28, 2026, and it merged in May 2026.

items.t: AI #2359: Add `Principal ID` column to `Cost and Usage` dataset
items.b: This PR introduces the `PrincipalId` column to the Cost and Usage dataset, identifying the `principal`: an entity defined in an identity and access management model (e.g., user, service account) to which access to resources or services is granted. shawnalpay proposed a PrincipalId column identifying the identity and access principal behind a charge, first paired with a ConsumerId column. ijurica pushed to align terminology and link the work to the broader AI attribution request #2018, and reviewers debated authenticated versus authorized, nullability and plain-text PII. Matt-Cowsert took over the PR in June 2026 while shawnalpay was away; ConsumerId moved to draft #2495 and a delivery grain idea was deferred. When udam-stitcher proposed a richer Principal object with names and emails, Maintainers decided in July 2026 to keep one IAM-based identifier, with details in a companion column on #2553. flanakin questioned what the IncludesPrincipals condition meant, and the final version keyed presence on requester attribution. Members approved it without objections on 10 September 2026, and it was merged.

items.t: AI #2361: Add Recommended Values to `UnitFormat` attribute
items.b: This PR expands the `UnitFormat` attribute's recommended count-based units to better support AI, ML, and modern SaaS billing constructs. It introduces six new unit types commonly used in GenAI and agentic workflows (such as image generation, document intelligence, and asynchronous fine-tuning). shawnalpay proposed adding six count-based units for AI, ML and SaaS billing, such as Image, Page and Session, to the UnitFormat recommended values (#2361), plus a Description column. Matt-Cowsert asked for consistent, non-circular descriptions and for Token, Job and Session not to be tied to AI; shawnalpay broadened them. A note rewording from jpradocueva was left for a separate editorial pull request. It was merged in May 2026.

items.t: AI #2378: Make `Service Category` descriptions technology-category-agnostic
items.b: This PR is re-scoped to the technology-category-agnostic cleanup only. It rewrites the existing `ServiceCategory` descriptions that referred to "cloud" so they apply equally to hybrid, SaaS, and on-premises environments, and moves `Multicloud` into alphabetical position. It is editorial and strictly backward-compatible: no allowed values are added, removed, or renamed. shawnalpay opened this PR, under #2377, to make Service Category apply beyond cloud. Early drafts added values such as Hardware, Software Licensing, Telecommunications and Facilities; Matt-Cowsert and mike-finopsorg argued Hardware overlapped Compute, Storage and Networking, so it was struck, and flanakin asked whether licenses and support belong in the category they serve. shawnalpay assigned the PR to ThavronNan during a leave. In July 2026 Task Force 1 split it (#2504): Matt-Cowsert re-scoped this PR to rewording five cloud-specific descriptions and reordering Multicloud, with no value changes, and moved the expansion to #2518. After approvals from Matt-Cowsert, davidearney and jpradocueva, Members approved it on July 23, 2026, and it was merged.

items.t: FR #2315: Add AllocatedServiceName column
items.b: Adds `AllocatedServiceName` as a new Conditional column to the Cost and Usage dataset to address a gap created by the origin-preservation requirement in `DataGeneratorCalculatedSplitCostAllocationHandling`. thecloudman proposed an AllocatedServiceName column because split cost allocation rules keep the origin ServiceName on allocated rows, so the consuming service, such as EKS running on EC2, could not be queried by name. ijurica found older gaps in the split cost allocation attribute, which thecloudman moved to #2515, and the appendix queries and requirements model rules were pulled out, the latter to #2554. Asked whether the need was AWS-specific, thecloudman found the service swap pattern was but argued for a FOCUS column anyway. flanakin approved while calling the whole Allocated column pattern tech debt. A requirement tying values to existing ServiceName values, raised by flanakin and kk09v, went to a follow-on PR by kk09v. Members approved it on 6 August 2026, and it was merged that month.

items.t: AI #2397: Address Spec-only issues identified during Spec–RM (v.1.4) comparison
items.b: This PR performs Spec-only cleanup addressing minor issues identified during the Spec–RM comparison, with no impact on RM. An editorial cleanup from the 1.4 specification versus Requirements Model comparison: ijurica removed a stray blank line in the custom column handling rules and standardised ContractCommitmentID to ContractCommitmentId in contract commitment examples. One reference in a requirement was left unchanged because fixing it would also need a Requirements Model update. Matt-Cowsert and jpradocueva approved, and it was merged in May 2026 after approval at the May 21 members' call.

items.t: Feedback #2419: Correct Payment Currency Feature Level in Invoice Detail overview table
items.b: The Invoice Detail dataset columns overview table lists the Payment Currency Feature Level as Mandatory, which contradicts the rest of the spec, where Payment Currency is Conditional: Payment Currency column definition Content Constraints: `Feature level: Conditional`; Invoice Detail presence requirement: "InvoiceDetail MUST include PaymentCurrency when the invoice issuer supports billing and payment in different cur… Matt-Cowsert opened this editorial pull request on 28 May 2026 to correct the Invoice Detail overview table, which listed Payment Currency's feature level as Mandatory while the column definition, normative requirement and Requirements Model all say Conditional. ijurica, beau-finopsorg and shawnalpay approved it on 28 May 2026, and jpradocueva noted group approval at the Members' call on 28 May 2026. It was merged the same day, resolving #2419.

items.t: AI #2364: Add `SKU Price` dataset
items.b: This PR introduces the SKU Price dataset, establishing a standardized schema for cloud provider catalog rates, internal multipliers, negotiated unit prices, and quantity-based tiers. Pull request #2424, by shawnalpay, added a SKU Price dataset for rate cards, negotiated prices and quantity tiers (#2364); Matt-Cowsert carried it during shawnalpay's leave from June 2026. TF-1 chose a current-snapshot model, renamed volume tiers to quantity tiers, dropped ChargeFrequency and kept commitment-discount signals out of prices. The price structure swung: UnitPriceCategory rows, then separate list and contracted price columns, then in September a single unit price column so each price keeps its own dates. deejacruz proposed extending UnitPriceCategory, and thecloudman flagged reused column IDs with different nullability. In October shawnalpay accepted making SkuPriceId tier-unique despite adoption concerns. flanakin's sustained objection at the 8 October Members meeting was met by #2752 marking the dataset as preview, and Members approved it on 29 October 2026.

items.t: AI #2431: Fix incorrect Allows Nulls value for HostProviderName in CostAndUsage column table
items.b: The Allows Nulls property for HostProviderName is incorrectly set in the CostAndUsage dataset column table overview. It is currently set to False, which conflicts with the normative requirements and Content Constraints for HostProviderName, where it is defined as True. ijurica corrected the Cost and Usage overview table, which said HostProviderName did not allow nulls, contradicting the column's own constraints and requirements. Matt-Cowsert confirmed the fix matched the column definition, and jpradocueva noted it did not affect the Requirements Model. Members approved it without objections on 4 June 2026, and it was merged.

items.t: FR #2325: Restore user-defined tag key preservation requirement to Tags column
items.b: Restores a normative requirement — removed in PR #691 — that user-defined tag keys in the `Tags` column faithfully represent the keys entered at the source. Originating feedback #2322 (TI724) surfaced the gap: Azure exports represent the same logical key as `Application`, `APPLICATION`, and `application` within a single dataset, forcing every consumer to implement defensive case-insensitive matching. Pull request #2434, by thecloudman, restored a requirement, dropped in #691, that user-defined tag keys match the keys provided, after feedback (#2322) that Azure exports showed one key in several casings. Maintainers framed it as fidelity to user input, not normalization. flanakin and thecloudman flagged that 'at the source' clashed with the Tag Source glossary term, so Matt-Cowsert's 'provided keys' wording was adopted; flanakin's worry that the prefix exception left prefixed keys unconstrained was also fixed. ijurica asked to revert requirements-model file changes as out of scope, and TF-2 moved the key-casing explanation into supporting content. jpradocueva's question about the normative subject was deferred to AI #2535. Members approved it on 6 August 2026.

items.t: FR #2018: AI model identity as SkuPriceDetails properties
items.b: Implements Approach A for FR #2018 (AI model identity and token consumption), tracked under AI #2417. It defines the model-identity dimensions as FOCUS-defined properties of `SkuPriceDetails`, and adds a worked appendix example. The naming and scoping questions raised in review are settled per the 2026-06-17 TF2 decision (see Naming and placement below), and the PR is out of draft. Matt-Cowsert's pull request (#2018) added AI model identity as FOCUS-defined SkuPriceDetails properties, not new columns, with an appendix example. shawnalpay asked why it used "Model" rather than the more general "Product"; Matt-Cowsert argued FOCUS had already retired a general producer column, PublisherName, and TF2 kept Model in June 2026. For the maker key, ModelProvider and ModelAuthor were set aside as too close to the deprecated Provider and Publisher terms, and Matt-Cowsert chose ModelDeveloper, which thecloudman backed with an app store analogy. davidearney questioned ModelId differing between sellers, so its description was clarified as seller-namespaced. TF2 dropped ModelVariant in July 2026 because market naming was unsettled. Members approved it on July 16, 2026, and it merged that month.

items.t: Part 3 of #2315: Add split cost allocation field mapping
items.b: Adds a new appendix section - Examples: Split Cost Allocation Field Mapping - providing a complete column-by-column reference implementation for the row-splitting transformation a data generator must perform when mapping native billing data into FOCUS split allocation rows. thecloudman's pull request, part 3 of #2315, added an appendix example mapping provider-native split cost allocation data, which puts all consumers on one row, to FOCUS origin and allocated charge rows. Matt-Cowsert flagged inconsistent BilledCost figures, a reservation narrative that conflicted with column definitions, broken anchors, a missing ConsumedUnit, AllocatedMethodId nullability, and a cross-provider note that #2395 did not support. jpradocueva posted findings from an AI-assisted validation skill. thecloudman remodelled the reservation as a commitment discount, dropped the cross-provider case and an invented native export schema, and populated AllocatedMethodId on the origin row while #2578 stayed open. ijurica asked for glossary terms instead of "consumer" and removal of notes citing issues, and Matt-Cowsert noted that adding CommitmentDiscountId required further columns. Members approved it and it merged in August 2026.

items.t: AI #2239: Validate spec components during build
items.b: (Add a summary of your PR here. Use of AI assistance is encouraged; once you have created your pull request, take a copy of the diff by appending `.diff` to the end of the PR URL, provide it an LLM, and edit this section to include the output.) Pull request #2510, by mike-finopsorg, was repository maintenance adding a pytest stage to the spec build that checks JSON blocks, JSON schemas, internal links and SQL examples, and fixing broken links the tests found. Matt-Cowsert ran the suite, confirmed it passed after automated review findings were addressed, and noted the description understated the test files. Members approved it on 30 July 2026.

items.t: AI #2530: Split the compound duration format bullet in ContractCommitmentDurationType
items.b: Assignee(s): @Matt-Cowsert Parent Issue: #1057 For #2530, Matt-Cowsert replaced a compound SHOULD bullet in ContractCommitmentDurationType with one format requirement, leaving quantity and unit detail to the Expected Format section; the matching fix for PurchaseDurationType was in #2424. kk09v wanted the time units linked to Unit Format and questioned Quarter; Matt-Cowsert kept them separate, adding a note, and sent the Quarter question to #2600. Members approved it in August 2026.

items.t: AI #2547: Add `Requester Details` and `Credential ID` columns to `Cost and Usage` dataset
items.b: This PR adds `RequesterDetails` and `CredentialId` to the Cost and Usage dataset, completing the three-column shape Maintainers converged on 2026-08-03. `PrincipalId`, which merged on PR #2360 on 2026-09-10, carries the principal to which access is granted. `CredentialId` carries the credential presented on the request that produced the charge. Matt-Cowsert opened this PR to add CredentialId and a JSON RequesterDetails column to Cost and Usage, completing the three-column requester model Maintainers settled on 3 August 2026 alongside PrincipalId from #2360. The details column was renamed several times before becoming RequesterDetails. flanakin pressed for explicit PII warnings, but TF-2 kept a single dataset-level note. udam-stitcher doubted a free-form object would work; Matt-Cowsert pointed to its strict published schema and applied most of udam-stitcher's wording changes. TF-2 ruled that RequesterDetails must not be null when either identifier is present, and the wider question of when details columns may be null went to #2718. The PR also revised PrincipalId nullability. Members approved it without objections on 24 September 2026, and it was merged.

items.t: AI #2562: Revisit ListCost, ListUnitPrice, ContractedCost, ContractedUnitPrice specs - Part 1
items.b: This PR clarifies the pricing model and the semantics of List and Contracted pricing metrics by consolidating pricing-related operating model conditions and explicitly defining which pricing and cost impacts are reflected in each metric. ijurica proposed revising ListUnitPrice, ContractedUnitPrice, ListCost and ContractedCost: removing two operating model conditions, calling List pricing service-provider-suggested rather than published, and separating negotiated pricing terms, reflected in Contracted metrics, from commitment discount effects, reflected in neither. The scope grew to SKU and pricing currency columns. Proposed glossary terms for unit price adjustments and post-pricing discounts were dropped after the August 10, 2026 maintainers meeting. Matt-Cowsert and jpradocueva flagged conflicting rules on credit rows, and Task Force 1 kept an unqualified rule that cost columns match for Tax and Credit charges. marc-perreaut questioned terms such as service-provider-suggested, flanakin proposed simpler wording, and udam-stitcher felt the aligned usage sentences undersold Billed and Effective Cost; ijurica kept most wording. The group agreed it on October 8, 2026, and it merged the next day.

items.t: FR #2130: Remove duplicative cost-formula requirement from PricingQuantity
items.b: This PR removes the duplicative cost-formula requirement from `PricingQuantity`. ijurica's pull request (#2130) removed a cost-formula requirement from PricingQuantity that duplicated ListCost and ContractedCost, following the approach of #2067. Matt-Cowsert noted that #1967 had since written this don't-repeat-yourself rule into the contributor guidelines, and jpradocueva and thecloudman also approved. Members approved it without objection on August 13, 2026, and it merged.

items.t: [AI] #2425: Add conditions to Content Constraints tables
items.b: This PR updates the Content Constraints tables throughout the specification to explicitly identify conditional column dependencies by populating the Conditions column where applicable. jpradocueva's pull request (#2425) began filling the Conditions row of Content Constraints tables, giving three template examples: no condition ("Not applicable"), one condition, and several. ijurica suggested dropping "Recommended when" because the feature level already says so, and kk09v agreed. flanakin asked about "None" versus "Not applicable" and how multi-row conditions render in the PDF. Members approved it on September 3, 2026, and it merged.

items.t: FR #2709: Require canonical largest-whole-unit form for ContractCommitmentDurationType
items.b: `ContractCommitmentDurationType` allows more than one conformant spelling of the same term: `"1 Year"` and `"12 Months"` are both valid for a one-year commitment, as are `"1 Week"` and `"7 Days"`. Providers selling identical terms can emit different strings, so cross-provider grouping splits one term into several buckets. flanakin proposed, for FR #2709, requiring ContractCommitmentDurationType to use the largest whole time unit, so 12 Months becomes 1 Year and providers group consistently. Matt-Cowsert noted that with Quarter allowed, the spec's own 3 Months examples would break; Task Force 1 dropped Quarter on September 1, 2026, accepting flanakin's view that it implies calendar or fiscal alignment, and adopted UnitFormat's time units. After kk09v asked about UnitFormat, Week and a general largest-unit SHOULD were added there. shawnalpay asked for the MUST to be scoped so it did not override the existing SHOULDs. rileyjenk wished for ISO 8601 durations, which flanakin called a breaking change worth revisiting for 2.0. A SKU consistency case moved to #2424. The group agreed it on October 1, 2026, and it was merged.

items.t: AI #1941: Add AI model billing examples and supported feature
items.b: Adds appendix examples and a supported feature entry for usage-based billing of AI model APIs, addressing FR #1941. No columns are added or changed; the examples show that existing Cost and Usage columns already carry token billing. ljadvey proposed appendix examples and a supported feature for usage-based AI model API billing under #1941, to show that existing Cost and Usage columns already carried token billing. Task force 2 kept all the scenarios in one pull request, with finops-DaveMoreau co-assigned. Matt-Cowsert questioned priced cached output tokens and the use of TokenType before #2606 defined it; #2606 replaced it with TokenDirection and TokenCacheAction, which the examples adopted. thecloudman and Matt-Cowsert found conformance errors in the drawdown example, which ljadvey fixed. finops-DaveMoreau proposed regrouping the examples, then withdrew it for a lighter table change. ijurica argued the two marketplace examples did not fit the FOCUS marketplace definition, and they were reworked with the model developer as seller. The group agreed it on October 8 and it merged in October 2026.

items.t: FR #2099: Distinguish cached from uncached token costs
items.b: Implements FR #2099, the feature request to distinguish cached from uncached token costs, by adding two FOCUS-defined `SkuPriceDetails` properties, `TokenCacheAction` and `TokenDirection`, each with allowed values, plus a worked appendix example and two example queries under the Resource Usage supported feature. No new columns. Matt-Cowsert's pull request (#2099) separated cached from uncached AI token costs using SkuPriceDetails properties, following #2442. In September 2026 TF2 replaced the single TokenType property with TokenCacheAction and TokenDirection, the first FOCUS-defined properties with allowed values; iwasinnam2 backed the token-specific names. flanakin asked that output rows and SKUs without caching not carry the cache property, which was adopted. thecloudman questioned a composite scenario, and ijurica and jpradocueva criticized a cache cost efficiency query, which was removed. Token, AI Model and Prompt Cache glossary entries were added. shawnalpay requested simpler wording for prose that seemed AI-generated, and many suggestions were applied. The group agreed to it on October 1, 2026, and it merged October 2.

items.t: AI #2550: Scope the `CurrencyFormat` virtual currency allowance to consumption currency
items.b: `CurrencyFormat` lists virtual currency as one of two allowed currency types in its preamble, while its requirements mandate an ISO 4217:2015 three-letter alphabetic code for every value. ISO 4217:2015 defines no code for a provider-issued currency, so no virtual currency value can satisfy both halves of the attribute. Matt-Cowsert opened this PR to fix a contradiction in the CurrencyFormat attribute, which allowed virtual currency but required ISO 4217 codes for every value, a leftover from the 1.4 refactor. The fix required ISO codes only for national currencies, barred them otherwise, and limited PricingCurrency to national or consumption currencies, keeping cryptocurrency out. shawnalpay asked that examples avoid the word "token", reserved for a unit of measure, so the sample currency became OmniBucks. ijurica flagged circular wording in the conditions, which was reworked, and Matt-Cowsert concluded that UnitFormat's token references could stay. TF-1 agreed in September 2026 to rename the IncludesVirtualCurrency condition to IncludesConsumptionCurrency here. The group agreed the PR on 1 October 2026, and it was merged.

items.t: AI #2616: Revise Compute Service Category and split Virtual Machines subcategory
items.b: This PR revises the Compute `ServiceCategory` description and splits the `Virtual Machines` `ServiceSubcategory` into `Bare Metal` and `Virtual Machines`. ijurica proposed adding physical compute to the Compute category and splitting the Virtual Machines subcategory into Bare Metal and Virtual Machines, depending on whether a provider-managed hypervisor is present. Matt-Cowsert noted that dedicated hosts fit neither row, so ijurica kept wording placing them under Virtual Machines, and shawnalpay had "high-performance" dropped. thecloudman approved but noted the requirements model lacked Bare Metal. Members approved it in September 2026 and it merged.

items.t: AI #2587: Remove repeated condition links from the dataset files

Repeated condition links in the Requirements lists are converted to plain text, keeping the link on the first occurrence of each condition reference (AI #2587).; 2. This editorial PR by ijurica removed repeated condition links from the dataset files, keeping one per condition, and dropped condition links from overview table cells because multi-condition columns linked only one (#2441). Matt-Cowsert noted column files did not yet state their conditions, which ijurica said #2580 addressed; the PR was retargeted to stand alone rather than depend on #2567. Members approved it on 3 September 2026, and it was merged.

items.t: AI #2614: Reconcile reused SkuPriceIds in the commitment discount example data
items.b: Seven of the ten SkuPriceId values in the commitment discount example data each named more than one price point, so no rate card could describe all of them at once. This corrects the example data so every SkuPriceId names exactly one price point, and states the granularity rule where an example author will find it. Matt-Cowsert opened this for #2614 because seven of ten SkuPriceId values in the commitment discount example data each named several price points. It split them into 24 single-price-point identifiers, aligned rates, and added granularity guidance plus two new Cost and Usage SkuPriceId requirements. flanakin approved but saw one requirement as duplicating the SKU Price key; Matt-Cowsert replied they constrained different things. It was approved and merged in September 2026.

items.t: FR #2315: (Replace #2612) Enhance normative requirements for AllocatedServiceName
items.b: This pull request changes the AllocatedServiceName requirements in the Cost and Usage dataset, as part of feature request #2315. It replaces #2612. kk09v proposed, for FR #2315 and replacing #2612, making AllocatedServiceName follow AllocatedMethodId for nullability, so the unallocated portion of a split carries a value, and adding a SHOULD to match the generator's ServiceName. kk09v compared how AWS and GCP report unallocated Kubernetes costs. ijurica questioned which value the unallocated row should take, thecloudman proposed a carve-out for multi-service splits, and shawnalpay queried the phrase "independently billed". Matt-Cowsert and thecloudman noted the rule also reached retained origin rows, left open in #2515. On September 30, 2026 Task Force 2 removed a MUST about the unallocated row after ijurica showed it could never fail; it may return in 1.6. beau-finopsorg queried the removal. The group agreed the PR on October 1, 2026, and it was merged.

items.b: This PR serves solely as a preview and discussion base and is not intended for merging into the working draft. ijurica opened this pull request as a preview, never meant to merge, setting original and candidate normative requirements for every column side by side for work item #557. Reviewers claimed columns through a spreadsheet and commented per file: ljadvey and smokemonster99 approved many columns, smokemonster99 queried requirements that seemed dropped (ijurica explained the new inclusive and exclusive charge period bounds), and davehatcher flagged inconsistent RegionId wording. shawnalpay proposed standard phrasing such as "adheres to the following additional requirements", which ijurica applied across the board. flanakin preferred requirements at root level rather than nested under presence, and cnharris10 favored general requirements followed by special cases. Open questions went to #719. shawnalpay closed it in February 2025 after the work moved into #787 and #798.

items.t: WI #556: Corrections - Credits - Refunds
items.b: ahullah drafted correction, credit and refund content for work item #556. ijurica set out options for extending ChargeClass Correction to open billing periods, and reviewers questioned credit definitions, the accounting sense of close, and whether refunds always stem from errors. Still in draft at the March 2025 freeze, it was postponed to 1.3. shawnalpay closed it in July 2025, with its content to be ported into #1151.

items.t: WI #534: Add Commitment Discount Unit Price and Cost columns
items.b: Authored by @qquigley and @cnharris10. cnharris10 and qquigley proposed CommitmentDiscountUnitPrice and CommitmentDiscountCost columns to break down pre- and post-negotiated discounted costs for forecasting. aws-letianfeng suggested a gross effective cost style column instead, and udam-f2 called it a niche case that would burden providers without commitments, suggesting a commitment properties column or SkuPriceDetails key. It was closed without merging in July 2025 after shawnalpay asked whether to close or repurpose it for #961, citing merge conflicts.

items.t: WI #647: Adds `Amortization Class` column
items.b: refs #647 JGrubb proposed a column, first AmortizationCategory and later AmortizationClass, marking amortized purchases and the rows they were spread across so savings calculations from ListCost and ContractedCost would not double count. shawnalpay floated widening it to commitment eligibility (#406), udam-f2 and GrinsteadJ raised negotiated burndowns and SaaS prepaid credits, GrinsteadJ suggesting Payment Category, and ijurica preferred reusing PricingCategory. A naming poll (#817) favored AmortizationClass, and flanakin held that other double-counting scenarios needed separate columns. aws-letianfeng requested wording changes for upfront-paid capacity blocks, and rileyjenk and UdamDewaraja requested changes, calling the name misleading and the scope too narrow for SaaS. After objections at the March 2025 Members meeting, maintainers pushed it to 1.3, and it was closed without merging in July 2025 to revisit in a future release.

items.t: WI #616: Addition of `Pricing Currency` and `Pricing Currency to Billing Currency` columns
items.b: This pull request creates two new columns for addition in the FOCUS specification: `PricingCurrency`: virtual currency (e.g. tokens, credits) for providers with virtual currency usage charges, and fiat currency (e.g. USD, EUR) otherwise; `PricingCurrencyToBillingCurrency`: the conversion factor from Pricing Currency to Billing Currency shawnalpay proposed two columns for work item #616: PricingCurrency, covering virtual currencies such as tokens or credits as well as government-issued ones, and PricingCurrencyToBillingCurrency, a conversion factor. The PR also widened CurrencyCodeFormat into CurrencyFormat and denominated list and contracted unit prices in the pricing currency. After TF3 discussion it dropped earlier Pricing Denomination names. flanakin called fiat jargon, wanted calculations kept in billing currency, suggested a shorter name such as BillingExchangeRate and asked about the exchange-rate date; shawnalpay defended self-documenting names and questioned needing the date. ijurica raised Microsoft mappings and presence options and noted #318 had proposed almost the same thing. amitkinha approved. shawnalpay closed it in March 2025, replaced by #848, which renamed the rate column Pricing To Billing Exchange Rate and used national instead of fiat.

items.t: WI #616: Provider, Publisher, Invoice Issuer, Datagenerator Consistency Refactor
items.b: As we have reviewed the changes to Host Provider I have observed the following: The spec is not internally consistant when using the word provider and the definition is confusing comparing it to Publisher; The metadata section for ProviderVersion is problematic because it is not specific; The introduction of Host Provider by naming may appear to be a sub class of provider, no hierarchy is intended, it is more specifi… rileyjenk proposed refactoring the definitions of provider, publisher, invoice issuer and data generator, citing inconsistent use of provider and a Host Provider name implying hierarchy. shawnalpay noted host relationships could be many-to-many, ijurica suggested reviewing display names, and GrinsteadJ argued for multiple data generators and an optional HostProvider. Maintainers limited it to definition clarifications. It closed in March 2025, split into #839 and #843, leftovers going to a work item.

items.t: P i h d refining definitions and usage
FR #962: Correction Handling Augmentation
items.b: Before specifying the objective of this PR, it is important to highlight the mismatch between: The current formal FOCUS definition of *Correction*, and; The actual usage of the term in discussions and draft implementations. ijurica proposed formalising a broader meaning of correction, covering any update to a previously generated charge whatever its invoicing status, through scenarios, examples, column requirements and a new CorrectionHandling attribute that would bar replacement-style corrections after a billing period closed. The task force agreed to rename restatement to replacement. It was closed without merging in August 2025 as a demonstration pull request, superseded by #1241, #1242, #1245 and #1368.

items.t: FR #982: Clarify EffectiveCost column semantics across all use cases
items.b: This PR aims to clarify the semantics of the EffectiveCost column to ensure accurate and consistent interpretation across all use cases. ijurica proposed clarifying the definition and requirements of EffectiveCost under #982, and built a sample dataset of standalone and prepaid-coverage scenarios. ijurica disputed a proposal describing BilledCost as accrual-based, calling it invoice-based; UdamDewaraja suggested separating or unifying amortization and drawdown cases, and cnharris10 found the text overly complex and asked for examples. It was closed without merging in September 2025, removed from 1.3 to revisit in 1.4.

items.t: FR #982: Clarifying EffectiveCost Definition
items.b: Modifying the effective cost description to ensure clarity that effective cost is to include amortization of upfront fees, reoccurring fees, and non-prepaid fees. rileyjenk drafted a change to the EffectiveCost description to make clear it includes amortized upfront fees, recurring fees and non-prepaid fees, for FR #982. shawnalpay gave process feedback: the PDF build failed on smart quotes, and the PR lacked an FR prefix and a full description. rileyjenk closed it without merging in August 2025 and moved the content into #1239.

items.t: AI #1311: Add Contract columns to Cost and Usage dataset (second draft)
items.b: This PR adds the following columns to the Cost and Usage dataset: `Contract ID`: the unique identifier of the contract representing one or more commitments associated with discounts negotiated between the provider and the customer; `Contract Applied`: a set of four datapoints that associate a charge to one or more contract commitments, denoted as key-value pairs in JSON format; `Contract Commitment ID`: The unique id… shawnalpay's second draft, following #1327, added ContractId and a ContractApplied JSON column to the Cost and Usage dataset to link charges to contract commitments. cnharris10 asked why a JSON object was preferred over four dedicated columns, and rileyjenk noted the key-value format could not show two commitments applying to one charge without arrays. It was closed without merging in August 2025 in favour of the more holistic #1350.

items.t: FR #962: Adding Correction Handling attribute
items.b: Note: This PR addresses part of the scope defined in FR #962. ijurica proposed a Correction Handling attribute for FR #962, setting rules for how corrections appear depending on whether original records were invoiced and whether data is delivered by replacement or append-only. jasonwucp asked which corrections are handled by restating past months. rileyjenk argued for a fundamental rethink: let data generators correct data whatever the mechanism, with separate rules for billed cost in closed and open periods, usage and EffectiveCost, and non-cost fields. shawnalpay asked that a normative requirement use the attribute and that invoice rules move to an Invoice Handling attribute from #1321; flanakin doubted invoice requirements belonged in a cost dataset. SatyaVandrangi1 questioned strict immutability, since invoices can be cancelled and reissued. In October 2025 shawnalpay closed it in favour of #1501, a heavy refactor done with ijurica.

items.t: AI #1838: Add TagDetails column to CostAndUsage
items.b: PR for #1124 introducing the TagDetails column kk09v proposed a TagDetails JSON column for FR #1124, recording tag provenance, inherited ancestor tags and untagged but taggable sources to support tag-coverage analysis. items.t: AI #1914: Reclassify unit price columns from Metric to Dimension
items.b: Reclassifies 4 unit price columns from Metric to Dimension. Unit prices are not summable and conflict with aggregation semantics — summing unit prices when rows are aggregated produces meaningless values. flanakin proposed reclassifying four unit price columns from Metric to Dimension because summing unit prices produces meaningless values, splitting the change out of #1816. shawnalpay noted it was outside 1.4 scope and that aggregation includes averages, min and max; udam-stitcher and aws-jrmarks argued unit prices are non-additive metrics used in calculations. Maintainers agreed to keep them as metrics, and shawnalpay closed it without merging in February 2026.

items.t: AI #1985: Restructure the JSON Object normative text to be more inline with Requirements Modelling - Option 1
items.b: This PR proposes restructuring the normative text for JSON Objects to align better with requirements modeling. It organizes the content into a hierarchical structure—separating requirements, object details, and column definitions—and moves detailed example scenarios to the appendix. This approach focuses on clarifying and organizing the existing textual definitions without introducing a new schema format. mike-finopsorg proposed restructuring the normative text for JSON object columns into a clearer hierarchy, as a text-based alternative to the JSON Schema approach in #2007. shawnalpay suggested placing object requirements next to column requirements, which mike-finopsorg adopted, and trialled the structure on a column from #1924; mike-finopsorg wondered whether JSON Schema would simplify the text. Maintainers chose #2007 instead, and it was closed without merging in February 2026.

items.t: AI #2359: Add `Consumer ID` column to `Cost and Usage` dataset
items.b: This PR introduces the `ConsumerId` column to the Cost and Usage dataset, identifying the `consumer`: the party a charge is attributed to for allocation, chargeback, or showback (e.g., end-user, application, autonomous agent). A `consumer` is distinct from the `principal` a service provider grants access to, and need not be an entity in that provider's identity and access management model. Matt-Cowsert split the ConsumerId column out of #2360 into this stacked pull request, to be picked up after PrincipalId lands. It was reworked in July 2026 to fit the revised principal definition. Open questions covered the consumer definition, moving IncludesConsumers to Allocation, and customer-supplied identifiers. ijurica proposed capability-based nullability wording; shawnalpay held changes pending wider discussion. The pull request is closed, but the thread doesn't record the final wording.

items.t: [Staging] FR #2492: Revisit specifications for ListCost, ListUnitPrice, ContractedCost, and ContractedUnitPrice
items.b: This PR addresses multiple related issues under FR #2492, affecting the same set of columns (`ListCost`, `ContractedCost`, `ListUnitPrice`, `ContractedUnitPrice`), in a single PR to make it easier to track how the changes interact across this column set. The underlying issues have been grouped into Action Items, each addressed in its own section below. ijurica opened a staging PR for FR #2492 to revise ListCost, ListUnitPrice, ContractedCost and ContractedUnitPrice together, saying it was not meant to merge as a whole; each agreed action item would be split into its own PR. Changes tied unit prices to SKU Price ID rather than SKU, reworked which discounts ContractedUnitPrice includes, and added wording on threshold-based tiered pricing. flanakin found the wording too complex and argued the negotiated-versus-public split did not separate what these columns needed. udam-stitcher offered simpler definitions, which ijurica accepted. In July 2026 TF1 agreed tiered pricing is a pricing mechanism rather than a discount, so contract commitment examples should stop calling it a discount, and the glossary umbrella term was renamed. ijurica closed it in August 2026 in favour of #2567 and #2564.

items.t: AI #2504: Expand Service Category allowed values for on-premises, SaaS, and physical infrastructure
items.b: This PR carries the `ServiceCategory` expansion that was split out of #2379 per TF1's decision (AI #2504). It extends the taxonomy to cover on-premises, SaaS, licensing, labor, and physical infrastructure so practitioners can classify these costs without defaulting to "Other". Matt-Cowsert opened this pull request on 7 July 2026 to add seven ServiceCategory values, such as Facilities, Software Licensing and Telecommunications, and to name physical infrastructure in Compute, Networking and Storage. ijurica questioned whether the Multicloud name fits its broadened description and argued bare-metal does not belong in the Compute description. On 17 August 2026 maintainers moved it to the 1.6 milestone for reassessment. It remains open.

items.t: FR #2712: Clarify the charge period scope of AllocatedRatio
items.b: The AllocatedMethodDetailsObject requirements say `AllocatedRatio` "MUST represent the allocated charge's percentage of the origin charge" and that the sum "across all allocated charges related to a single origin charge MUST be equal to 1 (100%)", but never state the charge period over which the ratio applies. Pull request #2713, opened as a draft by thecloudman on 22 September 2026, resolves #2712 by stating the charge period over which AllocatedRatio applies. It ties both requirements to the allocated charge's ChargePeriodStart and ChargePeriodEnd and adds an informative note on finer-grained calculation. The author expects the wording may change once #2515 and #2578 settle the origin-row model. The thread is still open and records no outcome. items.t: FR #2779: Tag entity references semantically across the specification
items.b: Today the specification source marks references to entities (columns, glossary terms, attributes, operating model conditions, datasets, allowed values, JSON objects and schemas, and metadata fields) with formatting alone: a hand-typed anchor link on the first mention in a file, italics for glossary terms, and plain text for ColumnIds. This PR tries the alternative proposed in #2779 on the whole specification. On 3 November 2026 finops-DaveMoreau opened draft pull request #2819, resolving #2779, to tag references to entities semantically across the specification instead of relying on formatting. A build resolver turns the tags into ordinary Markdown, and a generated registry checks them, reporting inconsistencies rather than fixing them. No review outcome is recorded. The pull request is still open, awaiting Working Group decisions on several questions.
