The fix in #828 waited on whether #675 would make version 1.2; when shawnalpay judged that unlikely, thecloudman was told to proceed without it. The group suggested removing the editor's note and adding a note to the supporting document, and shawnalpay closed the item in March 2025 after confirming with thecloudman.

items.t: [AI] Strike extra row in Billing Account Type and Sub Account Type
[Editorial] 1.2 Consistency Review
items.b: shawnalpay opened this March 2025 issue as a running list of 1.2 consistency review tasks, such as file naming, CSV examples, a stray table row and the changelog, each spun off into its own action item, and ijurica proposed more. At the April 7, 2025 maintainers meeting, revisiting "amortization" in EffectiveCost and settling row versus charge versus record were deferred to a future release. The thread doesn't record its closure.

items.t: [AI] Reorganize appendix section
[AI] Issue PR with grammar and typo cleanup
[AI] Create CSV section for examples
[AI] Fix wording in Commitment Discounts appendix – Usage section
[AI] Revise and align SKU and SKU Price related columns post-merge
[AI] Create Work Item to clarify inclusion logic for SkuPriceDetails: prefer FOCUS-defined over Provider-defined
[FR] Clarify guidance on including provider SKU price properties
items.b: Matt-Cowsert asked for clearer SkuPriceDetails rules, because the wording implied both a FOCUS-defined property and its provider-defined equivalent must appear, rather than preferring the FOCUS-defined one. flanakin supported it but said a PR would be better than task force time, and ijurica noted FOCUS-defined properties were new in 1.2. shawnalpay closed it as complete in September 2025 after #910 merged.

items.t: [AI] Review normative requirements of new columns
[AI] Review the spec and apply Editorial Guidelines (e.g., missing links to glossary terms, etc.).
[FR] Clarify roles of Provider, Publisher, and Invoice Issuer
items.b: Matt-Cowsert asked to clarify the ambiguous Provider, Publisher and Invoice Issuer columns, deferred from 1.2. jasonwucp urged setting breaking-change criteria first, and ijurica flagged inconsistent display names. Task Force 3 agreed in September 2025 to deprecate Provider and Publisher in favor of service provider and host provider columns, and shortened the deprecation window to one release. shawnalpay closed it in October 2025 after #1139, #1505 and #1524 were approved.

items.t: [FR] Expose host cloud provider leveraged by SaaS provider
items.b: Matt-Cowsert requested a way to show the cloud provider hosting a SaaS service such as Snowflake, which the Provider, Publisher and Invoice Issuer definitions did not capture. shawnalpay reframed it as a Host Provider request, questioned its use cases and made it depend on #1055. Matt-Cowsert later noted its scope was covered by #1139, and shawnalpay closed it as complete in October 2025 after the related PRs merged.

items.t: [FR] Clarify requirements to cover all invoiced charges in FOCUS datasets
items.b: Matt-Cowsert asked that the spec state every charge on an invoice must appear in FOCUS data, so BilledCost reconciles to the invoice. shawnalpay pressed for taxes and indirect charges such as training to be covered. TF-3 drafted an invoice handling attribute in #1321, debating SHOULD versus MUST, duplication and payable splits, and kept a single MUST. #1321 merged and the request closed as complete in September 2025.

items.t: [AI] Review PR for invoice-handling attribute with members
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this action item in August 2025 to draft an invoice-handling attribute, describing how invoiced charges relate to the FOCUS dataset, and review it with members (#1321). TF-3 asked for more specificity, chose to reference charge category requirements rather than repeat them, and parked the charge versus row debate (#1027). In August 2025 shawnalpay asked to close it once the draft was ready for member review, and Matt-Cowsert agreed.

items.t: [FR] Add support for multiple datasets within FOCUS
items.b: robmartin33 asked in May 2025 for FOCUS to be organised as related datasets, for easier use in BI tools, so finer detail could be added without bloating the main dataset. shawnalpay strongly supported it as a star schema, referencing #1006. In June 2025 the group agreed a six-week spike, ruling out a star schema for 1.3. Task Force 2 then produced design principles (#1150) and dataset definitions (#1337), rejecting fact and dimension terminology as too database-specific in favour of names like FOCUS Cost and Usage plus machine-readable IDs, and requiring datasets to be independent but joinable. Maintainers adopted dataset-level normative requirements, and #1431 tied attributes to datasets. A second dataset was left to #976 and editorial cleanup to consistency review. shawnalpay closed it as complete in October 2025.

items.t: [FR] Add support for negotiated discounts via contractual commitments
items.b: Matt-Cowsert asked FOCUS to represent contract-negotiated commitments, such as burn-down and build-up agreements, so practitioners could track progress against them; NASA, Autodesk, Atlassian, Google and others added support. Task Force 1 began in June 2025 with goals of giving each negotiated commitment an ID, linking usage to it and describing its terms. ijurica noted a single contract ID could not show drawdown against individual line items, and shawnalpay floated a mandatory Contract ID with an optional Commitment ID. shawnalpay renamed the request and opened #1327, then #1350. In August 2025 most participants favored always requiring the proposed JSON datapoints for usability, while cnharris10 and partly richkreitz prioritized dataset size. #1350 merged in September 2025, closing the request, with follow-on work in #1459.

items.t: [AI] Draft PR for Contract dataset
items.b: shawnalpay's action item was to draft a PR adding contract attributes such as start date and amount, needed to complete #976 beyond the columns in #1327. It was briefly blocked on #1090 until the August 11, 2025 Maintainers call set a direction. shawnalpay drafted #1350, revised it after TF1 feedback on contractual commitments, and closed the item in September 2025 once #1350 left draft.

items.t: [FR] Add mechanism to describe recency and completeness of FOCUS dataset
items.b: Matt-Cowsert asked for a way for data generators to state how recent and complete a FOCUS dataset is. TF-2 found the original scope hard for providers, so rileyjenk narrowed it to optional metadata with generators setting their own completeness thresholds; davidearney asked how later data changes would be handled. The work landed in #1374 and #1464, tying recency to charge period, and the issue closed as completed in October 2025.

items.t: [AI]Update PR to incorporate feedback for completeness metadata
items.b: This action item tracked revisions to the completeness metadata pull request: making completeness declarations a SHOULD, not a MUST, for data generators, and clarifying time sector requirements. Matt-Cowsert logged repeated TF-2 check-ins on rileyjenk's #1374; ijurica and vikramdesai01 questioned time sector semantics, and the group agreed time sectors apply only to usage, not billing periods. It closed as completed in September 2025 once TF-2 judged it ready for member review.

items.t: [FR] Add JSON data type and strategy for structured JSON columns
items.b: Matt-Cowsert requested a clearer JSON data type and a strategy for structured JSON columns, because the key-value format caused naming collisions, could not hold complex structures, and left unclear whether JSON or serialized strings were meant. shawnalpay first asked for examples, then pulled the work into 1.3 because the proposals for #962 and #956 used arrays of JSON objects. It was closed as completed in September 2025 after #1383 merged.

items.t: [FR] Add provider-calculated split cost allocation for provider-defined services
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this in May 2025 asking FOCUS to carry provider-calculated cost splits below the machine level, such as containers, pods and tasks, citing AWS, GCP, OCI and Azure features; many organisations registered support. shawnalpay argued the data adds rows and columns, so practitioners must be able to opt in (#1091, #1093). UdamDewaraja objected to calling it shared cost allocation, and TF-2 renamed it in July 2025. TF-2 compared split lines, double-entry rows and a secondary dataset; a poll (#1322) favoured split lines, while rileyjenk and jasonwucp worried about breaking existing reports. The group agreed allocations must reconcile to the original charge, be flagged and use a JSON details column (#1383). #1394, stewarded by kk09v and qquigley, was approved and merged in September 2025, closing the request as complete.

items.t: [AI] Create draft PR of split lines based on TF-2 discussions on 8/20
[AI] Incorpoate feedback into #PR 1394
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this action item in August 2025 to resolve review comments on #1394, about provider-calculated split cost allocation, ahead of the 1.3 release. TF-2 worked through the comments over several weeks, and qquigley asked whether a name change to allocated method details had been agreed. In September 2025 shawnalpay declared it done after members reviewed #1394 with no open threads.

items.t: [AI] Associate attributes explicitly with datasets
[FR] Augment requirements for correction-handling scenarios
items.b: Matt-Cowsert asked in May 2025 for an overarching correction-handling attribute, because correction rules were scattered across individual columns and practitioners needed to reconcile corrections with invoices. Most comments were task force updates from shawnalpay. ijurica split the work into several PRs, including #1241, #1242 and #1245 tightening existing column requirements, #1368 for the attribute and #1434 for examples. In October 2025 the maintainers deferred #1368, refactored as #1501, until an Invoice dataset (#1500) could ground rules on when data generators may revise invoiced data. By January 2026 #1501 covered both delivery handling and correction handling, and in March ijurica and rileyjenk agreed to split it further. Members merged #1434 and #1501, and shawnalpay closed the request as complete in April 2026.

items.t: [AI] Complete draft of PR for use case scenarios for correction handling
items.b: shawnalpay opened this action item for a draft pull request of example scenarios for correction handling, with candidate scenarios gathered in a shared spreadsheet. It replaced action item #756, after the group dropped #675 in favor of #1151. ijurica prepared the examples while the due date slipped several times. Once ijurica opened draft #1434, task force 1 reviewed it and the item was closed as completed in September 2025.

items.t: [AI] Convert Spreadsheet-Based Examples to CSV files as part of PR #1434 follow-up
items.b: In February 2026, ijurica opened #2020 asking for the spreadsheet-based examples linked from PR #1434 to be converted into CSV files under the specification data folder, at the latest during consistency review if that PR was approved. On 29 March 2026, shawnalpay closed the issue as complete, noting the conversion had already been done in PR #1434.

items.t: [AI] Complete draft of dataset metadata PR
[FR] Clarify commitment concepts and glossary entries
items.b: Issue #1070, opened by Matt-Cowsert in May 2025, argued that FOCUS's use of 'commitment discount' excluded negotiated commitments and assumed a burn-down model, which caused problems for SaaS. shawnalpay asked how it overlapped with #976, and ijurica gathered the existing glossary definitions. In September 2025 it was renamed and moved from 1.3 to 1.4 as tied to Contract Commitment work in #1459. It closed in March 2026, completed via #1964.

items.t: [Process] 1.3 consistency review
items.b: shawnalpay opened this issue in August 2025 to collect work for the 1.3 consistency review, planned for October 16 to 30. Contributors logged many items, each turned into an action item or pull request: adding Requirements subheaders (#1508), restructuring supporting content (#1510), replacing "term" with "duration" (#1493), JSON string versus object typing (#1480), standardizing .mdpp files (#1512), drafting changelog entries, fixing the Commitment definition to include spend (#1514), clarifying "data artifact" and "FOCUS dataset" usage (#1515), and ijurica's EffectiveCost wording and nesting suggestions. Matt-Cowsert reported TF-3 agreed to revert display-name changes on deprecated columns; shawnalpay argued that belonged in #1139 rather than consistency review. Remaining items were assigned in October task force meetings, and the issue closed when 1.3 was released in December 2025.

items.t: [AI] Prepare InvoiceHandling for TF review
items.b: This issue, opened by ijurica in February 2026, asked for the InvoiceHandling work to be prepared for TF review as part of pull request #1501. Its only completion item was that the material be prepared and presented. shawnalpay closed the issue as completed on 11 February 2026, noting it was closing per a discussion held on 10 February. The thread is mostly mechanical and records no further debate.

items.t: [AI] Update Section 1.8 (Conformance Checks and Validators)
items.b: shawnalpay noted in October 2025 that Section 1.8 wrongly said no conformance validators existed. mike-finopsorg offered three options: remove the section, link only the foundation's validator, or list other tools too. Matt-Cowsert preferred linking the validator without implying an exhaustive list. mike-finopsorg drafted text saying third-party tools may exist and none is mandated; it went into #1513, which members approved in October 2025.

items.t: [AI] Reduce nesting from three to two levels in CommitmentDiscountQuantity
[AI] Address ambiguous normative requirement for EffectiveCost
[AI] Address editorial refinements to Metadata specification
[AI] Remove use of markdown directly within .mdpp files
[AI] Revisit and address Metadata - Date/Time column names
items.b: ijurica asked to align the suffixes of the date and time properties newly added to Metadata in 1.3. TF-2 agreed to standardise them, initially suggesting "last updated at", and ijurica proposed wider renaming plus naming principles for state and timestamp properties. TF-3 limited 1.3 to renaming RecencyLastUpdateDate to RecencyLastUpdated, moving the rest to #1060 and #1533. It closed as completed in October 2025.

items.t: [AI] Add Requirements subheader to every column definition
[AI] Apply dataset-level normative requirements guidelines
[AI] Draft PR implementing editorial changes per column clarifications
items.b: shawnalpay opened this action item in August 2025 to review the spec's 149 uses of "provider" and replace them with terms such as service provider, host provider or data generator, following #1055 and #1139. shawnalpay urged starting early in 1.3 development; rileyjenk volunteered but preferred waiting until spec development finished. The work landed in #1567, which was approved and merged, and the item closed in November 2025.

items.t: [AI] Revise spec content to address the existence of multiple datasets
items.b: shawnalpay noted in September 2025 that spec text often assumed "a FOCUS dataset" meant the Cost and Usage dataset, citing Column Handling wording raised by ijurica, and asked for a scrub. After TF-2 discussion, Matt-Cowsert added it to the 1.3 consistency review (#1380). Matt-Cowsert closed it in October 2025 after the related pull request was approved at the members meeting.

items.t: [AI] Clarify use of `dataset` vs `dataset artifact`
items.b: shawnalpay opened this action item to define dataset and dataset artifact in the glossary, after #1464 introduced the second term, and to review every use of dataset in the specification. Matt-Cowsert suggested also covering dataset instance artifact, and ijurica proposed agreeing the glossary terms first through #1527. rileyjenk's #1568 was replaced by #1576, which Members approved on November 6, and the item was closed as completed in November 2025.

items.t: [AI] Fix bug in Requirements Model EffectiveCost-C-004-M has incorrectly defined requirements
[AI] Fix old reference to ChargeType
[AI] Repair value format references
[FR] Standardize Normative Language: Convert All RECOMMENDED Statements to SHOULD
[FR] Standardize normative keywords from RECOMMENDED to SHOULD
items.b: Matt-Cowsert proposed replacing RECOMMENDED with SHOULD throughout the spec, since RFC 2119 treats the two as equivalent and mixing them could confuse implementers. Matt-Cowsert asked whether practitioners had reported problems; jpradocueva knew of none, and qquigley supported it while expecting it to be a low priority. In February 2026 shawnalpay said #1647 had already done the work and closed the request.

items.t: [AI] Handle for HTML/PDF anchor links for columns used in multiple datasets
items.b: shawnalpay opened this action item in November 2025 to fix anchor links for columns sharing a name across datasets and to document how anchors work, per #1569. ijurica noted that the PDF outline showed more heading levels than the on-page contents. mike-finopsorg opened #1656 for the link fix and asked for a separate feature request about the contents. No comment records the outcome; GitHub shows it closed as completed.

items.t: [FR] Handle for HTML/PDF anchor links for columns used in multiple datasets
items.b: shawnalpay reported that the HTML and PDF builder numbered duplicate anchors for columns used in several datasets, which would break links as datasets were added, and proposed prefixing anchors with the dataset name. mike-finopsorg suggested extending the vendored Markdown-PP tool to build anchors from the full heading path, and shawnalpay widened the scope to name overlaps between attributes and supported features. It was completed through #1656 in January 2026.

items.t: [Process] 1.4 procedural tasks
[AI] Draft PR for Billed Cost and Effective Cost definition updates (#982)
[FR] Clarify definitions of EffectiveCost vs BilledCost across providers
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this in May 2025 because ambiguous EffectiveCost and BilledCost definitions led data generators to implement them inconsistently, including a rule zeroing BilledCost for all marketplace purchases. Through 2025 Task Force 3 split over partial-upfront commitments: rileyjenk wanted billed cost distributed to usage records, while ijurica wanted it kept on purchase records. In September 2025 the work was cut from 1.3. For 1.4 the group reframed the problem as accuracy rather than double counting, adopted three milestones and, as shawnalpay urged, avoided the term amortization. Definitions were refined in #1678, and #1966 rewrote the normative requirements around covered and covering charges and the invoice issuer. After #1966 and #2022 were approved and merged, shawnalpay closed it as complete in April 2026.

items.t: [FR] Add non-FOCUS columns to FOCUS datasets as a non-functional requirement
items.b: Matt-Cowsert asked that FOCUS datasets carry custom x_ columns for any native billing data not covered by FOCUS columns, so practitioners could rely on FOCUS alone. ijurica added correlation use cases, such as carrying a provider's unique charge ID as a custom column. flanakin said only MUST would achieve the goal, though SHOULD might win provider buy-in, and in January 2026 opened #1800 with a new Scenario Completeness attribute. A provider-side request to soften MUST to SHOULD was settled by keeping MUST while letting data generators default to a subset of columns. The group made correlation a separate SHOULD and, in March 2026, simplified the core rule to include all native columns except documented, justified exclusions. #1800 merged and shawnalpay closed the issue in March 2026.

items.t: [AI] Review PR #1800 comments and align normative requirements language for custom columns
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this action item on 22 January 2026 to review comments on pull request #1800, align normative requirement wording with the "FOCUS datasets must" pattern, and consider renaming Scenario Completeness to Dataset Completeness. Flanakin had outstanding changes to make. The item was discussed at TF-2 and extended on 31 January 2026. Matt-Cowsert closed it as completed on 6 February 2026, with feedback still being gathered before member review.

items.t: [FR] Add column selection as a non-functional requirement
items.b: Matt-Cowsert asked in May 2025 for data generators to let practitioners choose which columns to export, and maintainers debated whether this was within FOCUS's remit. #1816 first added aggregation and time granularity; shawnalpay objected that aggregation belonged to consumers, and flanakin disagreed but accepted dropping it, which thecloudman and mike-finopsorg supported. #1816 was approved and merged, and the issue was closed in February 2026.

items.t: [AI] Create draft PR for column selection requirement
[AI] Open draft PR to bring to TF-2 for discussion on the planned approach for relocating presence rules in normative requirements
[FR] Relocate all normative requirements that apply to the dataset level to the dataset section of the document
items.b: mike-finopsorg proposed moving normative requirements that apply to a whole dataset, chiefly column presence rules, into each dataset definition, rephrased so the dataset carries the requirement. shawnalpay saw it as a subset of #1090, and the work was combined with #1796. Task Force 2 confirmed the approach in January 2026. It closed via #1865 in February 2026, was reopened for #2138, and closed again in April 2026.

items.t: [AI] Update PR #1865 with wording revisions and reorder guidelines
[FR] Add Line-Item Examples for Non-Negotiated Commitment Scenarios
items.b: Matt-Cowsert asked for appendix line-item examples for non-negotiated commitments (reserved instances, savings plans, CUDs) that explain why each column holds its value, so providers could implement them correctly and practitioners could validate their data. The thread logged TF-2 progress. ljadvey was assigned in January 2026, and the group chose provider-specific data, kept charge subcategory out of scope, and agreed to replace rather than supplement the existing appendix examples, with the work done in #1877. There, ijurica flagged duplicate rows and the undefined term "effective unit price", and thecloudman flagged a misleading claim that BilledCost equals ListCost. In March the group removed non-EC2 rows and savings calculations and pushed commitment eligibility to a later feature request. shawnalpay closed it as completed in March 2026.

items.t: [AI] Upload line-item examples PR for non-negotiated commitment scenarios
[AI] Draft PR for FR #958 Commitment Eligibility Indicator
items.b: Matt-Cowsert logged this action item in December 2025 to draft a PR for #958's commitment eligibility indicator, which Task Force 3 had agreed should be a JSON structure holding the provider's term and a FOCUS category such as spend-based or usage-based. It waited on input from cnharris10, then SanjnaSrivatsaVMware published the draft PR. It was closed in January 2026, with supported-feature content still to come.

items.t: [FR] Add commitment eligibility indicator
items.b: Matt-Cowsert asked for an indicator showing which non-negotiated discount programs, such as commitment discounts or SaaS public pricing tiers, a charge was eligible for, to support coverage and savings-rate analysis. qquigley supported a simple boolean but warned that hypothetical cost columns could taint reporting; shawnalpay suggested a JSON column of eligibility flags. Scoped for 1.3, it was repeatedly bumped and then descoped in August 2025. From November 2025 SanjnaSrivatsaVMware sponsored and drafted it in Task Force 3, where the group chose JSON over a boolean, broadened scope beyond commitment discounts after cnharris10 raised hybrid SaaS cases, added capacity reservations, and made negotiated programs a MAY. The name became Commitment Program Eligibility Details, and shawnalpay closed the issue in April 2026 after #1882 and #2025 merged.

items.t: [AI] Add examples to Commitment Discount Eligibility column PR
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this item on 30 January 2026 requesting examples for the draft Commitment Discount Eligibility pull request, covering uncovered-but-eligible charges and actual coverage. SanjnaSrivatsaVMware was to model them on AllocatedMethodDetails and wrap the string array in a JSON object. Reviewed in TF-3 on 13 February 2026, the item closed as complete. The pull request was to cover commitment discounts first, leaving room for other types. No merge is recorded.

items.t: [AI] Draft PR for Invoice Detail and Billing Period datasets
items.b: This was shawnalpay's action item to draft the Invoice Detail and Billing Period datasets. shawnalpay opened #1900 in January 2026 but kept the item open to finish TODO sections, after delays from Contract Commitment work. After reviews in TF-1 brought no outstanding feedback, shawnalpay closed it as complete in February 2026.

items.t: [FR] Add FOCUS Invoice Dataset
items.b: rileyjenk requested an Invoice dataset so finance teams could reconcile FOCUS data against invoices. qquigley urged involving finance personas, and beau-nelford-anglepoint offered support. From November 2025 shawnalpay led modeling in Task Force 1 with finance experts, Matt-Cowsert gathered data generator input, and thecloudman asked for an FX rate column. #1900 advanced toward member review in February 2026, and shawnalpay closed the issue in April 2026 when #2100 merged.

items.t: [AI] Draft PR for Contract Commitment dataset extension
items.b: shawnalpay logged this action item in January 2026 to draft a PR extending the Contract Commitment dataset. The work became #1924, which left draft in early February 2026 after incorporating feedback. shawnalpay closed the item on February 11, 2026, once #1924 was stable, aiming for Member review by February 17.

items.t: [FR] Extend support for Contract Commitment dataset
items.b: shawnalpay proposed in September 2025 extending the Contract Commitment dataset, founded in 1.3 by #1350 under #976, with columns for balances, scope rules, attestation and commitment models. It was paired with #1070 for 1.4, and Task Force 1 asked for use cases, examples and supported features. A data model drafted in January 2026 became PR #1924. shawnalpay closed it in March 2026 as completed via #1924, continuing in #1938.

items.t: [AI] Draft PR that removes ProviderName and PublisherName from specification
items.b: Issue #1889, opened by shawnalpay on 25 January 2026, asked for a draft pull request removing ProviderName and PublisherName from the specification. On 11 February 2026 shawnalpay said the work was done in #1955 and asked Matt-Cowsert to review it. Matt-Cowsert closed the issue as complete the next day, noting the draft had been written and feedback rounds had begun. The thread doesn't record whether #1955 merged.

items.t: [FR] Remove ProviderName and PublisherName from specification
items.b: shawnalpay proposed in January 2026 removing ProviderName and PublisherName, deprecated in 1.3, from the 1.4 specification, and documenting how removals are done. qquigley and TechinMama took on the work with help from davidearney, and the group agreed to generalise the removal process to all spec entities, not just columns. PR #1955 was approved and merged, and shawnalpay closed it as complete in March 2026.

items.t: [AI] Draft EffectiveCost Zero-Value Normative Requirements
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened #1892 in January 2026 to draft normative requirements for when EffectiveCost must be zero or non-zero, covering prepaid commitments, missing usage data and unused commitments. On 5 February 2026, ijurica shared a comparison spreadsheet as a starting point. On 6 February, Matt-Cowsert reported that TF-3 had reviewed the draft but not finalized it. The issue is marked closed as completed, but the thread does not record final language.

items.t: [AI] Revise BilledCost Marketplace Normative Requirement
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 26 January 2026 to make the BilledCost marketplace requirement conditional on InvoiceIssuer, since the current zero-cost rule breaks reconciliation when a cloud marketplace issues the invoice. It is not covered by #1488. On 6 February 2026 Matt-Cowsert reported that TF-3 had reviewed it and would keep iterating before member review. The thread is closed as completed, but it doesn't say when.

items.t: [AI] Add Conformance Requirement: MUST NOT Estimate EffectiveCost
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 26 January 2026 after an October meeting flagged data generators estimating EffectiveCost without actual usage or accrual data. The proposal sought a conformance requirement forbidding such estimates. On 6 February 2026 Matt-Cowsert reported the task force was still debating MUST versus MUST NOT framing, expecting member review within two weeks. It is marked closed as completed, but the thread doesn't record the outcome.

items.t: [AI] Draft a PR applying FOCUS Attributes' normative requirements guidelines
items.b: ijurica's action item was to draft a PR applying the normative requirements guidelines for attributes to the existing FOCUS attributes. ijurica posted draft #1967, still a work in progress, for TF-RM feedback. shawnalpay closed the item in February 2026, noting that #1981 was in draft.

items.t: [FR] Establish and apply FOCUS attribute-specification guidelines
items.b: ijurica opened this in May 2025 because FOCUS had no formal guidelines for writing attribute specifications, risking inconsistent or unclear requirements; the plan was to write guidelines and apply them to existing attributes without material changes. shawnalpay pointed to precedent PRs #787 and #798 and later urged priority, since compound requirements such as those in Discount Handling were hard to turn into conformance rules. The item moved between task forces and went undiscussed for months until February 2026, when ijurica presented #1967 (guidelines) and #1981 (refactoring), rephrasing requirements as verifiable states for the FOCUS Validator. A few deliberate material changes were accepted and others deferred. For binding requirements to custom columns, mike-finopsorg proposed a hybrid approach. shawnalpay closed it as complete in April 2026 after #1967, #1981 and #2166 merged.

items.t: [AI] Create proposal AI that restructures JSON Object normative text to better align with Requirements Modelling
items.b: In February 2026, mike-finopsorg opened this issue because JSON object text in the FOCUS specification did not clearly show entity and structure. The proposal was to restructure JSON object normative text to align with requirements modelling, for group approval. shawnalpay gave feedback on PR #1986. On 17 February 2026, mike-finopsorg closed the issue as completed once the pull request opened. The thread does not say whether the pull request merged.

items.t: [FR] Rephrase schema object normative text
items.b: In January 2026, mike-finopsorg asked that FOCUS 1.3 schema normative text name the bearing entity explicitly, such as AllocatedMethodDetailsObject.Elements, and state grouping keys for the AllocatedRatio sum-to-1 rule. The maintainer assessment labelled it a technical improvement with no requesting organizations. In February 2026, mike-finopsorg asked Matt-Cowsert how to close it while the related PR was in review. In March 2026, shawnalpay closed it as complete via PR #2007.

items.t: [AI] Create PR for the restructuring of Object normative text in the FOCUS specification
items.b: mike-finopsorg opened this action item in February 2026 to make the nested Object entity in JSON columns explicit in normative text, and raised #1986. shawnalpay reopened it after agreeing that mike-finopsorg would write a new pull request using JSON schema for presence and format requirements. Maintainers agreed on February 23 to proceed with #2007 over #1986, and the issue closed in favor of follow-up #2019.

items.t: [AI] Phase 1: Automate Normative Requirements Extraction (Markdown --> JSON)
items.b: jpradocueva opened this action item to automate extracting normative requirements from the spec's Markdown into JSON with at least 90% accuracy. jpradocueva found that lead-in statements such as "adheres to the following requirements" carried mandatory intent without BCP-14 keywords, and proposed explicit MUST wording; mike-finopsorg preferred "MUST adhere to the following requirements". After due-date delays, tracking moved in March 2026 to #2083, with the changes in #2090.

items.t: [FR] Add 1.4 Specification revisions to Requirements Model
[AI] Adjust ContractCommitmentID → ResourceID match in ContractApplied column
items.b: ijurica logged this in February 2026 because ContractApplied required ContractCommitmentId to match ResourceId on all purchase charges, rather than only on purchases of that commitment and usage of its unused portion, as in DiscountHandling. shawnalpay would not add it to 1.4 without a Feature Request explaining the bug and another approval. ijurica created FR #2036, and in March 2026 the item was closed with PR #2017 in Member review.

items.t: [FR] Revisit ContractApplied.ContractCommitmentID Requirements to Align with CommitmentDiscount Handling
items.b: ijurica opened this feature request on 3 March 2026 asking that the ContractApplied.ContractCommitmentID rules be aligned with DiscountHandling. The existing rule required ContractCommitmentID to equal ResourceID for every Purchase row, while DiscountHandling limited that to purchases of the commitment itself. The proposal scoped the rule and added one for unused commitment usage rows. Neos requested it as nice to have. Maintainers labelled it a practitioner enhancement. The issue remains open.

items.t: [AI] Provide draft PR with additional 982 example scenarios
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened #2014 on 20 February 2026 to produce a draft pull request with example scenarios beyond the marketplace multi-provider examples in #2013, as required by parent issue #982. The examples were to follow the CSV structure of the existing SaaS appendix examples, and gparker-at-sf offered to help. On 27 February 2026 Matt-Cowsert closed the issue as complete, noting that remaining work to leave draft status would happen within TF-3.

items.t: [AI] Draft SaaS Licensing Scenario Guidance (Appendix)
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this action item to draft appendix guidance on SaaS licensing where usage cannot be tracked, such as seat-based, flat-rate and tiered pricing with committed minimums, including when EffectiveCost should equal BilledCost; it was outside the scope of #1488. Matt-Cowsert later suggested merging it with another scenario-drafting item and closed it as completed in February 2026, leaving the remaining work to task force 3.

items.t: [AI] Draft PR for supported features content for Commitment Eligibility
items.b: In January 2026 Matt-Cowsert opened this issue for a follow-on pull request adding supported features for the CommitmentEligibility column, separate from #1898. It was to give CSP and SaaS examples and clarify commitment discount naming. On 20 February 2026 Matt-Cowsert agreed to draft the PR, as the call had focused on normative requirements. On 27 February 2026 it was closed as complete, with remaining work deferred to TF-3.

items.t: [AI] Strike "valid decimal value" normative requirements from the spec
items.b: shawnalpay proposed on 9 March 2026 striking spec requirements that a column be a valid decimal value, arguing they duplicate existing type Decimal and NumericFormat requirements and are harder to verify. Maintainers agreed in principle. The definition of done keeps the non-negative decimal value entries for unit price columns. The issue was closed by shawnalpay on 16 March 2026, as #2047 now covers the change.

items.t: [AI] Issue 1.3 errata
items.b: On 5 March 2026, shawnalpay opened this issue to publish an errata document for FOCUS 1.3, covering editorial problems surfaced during 1.4 development. The definition of done was a draft pull request listing the errata. On 12 March 2026, shawnalpay reported the work was complete through #2041 and #2052, and the issue was closed as completed. The thread contains no further debate.

items.t: [Feedback] Correct various 1.3 non-material issues as errata
[Feedback] `PricingCurrency` allows null in content constraints but requirements doesn't
items.b: tk3fftk reported on 18 March 2026 that the PricingCurrency requirement bans nulls while its content constraints allow them. shawnalpay agreed, noted PricingCurrencyEffectiveCost had the same mismatch, and confirmed neither allows nulls. Both were logged as 1.3 errata (#2041) and fixed in #2052, pending member approval. On 23 March 2026 the issue was closed as addressed via #2052. The thread doesn't record member approval.

items.t: [AI] Shorten Table of Contents
items.b: shawnalpay proposed in January 2026 shortening the Table of Contents, keeping one sub-level only under Datasets and giving each section an overview with links. The Use Case Library's future was raised. Maintainers reviewed it on 3 February 2026. Though PR #1942 lacked full consensus and wasn't yet perfect, it had enough support to proceed, so the issue was closed as completed. The thread doesn't record whether that PR merged.

items.t: [Process] 1.4 consistency review
items.b: shawnalpay opened this placeholder in January 2026 to collect work for the FOCUS 1.4 consistency review, scheduled for April 9 to 30, and triaged each reported inconsistency into an action item or pull request. shawnalpay's own items included a dedicated Allowed Values subsection (#2106), an invoice issuer glossary entry (#2107), an explicit JSON type requirement for Tags (#2114) and dataset ordering (#2120). ijurica flagged broken links, over-linking against the editorial guidelines and inconsistent references to participating entities. davidearney logged many editorial fixes, such as header capitalization, contractions, dash style and quoting of allowed values, and agreed to bundle them into one PR, #2200, with later fixes in #2203, #2204, #2205 and #2207. shawnalpay closed the task as complete in May 2026.

items.t: [AI] Create PR resolving duplicative requirements across ListUnitPrice and ListCost
items.b: The issue, opened by shawnalpay on 16 March 2026, asked for a pull request to resolve duplicative requirements across the ListUnitPrice and ListCost columns. On 20 March 2026, Matt-Cowsert reported the work was done after members reviewed the initial pull request the day before. The issue was closed as completed. The thread doesn't describe the duplicates or changes, nor whether the pull request was merged.

items.t: [Feedback] List Unit Price has normative requirement that belongs to List Cost
items.b: mike-finopsorg reported that the FOCUS 1.3 List Unit Price requirements included a rule that really applied to ListCost and was already stated there. shawnalpay objected to parking it under the 1.4 consistency review and said it was not errata either. The March 16, 2026 Maintainers call brought it into scope, with Matt-Cowsert writing a PR. It was implemented through #2067 in March 2026.

items.t: [FR] Add tag details for source attribution and eligibility
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this request because practitioners could not tell which charges can be tagged or where a tag value came from. With kk09v and qquigley as sponsors and work starting in 1.4, TF-2 widened it from resource to charge tagging after cnharris10 noted SaaS tags without resources, and ruled out SKUs as the basis. From eleven candidate structures the group chose a key-driven TagDetails column alongside Tags, after kk09v's BigQuery tests, drafted as #1904. An AWS test showed data growing seven to eight times, tying it to column selection (#1091). In March 2026 shawnalpay opposed adding Recommended columns; maintainers found little support for #1904 as written, felt the scope had grown without re-review, and believed time had run out in the release.
