items.t: [AI] Resolve $ vs $ inconsistency in spec markdown files
items.b: In March 2026, ljadvey opened #2064 because FOCUS example files mixed literal dollar signs with $ entities. shawnalpay had flagged this during #1877 review, and a Maintainers Meeting moved it to a separate issue. The issue listed three options. On 7 April 2026, mike-finopsorg opened #2167 to resolve it, and shawnalpay closed #2064 as complete. The thread doesn't record which convention was chosen.

items.t: [AI] Fix tiny editorial issues
items.b: shawnalpay opened #2110 in March 2026 to bundle editorial fixes: a broken link in section 1 and alphabetical sorting of the Invoice Detail table. On 1 April 2026 shawnalpay added a fix to a Contract Commitment Period End example, flagged by a Copilot comment on #2060 for a mistargeted anchor and an end date that contradicted the text. The issue is closed as completed; the thread gives no closing date.

items.t: [AI] Add "match" vs "equal" terminology check to consistency review checklist
items.b: Issue #1998, opened by Matt-Cowsert in February 2026 under #982, was an action item to standardize the inconsistent use of 'match' and 'equal' in normative requirements, noticed while reviewing #1966. kk09v proposed 'equal' for numeric metric values and 'match' for everything else, and raised #2175. shawnalpay closed it in April 2026 as complete via the merged #2175.

items.t: [AI] Tense inconsistency between Invoice Detail and Billing Period
items.b: davidearney reported that InvoiceIssuerName used present tense in the Invoice Detail dataset but past tense in the Billing Period dataset. shawnalpay agreed it belonged in the consistency review, and Task Force 3 agreed on April 10, 2026 to use present tense. It was completed by merged #2182 in April 2026.

items.t: [AI] InvoiceIssuerName: Requirement present in two datasets but absent in two others
items.b: davidearney pointed out in March 2026 that the requirement that InvoiceIssuerName represent the invoicing entity appeared in two datasets but not in the Cost and Usage or Contract Commitment definitions. shawnalpay agreed it was a consistency issue and noted a wider pass was planned via #1890. It was completed by Matt-Cowsert's #2182, merged in April 2026.

items.t: [AI] Apply Finalized Fictitious Names Across All Appendix Entries
items.b: shawnalpay opened this action item to replace legacy and real-world names across every appendix entry with the trademark-safe fictitious names agreed in #2115. thecloudman updated the entries in several pull requests and judged some needed no change, but shawnalpay noted that one still used TinyCloud and another used ACME Corp as invoice issuer, though Acme Corp is a reference customer. It was closed as completed in April 2026.

items.t: [AI] Pivot scaled-down tables from horizontal to vertical
items.b: shawnalpay opened this issue on 1 April 2026. PR #2038 had scaled down two overlong tables, which had forced the PDF renderer to shrink the whole document. mike-finopsorg had added a fix there. shawnalpay proposed keeping that code but pivoting the affected tables from horizontal to vertical, via a new PR. The issue was closed as completed; the thread doesn't give a date.

items.t: [AI] Update all relevant Invoice Issuer references in the spec
items.b: Opened by shawnalpay on 15 April 2026, this issue asked for generic references to Invoice Issuer in the spec to use a new glossary entry, once #2107 was complete. It warned that the change needed careful human review, since some datasets should keep the InvoiceIssuerName column reference. On 24 April 2026 shawnalpay recorded it as completed through merged #2258. The issue was closed as complete.

items.t: [AI] Standardize "Allowed Values" Subheaders Across Datasets
items.b: Issue #2106, opened by shawnalpay in March 2026, was an editorial task asking every column with a restricted value list to use a dedicated Allowed Values subheader, across four datasets. ijurica suggested placing it right below Requirements, and shawnalpay removed an incorrect link to #2200. davidearney's #2260 covered every item, and the issue closed in April 2026 as completed via that PR.

items.t: [AI] Clean up DeliveryHandling and CorrectionHandling attributes
items.b: ijurica opened this issue on 16 April 2026 to remove leftover Exceptions sections containing None from the DeliveryHandling and CorrectionHandling attribute specifications, and to align their section ordering with other attributes. The definition of done asked for those changes and a pull request that passed the linter. The issue was closed as completed, but the thread does not record the closing date, a linked pull request, or any other discussion.

items.t: [AI] Update ProgramType examples to use Title Case in Commitment Program Eligibility Details column examples and supported features
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 9 April 2026 to change ProgramType value examples in the Commitment Program Eligibility Details column and related files from PascalCase to Title Case. It followed TF-3's decision on #1882 to remove value examples from a normative requirement and defer informative changes here. No disagreement is recorded. On 1 May 2026, shawnalpay noted it was closed as completed via #2266.

items.t: [AI] Change `$` to `$` in new Commitment Eligibility examples
items.b: In April 2026 shawnalpay opened #2179 because the Commitment Eligibility examples added by #2025 still used the dollar HTML entity instead of the plain dollar sign, even though #2167 had already made that change elsewhere. The stated goal was a pull request changing every instance to the plain sign. On 24 April 2026 shawnalpay reported the work complete through merged pull request #2268, and the issue closed.

items.t: [AI] Update column-level normative requirements to use "dataset instance" in non-subject positions
items.b: Matt-Cowsert logged this action item in February 2026 to use the term dataset instance where requirements meant concrete delivered data rather than the abstract FOCUS dataset. In April 2026 shawnalpay found the definition of done unclear, and ijurica pointed to a new convention making FOCUS Dataset the canonical normative subject. The scope was narrowed to four BilledCost and EffectiveCost requirements, and it was closed via #2269 in May 2026.

items.t: [AI] Enforce title case in headers
items.b: On 17 April 2026, shawnalpay opened this issue asking that the newly adopted MarkdownPP title case rule apply to headers. The rule capitalises most words but leaves short articles, conjunctions and prepositions lowercase unless they open a subheader. The stated goal was a pull request updating the linter. The thread has no other discussion. On 1 May 2026, shawnalpay closed the issue as completed, stating it was closed via #2271.

items.t: [AI] Add Explicit Data Type Requirements for Key-Value Columns
items.b: On 26 March 2026, shawnalpay opened this issue because the Allocated Tags, SKU Price Details and Tags columns lacked an explicit "MUST be of type JSON" requirement, unlike other JSON columns. At the 6 April 2026 maintainers meeting, members agreed to add the JSON type to all relevant columns. On 1 May 2026, shawnalpay closed the issue as complete, linking it to #2274.

items.t: [AI] Standardize Internal Linking and Attribute Referencing Formatting
items.b: In March 2026, shawnalpay opened this issue to fix inconsistent internal links in the FOCUS markdown. Problems included links missing the attributes parent prefix, requirements naming attributes by display name rather than ID, and anchors containing hyphens. ijurica had listed these problems in a comment on #1878. The issue was closed as completed on 24 April 2026, when shawnalpay noted the work was done through merged #2275.

items.t: [AI] Suggest updating wording on data_generator_calculated_split_cost_allocation_handling.md to remove duplicate wording
items.b: thecloudman proposed removing the repeated "more granular" wording from the opening paragraph of the calculated split cost allocation handling attribute, including a parenthetical about splits that only add detail, and supplied a rewrite. shawnalpay asked for the parent issue #1878 to be set. The issue was closed as completed on 24 April 2026, with merged #2277 completing the work.

items.t: [AI] Fix broken internal links outside Attributes section
items.b: ijurica opened this issue on 20 April 2026 to fix broken internal links outside the Attributes section, such as wrong path segments, missing glossary anchors and case mismatches. Attributes links were excluded because #2127 and PR #2275 covered them. The work assumed the Service Provider anchor would change to glossary:service-provider under #2107 and PR #2256. shawnalpay closed the issue as completed on 1 May 2026, citing #2281.

items.t: [AI] Broken glossary anchor: glossary:charge-period vs glossary:chargeperiod
items.b: davidearney reported a broken glossary link: effectivecost.md pointed to a hyphenated Charge Period anchor, while the glossary anchor had no hyphen. shawnalpay assigned it to consistency review. ijurica asked whether #2281 covered it, kk09v confirmed it did, and the issue was closed via #2281 in May 2026.

items.t: [AI] Revise CommitmentProgramEligibilityDetails to use refactored JSON object schema
items.b: In March 2026 shawnalpay opened this issue to revise CommitmentProgramEligibilityDetails to use the refactored JSON object schema. The work was conditional on #1882 being approved, and the target format was the one agreed in #2007. On 1 May 2026, shawnalpay closed the issue as complete, noting that it was done through #2283.

items.t: [AI] Align AllocatedMethodDetails.AllocatedRatio requirement with aggregate expression guideline
items.b: ijurica's action item was to reword the AllocatedRatio sum requirement in AllocatedMethodDetails to follow the aggregate expression pattern in the normative requirements guidelines. shawnalpay closed it in April 2026, reopened it on finding #2285 was not yet merged, and closed it via #2285 in May 2026.

items.t: [AI] Add data volume considerations to Correction Style descriptions in Appendix section
items.b: ijurica opened #2286 on 21 April 2026 to add data volume considerations for Replacement, Delta and Ledger to the Appendix Correction Style table. These considerations already appeared in the Correction Handling attribute but not in the appendix overview, which stressed traceability and could imply Ledger is preferred. On 24 April 2026 shawnalpay reported completion through merged #2287, and the issue closed as completed.

items.t: [AI] Revisit `Total Term` allowed value name and description in `Contract Commitment Fulfillment Interval`
items.b: ijurica opened this issue on 21 April 2026 to revisit the Total Term allowed value in ContractCommitmentFulfillmentInterval. The name conflicts with the glossary meaning of Term, an agreement rather than a time duration, and the description referred to the whole contract rather than the contract commitment. On 1 May 2026, shawnalpay noted it was closed via #2289, and the issue was marked completed. No other discussion is recorded.

items.t: [AI] Apply consistent section ordering within column files
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 20 April 2026 to apply one agreed section order to column files across four datasets, based on a 17 April audit of #2108. Requirements were to come before contextual content. Renaming non-standard sections was left to #2108. Work was split among Matt-Cowsert, ijurica and flanakin. On 24 April 2026 shawnalpay reported completion via merged #2290, and the issue was closed as complete.

items.t: [AI] ChargeCategory (Invoice Detail) has an extra normative requirement absent from Cost and Usage
items.b: davidearney noted in March 2026 that Invoice Detail's ChargeCategory had a requirement allowing "Usage" for aggregated records that Cost and Usage lacked, and asked for a fix or explanation. shawnalpay said the difference was intentional and, at an April 2026 meeting, agreed to add a guideline allowing same-named columns to differ across datasets, with explanatory text. It was closed via #2295 in May 2026.

items.t: [AI] Enforce "First Occurrence" Linking Rule and Clarify "Section" Boundaries
items.b: shawnalpay reported that the editorial rule to link only the first occurrence of a column or attribute name was widely broken and unclear about what a "section" is. Maintainers agreed on once per source file, and shawnalpay proposed a glossary exception of once per entry. ijurica's #2312 defined the scope as the file and added exceptions for Content Constraints and the glossary. shawnalpay closed it via #2300 in May 2026.

items.t: [AI] Use semicolons in nested comma lists
items.b: Issue #2297, opened by kk09v on 22 April 2026, proposed replacing commas with semicolons in lists whose elements already contain commas, because such sentences were hard to read. The example was in string_handling.md. The scope also covered other occurrences and editorial guidance. On 1 May 2026, shawnalpay noted it was closed via #2303, and the issue was closed as completed. The thread does not record any alternatives discussed.

items.t: [AI] Missing Dataset row in Content Constraints tables for Invoice Detail and Billing Period
items.b: davidearney reported that column files in the Invoice Detail and Billing Period datasets lacked the Dataset row that other datasets have in their Content Constraints tables. davidearney said #2200 fixed it, but shawnalpay reopened it in April 2026 because the row was still missing. It was closed in May 2026 via #2306.

items.t: [AI] Improve column heading structure and ordering; consolidate Implementation sections
items.b: In April 2026, ijurica proposed reordering and renaming column headings in the FOCUS specification. Proposals included merging Implementation Context into Implementation Guidance, adding a Domain Concepts heading, and prefixing JSON object-level headings with "Object." On 1 May 2026, shawnalpay noted the issue was closed as completed via #2310 and #2311. The thread records no separate debate on the proposals.

items.t: [AI] Address remaining Content Constraints inconsistencies
items.b: On 29 April 2026, ijurica opened #2320 to fix remaining Content Constraints inconsistencies across four datasets. It proposed reclassifying two Contract Commitment percentage columns from Dimension to Metric, changing five Invoice Detail value formats to not specified, correcting one attribute format in CommitmentProgramEligibilityDetails, and retyping ContractApplied. On 1 May 2026, shawnalpay noted it had been closed via #2321, and the issue was closed as complete.

items.t: [AI]  Fix broken internal links in JSON Object Format columns
items.b: ijurica opened this issue on 4 May 2026 reporting that the heading restructuring in the 1.4 release left broken internal links. Six links in Allocated Method Details, Contract Applied and Contract Commitment Applicability pointed to old anchor paths, and two links in Commitment Program Eligibility Details included an extra datasets segment. On 8 May 2026 shawnalpay commented that the fix was completed through #2340 and the issue closed as completed.

items.t: [AI] Address remaining consistency issues in 1.4 candidate release
items.b: In April 2026, shawnalpay reviewed the 1.4 candidate release draft and listed consistency errors to fix. These covered missing BCP-14 keywords, data generators used as subjects, prohibited process verbs, "if" used in conditionals, keyword casing, and naming typos. The issue was closed as completed on 8 May 2026, with shawnalpay noting the fixes were addressed through #2342 and #2344.

items.t: [AI] Graduate dataset requirements to data model level
items.b: Issue #2348, opened by shawnalpay on 6 May 2026, proposed moving dataset presence requirements up to the data model level, because they belonged one level higher. The definition of done was a draft pull request doing so. On 18 May 2026 shawnalpay noted the work was completed through #2349, and the issue was closed as completed. The thread has no further discussion.

items.t: [AI] Draft PR with applicability criteria
items.b: The issue, opened by shawnalpay on 6 May 2026, asked for a draft pull request adding a few applicability criteria to the spec, to be presented in TF-RM. shawnalpay presented it on 12 May 2026 and planned to act on feedback. On 19 May 2026 it was reviewed again in TF-RM, moved out of draft, and sent to member review. The issue was then closed as completed.

items.t: [FR] Define applicability criteria in the specification
items.b: shawnalpay asked for the applicability criteria that decide when conditional columns must be present to be defined in the spec itself, not only in the downstream Requirements Model. mike-finopsorg asked whether criteria should be defined first and cited in normative text, or derived from it. shawnalpay's #2351 was merged in May 2026; the issue was reopened to add conditions to column constraint tables via #2423, and closed in July 2026.

items.t: [AI] Draft PR proposing the addition of Consumer ID and Principal ID
items.b: shawnalpay opened this draft pull request on 8 May 2026, proposing to add Consumer ID to Cost and Usage, with Principal ID also in the title. On 19 May 2026, shawnalpay said the related work in #2360 was complete, that much discussion remained, and that the proposal was out of draft. The thread then closed as completed, with the work carried on in #2360.

items.t: [AI] Rework Actor dimensions to a PrincipalID-only scoped PR and tighten the Principal glossary definition
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue in June 2026 to narrow #2358 to PrincipalID, splitting off ConsumerID because providers rarely see the end user. TF2 kept the name Principal but asked for a glossary definition distinguishing it from the downstream consumer. Matt-Cowsert reviewed the scoped pull request with TF2 on 1 July 2026 and closed the issue as completed on 6 July 2026. The thread doesn't confirm the final glossary wording.

items.t: [AI] Propose a broader condition name covering PrincipalId, CredentialId, and CredentialDetails
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened #2651 on 20 August 2026 because IncludesPrincipalAttribution fails when a generator holds an API key but cannot resolve the principal behind it. ijurica and Matt-Cowsert both preferred broadening that single condition over the alternatives, which would set new precedent for presence conditions. On 25 August 2026 Matt-Cowsert recorded that the group settled on RequesterAttribution, covering principals and credentials. The issue was closed as completed.

items.t: [AI] Draft PR adding recommended values to `UnitFormat` attribute
items.b: In May 2026, shawnalpay opened an issue for a draft pull request adding recommended values to the UnitFormat attribute, aimed at TF-2. On 13 May, shawnalpay assigned Matt-Cowsert to ensure review at the 20 May TF-2 meeting. On 21 May, Matt-Cowsert reported that TF-2 and members had reviewed it and expected approval at the next members' meeting. It was closed as completed, its current state exceeding the action item's scope.

items.t: [FR] Expand list of recommended `Unit Format` values
items.b: shawnalpay requested adding Character, Image, Job, Message, Page and Session to the recommended count-based units, with a Description column, so practitioners could compare AI and SaaS unit costs across vendors without custom mapping. A task force update recorded keeping tokens as the base unit, with variations such as input versus output carried in SKU price properties. It was closed as completed in May 2026 via #2362.

items.t: [AI] Draft PR with revisions to Service Categories
items.b: shawnalpay opened this task on 13 May 2026 to draft a pull request revising Service Categories. On 19 May 2026, #2379 was taken out of draft ahead of the Maintainers meeting. On 27 May 2026, shawnalpay reported that it had been presented at the 26 May TF-1 and Maintainers meetings, that further discussion was needed, and closed the task as complete. The thread does not record a merge.

items.t: [FR] Revise `Service Category` allowed values to include all Technology Categories
items.b: Issue #2377, opened by shawnalpay in May 2026, proposed new Service Category values and cloud-neutral descriptions so on-premises, SaaS and licensing costs need not default to Other. ThavronNan took it over, and TF-1 split it into cleanup (#2379) and expansion (#2518) PRs, the expansion moving toward 1.6. By August 2026 the remaining scope was #2624, fixing the Compute description and splitting out Bare Metal. No comment records the outcome; GitHub shows it closed as completed.

items.t: [AI] Propose revision of Service Categories
items.b: shawnalpay opened this action item to propose revisions to the Service Categories in #2379. ThavronNan shared spreadsheets of category and subcategory recommendations covering on-premises spend, discussed over several June 2026 Task Force 1 meetings, and davidearney proposed AI and Machine Learning description fixes and new Generative AI subcategories. Matt-Cowsert closed it in July 2026, since the expansion was tracked in #2518 and #2379 was in member review.

items.t: [FR] Improve split cost allocation guidance for data generators and practitioners
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this request after community feedback that the spec gave too little guidance on producing and querying split cost allocation data. thecloudman added an AllocatedServiceName column in #2395, merged by August 2026, with follow-ups #2493 and #2494, and #2655 refined its requirements. TF-2 argued at length over what an unallocated portion row should carry, and dropped that requirement in September 2026. No comment records the outcome; GitHub shows it closed as completed.

items.t: [AI] Draft PR adding AllocatedServiceName and AllocatedServiceCategory columns
items.b: thecloudman opened an action item, for #2315, to draft columns naming the consuming service on split cost allocation rows while keeping the original service intact. shawnalpay repeatedly asked for a due date and removed it from the 1.5 milestone until a Maintainer approved a PR. In July 2026 Matt-Cowsert reported it complete, with the scope cut to AllocatedServiceName and AllocatedServiceCategory dropped.

items.t: [AI] Address Spec-only issues identified during Spec–RM (v.1.4) requirements comparison
items.b: ijurica opened an action item to fix minor specification-only issues found while comparing the 1.4 specification with the Requirements Model, such as an extra empty line in CustomColumnHandling, without changing the model. shawnalpay moved it under #1878. It was closed as completed in May 2026 after #2398 was approved at the May 21 members' meeting and merged.

items.t: [Feedback] Invoice Detail overview table lists Payment Currency as Mandatory (should be Conditional)
[AI] Draft PR of price sheet
items.b: Issue #2364 asked for a draft pull request of a price sheet and was opened by shawnalpay on 8 May 2026. On 31 May 2026 shawnalpay reported that the first draft was done in #2424 and would be presented at the 2 June 2026 TF-1 meeting. Feedback from that meeting was incorporated, though more discussion remained. The issue was closed as complete on 2 June 2026.

items.t: [FR] Add separate SKU-price dataset
items.b: Matt-Cowsert requested a separate dataset of a provider's SKUs and prices for lookups, joins and pre-purchase estimation. shawnalpay asked for scope and use cases and distinguished a SKU dataset from a SKU Price dataset. From May 2026 shawnalpay drafted a model and #2424, which Matt-Cowsert stewarded during shawnalpay's leave. Task Force 1 worked through tier boundaries, PricingCategory, dropping ChargeFrequency, snapshot versus history, and the dataset's condition, keeping IncludesUnitPricing in September 2026. The longest dispute was two price columns on one row versus one row per price under a single UnitPrice; shawnalpay argued for rows to avoid fabricated effective dates, while flanakin's queryability concern stayed open. Members approved releasing the dataset as a preview on October 22, 2026, and GitHub shows the issue closed as completed on 31 October 2026.

items.t: [AI] Create Appendix Entry for SKU Price Sample Data
items.b: In May 2026, shawnalpay requested a new appendix section with sample SKU Price data: realistic mock rate card rows covering list prices, partial upfront commitments, volume tier boundaries, and JSON formatting for SKU Price Details and SKU Price Eligibility, drawn from a data model spreadsheet. On 18 August 2026, Matt-Cowsert closed the issue as completed, saying the work had been added to the SKU Price dataset.

items.t: [AI] Decide which condition gates ContractedUnitPrice in the SKU Price dataset
items.b: Matt-Cowsert questioned the Includes contract commitments gate on ContractedUnitPrice in the SKU Price dataset, since providers with negotiated rates but no commitment instruments fell outside it. On 19 August 2026 the column was made unconditional and Mandatory, following the Maintainer decision to remove Includes Negotiated Pricing. ContractId also lost its gate and became Mandatory, since two composite-key requirements name it. Applied to PR #2424, the issue closed as completed.

items.t: [AI] Reconcile ContractedUnitPrice null semantics between SKU Price and Cost and Usage
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 11 August 2026 because ContractedUnitPrice was null in SKU Price but equal to ListUnitPrice in Cost and Usage for uncontracted charges, breaking joins on SkuPriceId. On 19 August 2026 the thread chose to follow Cost and Usage: uncontracted SKU Price records now carry their ListUnitPrice, and the column is Mandatory and non-nullable, decided jointly with #2618. The change went into #2424. Closed as completed.

items.t: [AI] Fix incorrect `Allows Nulls` value for HostProviderName in CostAndUsage dataset column table overview
items.b: On 1 June 2026, ijurica opened #2431 because the CostAndUsage dataset column table overview marked HostProviderName as not allowing nulls. That conflicted with the normative requirements and content constraints, which define it as allowing nulls. On 2 June 2026, shawnalpay commented that the fix was completed through #2432 and closed the issue as completed. The thread has no further discussion.

items.t: [FR] Standardize tag key handling in the Tags column
items.b: Matt-Cowsert asked that tag keys, like tag values, be preserved as provided, after #2322 reported mixed-case versions of one key in Azure exports. #2434 carried the change: TF-2 adopted "provided keys" wording, moved a section on platform key handling to supporting content and cut a sentence contradicting the case-sensitive requirement. In July 2026 the PR went to member approval. No comment records the outcome; GitHub shows it closed as completed.

items.t: [AI] Draft PR restoring user-defined tag key preservation requirement to Tags column
items.b: thecloudman opened this issue, with kk09v as co-assignee, to restore a ban on generators altering user-defined tag keys, dropped by #691. Azure case variants of one key (#2322) prompted it, under #2325. Draft PR #2434 added the bullet to tags.md and allocatedtags.md, plus a non-normative section. The checklist records maintainer approval and a merge to working_draft by October 2026, though the exact date isn't recorded. The issue closed as completed.

items.t: [FR] Surface AI model identity and token consumption in FOCUS
items.b: Matt-Cowsert asked in February 2026 for FOCUS to show which AI model was used and to split input from output token costs, and shawnalpay strongly backed it for 1.5. DaveMoreau raised cached tokens, token units and inconsistent model names; kk09v raised context-window pricing, provisioned throughput and the risk of overloading properties. Task Force 2 proposed folding all AI scope into this request, but maintainers on May 11, 2026 kept it narrow, with topics such as #2371 and #2099 tracked separately. In June the group chose FOCUS-defined SkuPriceDetails properties over new columns, reused existing unit and quantity columns, and named the originator property Model Developer; ModelVariant was dropped in July. PR #2442 was merged by late July 2026, but the thread doesn't record the request's closure.

items.t: [AI] Validate anchor links during build
items.b: shawnalpay opened this issue on 13 April 2026 asking for the spec build to flag ill-formed anchor links, since they are hard to keep valid otherwise. A manual-only flag was suggested in case the check runs slowly. mike-finopsorg opened #2510 on 2 July 2026 to resolve it, and on 8 July 2026 noted the validation was implemented in that pull request. The issue was closed as completed.

items.t: [AI] Split the compound duration format bullet in ContractCommitmentDurationType and PurchaseDurationType
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened #2530 on 14 July 2026 after a review of #2424 found the ContractCommitmentDurationType SHOULD bullet bundles three constraints and repeats Expected Format. The proposal was to split or consolidate it and make the same change to PurchaseDurationType. A later comment flagged that both units tables are headed Allowed Values though they list time units, not values. The issue is closed as completed; no closing date is recorded.

items.t: [AI] Draft a companion details column PR for PrincipalId
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened the issue in July 2026 to draft a details column for PrincipalId under #2358. Maintainers agreed PrincipalId holds the IAM principal, with richer attributes in a companion column. It was split out so the column design could be settled without delaying #2360. On 28 July 2026 Matt-Cowsert said the draft existed but its shape was unsettled. The issue is closed as completed; the final design is not recorded.

items.t: [AI] Issue PR Part 1 for FR #2492: Revisit ListCost, ListUnitPrice, ContractedCost, ContractedUnitPrice specs
items.b: Issue #2562, opened by ijurica in July 2026, was an action item to extract the agreed description changes for ListCost, ContractedCost, ListUnitPrice and ContractedUnitPrice from staging PR #2513 into a dedicated PR for FR #2492. ijurica published the draft on 28 July, extended the deadline and added a requirement for alignment with another contributor. On 4 August 2026 ijurica reported the PR issued, alignment reached and the task complete.

items.t: [FR] Revisit specifications for ListCost, ListUnitPrice, ContractedCost, and ContractedUnitPrice
items.b: ijurica opened this feature request in June 2026 listing gaps in ListCost, ListUnitPrice, ContractedCost and ContractedUnitPrice, such as unclear discount boundaries and no rule on which pricing tier to report. Matt-Cowsert's TF1 updates tracked tiered-pricing glossary terms (#2564) and revised definitions (#2567, #2690), with IncludesUnitPricing kept for v1.5. In November 2026 #2564 was still unmerged and ijurica opened #2839. The thread doesn't record the final outcome.

items.t: [AI] Align Aggregation Guidance with Covering/Covered Charge Terminology Across the Spec
items.b: ijurica asked in July 2026 that aggregation guidance for ListCost, ContractedCost, PricingQuantity and CommitmentDiscountQuantity use covering and covered charge terms, treating commitment discounts as one example. On 18 August 2026 Matt-Cowsert folded the work into existing PRs for #2492. On 25 August 2026 ijurica offered revised wording in PR #2567. The issue was closed as completed, with changes incorporated into #2567. The thread doesn't record a closing date.

items.t: [FR]: Remove duplicative cost-formula requirement from PricingQuantity
[AI] Add Condition to Content Constraints table for every Conditional column
items.b: shawnalpay opened #2425 on 29 May 2026 asking for a Condition row in the Content Constraints table for every Conditional column in the FOCUS data model, adding to the conditions introduced in #2351. Success was defined as a draft pull request. On 18 August 2026, Matt-Cowsert reported it met that definition and was in release management review. The thread doesn't record a merge date. The issue is closed as completed.

items.t: [FR] Normalize how contract commitment durations are expressed
[Feedback] contractcommitmentdurationtype: introductory sentence between ## Allowed Values and table
items.b: davidearney asked whether ContractCommitmentDurationType should lose a lead-in sentence above its Allowed Values table, since #2106, via #2260, put such tables directly under the heading. shawnalpay kept it as an exception for now, noting the guidelines should cover such cases. In August 2026 davidearney reported it unchanged and suggested either recording a formal exception decision or removing the sentence. The thread doesn't record the outcome.

items.t: [FR] Add examples for token and generation-based AI billing in FOCUS
items.b: Matt-Cowsert asked for worked examples showing practitioners how AI token and image-generation billing maps onto existing FOCUS columns. TF-2 held the work until #2018 settled, then limited it to the Cost and Usage dataset and already-defined columns; ljadvey and finops-DaveMoreau built the examples in #2605, including a prepayment drawdown case. After seven approvals #2605 went to the October 2026 Members meeting, and the issue closed as completed that month.

items.t: [FR] Distinguish cached from uncached token costs
items.b: Matt-Cowsert asked in March 2026 for cached and uncached token costs to be distinguished; cache duration was later deferred. Task Force 2 voted in May to fold it into #2018, yet work continued here. In September a single TokenType property in #2606 became two, TokenCacheAction and TokenDirection, after flanakin argued for one attribute each. #2606 went to the October 1, 2026 members meeting; no comment records the outcome, and GitHub shows it closed as completed.

items.t: [AI] Review virtual currency treatment of tokens, credits, and crypto in the CurrencyFormat attribute
items.b: Matt-Cowsert, assigned with ijurica, reviewed virtual currency wording, since "tokens" now also meant an AI unit and "credits" clashed with the Credit charge category. In August 2026 Matt-Cowsert found CurrencyFormat contradicted itself, allowing virtual currency yet requiring ISO 4217 codes, and recommended narrowing the allowance to consumption currency and keeping cryptocurrency out, in draft #2617. The item closed that month, with tracking moved to the PR.

items.t: [AI] Restore the consumption currency glossary links unwrapped on PR #2617
items.b: In September 2026 Matt-Cowsert asked for five consumption currency glossary links, unwrapped on #2617, to be restored, since the anchor was missing until #2424 merged and broke the gen_pdf check. #2617 carried the glossary entry itself, so the links were restored there. #2617 merged on 1 October 2026 and the issue was closed as complete on 12 October 2026. #2424 is still open, so the separate pull request was unnecessary.

items.t: [AI] Draft the compute Service Category revision for FR #2377
[AI] Issue an editorial PR removing repeated condition links from the Cost and Usage dataset file
items.b: In July 2026, Matt-Cowsert opened an editorial issue to remove repeated condition links in the Cost and Usage dataset file, keeping one link per term. It was kept separate from #2582 and the follow-on IncludesUnitPricing removal so material changes would not be buried, and it was to be sequenced after the open condition PRs. On 11 August 2026, Matt-Cowsert closed it as complete, noting the PR was in place.

items.t: [FR] Convention for representing multi-condition presence triggers in dataset overview tables
items.b: Matt-Cowsert noted during review of #2390 that dataset overview tables linked each conditional column to a single condition, even when presence depended on several, and asked for a convention. Task force updates in August 2026 recorded that ijurica's #2625 would instead drop those links, relying on a planned conditions row in each column's constraints table. No comment records the outcome; GitHub shows it closed as completed.

items.t: [AI] Reconcile reused SkuPriceIds in the commitment discount example data with SKU Price row uniqueness
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened #2614 on 10 August 2026 over reused SkuPriceId values in the commitment examples that clash with SKU Price uniqueness. On 11 August 2026 the work was acknowledged on the TF-1 call and a new pull request planned. By 25 August 2026 it was drafted and in review with TF-1. The issue is closed as completed, but the thread doesn't record a merge date.

items.t: [AI] Submit a PR against PR #2395 covering the open AllocatedServiceName requirement threads
items.s: Issue · closed as not planned · 2026-09-29 · Matt-Cowsert

items.t: [AI] Re-apply the #2625 condition link removals that the #2580 merge overwrote
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this on 15 September 2026 after #2580 restored repeated condition links that #2625 had removed from four dataset files. The plan was to reapply #2625's removals to current content, keeping the first occurrence of each condition link, and to leave repeated column links for the v1.5 review (#2509). jpradocueva posted PR #2719 on 23 September 2026. The issue is closed as completed.

items.t: [AI] Capitalize glossary terms linked as the column subject
[AI] Align the Token and Consumption Currency glossary entries on measuring consumption
[AI] Add the Operating Model Conditions row to the AllocatedServiceName Content Constraints table
[AI] Align references and links in the specification with the contributor guidelines
items.b: In October 2026, ijurica opened this item to align references and links in the specification with the contributor guidelines. It covered entity IDs, display names, glossary terms, first-occurrence linking and link targets, and was described as best-effort. On 30 October 2026, ijurica reported that pull request #2773 had been approved and merged, added follow-up items to the backlog under #2798, and closed the item as completed.

items.t: [AI] Align the example-note rule between AGENTS.md and the Editorial Guidelines
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this action item because AGENTS.md and the Editorial Guidelines disagreed on where the informative, non-normative note belongs in example content, and the specification matched neither. ljadvey opened #2775 and #2777 and proposed notes only in the three top-level overview files, excluding the normative Rounding Variance Tolerance entry. Matt-Cowsert agreed, and the item was closed as completed in October 2026.

items.t: [AI] Align the casing of the Operating Model Conditions label in Content Constraints tables during the 1.5 consistency review
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened #2715 on 22 September 2026 to align the casing of the "Operating Model Conditions" row in Content Constraints tables, which uses title case while other rows use sentence case. A Task Force 1 member spotted it while reviewing #2424, which has the same label. The group agreed to fix it across the specification in the 1.5 consistency review, not on #2424. It remains open with no recorded outcome.

items.t: [AI] Decide whether JSON columns keep the second link to their schema and apply it consistently
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 17 September 2026 to decide whether JSON columns should keep a second, pointer-line link to their schema. Five columns share the pattern. The editorial guidelines and AGENTS.md differ on the repeat, and PR #2514 would drop AGENTS.md's functional-link exemption. jpradocueva suggested removing the pointer link on #2553, which kept it for consistency. The issue is open and no decision is recorded.

items.t: [AI] Fix note and notes blockquote formatting across the specification
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 9 July 2026 to fix 19 uses of "note" or "notes" across the specification, only a couple of which used the standard blockquote format. The work was part of the 1.5 consistency review (#2509) and arose from the #2360 review. On 27 October 2026, ijurica said PR #2791 was in good shape and suggested closing; Matt-Cowsert agreed. The issue is closed as complete.

items.t: [AI] Fix the remaining heading and column coverage items left out of #2766
items.b: In October 2026 thecloudman opened this issue to finish what PR #2766 left out of #2573: unused columns on the AI model billing page and ColumnId headings in the commitment discount appendix. Matt-Cowsert proposed in #2778 that headings use Display Names and JSON properties keep schema names. thecloudman also added three related title fixes. The issue is closed as completed, but the thread doesn't record the closing date.

items.t: [AI] Align the condition files with the editorial guidelines during the 1.5 consistency review
items.b: After TF-2 agreed to log repeated editorial guideline issues for the 1.5 consistency review rather than hold the pull request that surfaced them, Matt-Cowsert opened this item for ijurica, covering link-on-first-use and "evaluate to" findings jpradocueva raised on #2360. ijurica found the phrasing already consistent and scoped the work to missing links. It closed as completed in October 2026 after #2797 merged.

items.t: [AI] Rename RequesterDetailsValue to RequesterDetailsObject so the requirements model extracts it
[Feedback] Replace undefined Entry references in Requester Details object requirements
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 4 November 2026 because the Requester Details requirements use "Entry", which the specification never defines. The proposal swaps these for paths starting from RequesterDetailsObject, matching other columns, without changing the data shape or constraints. Matt-Cowsert says this would let validators use only dataset facts. The Requirements Model meeting discussed it on 3 November 2026. The issue remains open within the 1.5 errata bundle.

items.t: [AI] Draft PR adding Tiered Pricing-related glossary entries
items.b: Issue #2563 was opened by ijurica on 28 July 2026. It asked for a dedicated pull request gathering the agreed Tiered Pricing glossary entries for review and merge. Its only checklist item was issuing that pull request. Matt-Cowsert closed the issue as complete the same day, since the draft now existed. The thread has no further discussion and doesn't record whether the pull request was later merged.

items.t: [AI] Draft PR addressing critical tier mentions (focus: tiered pricing)
items.b: In July 2026, ijurica opened #2570 to create a dedicated pull request covering the critical tier-related mentions, especially tiered pricing, identified in the prioritised list from #2569. On 13 August 2026, ijurica said the work would reuse the existing pull request #2564 instead. On 18 August 2026, Matt-Cowsert marked the issue completed, and it was closed as complete. The thread doesn't say whether #2564 was merged.

items.t: [AI] Draft the appendix sample data for the Recommendation dataset
[Editorial] Correct the Contract Commitment and commitment program examples for the 1.5 release
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 5 November 2026 after a reviewer checked the 1.5 specification. It lists wrong examples, example data, and descriptions in the contract commitment and commitment program eligibility text, including invalid category values, a discount formula, and period dates. The editorial fixes aim to merge before the 1.5 IP Review ends on 1 December 2026. No comments or decisions are recorded, and the issue is open.

items.t: [Editorial] Correct the split cost allocation and commitment discount examples for the 1.5 release
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 5 November 2026 to collect errors in 1.5 appendix examples found during a 4 November review. The proposed fixes covered commitment discount and split cost allocation numbers, a ServiceSubcategory value, a null origin-row field, and two supported feature queries. They were meant to merge before the review ended on 1 December 2026. The issue was open, and the thread doesn't record the outcome.

items.t: [Consistency Review]: Use consistent casing for the word decimal
items.b: udam-f2 raised an editorial issue: the word decimal was capitalized inconsistently, and udam-f2 proposed standard casing. In an October 2024 task force call a suggestion was made to capitalize the Decimal type and lowercase it for values. The issue was closed as completed in October 2024 after udam-f2 agreed it could be closed.

items.t: [Editorial] Correct the metadata links, key names, and examples for the 1.5 release
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 5 November 2026 to fix errors in the 1.5 Metadata section and examples, found in a 4 November review. Fixes cover broken links, wrong key names, a nonexistent Contract dataset, and timestamp format. Changes are informative only and may merge into working_draft before the IP Review ends 1 December 2026. Requirement-text fixes are proposed in #2836 and #2837. No decisions recorded; the issue remains open.

items.t: [WI] Add a pre-discount amortized cost column
items.b: cnharris10 proposed CommitmentDiscountUnitPrice and CommitmentDiscountCost columns, because the committed rate of a commitment discount was not exposed and could not be separated from negotiated discounts in EffectiveCost, which practitioners with high commitment coverage wanted for forecasting. ijurica agreed and corrected the example values, smokemonster99 saw value for auditing, and maintainers rated it high impact. cnharris10 linked it to the savings-rate work in #298 and modeled two options, which ijurica found described the same concept. aws-letianfeng preferred treating it as a pre-discount amortized cost. It was moved out of 1.2 for lack of consensus in March 2025. Matt-Cowsert closed it, marked completed, in October 2025, saying neither #961 nor #1384 had gained traction and the request had changed greatly.

items.t: [Editorial] Correct summary tables, glossary entries, labels, and links for the 1.5 release
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this editorial issue on 5 November 2026 to list errors found in a review of the 1.5 specification. Fixes covered summary tables, glossary entries and order, preview labels, relationships, section order and links. Text-only fixes were to merge into working_draft before the IP Review's end on 1 December 2026. Requirement-text fixes were proposed as errata in #2836. The thread records no discussion, and the issue was open.

items.t: [AI] Draft PR for Contract columns in Cost and Usage dataset
[AI] Present strawman for Feature Level revisions
items.b: This action item asked shawnalpay to present a strawman of proposed Feature Level changes to the Maintainers. The concept was presented on May 11, and PRs #2374, #2375 and #2376 were assembled and reviewed on May 18. It was closed as completed in May 2026, with much more still to discuss. The thread is housekeeping.

items.t: [FR] Clarify included/excluded Discounts in Contracted Unit Price (and Contracted Cost)
items.b: ijurica requested in January 2026 that the Contracted Unit Price and Contracted Cost definitions state which discounts are included or excluded, especially negotiated commitment-based discounts. aaronmsoto agreed that the phrase "any other discounts" was ambiguous. Matt-Cowsert closed the issue in August 2026 as superseded by #2492, whose work moved to PR #2567, then in Task Force review. Bundled discounts and a discount taxonomy were carried to #2641 and #2642.
items.s: Issue · closed as not planned · 2026-08-14 · ijurica

items.t: [Proposal] "Billing Account" term and description confusion
items.b: flanakin raised that the billing account description did not make clear it is the scope where an invoice is generated. udam-f2 asked to separate that from a side point about linking glossary terms. TF1 agreed to add a glossary link and await practitioner feedback, though ahullah found such links did not work. The group judged the glossary description good enough, and the issue closed as completed in June 2024.

items.t: [WI] Augment support for correction handling
items.b: ijurica opened a work item for an overarching correction-handling attribute, since correction rules were scattered and inconsistent across columns. Calls showed divergent views on how much specification was needed; the work was tied to refund handling in #636, with ahullah drafting an appendix and ijurica drafting refund and correction definitions. shawnalpay objected when it was auto-closed while incomplete. Matt-Cowsert closed it in October 2025, its scope captured in #962.

items.t: [AI] Draft skeleton PR for tag details (Column J key-driven approach)
[AI] Facilitate decision on naming via spreadsheet and/or vote
items.b: shawnalpay opened this action item to settle a column name through a spreadsheet or vote, including use cases, and in March 2025 pressed flanakin on whether a poll existed, warning that the related pull request might miss its deadline. A naming spreadsheet for the double-counting column was then shared. It was closed as completed in March 2025 with no further discussion.

items.t: [Proposal] PricingSubcategory to describe the pricing model more precisely
items.s: Issue · closed as not planned · 2024-02-14 · flanakin

items.t: Handle UC scenarios when pricing and billing are in different currencies
items.b: ijurica proposed PricingCurrency, ExchangeRate and ExchangeRateDate columns for charges priced and billed in different currencies. udam-f2 suggested splitting PricingCurrency from the harder exchange-rate problem, while flanakin wanted both together because exchange rates were needed to do the math. In March 2024 TF-1 moved it after 1.0, noting a ListUnitPriceInPricingCurrency column as an alternative. shawnalpay closed it as completed in May 2025, done as work in #616.

items.t: Add Support Service Category
items.b: yprikhodko asked for a Support value in ServiceCategory to separate support charges from workload charges, pointing to #251. thecloudman agreed but noted Microsoft did not include support in usage data while other providers did. With no PR by the 1.0 deadlines jpradocueva set, maintainers moved it to v1.1 in April 2024. In May 2024 the description was copied to #379 and the issue was closed as completed.

items.t: [AI] Draft PRs of Feature Level revisions and new column
items.b: Opened 13 May 2026 by shawnalpay, #2373 asked for draft pull requests for Feature Level downgrades, Feature Level upgrades and a Data Generator Name column. On 19 May 2026 shawnalpay reported the drafts were done and out of draft. On 28 May 2026 shawnalpay finished an initial review of them and closed the issue as completed, with further discussion expected. Mostly status updates; no merges are recorded.

items.t: [AI] Draft Wireframe PR for Recommendations Dataset
items.b: qquigley's action item was to open a draft wireframe pull request for a recommendations dataset under #975, covering MVP questions such as a recommendation type taxonomy, core columns, savings format and join keys to Cost and Usage. qquigley opened #2444, and shawnalpay asked for a follow-up action item, which qquigley created as #2446. Matt-Cowsert closed it as completed in June 2026, noting qquigley was still gathering practitioner support on scope.

items.t: [AI] Revise data issues in examples for Simple & Spend SaaS Agreements
items.b: This action item, from #830, asked for fixes to data issues in the Simple and Spend SaaS Agreement examples. ijurica compiled proposed changes and raised whether ConsumedQuantity requirements fit unused-fee rows and whether ListCost and ContractedCost should be 0 on them, preferring 0. UdamDewaraja and ijurica aligned on the sheet, and UdamDewaraja took on CSV conversion following #896. It was closed as completed in April 2025.

items.t: [FR] Specify tier handling in requirements for List Unit Price and List Cost
items.b: shawnalpay asked that ListUnitPrice and ListCost requirements say which pricing tier they reflect, because AWS fills them from the highest tier, inflating savings. cnharris10 asked about negotiated tiers, which udam-stitcher said affect only contracted prices. udam-stitcher also noted a contradiction in the issue text and argued list price should follow the row's SKU Price ID, so existing rules may already cover tiers. It remained open, last discussed in November 2025. shawnalpay asked that ListUnitPrice and ListCost requirements say which pricing tier they reflect, because AWS fills them from the highest tier, inflating savings. cnharris10 asked about negotiated tiers, which udam-stitcher said affect only contracted prices. udam-stitcher also noted a contradiction in the issue text and argued list price should follow the row's SKU Price ID, so existing rules may already cover tiers. It remained open, last discussed in November 2025.

items.t: [FR] Distinguish global from regional prices by region scope
items.b: Matt-Cowsert proposed a FOCUS property distinguishing globally routed from region-pinned prices, mainly driven by AI model serving. The group debated its name and its link to the SKU Price dataset, with flanakin and ijurica raising naming and consistency concerns. On 23 September 2026 PR #2613 was postponed to the 1.6 cycle, and by 7 October 2026 no one had volunteered to take it up. The issue remains open. Matt-Cowsert proposed a FOCUS property distinguishing globally routed from region-pinned prices, mainly driven by AI model serving. The group debated its name and its link to the SKU Price dataset, with flanakin and ijurica raising naming and consistency concerns. On 23 September 2026 PR #2613 was postponed to the 1.6 cycle, and by 7 October 2026 no one had volunteered to take it up. The issue remains open.

items.t: Should Availability Zone be a conditional field for all providers that support an availability zone concept (today it's optional)
items.b: ahullah asked whether AvailabilityZone, then optional, should be required for providers that support availability zones, following up a compromise reached in #331, and cited cross-zone data transfer and resilience use cases. In April 2024 the group agreed to revisit it after 1.0, expecting it to become a MUST for such providers. The issue was closed as completed in April 2024 after the associated PR #369 was closed.

items.t: [AI] Draft Delivery Grain attribute PR for FOCUS
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 28 May 2026 to draft a PR tied to #2358 on an opt-in delivery grain concept. The group agreed it should be opt-in but rejected placing it under column content constraints, and left open whether it should be standalone or part of Dataset Configuration. finops-DaveMoreau drafted it as a prerequisite for #2360. It was reviewed 17 June and closed as complete on 18 June 2026.

items.t: [AI] Create draft PR for unit price columns metric-to-dimension reclassification
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this action item to split a reclassification of four unit price columns from metrics to dimensions out of #1816 into a separate draft pull request. flanakin created #1908, but shawnalpay considered the change outside 1.4 scope and udam-stitcher argued unit prices are metrics. TF-2 agreed the pull request had been premature, and the item was closed as completed in February 2026 as work not planned for 1.4.

items.t: Update to allowed ServiceCategory values
items.b: AWS-ZachErdman asked to add ServiceCategory values so AWS could represent its own service groupings. mike-finopsorg said a normalized list could not match every provider, flanakin shared the group's principles for adding categories, and AWS-ZachErdman still questioned some placements. SonalGarg-SG proposed a partial set in #403, but TF2 deferred the issue to 1.1 pending a subcategory column, and it was closed as completed in June 2024, linked to #404 and #321.

items.t: [WI] Prevent double-counting list/contracted cost for commitment discounts
items.b: flanakin reported that savings calculations double-counted commitment purchases, because purchase and usage rows both carried ListCost and ContractedCost, and proposed an AmortizationCategory column. cnharris10 asked whether PricingCategory already covered this; flanakin said standard purchases could be amortized too. JGrubb suggested accounting terms such as prepayment, and shawnalpay floated adding coverage-eligibility values. Matt-Cowsert closed it in October 2025, its scope captured in #974.

items.t: [AI] Revise draft Recommendation dataset PR and obtain Maintainer approval
items.b: qquigley opened this task on 6 June 2026 to revise the wireframe Recommendation dataset pull request (#2381) through review until a Maintainer approved it, gathering feedback from Maintainers, the Working Group and the community. shawnalpay replied on 7 June 2026 that it looked good and suggested setting a due date. The issue is closed as completed, but the thread doesn't record an approval.

items.t: [AI] Introduce Correction Handling attribute
items.b: This action item asked for PRs introducing a Correction Handling attribute and its supporting content. ijurica brought a draft, and TF1 reviewed #1368, a lift-and-shift from #1151, in August 2025. Once #1368 was authored, shawnalpay noted PRs now covered the whole feature request and closed the item as completed in August 2025. The thread is mostly housekeeping.

items.t: [WI] Add support for coverage eligibility
items.b: cnharris10 asked for a way to tell whether a usage charge was eligible for a commitment discount, since coverage analysis otherwise needed extra data. mike-finopsorg cautioned that eligibility should not be read as a coverage target, which cnharris10 accepted; TF-2 split on priority but made it a work item, rated medium effort and high impact. items.t: How a token charge is recorded
items.b: A token charge is an ordinary Cost and Usage row. ServiceCategory is "AI and Machine Learning", ConsumedUnit is "Tokens" and ConsumedQuantity counts them. PricingQuantity and PricingUnit say how they were priced, which can be in blocks, such as per million tokens. Which model, and which kind of token, are recorded inside one JSON column, SkuPriceDetails, as FOCUS-defined properties. ModelDeveloper, ModelFamily, ModelId and ModelVersion describe the model. TokenDirection (input or output) and TokenCacheAction (uncached, cache read, cache write) describe the tokens. All six are new in the 1.5 candidate. Who made the request can be recorded in three columns, also new in 1.5: PrincipalId, CredentialId and RequesterDetails, for example the service account or API key behind the calls. Everything else, such as cost, currency, period and provider, uses the same columns as any other charge. FOCUS enables normalization of usage-based billing data from artificial intelligence and machine learning services, including token consumption for AI model APIs. Token quantities are represented through consumption and pricing columns, allowing consumption and cost to be tracked by [*SKU*](#glossary:sku), token direction, and cache interaction. The TokenDirection and TokenCacheAction properties of [SkuPriceDetails](#datamodel.costandusage.skupricedetails) label the direction of the metered tokens and their interaction with a cache, so those attributes can be compared across service providers independently of provider-specific meter names, with model identity carried in the same SkuPriceDetails object.

items.t: The token details are optional
items.b: SkuPriceDetails is a conditional column that may be empty even when a price is identified, and the model and token properties are recommendations (SHOULD), not requirements. A provider can conform without them, so comparing token costs across providers depends on each one choosing to fill them in.
items.x: SkuPriceDetails MAY be null when SkuPriceId is not null. SkuPriceDetails SHOULD include TokenDirection when the *SKU Price* meters only input or only output tokens.

items.t: They sit inside a JSON column
items.b: The working group chose properties inside SkuPriceDetails over new columns (#2018, #2442), and the newer proposals follow the same pattern: region scope (#2613), processing tier (#2873) and context window bounds (#2871). That keeps the column list stable, but every token query has to unpack JSON. The specification's queries use BigQuery's JSON_VALUE, which other databases write differently: the lab runs them in DuckDB through a small json_value macro. The context window proposal would also put its bounds in named columns of the SKU Price dataset, a preview in 1.5 (#2872). Whether SKU properties belong in SKU Price, in a separate SKU details dataset or only in Cost and Usage is an open action item for making SKU Price generally available (#2807, #2888).
items.x: Similar JSON functions are widely available across major SQL engines with variances in syntax, so the examples may need to be adapted for other database engines.

items.t: Models and tokens don't line up across providers
items.b: The same model can carry a different ModelId from each seller, and a token is not a fixed amount of content. So a cost per million tokens compares prices, not work done, and comparing one model across providers needs ModelDeveloper, ModelFamily and ModelVersion filled in as well.
items.x: ModelId: Identifier for the model as it appears in billing, which may be namespaced by the service provider and is not guaranteed to match across service providers. The amount of content a single token represents is determined by the model, so token counts are not directly comparable across models.

items.t: Pricing dimensions not covered yet
items.b: The specification names dimensions that the token properties deliberately leave out, and each has an open request. Others have been raised since: processing tiers such as batch or priority, provisioned throughput, regional prices and finer AI service subcategories. Work on AI pricing for 1.6 started with context window size (#2521), with processing tiers and provisioned throughput to follow. Two now have pull requests: context window bounds as SkuPriceDetails properties and as SKU Price columns (#2871, #2872, both drafts), and a ProcessingTier property with the values Standard, Priority, Flex, Batch and Other (#2873). They take opposite sides of a question still open: #2873 gives each processing tier its own SkuId, while #2871's examples keep one SkuId and give each context window tier its own SkuPriceId, as the quantity tier pricing example does. Google Cloud's billing data gives each context window tier its own SKU ID, as noted at Task Force 1 on 17 November, and an example dataset drawn from providers' billing data is being built to ground the next discussion (#2877). A query for what caching saves was taken out until the SKU Price dataset can supply the uncached price (#2702).
items.x: Dimensions that qualify a charge without describing the direction of its tokens or their interaction with a cache, such as token modality, reasoning effort, cache retention duration, and context window size, are not values of these properties.

items.t: No public data with token charges yet
items.b: Only the specification's worked examples contain token rows. The token queries return nothing on the accepted 1.0 sample or on the samples proposed for 1.3 and 1.4, so no public FOCUS sample data yet shows token billing.

items.t: No place for cost a gateway works out
items.b: An LLM gateway between a company's teams and a model provider knows which team made each call and how many input, output and cache tokens it used, and can price them before the invoice arrives. FOCUS says an entity that doesn't invoice, or doesn't originate the cost and usage data, must report BilledCost and EffectiveCost as 0, so merged datasets don't count the cost twice. It doesn't say where such a layer should put the cost it worked out. Feedback raised on 20 November asks whether ListCost or ContractedCost may carry it, or whether it belongs in x_ columns or a separate allocation dataset (#2885).
items.x: BilledCost MUST be 0 for *charges* generated by entities that are not responsible or authorized for invoicing, to avoid double-counting when merging multiple [*dataset instances*](#glossary:dataset-instance). items.t: Because FOCUS did not show which charges could be tagged, tag coverage reports penalised teams for untaggable resources and made governance targets unrealistic; practitioners also could not tell where an inherited value in the Tags column came from.

items.t: Container platforms split applications into pods, tasks and executors below the machine level, while providers reported compute cost per virtual machine, so practitioners could not report accurate showback and chargeback without provider-calculated split cost allocation.

items.t: FOCUS supported only pre-purchased burn-down commitments such as RIs and Savings Plans; contract-negotiated commitments could not be identified or linked, burn-down and build-up progress could not be tracked, and threshold deals without a pre-purchase could not be represented.
items.b: negotiated burn-down and build-up commitments are incompletely represented in FOCUS

items.t: The umbrella term Commitment Discount excluded negotiated agreements and assumed pre-purchased burn-down commitments, so the spec kept adding disclaimers; that broke down for SaaS and for negotiated deals such as OCI Universal Credits, Microsoft MACC and AWS EDP.
items.b: it becomes problematic when applied more broadly

items.t: Without a commitment eligibility indicator, practitioners could not tell which on-demand charges could move to commitment discounts or public pricing tiers; effective savings rate calculations meant joining external datasets and switching to provider consoles.
items.b: Optimization recommendations require context-switching between FOCUS data and provider consoles

items.t: A BilledCost rule requiring zero for charges paid to a third party zeroed out every marketplace purchase, even where the cloud marketplace issued the invoice, breaking invoice reconciliation; the fix proposed tying the rule to the invoice issuer.
items.b: This creates invoice reconciliation problems because it zeros out BilledCost for ALL marketplace purchases

items.t: Because the InvoiceId definition did not require every invoiced charge to appear in FOCUS, total BilledCost could differ from the invoice, leaving practitioners making manual adjustments and chasing variances during invoice reconciliation.

items.t: A contributor argued that setting BilledCost to zero for marketplace-billed SaaS charges would block chargeback; BilledCost rules were later changed to prevent double counting between vendor and marketplace records by tying sums to the invoice issuer's invoices.

items.b: invoices do not typically contain a complete list of all goods and services purchased

items.t: The Tags column banned altering user-defined keys, so providers with two tagging systems, AWS resource tags and cost categories or GCP tags and labels, would overwrite one value when the same key existed in both.

items.t: Summing ListCost or ContractedCost double-counted commitment discounts, because the purchase row and every amortized usage row carried those costs; a worked example summed $1,095 of list cost against an actual $730, with no provider-agnostic way to exclude rows.
items.b: Given the extreme likelihood that nearly every practitioner will get caught by this

items.t: CommitmentDiscountStatus was added as its own column, rather than as ChargeCategory values, because practitioners wanted unused commitment amounts included when filtering on Usage; its name was settled by a naming poll.

Many providers priced in one currency and billed in another, but FOCUS 1.0 preview had only BillingCurrency, so practitioners could not spot such charges or reconcile them with prices shown elsewhere; PricingCurrency and exchange rate columns were proposed.
items.b: Practitioners should be able to identify when charges are priced in a different currency

items.t: To open FOCUS to flat-fee vendors without breaking practitioners' schemas, the proposal kept ListCost and ContractedCost in the schema but made them conditionally nullable, so complex cloud providers still had to supply detailed metrics.
items.b: the columns remain present in the schema but become conditionally nullable

items.t: To let flat-fee SaaS and non-cloud vendors conform without inventing data, columns such as ListCost and ContractedCost were proposed as conditional; a reviewer objected most were essential for FinOps use cases, so work narrowed to a classification rubric, deferring existing columns to 1.6.

To attribute SaaS and GenAI spend to actors while avoiding personal data, PrincipalId shipped first with ConsumerId carved out; maintainers kept one IAM-based identifier rather than an object with names and emails, and high-cardinality opt-in moved to 1.6.

Contributors warned that limits on correcting closed billing periods could deter vendors, while others held data must be accurate before being marked final; the Correction Handling work converged on separating invoice status from data delivery status.

Cache duration was deferred from the cached-token request because only one surveyed provider priced retention as a user choice, values did not align and a task force discussion could not classify duration; retention price points stayed visible through separate SkuPriceId values.
items.b: The cache duration portion of these criteria is deferred.

items.t: A reviewer argued an exchange rate column was vital in the Invoice Detail dataset, but TF-1 had not supported it, since one invoice rate would create rounding errors against daily rates and an effective rate can be derived; payment-related statuses were ruled out.

The AI model identity request was limited to data appearing in or alongside billing records; telemetry such as latency, CPU utilisation and sampling parameters like temperature was ruled out of scope as belonging to observability tools.
items.b: Those belong in observability tooling, not cost and usage data.

items.t: For AI model identity and input versus output token costs, maintainers kept the request narrow, chose FOCUS-defined SkuPriceDetails properties over new columns, reused existing unit and quantity columns, and dropped ModelVariant because market naming was unsettled.

Column selection was framed as a data delivery requirement that offset the bloat of FR #1094's rule to carry all native provider columns; the group agreed to test an existing attribute construct before inventing new specification sections.
items.b: stress-test against existing constructs (attribute) before inventing new spec sections

items.t: The AI billing request was scoped as supporting content rather than new columns, because FOCUS 1.3 already had ConsumedQuantity, ConsumedUnit, PricingQuantity, PricingUnit and ServiceCategory; the gap was practitioners' understanding of how to map tokens and generations.
items.b: The gap is not in the specification schema but in practitioner understanding
