items.t: The TagDetails column was descoped from FOCUS 1.4 when maintainers judged it would not survive member review: its scope had grown without re-review, a reviewer backed SHOULD presence on dataset-size grounds, and another opposed adding a Recommended column without solid reason.

The task force chose a JSON structure rather than a Boolean for Commitment Eligibility, carrying both the provider's own eligibility term and a FOCUS category (spend-based or usage-based), to support true coverage rates and effective savings rate.
items.b: uses a JSON structure (not Boolean) to indicate commitment eligibility

items.t: Deprecating ProviderName and PublisherName for Service Provider and Host Provider columns, FOCUS's first deprecation, drew an objection that customers would have to change their queries; the author replied naming was better fixed now, and the deprecation window was shortened to one release.

FOCUS 1.3 shipped only a basic foundation of Contract Commitment columns; further columns shown in a modelling spreadsheet were held back for more discussion and refinement in a future release, and a follow-on request gathered the use cases for them.
items.b: require further discussion and refinement, to be added in a future release

items.t: The commitment eligibility request was scoped to non-negotiated programs, publicly listed reduced rates open to every customer, covering CSP commitments and SaaS public pricing tiers; negotiated discounts set by spend volume or relationship were declared out of scope.
items.b: The provider would not refuse any customer seeking to enter the program

items.t: User feedback said the provider and publisher columns were confusing and inconsistent, but the working group chose not to make aggressive corrective changes in FOCUS 1.2, deferring a fix to 1.3 so marketplace buyers would know whom they bought from.
items.b: In 1.2 it was decided that we not make any aggressive corrective changes

items.t: Rather than add more SKU details to cost and usage rows, which would duplicate data massively, the request proposed a separate SKU Price dataset joined to Cost and Usage by SkuId, extending analysis without modifying existing columns.
items.b: given the massive amount of duplication

items.t: For the ContractApplied column, most participants in August 2025 favoured always requiring the proposed JSON datapoints for usability, while some prioritised dataset size; maintainers let data generators omit inapplicable cost, quantity or unit values.

For split cost allocation, TF-2 compared split lines, double-entry rows and a secondary dataset; a poll favoured split lines despite worries about breaking existing reports, and allocations had to reconcile to the original charge and be flagged.

In October 2025 maintainers deferred the Correction Handling attribute until an Invoice dataset existed, so rules on when data generators may revise invoiced data had something to stand on; it shipped with a Delivery Handling attribute in April 2026.

Because TF-2 found the original scope for dataset recency and completeness hard for providers, it was narrowed to optional metadata with data generators setting their own completeness thresholds, and completeness declarations became a SHOULD rather than a MUST.

After ambiguous EffectiveCost and BilledCost definitions led data generators to implement them inconsistently, the work got a late-September deadline, was cut from 1.3 when no path emerged, and was reframed for 1.4 around accuracy, avoiding the term amortization.

To let practitioners rely on FOCUS alone, datasets were required to carry x_ custom columns for uncovered native billing data; a provider-side request for SHOULD warned AWS exports would exceed 100 columns, so MUST stayed while data generators could default to a column subset.

Asked to organise FOCUS as related datasets for BI tools without bloating the main dataset, the group ran a six-week spike, ruled out a star schema for 1.3, and rejected fact and dimension terminology as too database-specific.

The SKU Price dataset, requested for lookups, joins and pre-purchase estimation, took a current-snapshot model with one row per price so each keeps its own dates; a sustained objection was met by releasing it as a preview in FOCUS 1.5.

Because some members rejected redefining existing unit price columns, pricing currency support was added as four new columns, leaving existing ones unchanged; maintainers struck the exchange rate column and deferred exchange rates, a problem first moved past 1.0 in 2024.

A request to relax the BillingCurrency rule from MUST to SHOULD, because AWS exports bill in USD while invoices may be in other currencies, was refused during consistency review because the MUST dated from release 0.5, and was closed pending an advocate.

To spare providers from updating every row when an invoice is issued, the InvoiceId proposal noted a possible separate table mapping invoices to rows; a reviewer worried that providers such as GCP cannot restate exported data.

The follow-up work item struck out splitting ListCost and ContractedCost into separate actual and amortized columns, proposing instead a flag column such as AmortizationCategory, deliberately named to cover future amortized recurring purchases, not just commitment purchases and usage.
items.b: I avoided the words "purchase" and "usage" here since we could have purchases amortized

items.t: Because breaking changes forced upgrading practitioners to rewrite SQL queries or reshape exports, the working group set rules to avoid them unless the benefit outweighed the adoption cost, and to weigh that in its development process.
items.b: when the benefit of the change outweighs the cost it presents to practitioners

items.t: To stop savings calculations double counting commitment purchases in ListCost and ContractedCost, an AmortizationClass column won a naming poll, but reviewers called the name misleading and the scope too narrow for SaaS; it was pushed to 1.3 and closed unmerged.

A November 2024 work item set out to define what counts as a breaking change and how to weigh its cost to practitioners against its benefit, with use cases classified by whether they changed between FOCUS 1.0 and 1.1.

Because FOCUS had been built around cloud providers and offered SaaS providers no onramp beyond custom columns, the work item proposed a time-boxed analysis of major SaaS providers first, with an MVP only if time allowed, mirroring FOCUS 0.5 for clouds.
items.b: We propose performing a time-boxed analysis of SaaS concepts

items.t: Because of deadlines, a consistency review standardising how columns handle correction charges was cut to ConsumedUnit and ConsumedQuantity, leaving the other columns unchanged for 1.1.

Naming the column that describes what a SKU meters was put to the community: from August 2024 TF-2, maintainer and member calls used naming spreadsheets and polls, and a revote added alternatives from a contributor who did not want the name to look chosen by Microsoft. SKU Meter was the result.
Rather than prefix every tag, the Tags fix let providers prefix keys for all but one user-defined tagging scheme, so practitioners could still reference one scheme without a prefix.
items.b: This allows for 1 tagging scheme to remain without a user-defined `prefix`

items.t: Capacity Reservation ID was made a SHOULD rather than a MUST because AWS would not initially provide values and conformance had to stay possible without labelling used reservation charges; a status was required only when an ID is present.

For SkuPriceDetails, a maintainer asked for SHOULD rather than MUST on consistent properties, fearing it would block support, but maintainers kept MUST on the principle that no data is better than bad data; TF-2 also merged two proposed columns into one.

When approval of commitment burndown columns failed amid fears that redundant columns would bloat datasets, separate consumed and purchased quantity columns were merged into one CommitmentDiscountQuantity column, which members approved in September 2024.

Commitment discount unit price and cost columns, wanted by practitioners with high commitment coverage for forecasting and rated high impact, were moved out of 1.2 for lack of consensus; one maintainer called them a niche case that would burden providers without commitments.

For the ListCost and ContractedCost double counting, the proposer weighed three routes: a prescriptive cross-provider filter, leaving both columns null on affected rows, or polling practitioners on whether double-reported costs were acceptable.
items.b: Poll practitioners to confirm that they find it adequate to double-report the costs

items.t: Columns for negotiated prices were debated as Negotiated or OnDemand, the latter because many organisations have no negotiated discounts; a vote produced ContractedUnitPrice and ContractedCost, though one member objected that negotiated discount is established FinOps parlance.

A commitment coverage-eligibility indicator split TF-2 on priority but became a work item rated medium effort and high impact; scoped for 1.3, it was repeatedly bumped and descoped, then shipped as Commitment Program Eligibility Details once a sponsor drafted it.

A request to add ServiceCategory values so AWS could represent its own service groupings met the reply that a normalised list could not match every provider, and TF2 deferred it to 1.1 pending a subcategory column.

Making AvailabilityZone mandatory was withdrawn until after the v1 GA because it does not affect cost and had been left as SHOULD to avoid blocking adoption; the group expected it to become a MUST for providers that support zones.

EffectiveCost's wording, inclusive of all reduced rates, left unclear whether tier-blended rates like AWS BlendedCost counted; the proposal kept EffectiveCost unblended and said so explicitly, because most practitioners worked with unblended rates.
items.b: Most practitioners use and are familiar with rates that do not blend rates

items.t: Unsure what the top-level breakdown of usage charges in ChargeSubcategory should be, the group moved Used and Unused Commitment to a dedicated column for 1.0 GA and left the breakdown to revisit with post-GA feedback.
items.b: We did not have a clear idea of what this should be

items.t: Asked whether small SaaS vendors must provide every column even when most would be null, contributors favoured a smaller required core; 16 columns were chosen as FOCUS Essential, later reworked into mandatory, conditional and optional feature levels.

BillingAccountType and SubAccountType were held back from v1.0 after members questioned their practical value and added schema size and maintainers leaned toward metadata; moved to v1.1, they were finally added as conditional columns in 1.2.

Pricing Unit was renamed PricingMeasure and left non-normalised, but after objections that Measure means something else in reporting models, the group reversed within days to a semi-normalised Pricing Unit, with a separate PricingBlockSize proposed as a v1.x follow-up.

Custom columns were first to start with an underscore; a working-group call then chose a vendor prefix, a reviewer warned leading underscores need special handling in engines such as Athena, and the rule settled on a required x_ prefix that others may extend.

Rather than drop the word discount from CommitmentDiscountId so it also covered on-demand capacity reservations, which have no term, the group kept the column to commitment discounts and put a separate capacity reservation column on the backlog.

items.t: [FR] Define path to mandatory, testable FOCUS metadata
items.b: Matt-Cowsert proposes a path to mandatory, testable FOCUS metadata. Today the specification recommends metadata alongside a dataset but does not require it, and nothing standard says where metadata lives, when it arrives, or how a delivered file links to it. Data engineers, practitioners and vendors therefore write custom logic for each data generator to learn dataset versions, structure and completeness. The request asks for required metadata rules, scoped by which datasets are time series, that reviewers can mark pass or fail from a delivery. If adopted, data generators would know what a conforming delivery must provide, including preview datasets and version changes. The issue is open with no comments yet. Provider support is unknown and an inventory is still to be collected, so nothing has been decided.

items.t: AI #2460: Remove dependency loop from 1.5 Requirements Model
items.b: Matt-Cowsert proposes a small change to the 1.5 Requirements Model, part of #2460's work to add all 1.5 changes. Thirty-six rules form a dependency loop, and every circular path runs through one edge: CAU-ChargeCategory-C-009-C depends on the whole SkuPriceId group, which depends back on ChargeCategory. The PR repoints that rule to CAU-SkuPriceId-C-001-M, the SkuPriceId type rule, which has no dependencies. This is a deliberate exception to the contributor guidelines, which would otherwise mean narrowing at least six other rules. The rule also stops inheriting an IncludesUnitPricing condition, so the target choice affects validation results. Only working_draft changes; the same dependency remains in other 1.5 tags. The PR is open with no approvals, reviews or comments yet, so reception is untested, and the thread says nothing about next steps.

items.t: [FR] Enable comparing delivered capacity with reserved capacity
items.b: undiscopurrr proposes a conditional column, provisionally Capacity Reservation Delivered Quantity, stating how much of a reserved charge the data generator counts as delivered. Today, capacity made unavailable by host failures or unscheduled maintenance shows as Unused, just like capacity the customer chose not to use, and reserved GPU clusters often settle shortfalls later through service credits. Practitioners therefore rebuild delivered capacity outside FOCUS. The proposal counts hours the agreement excludes, such as scheduled maintenance, as delivered, and wants consistent treatment across generators. PSYCHE wants it to compare with its SQCD-1 format. Generator support is unknown. The issue was opened on 22 November 2026 and has had no replies, so its direction is untested.

items.t: [Feedback] How should a non-invoicing metering layer (such as an LLM gateway) carry its computed cost when BilledCost and EffectiveCost must be 0?
items.b: andrasKelle asks how a non-invoicing metering layer, such as an LLM gateway that prices usage into per-team costs, should carry that computed cost when FOCUS 1.4 requires BilledCost and EffectiveCost to be 0. The open questions are whether ListCost or ContractedCost can hold it without double counting when datasets merge, whether originating usage detail without cost counts as originating, and whether the data belongs in custom columns or a separate allocation dataset. roy-tong replies that the metered and billed distinction should be kept: BilledCost should stay absent rather than copy an estimate, EffectiveCost should hold the best per-request figure, and a provenance field should show whether a number came from an invoice or a local estimate. No maintainer has responded yet, so the thread looks unresolved and no specification change is proposed.

items.t: [FR] Add granular sustainability dimensions and metrics
items.b: #972, opened by Matt-Cowsert in May 2025, asks for optional carbon, power and water columns in FOCUS datasets, keyed to the same resources and regions as cost. A comment from guillermollopis narrows this to AI token rows, which already carry model and token fields in FOCUS 1.5. It proposes optional estimated energy in kWh and location-based emissions in kg CO2e, plus a provenance field stating the method and grid-intensity basis. Most AI providers won't publish measured energy per request, so estimates will come from third parties, and provenance keeps them labelled. Cost and carbon would then sit on one row. guillermollopis also asks where the fields belong, whether location-based should be the default, and whether kWh or joules is the right unit. No replies appear in the last two weeks, so the thread looks quiet.

items.t: Split Append delivery into Additive and Versioned Append
items.b: This draft PR from flanakin, opened on 21 November 2026, splits the Append delivery mechanism into two. Additive Append adds new rows that practitioners sum. Versioned Append adds new versions of earlier rows, and practitioners keep the latest per row key, which needs a row key and a last-updated column. The no-deduplication rule would exclude Versioned Append, while the preserve-all-artifacts rule would cover both. SKU Price would use Versioned Append when UpdatedSince is configured, and Delta and Ledger corrections would move to Additive Append. It updates the 1.5 requirements model text for three DeliveryHandling rules. The description covers the mechanics but gives little motivation, so the reason is implied. No comments, reviews or approvals exist yet, and the PR is stacked on #2826, which must merge first, so it looks like it is waiting on that work.

items.t: AI #2751: Adding CommitmentApplicability to the SKU Price dataset
items.b: ijurica's draft adds a CommitmentApplicability JSON column to SKU Price commitment purchase records, so covered usage's unit price can be derived without separate rows for each covered SKU, term and payment model. The argument is that a commitment changes the price of the same SKU Price rather than creating a new one, so a separate ID per commitment would only multiply records. The column is tied to commitment discounts, the existing operating model condition, so broader programs would need a new condition. For producers this means fewer rows, though users would need joins to reach the price. TF2 reviewed it on 18 November and wants to see it in practice first. The 21 November action item asks ijurica for worked examples, before-and-after ID views and a size comparison. Nothing newer is recorded, so it remains an open draft.

items.b: flanakin opened this issue on 21 November 2026 after the scenario review of PR #2879 found minor gaps in the SKU Price dataset. The scenario queries have not yet been run against a database. Three gaps are named: commitment eligibility, which the toolkit exposes in Prices() but has no query for; tiered commitment rates, which are not repriced; and SKU attribute comparisons such as VM size or generation, which have no query. Until then, people relying on SKU price data for commitment or VM-level questions have no ready query. The work is to run the queries, then add or defer each gap with a reason, and confirm in TF2 which gaps block general availability. There are no comments yet, so no view on which gaps matter most. items.t: [AI] Finalize where SKU properties live for SKU Price general availability
items.b: The issue asks where SKU properties should live before SKU Price reaches general availability. They sit outside Core scope, and feature request #2807 offers three placements: the SKU Price dataset, a SKU Details dataset, or only the Cost and Usage dataset. The choice changes dataset size, so the work is to compare the options, decide in TF-Core 2, and open a PR or feature request if the specification must change. Related work includes #2749 and #2613, and TF2 discussed on 18 November 2026 how SKU properties differ from SKU price properties. flanakin opened it on 21 November 2026 and assigned ijurica and finops-DaveMoreau. There are no replies yet, so no positions on the options are visible. It looks to be at the very start, waiting for the comparison.

items.b: Opened on 21 November 2026 under #2807, this item asks Task Force 2 to settle how the SKU Price dataset links billing accounts, contracts and contract commitments. ijurica noted that contract ID and contract commitment ID look like parent and child, but billing account ID and contract ID are not defined against each other, and some cases have many of each per the other. flanakin asked whether the contract ID on commitment prices marks the scope where prices are locked for an account or the specific commitment. items.t: [FR] One Participating Entity FR Definition To Rule Them All
items.b: rileyjenk opened this issue on 20 November 2026 to tighten FOCUS's participating entity definitions. The main problem is that 'data generator' implies the entity originally created the data, which does not fit parties that only manipulate or pass it on. The proposal refines the roles for original creator, later manipulators, last toucher and intermediaries, fixes the examples for data generators, MSP and resellers, and avoids renames where possible. If it goes ahead, source providers and processors such as FinOps tools would know which requirements apply to them, and the metadata work in #1131 could move to GA. Domo, NEOS, Walmart and Stitcher.ai each raised it as nice to have, and the FinOps Foundation prefers a processor role over redefining data generator. No responses have been posted yet, so the group's view is not yet known.

items.t: [FR] Add machine-readable FOCUS column metadata
items.b: Matt-Cowsert asks for a machine-readable metadata artifact, in YAML or JSON, published with each FOCUS release. It would list column descriptions, units, data types, relationships and sample values, so AI copilots and tools could query FOCUS data in natural language without hand-extracting the schema. Adobe and AWS are named as requesters, and the maintainers triaged it as an adoption accelerator. The proposal extends the existing Schema Metadata supported feature from runtime dataset metadata to a design-time artifact. Only one comment falls in the last two weeks: rileyjenk says it is the same thing as metadata, which suggests overlap with existing work. No reply from Matt-Cowsert or the maintainers appears in the activity shown, so the thread looks to be waiting on how this differs from current metadata. No next steps are recorded.

items.t: [FR] Data Lineage Support - Distinguish data originators, processors, and intermediaries
items.b: FR #2174 asks FOCUS to separate the roles behind "data generator", which currently covers both source providers and FinOps tools that transform their data. The aim is that requirements say who they apply to and practitioners can trace who changed a number. The Maintainers could not rate it yet. One participant doubts the problem statement, while others see value in tracing each change. Matt-Cowsert marked it blocked by metadata FRs #1060 and #1131, though participants disagree that the dependency is firm. On 16 November 2026 the Maintainers agreed to split the work: a new FR defining participating entities comes first, then metadata, then lineage, tracked as #2875. rileyjenk argues direct payment to a marketplace seller is an outlier that major clouds prohibit. The FR looks stalled in its current form, and its future depends on the entities FR.

items.t: [FR] Define Billing Period population relative to Cost and Usage
items.b: Issue #2294, opened by Matt-Cowsert in April 2026, asks the specification to say which billing periods need a Billing Period row. The aim is to let practitioners join Billing Period metadata such as status and timestamps onto Cost and Usage without missing rows, and to give data generators a testable rule. The direction raised by shawnalpay is that every distinct billing period start and invoice issuer pair in Cost and Usage should have a matching Billing Period row. The only recent activity is a comment from rileyjenk on 20 November 2026, arguing that much of the use case is already covered by recency and that the feature could adapt that. rileyjenk thinks it is close but needs some work. No other replies appear, so the thread looks quiet and the next step is not defined.

items.t: [Feedback] Clarification Request: Intended HostProviderName and ServiceProviderName Values for Sovereign Clouds (e.g., Azure operated by 21Vianet)
items.b: jngibert asks how HostProviderName and ServiceProviderName should be filled for Azure China, which Microsoft Azure sells but 21Vianet operates. Three options are on the table: Microsoft Azure as service provider with 21Vianet as host, the reverse, or Microsoft Azure for both. The reporter notes the existing example covers third-party operation, not a brand and operator split, and wants a consistent answer for normalising data. The only reply, from rileyjenk on 20 November 2026, moves the question toward the invoice: for operator-run regions the payee may be a local billing entity, as with AWS China, and they ask for a recent example. No one has picked an option or answered yet, so the thread looks stalled. Whatever is chosen would decide which entity normalised data lists as provider.

items.t: [Feedback] Commitment discount scenario CSVs still use the removed ProviderName and PublisherName columns
items.b: Matt-Cowsert reports that all 14 commitment discount scenario CSVs still carry the ProviderName and PublisherName columns, which 1.4 removed, and none has ServiceProviderName. So the 1.5 supported-feature queries that group or filter on ServiceProviderName cannot run against these files without edits. The proposal is to rename ProviderName to ServiceProviderName, keeping its values, and drop PublisherName, since all three name columns hold the same single value in each file. items.t: [Feedback] Contract Commitment by Category query: unqualified ContractCommitmentId in GROUP BY fails on PostgreSQL-style engines
items.b: Matt-Cowsert reports that the contract commitment by category query uses the bare name ContractCommitmentId in GROUP BY, which is ambiguous because the joined Contract Commitment table has a column of that name. items.t: Period and Update Date Filtering for DatasetConfiguration
items.b: flanakin proposes a changed-since option for the SKU Price dataset, so practitioners receive only prices created or modified after a chosen point in time. The need is size: re-sending every row monthly would reach about 7.5 GB, against 2.34 GB for today's Azure EA monthly price sheets. A changed-since delivery would include changed records, let later rows supersede earlier ones with the same key, and carry retired prices with an end date; overwrite delivery still applies when no point is set. flanakin's four revisions on 18 November 2026 tighten the design: changed-since now uses Append, key-changing corrections need a full delivery, cutoffs move to the previous capture time, and retirements update the cutoff field. items.t: AI #2364: Add `QuantityTierCategory` to `SkuPrice` dataset
items.b: This pull request adds a QuantityTierCategory column to SKU Price. Graduated means a tier's price applies only to units inside that tier, as in waterfall models, while Retroactive means the tier a total falls in prices every unit, as in step-function models. items.t: [AI] Decide the conversion and rendering rules for semantic tags
items.b: Opened by finops-DaveMoreau on 12 November 2026 under #2779, this issue writes down the rules for converting the specification to semantic tags, so the Working Group approves each rule once rather than reviewing 300-plus files line by line. Translations carry over existing markup, wrong links included, and account for 6,841 tags in 332 files. Inferences go further: plain Display Name matching adds 866 tags in 231 files, with Title Case words meaning a concept rather than a column as the main risk. Each rule becomes a separate converter switch, and later conversion PRs would be checked only against approved rules. In practice, non-cloud vendors could conform cleanly, while cloud providers would keep detailed cost fields under conditional rules. Support looks thin: the latest update returns the request to Seeking Champion and says it is not pressing until a task force needs it. A possible trigger is dataset-level feature levels arising from TF2's SKU Price work. Matt-Cowsert still plans to progress #2604 in 1.6.

items.t: [AI] Track the 1.5 errata from Maintainer assessment to one errata PR
items.b: This Action Item tracks the 1.5 errata candidates, filed as separate Feedback issues, from Maintainer assessment to one errata PR against working_draft, merged after 1.5 is published. Three are listed: #2836 corrects casing, IDs and links in 1.5 requirement text; #2837 corrects the PaymentCurrency, ContractId and TimeSectorEnd requirements; and #2783 points out that two CAU commitment discount requirements have no Condition, so a null value fails them, also in 1.2 to 1.4. Under the Errata Guidelines, changes to BCP-14 keywords, added columns or properties, or validation logic go to Feature Request instead. An open question is whether SkuPrice rules should join the 1.5 model through errata. The thread was opened by Matt-Cowsert on 10 November 2026 with no comments or assessments yet, so support can't be judged; all three candidates still await Maintainer assessment.

items.t: AI #2486-Ext: Review changes to entity reference and linking rules proposed in #2514
items.b: This do-not-merge draft by ijurica set out entity reference and linking rules as one consistent set across the editorial guidelines, AGENTS.md and the normative requirements guidelines. Its purpose was to compare the full version with the head of #2514 before deciding what would go into #2514, so nothing in it was decided. It sits under #2486, which aims to turn the editorial and normative guidelines into AGENTS.md rules and EDITORIAL_VALIDATION.md checks. The background summary says jpradocueva asked for rules on schema-facing references to be restored and dense rules split into separate bullets, and ijurica agreed. In the last two weeks there was little activity beyond a task force label change on 2 November 2026. On 10 November 2026 ijurica closed the draft in favor of #2848, so the work continues there and this thread has no open questions left.

items.t: Label Version Introduced with GA
items.b: flanakin's draft pull request #2776 adds a GA: prefix to every existing Version Introduced value, so 1.4 becomes GA: 1.4, matching the Preview and GA format set out in #2762. Real version names such as 1.0-preview stay as they are, and the one section with trailing text keeps that text on its own line. The open question, raised by Matt-Cowsert, is how content first published in 0.5 and 1.0-preview should be labelled. flanakin treated those as implicitly preview, but Matt-Cowsert said in October 2026 that the change did not clearly suit consistency review, and that remains the only recorded objection. In the last two weeks the only activity was jpradocueva resolving an inline comment on the dataset document without action on 10 November 2026, thanking flanakin. That does not settle the question, so the draft still looks unresolved.

items.t: [FR] Add specification-level privacy and data protection statement
items.b: Practitioners asked for a specification-level privacy statement showing which FOCUS values can identify an individual, rather than checking column by column. The Maintainers closed it on 9 November 2026, judging that protecting sensitive data is the job of each provider and its customers. Matt-Cowsert said the topic is important but outside FOCUS's scope. On the call, one maintainer said it grew from an identity column statement implying no PII, which needed fixing, and was open to a note alerting readers that any field can hold PII. Others worried a partial list would read as a promise, or asked whether the specification should cover PII at all. A check showed the Cost and Usage note already covers all its columns. Closure looks uncontested and changes little in practice, though it can be reopened.

items.t: [AI] Create the FOCUS 1.5 Data Model spreadsheet
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this action item to produce the FOCUS 1.5 Data Model spreadsheet, the filterable file listing every dataset and column, which the website still links only for 1.4. It is built from the 1.5 release candidate and adds the preview SKU Price dataset (23 columns), four Cost and Usage columns, and operating model conditions replacing free-text conditions and the Applicability Criteria tab. Two of those conditions are also preview, and some allowed values change, such as ServiceSubcategory gaining Bare Metal. A draft exists but will be rebuilt from the release tag after ratification. Maintainers must still settle choices the specification leaves open, such as column categories and whether to keep shortened descriptions. It moved to In Progress on 10 November 2026, due 17 November 2026, and no one has commented yet.

items.t: [FR] Demonstrate reusable scope rule evaluation in supported features
items.b: The request asks for a complete, reusable evaluation of the scope rules shared by eligibility and applicability columns, so data engineers need not derive it from the processing workflow. Today SKU Price Eligibility queries evaluate only part of the rules, and no supported feature uses Contract Commitment Applicability. Replying to triage feedback from Matt-Cowsert, ijurica narrowed 'reusable' to reuse across supported features rather than across columns, with one non-normative evaluation per column. In scope are SKU Price Eligibility and Contract Commitment Applicability; the draft column from #2753 is optional. Edge cases such as In and NotIn on a null dimension, which the applicability definition does not cover, remain an open question. No one else has commented yet, so support is untested; the author will revise the problem statement, use case and success criteria to match.

items.t: AI #2563: Add tiered-pricing-related glossary terms
items.b: ijurica opened this pull request to add glossary entries that separate different meanings of tier and tiered in FOCUS, including Threshold-Based Tiered Pricing, Quantity-Based Tiered Pricing, Tiered Commitment Discount and Commitment Tier, plus an editorial rule requiring qualified tier terms. The aim was to stop one word covering several pricing and commitment concepts. Matt-Cowsert raised conflicts with the SKU price tier columns in #2424 and with published requirements that still used pricing tier, and flanakin approved while flagging consistency issues. Agreement on the goal was not matched by a settled wording. In November 2026 ijurica agreed the PR could close while the underlying naming problem remained, tracked in #2839. Matt-Cowsert closed it after the 1.6 open-PR outreach. It may be reopened or redone if #2839 makes 1.6, and the branch has been kept.
items.s: Pull request · closed · last activity 2026-11-09 · ijurica

items.t: FOCUS #2183: Adding Development Process Supporting Content - FOCUS 1.5 Operating Model Augmentation Discussion
items.b: This closed pull request aimed to turn operating-model concerns raised at TF3 on 10 April 2026 into structural proposals for FOCUS 1.5, complementing the Scope Proposal. The concerns were PR comment volume rising from 60 to 70 into 300+ per release, a widening gap between domain practitioners and normative authoring, and contribution happening outside GitHub. It was framed as a discussion starting point, but the thread shows little substantive debate. The only activity in the last two weeks is Matt-Cowsert's comment of 9 November 2026 closing the PR after 1.6 open-PR outreach, as requested because the Candidate Release was already cleared. The branch is kept and reopening remains possible. The ideas look shelved rather than decided, and the thread does not say what comes next.

items.t: FR #2782: Define the preview lifecycle for whole datasets
items.b: Matt-Cowsert opened this draft pull request as a starting point for feature request #2782, which asks how a whole-dataset preview moves to stable or is removed, since the merged rules only cover its start. It adds markers to the Preview Process in the spec change guidelines: Proposed answers where existing evidence supports one, and TODO markers elsewhere. Proposals cover supporting entities, the scope list rule for requirements, and which Version Introduced value shows after promotion, and drafted text covers four questions. Nothing merges until the Task Force settles each answer. No approvals, change requests or comments are recorded yet, so reaction is not visible. The description says Task Force 1 took it up on 10 November 2026, but the record shows the change to TF-Core 1 that day, so its placement looks unsettled.
